title: HKIC shifts AI investment focus to downstream applications; BOC Investment eyes cross-border industrialisation
zh_title: HKIC将人工智能投资重点转向下游应用；中银投资着眼跨境工业化
summary: 人工智能 HKIC 表示，其超过 70% 的资本都针对早期和成长期公司，250 家投资组合公司中有 11 家在香港上市，今年计划上市的公司有 30 多家。其首席执行官概述了人工智能应用和开源创新的重点。中银投资计划跨境工业化 [![图 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:17 HKT · 2 分钟读香港投资公司 (HKIC) 行政总裁 C
content:
人工智能
HKIC 表示，其超过 70% 的资本都针对早期和成长阶段的公司，250 家投资组合公司中有 11 家在香港上市，今年还有 30 多家计划上市。其首席执行官概述了人工智能应用和开源创新的重点。中银投资计划跨境产业化

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:17 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港投资公司（HKIC）行政总裁陈嘉敏表示，公司70%以上的资金投放于早期和成长期的企业，目前投资已初见成效。她在活动上表示，在250个投资项目中，已有11家公司已在香港上市，超过30家公司计划今年上市或提交上市申请。

陈表示，未来的技术应该满足不同人群的需求，易于获取且价格实惠。以人工智能为例，她表示HKIC正在逐步将投资重点转向人工智能价值链的中下游部分，包括实际应用场景。她强调了对开源人工智能的特别关注，她说开源人工智能可以显着降低创新成本，让年轻一代和小型初创企业能够快速创新、蓬勃发展和竞争。
中银集团投资副总裁王军在同场活动中表示，公司正在实施以早期投资、小额投资和硬技术投资为重点的转型战略，以支持香港的研究成果商业化。他表示，该公司已投资超过10只科技基金和9个香港科技项目，重点关注人工智能、生物材料制造和新材料等领域。

王先生表示，中银投资将优先选择香港特区政府支持的项目，并积极探索香港科研与大湾区转型相结合的跨境产业化路径。他主张推广香港研发、内地验证的模式。

王毅表示，中银投作为立足香港的全球投资平台，将发挥国家风险资本、耐心资本和长期资本的作用。他表示，公司在能源、航空、半导体、先进制造等领域投资了一批行业影响力大、金额大、回报丰厚的重大项目。三年来，大湾区科技贷款已突破7000亿元。
王强调，公司将利用全球机构网络和跨境金融服务，助力科技走出去，推动科技创新链与制造产业链无缝对接。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Artificial Intelligence
HKIC says over 70 per cent of its capital targets early and growth-stage firms, with 11 of 250 portfolio companies listed in Hong Kong and over 30 planning listings this year. Its CEO outlined a pivot to AI applications and open-source innovation. BOC Investment plans cross-border industrialisation

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 13:17 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Investment Corporation (HKIC) Chief Executive Clara Chan said more than 70 per cent of the company's capital is placed in enterprises at early and growth stages, and the investments are already showing results. Speaking at an event, she said that among 250 portfolio projects, 11 companies have listed in Hong Kong, and over 30 plan to list or submit listing applications this year.

Chan said future technology should serve the needs of different groups of people, be easy to access and affordable. Taking artificial intelligence as an example, she said HKIC is gradually shifting its investment focus to the middle and downstream parts of the AI value chain, including practical application scenarios. She highlighted particular attention to open-source AI, which she said can significantly lower innovation costs and allow younger generations and small startups to innovate quickly, thrive and compete.

Wang Jun, deputy chief executive of BOC Group Investment, said at the same event that the company is implementing a transformation strategy focused on investing early, investing small and investing in hard technology, to support the commercialisation of research in Hong Kong. He said the firm has invested in more than 10 technology funds and nine Hong Kong technology projects, focusing on sectors including artificial intelligence, biomaterials manufacturing and new materials.

Wang said BOC Investment will give priority to projects supported by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government and is actively exploring a cross-border industrialisation pathway that combines Hong Kong research with Greater Bay Area conversion. He argued for promoting a model of Hong Kong research and development with mainland verification.

As a global investment platform based in Hong Kong, Wang said BOC Investment will play the role of national risk capital, patient capital and long-term capital. He said the firm has invested in a number of major projects with significant industry influence, large amounts and attractive returns in energy, aviation, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing. Over the past three years, technology loans in the Greater Bay Area have exceeded 700 billion yuan.

Wang stressed that the company will use its global institutional network and cross-border financial services to help technology go global, and promote seamless connection between the technology innovation chain and the manufacturing industry chain.

FOR most Filipinos, retirement is something we look forward to. After decades of working, raising a family, paying the bills and meeting deadlines, we see retirement as a reward. No more alarm clocks. No more traffic. No more office politics. Finally, we can sleep late, travel, enjoy hobbies, spend time with our family and do the things we never had time to do.

That was exactly how Miguel imagined his retirement.

At 62, after almost four decades of chasing business goals, Miguel was ready. He had saved enough to feel reasonably comfortable. His children were grown, his house was fully paid and he had been looking forward to retirement for years.

“I can finally enjoy life,” he told his friends.

During the first few months, he did. He played golf during weekdays, watched movies and enjoyed leisurely breakfasts with his wife. They went on trips. He visited friends. For the first time in many years, he had nowhere he needed to be.

It was wonderful. Until it wasn’t.

After a while, the days began to look the same. Monday no longer felt different from Saturday. His golf games became routine. Some of his friends were still working, while his children were busy with their own careers. His wife had her own activities and interests.

One morning, Miguel woke up and realized something uncomfortable. He had plenty of time, but he didn’t know what to do with it.

Miguel was bored. This may sound surprising. After all, isn’t having more free time what we all dream about? But perhaps we have misunderstood retirement.

We often think of work as something that takes time away from us. We forget that work also gives us many things beyond a salary. It gives us purpose, people and structure. It gives us responsibilities, relationships and a sense of achievement. It makes us feel that we are valued.

For 40 years, Miguel knew what he was supposed to do every Monday morning. People depended on him. He had colleagues to talk to, problems to solve and goals to achieve.

Then, suddenly, all of that disappeared.

Miguel had prepared to retire from work. He had not prepared to retire to something.

This is an important lesson in retirement planning.

We spend years asking, “How much money do I need to retire?” That is certainly an important question. We need enough money to pay for food, housing, health care, travel and the many years that may lie ahead.

We have become very good at calculating how much money we need to retire, and surprisingly, poor at imagining what we will retire to.

AARP, the American Association of Retired Persons, reported in a US study that 14 percent of retirees felt bored, while 13 percent felt isolated and another 13 percent lacked a sense of purpose. These figures are not representative of Filipino retirees, but they point to a challenge we should not ignore: Financial security alone does not guarantee a fulfilling retirement.

We should also ask: What will I do with my time? Who will I spend it with? What will give me a reason to get up in the morning?

Retirement does not have to mean doing nothing. A fulfilling retirement may require us to become more intentional about how we spend our time.

For some, it may mean mentoring younger people. After decades of experience, retirees have something valuable to give. For others, it may mean volunteering, teaching, joining a church organization or supporting a cause close to their hearts.

For some, retirement may be the opportunity to finally pursue a passion postponed because of work and family responsibilities — painting, writing, traveling or learning something completely new.

And for others, retirement may include working, but on their own terms. Part-time consulting, entrepreneurship or board work can provide both income and purpose, without the demands of a full-time career.

Relationships also matter.

During our working years, we often have hundreds of people around us. Then retirement comes and that circle suddenly becomes smaller. Our children may live in another country. Friends may still be working. Some relationships may have faded simply because schedules no longer align.

For Filipinos, there is an added reality. We naturally look to our children and grandchildren as an important part of our later years. But our children have their own careers, families and responsibilities. They can enrich our retirement, but they cannot be our entire retirement plan.

That is why we should build our social life before retirement, not wait until after we retire.

We also need structure. Freedom sounds wonderful, but too much unstructured time can become difficult. A retirement filled with exercise, family, friends, learning, hobbies, travel, service and rest can feel very different from simply having nothing to do.

This is the irony of retirement, we spend our working lives wishing we had more time, and when we finally get it, we discover that time itself needs to be planned.

Miguel eventually understood this.

He did not need another full-time job. He needed a reason to look forward to Monday.

He began mentoring younger professionals. He volunteered with a church organization. He committed to exercising regularly and made time for his family. He continued playing golf, but it became only one part of his retirement rather than the whole of it.

Slowly, retirement became interesting again.

Miguel’s experience reminds us that retirement planning should not begin and end with money.

Yes, we need to know whether our savings and investments can support us for the rest of our lives. But we also need to prepare for the life we want to live when the paycheck stops.

We should ask ourselves: What am I retiring to?

Because it is possible to have enough money and still have an empty retirement. It is possible to have financial security but no sense of purpose. It is possible to have all the time in the world and still wonder what to do with it.

Retirement should not simply be the end of our working years. It should be the beginning of a new chapter where we have greater freedom to choose how we spend our time, whom we serve and what gives our life meaning.

So, before you retire, don’t just plan your finances. Plan your life.

Because someday, you will retire. And when that day comes, the question may not be, “Do I have enough money?”

It may be an even more important one: “What will I do with all this time?”

title: 美前太平洋司令称中国灰色地带策略“空洞”，促台湾强化战时拒止能力
summary: 华盛顿 — 美国前国家情报总监、海军退役四星上将丹尼斯·布莱尔(Dennis Blair)星期三(10月14日)表示，中国在台湾周边持续进行海空演习及灰色地带行动，主要目的在于制造恐惧并迫使台湾作出政治让步。他称这种依赖台湾“不战而降”的策略是“空洞的”，台湾真正需要强化的是战时阻止解放军取得制海权和制空权的能力，同时防范中国将军事演习突然转为攻击行动。 曾任美军太平洋司令部司令的布莱尔当天通过视频，在台湾海洋委员会主办的“2026海线安全国际会议”上发表主题演讲。会议聚焦中
content:
华盛顿 —

美国前国家情报总监、海军退役四星上将丹尼斯·布莱尔(Dennis Blair)星期三(10月14日)表示，中国在台湾周边持续进行海空演习及灰色地带行动，主要目的在于制造恐惧并迫使台湾作出政治让步。他称这种依赖台湾“不战而降”的策略是“空洞的”，台湾真正需要强化的是战时阻止解放军取得制海权和制空权的能力，同时防范中国将军事演习突然转为攻击行动。

曾任美军太平洋司令部司令的布莱尔当天通过视频，在台湾海洋委员会主办的“2026海线安全国际会议”上发表主题演讲。会议聚焦中国灰色地带行动、海上封锁威胁及台湾的海线安全韧性。所谓灰色地带行动，一般是指低于公开武装冲突门槛、但旨在逐步改变现状或对对手施压的军事及准军事活动。

**“目标是恫吓台湾”**

布莱尔说，中国通过军机、军舰及其他政府船只在台湾周边活动，试图让台湾民众和领导人相信，由于中国拥有更大的体量和军事实力，北京最终吞并台湾是不可避免的。

“这场海空行动的总体目标就是恫吓--恫吓台湾民众及其领导人，”布莱尔说。“中国试图制造一种印象：仅凭它更大的体量和实力，就必然能够吞并台湾。”

他表示，北京希望借助这种压力促使台湾政府作出政治让步，并让国际社会逐渐接受中国所希望的结果。

“然而，中国的策略是空洞的，”他说。“因为它依赖台湾在没有真正被征服的情况下投降，依赖台湾作出让步。”

布莱尔认为，台湾能否抵御北京要求其放弃主权的压力，最终取决于台湾是否具备在战争中阻止中国取得海空控制权的能力，而不是取决于解放军在和平时期能够派出多少舰艇和军机。

“台湾抗拒中国要求其交出主权的能力，取决于它能否在战时阻止中国控制海域和空域，”他说。“这并不取决于中国在和平时期的行动。”

**以“陆战思维”处理海洋问题**

布莱尔用中世纪欧洲军队围城作为类比。他说，古代军队通常包围城市、挖掘壕沟并逐步接近城墙，迫使守城一方相信防线终将被突破，从而选择投降。

但他认为，这种围城思维不适用于台湾，因为台湾周围是海洋，中国的军机和舰艇在附近活动，并不等同于陆军实际占领了台湾管辖的土地或突破了台湾防线。

“中国目前的灰色地带策略不是由水兵设计的，而是由陆军设计的，”布莱尔说。“陆军并不了解海洋环境，而是以陆战概念看待问题。”

他表示，解放军舰艇和军机数量增加并更加靠近台湾，固然可能引发警觉，但距离台湾更近也可能使它们在战争爆发时更加容易遭到攻击。

“我知道，看到数量更多的解放军舰艇和军机比过去更靠近台湾，可能令人不安，”他说。“但对一名职业海军军官来说，它们越靠近台湾，一旦战争爆发，也就越容易被摧毁。”

这些看法是布莱尔个人的军事判断。其他美国和台湾安全专家警告，解放军频繁在台湾附近活动，也可能缩短台湾方面的预警时间、消耗其防务资源，并使外界更难判断北京何时会从演习转向实际军事行动。

**防范演习突然转为攻击**

布莱尔承认，台湾和其他海洋国家不能因此忽视中国的行动。解放军近年来在台湾周边演练导弹及空中攻击、海上封锁等军事行动，台湾必须防范北京利用演习部署发动突袭。

“从军事角度而言，台湾必须警惕中国可能从演习状态转为攻击行动，”他说。

布莱尔表示，每当中国举行大规模海空演习时，台湾都应提高整体战备水平，周边国家的武装力量也应加强警戒，以免措手不及。

他认为，关键问题并不是解放军在和平时期能够派出多少兵力，而是台湾能否在友好国家支持下，于战时击败或阻止承担攻击任务的解放军部队。

“如果台湾有信心依靠自身能力，并在朋友支持下击败中国的战时侵略，那么中国的灰色地带声明和行动，就只能产生经过媒体放大的表面恫吓效果，”他说。

**加强监控、执法和公共外交**

布莱尔建议台湾密切监视中国在周边海域的军方、海警、科考和民用船只活动，审慎配置执法资源，并运用无人系统、卫星、雷达和社交媒体等工具，及时向国内外公布相关活动。

他说，如果中国舰艇或飞机接近台湾领海或领空，应受到警告和伴随监视；如果实施发射武器、派遣突击队登陆，或侵害台湾民众和财产等敌对行为，则应受到制止，必要时可以使用武力。

布莱尔还呼吁台湾加强公共外交，用持续且具有新意的方式向国际社会说明中国行动的性质。

“台湾不能允许中国在国际公众认知中建立一个‘新常态’，”他说。最重要的是，台湾应强化并展示其军队和社会在战时反制中国海空攻击的能力。

布莱尔也肯定台湾近年来将“汉光演习”从以军方为主的演练，扩大为包含民防和全社会韧性的防卫演习。他认为，台湾展现保卫自身的决心和能力，有助于争取理念相近国家在危机发生时提供支持。

**中国扩大台湾东部海域活动**

布莱尔发表上述评论之际，中国军方、海警、科考船和其他公务船近年来持续扩大在台湾周边的活动。

路透社上星期援引台湾民营航空公司安捷航空(Apex Aviation)的监控报告说，该公司一架侦察机今年8月在台湾花莲海岸约50公里外，发现被台湾方面认定为中国海上民兵船的“闽福鼎渔07902”，与中国海警2502舰及“向阳红03号”科考船在同一区域活动。这是已知中国海上民兵船首次出现在台湾东部海域。相关船只当时均在台湾所称的“限制水域”以外。

台湾国防部指责中国以执法和科研为掩护扩大非冲突状态下的行动范围，试图制造拥有“事实管辖权”的假象。中国国台办和国防部没有回应路透社就这起事件提出的置评请求。

美国国务院随后对美国之音表示，中国在台湾以东的行动“深度破坏稳定”，只会加剧紧张局势。美国敦促北京停止对台湾施压，转而与台湾民选当局展开有意义的对话。

北京主张台湾是中国领土的一部分，并表示不排除使用武力实现统一。台湾政府拒绝北京的主权声索，强调台湾的未来只能由台湾人民决定。

title: Top ‘Cockroach’ leaders sent to jail after protest
summary: **NEW DELHI** — Two leaders of India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were remanded in custody for five days on Wednesday, as police ratcheted up efforts to clamp down on anti-election commission protests. CJP activists and oppositio
content:
**NEW DELHI** — Two leaders of India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were remanded in custody for five days on Wednesday, as police ratcheted up efforts to clamp down on anti-election commission protests.

CJP activists and opposition parties have defied a security crackdown to demand the resignation of India's chief election commissioner, accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party.

The commission, which oversees voting in the world's most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

*   [Ukraine accuses US of helping Russia as missiles hit Kyiv](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/world/ukraine-accuses-us-of-helping-russia-as-missiles-hit-kyiv/2446078)

Delhi Police said CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka, 30, and Saurav Das, 27, were taken into custody for their "alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and violate the law."

At the end of the five-day remand period, they could have their detention extended, be granted bail or be released.

[![Image 1: RESILIENT RALLYISTS Student activists shout slogans during a protest demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner in the capital New Delhi on Oct. 14, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259329.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259329.jpg)
RESILIENT RALLYISTS Student activists shout slogans during a protest demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner in the capital New Delhi on Oct. 14, 2026. AFP PHOTO

On Tuesday, the pair jumped security barricades to wave the national flag at Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have barred people from using.

*   ![Image 2: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

"Their alleged attempts to instigate others through social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration," police said.

Parliamentary opposition leader Rahul Gandhi of the Indian National Congress party backed the men, who were detained after entering the site.

Jantar Mantar, in the heart of the capital New Delhi, has been sealed off for days with yellow metal barricades and guarded by security personnel.

Delhi Police said on Monday it had removed the site from its list of designated protest venues.

*   ![Image 3: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

"Waving the Tricolor at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime," Gandhi said in a post on social media. "Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice."

The Congress and CJP have both protested over the voter roll revision. Gandhi said on Wednesday that "all protests are one."

"Different banners, one cause," he added.

'Stand up'

*   ![Image 4: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke praised the men, saying they "knew they could be thrown behind bars" but went ahead to wave the national flag.

"They've shown the entire country that the only way to stand up to a bully like Modi is to never bow down, no matter the consequences," he said in a social media post.

Das has worked as a journalist, while Ranka, an engineer, studied at the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology and the London School of Economics.

Rights advocates and critics say Modi's government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents — allegations the government rejects.

Human Rights Watch said on Wednesday the Indian government must uphold the right of citizens to protest peacefully.

"The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections," it said in a statement.

Journalists in New Delhi marched on Tuesday to protest the detention of reporters during demonstrations. The Press Club of India said attacks on journalists doing their jobs were "unacceptable."

The electoral list revision, which began last year, has led to more than 133 million names being removed from electoral rolls, according to media reports. Critics say the exercise has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.

Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

Members of Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.

Home Minister Amit Shah, Modi's powerful right-hand man, dismissed the protests as localized and accused Gandhi of pursuing an "action plan to protect infiltrators."

"The people of India are not going to fall for your deception," he said, predicting a "resounding majority" for government in the next general election, due in 2029.

summary: 首尔无法承担裂痕 驻美国大使将情报共享异常视为主要挑战 统一部长官郑东泳周一在首尔政府大楼对记者表示，在华盛顿限制与首尔共享情报的争议中，韩美同盟没有问题。郑先生拒绝了华盛顿方面的评估，即他有关朝鲜平安北道久城核设施的言论泄露了美国机密情报，称这是“误解”，并坚称“美国错了”。在国家A级
content:
首尔无法承受的裂痕
驻美大使认为情报共享异常是主要挑战

统一部长官郑东泳周一在首尔政府大楼对记者表示，在华盛顿限制与首尔共享情报的争议中，韩美联盟没有问题。郑先生拒绝了华盛顿方面的评估，即他有关朝鲜平安北道久城核设施的言论泄露了美国机密情报，称这是“误解”，并坚称“美国错了”。

同一天在华盛顿举行的国会审计中，韩国驻美国大使康京和表示，两国之间的高层磋商次数如此之少，以至于局势令人沮丧。 “我承认与白宫的沟通是有限的，”她补充道。当被问及双边关系中最困难的悬而未决的问题时，康还指出“情报合作”是一个重大挑战。

在周二的内阁会议上，韩国总统李在明表示，韩美同盟非常重要，但他补充说，在国家关系中应避免顺从和屈从的态度。他还强调，韩国是一个主权独立的国家，处理好与周边大国的关系很重要。
美国的任何盟友都无法幸免于与唐纳德·特朗普政府在安全和贸易方面的摩擦。然而，大多数盟国领导人都考虑到华盛顿的影响力，寻求通过幕后谈判解决争端。李明博关于维护国家尊严的言论，原则上是完全合理的。但刻意宣称韩国不会屈服在外交上是不明智的。现在的问题是华盛顿将如何解读他的话。

朝鲜战争期间，美国向半岛部署了近180万军队，其中3.6万多人阵亡。目前，仍有超过2.8万美军驻扎在韩国，帮助维护朝鲜半岛的稳定与和平。韩国还严重依赖美国的延伸威慑，包括核保护伞，来应对朝鲜核武库构成的威胁。在此背景下，将美国与中国、俄罗斯等邻国置于同等地位根本站不住脚。

李明博的言论似乎强化了郑先生的主张，即韩美同盟没有任何问题。但总统和统一部长是否充分认识到联盟的重要性？

郑在三月份揭露了龟城核设施的存在后，华盛顿对该地点的机密情报被泄露感到愤怒，开始限制其卫星收集的一些有关朝鲜的情报。
美国军方通过数百颗侦察卫星和其他监视设备监视朝鲜的核活动。它收集的图像和信号情报对于韩国应对拥有核武器的朝鲜威胁的能力至关重要，特别是考虑到首尔自己没有核武器。因此，任何对此类情报共享的限制都是令人严重关切的问题。

最重要的是，情报和军事合作取决于相互信任。对情报共享的限制发出了一个令人不安的信号，即人们之间的信心

【原文 English Original】
A rift Seoul cannot afford
Ambassador to US identifies abnormality in intelligence sharing as major challenge

Unification Minister Chung Dong-young told reporters at Government Complex Seoul on Monday that there is no problem with the South Korea-US alliance amid controversy over Washington's restrictions on sharing intelligence with Seoul. Chung rejected Washington's assessment that his remarks about nuclear facilities in North Korea's Kusong, North Pyongan Province, had disclosed classified US intelligence, calling it a "misunderstanding" and insisting that "the US is wrong."

At a National Assembly audit in Washington on the same day, South Korean Ambassador to the United States Kang Kyung-wha said high-level consultations between the two countries were taking place so infrequently that the situation was frustrating. "I acknowledge that there are limits to communication with the White House," she added. Asked about the most difficult outstanding issues in bilateral relations, Kang also identified "intelligence cooperation" as a major challenge.

At a Cabinet meeting on Tuesday, President Lee Jae Myung said the South Korea-US alliance is very important, but added that submissive and subservient attitudes should be avoided in relations between countries. He also stressed that South Korea is a sovereign, independent nation and that managing relations with the major powers surrounding it was important.

No US ally is immune to friction with the Donald Trump administration over security and trade. Yet most allied leaders seek to resolve disputes through behind-the-scenes negotiations, mindful of Washington's influence. Lee's remarks about the need to maintain national dignity are perfectly reasonable in principle. But going out of one's way to declare that South Korea will not submit is diplomatically unwise. The question now is how Washington will interpret his words.

During the Korean War, the United States deployed nearly 1.8 million troops to the peninsula, more than 36,000 of whom were killed in action. Today, more than 28,000 US troops remain stationed in South Korea, helping maintain stability and peace on the Korean Peninsula. South Korea also relies heavily on US extended deterrence, including the nuclear umbrella, to counter the threat posed by North Korea's nuclear arsenal. Against this backdrop, putting the United States on the same footing as neighboring powers such as China and Russia is simply untenable.

Lee's remarks appear to reinforce Chung's assertion that there is nothing wrong with the South Korea-US alliance. But do the president and the unification minister fully appreciate the alliance's importance?

After Chung exposed the existence of nuclear facilities in Kusong in March, Washington, angered by what it regarded as a leak of classified intelligence about the site, began restricting some intelligence on North Korea gathered by its satellites.

The US military monitors North Korea's nuclear activities through hundreds of reconnaissance satellites and other surveillance assets. The imagery and signals intelligence it collects are vital to South Korea's ability to counter the threat from a nuclear-armed North Korea, especially given that Seoul has no nuclear weapons of its own. Any curtailment of such intelligence sharing is therefore a matter of grave concern.

Above all, intelligence and military cooperation depend on mutual trust. Restrictions on intelligence sharing send a troubling signal that confidence between the two sides has been eroded.

The two countries also face a host of major unresolved issues, including tariffs, South Korean investment in the United States and nuclear energy cooperation. If Seoul cannot maintain effective communication with key decision-makers in the White House, its national interests risk being pushed aside.

The US alliance remains a lifeline for South Korea. The stark reality is that Seoul still has much to seek from Washington on a range of issues. It cannot afford to let rifts in the alliance deepen and then pay the price in both security and economic terms.

The government must act swiftly to restore trust and resolve the intelligence-sharing dispute through concrete confidence-building measures. This should include reviewing personnel arrangements where necessary to address US concerns. Reassuring Washington that Seoul takes the alliance seriously is not a matter of submission; it is a matter of protecting South Korea's national interests.
(END)

title: 12 plays, musicals make the cut in new theater festival
summary: **MANILA, Philippines —** From a total of 373 submissions for the first Puregold Teatro Panalo, the 12 finalists were announced at Gateway Mall today, Oct. 14. [![Image 1: Teatro Panalo finalists with members of the selection committee. PHO
content:
**MANILA, Philippines —** From a total of 373 submissions for the first Puregold Teatro Panalo, the 12 finalists were announced at Gateway Mall today, Oct. 14.

[![Image 1: Teatro Panalo finalists with members of the selection committee. PHOTO BY RAOUL CHEE KEE](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/15/1260629.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/15/1260629.jpg)
Teatro Panalo finalists with members of the selection committee. PHOTO BY RAOUL CHEE KEE

The eight one-act plays and four musicals are “The Girl Scout Law" by Rhain Alcoriza; “True to Life" by John Lapus; "Trahedya ng Kamote" by Marjay Manalastas; “The Boy Foretold by the Stars (One-Act Play)” by Dolly Dulu; “Nothing but Dreams" by Ricardo Novenario; "Youngstunna" by Jerom Canlas; “Walang Maliit na Bagay" by Joshua Lim So; "@HOME" by Edralin Cabrera, Kathlyn Castillo, Michael lan Lomongo, Marjorie Lorico, Maria Teresa Jamias, and J Victor Villareal; “Ang Maayong Balita Sumala Kang Bibo Bautista" by Jude Thaddeus Gitamondoc; "Baka Mali ang Tamaraw” by Emmanuel Antonio; “ Manang-Mana Nga!" by Steven Hotchkiss and Jay Pangilinan; and “The Fourth Wall has Fallen" by Heber O'Hara.

Each finalist was awarded a P100,000 talent fee to officially mark the start of their journey.

“For this incubation-based theater festival of one-act plays, there were entries from Manila, Cebu, Zamboanga, Dumaguete and even Arizona in the United States,” said Vincent de Jesus, two-time Palanca Award-winning playwright and festival director.

Despite this, Gitamondoc and his musical “Ang Maayong Balita Sumala Kang Bibo Bautista” appears to be the only regional finalist. In an interview with the Cebu-based writer after the announcement, he said he has been writing since 2002 “but this is the first time I’ve ever entered and won in a contest like this.”

“Ang Maayong Balita” is about a gay man who enters the seminary for less than holy reasons. “He follows the man he loves only the realize something about himself and his faith once he’s inside the seminary,” Gitamondoc told The Manila Times.

*   ![Image 2: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

De Jesus said Teatro Panalo is not the first theater fest of its kind but credited Puregold for creating the platform for more creatives “to continue to be brave and to tell their stories.”

“With Teatro Panalo, ordinary people [like] those who shop at Puregold will now get a chance to watch live theater. Because there are some stories that are best experienced live,” said festival chair Ivy Hayangan-Piedad.

The 12 finalists were chosen by a selection committee that included playwright and festival director De Jesus, director and actor Jenny Jamora, playwright Liza Magtoto, film director and producer Marlon Rivera, and theater artist and lyricist Nicolas Pichay.

Joining the team as Screening Committee members were Palanca winners Dr. Layeta Bucoy and Allan Lopez, who screened the festival submissions and shortlisted the entries. National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee provided invaluable expertise and creative guidance as artistic adviser.

*   ![Image 3: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

The inaugural theater festival is the latest artistic project of grocery chain Puregold, which held its annual movie and short film festival CinePanalo earlier this month.

“With Puregold Teatro Panalo, we hope to give these works the stage they deserve and, in our own way, help Philippine theater continue to grow,” Hayangan-Piedad said.

*   ![Image 4: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Puregold Teatro Panalo will run from February 20 to March 14, 2027.

title: FC Seoul on verge of clinching 1st S. Korean football title in 10 yrs
zh_title: 首尔FC有望夺得10年来首个韩国足球冠军
summary: 作者：Yoo Jee-ho 首尔 10 月 15 日（韩联社）——首尔 FC 队即将在 10 年来首次夺得韩国顶级足球联赛冠军，最早将于周日开香槟庆祝。进入周末比赛，首尔FC在12支球队的K联赛1中以20胜5平6负积65分稳居榜首。蔚山HD FC积47分排名第二。两家具乐部还剩七场比赛，如果蔚山HD FC周六没有获胜并且首尔FC周日获胜，那么FC首尔将获得第七个冠军。首尔FC球员在俱乐部K赛中庆祝1-0战胜仁川联队
content:
作者：柳智浩

首尔10月15日电（韩联社）——首尔FC最早将于周日开香槟庆祝，距离他们10年来在韩国顶级足球联赛中的首个冠军已经很近了。

进入周末比赛，首尔FC在12支球队的K联赛1中以20胜5平6负积65分稳居榜首。蔚山HD FC积47分排名第二。

两家具乐部还剩七场比赛，如果蔚山HD FC周六没有获胜并且首尔FC周日获胜，那么FC首尔将获得第七个冠军。

2026 年 9 月 5 日，首尔足球俱乐部球员在首尔世界杯体育场举行的俱乐部 K 联赛 1 场比赛中庆祝 1-0 战胜仁川联队（这张资料照片由韩国职业足球联盟提供）。球员们举着一条围巾，上面写着“走向第七颗星”，指的是为赢得联赛冠军而刻在球队队服上的一颗星星。 （照片非卖品）（韩联社）

蔚山HD FC将于下午4:30迎战富川FC 1995。周六，一场平局将使蔚山队的积分达到 48 分。如果首尔FC第二天击败金泉尚武FC，他们的积分将提高到68分。

在这种情况下，在还剩六场比赛的情况下，20分的差距将是难以逾越的。随后，首尔FC将与2018年和2025年的全北现代汽车队并列，成为在当前设置下最快夺得K联赛1冠军的俱乐部，在32场比赛后实现这一目标。
首尔FC是本赛季唯一一支没有连续输球的俱乐部。他们是联赛中进球数最多的球队，为 58 个，比蔚山队多 10 个；失球最少，为 26 个，比江原 FC 少 2 个。

前锋方面，波兰前锋帕特里克·克利马拉以14个进球领先，仅落后蔚山队的亚戈·卡里略1个，边锋郑承元则贡献了8个进球和6次助攻。

守门员具成润作为最后一道防线的稳定力量，首尔FC已经有13次不失球，排在联赛第二位，仅次于江原FC的14次。

主教练金基东终于享受到了首尔FC在2024赛季之前任命他时最初设想的成功。首尔FC在金的第一个赛季获得第四名，并在2025年跌至第六位，导致一些沮丧的球迷有时对金发出嘘声。但这位 55 岁的战术家现在带领首尔 FC 即将获得期待已久的冠军。

2026 年 10 月 10 日，首尔足球俱乐部主教练金基东在首尔世界杯体育场举行的 K 联赛 1 场比赛中观看球队对阵济州 SK FC 的比赛（这张照片由韩国职业足球联盟提供）。 （照片非卖品）（韩联社）

jeeho@yna.co.kr
（完）

【原文 English Original】
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 15 (Yonhap) -- Nearing their first title in the top South Korean football league in 10 years, FC Seoul can pop champagne as early as Sunday.

Entering weekend play, FC Seoul are sitting pretty atop the tables of the 12-club K League 1 with 65 points on 20 wins, five draws and six losses. Ulsan HD FC are in second place with 47 points.

With seven matches left for both clubs, FC Seoul will clinch their seventh championship if Ulsan HD FC do not win Saturday and if FC Seoul themselves win Sunday.

FC Seoul players celebrate their 1-0 win over Incheon United in the clubs' K League 1 match at Seoul World Cup Stadium in Seoul on Sept. 5, 2026, in this file photo provided by the Korea Professional Football League. The players hold up a muffler that reads, "Toward the Seventh Star," referring to a star placed on a team's uniform for winning a league title. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

Ulsan HD FC will face Bucheon FC 1995 at 4:30 p.m. Saturday, and a draw will take Ulsan to 48 points. And if FC Seoul beat Gimcheon Sangmu FC the following day, they will improve to 68 points.

In that scenario, the 20-point gap will be insurmountable with six matches to go. FC Seoul would then tie the 2018 and 2025 Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors as the fastest club to clinch a K League 1 title under the current setup, doing so after 32 matches.

FC Seoul are the only club this season not to have lost consecutive matches. They have scored the most goals in the league with 58, 10 more than Ulsan, and have also conceded the fewest goals with 26, two fewer than Gangwon FC.

Up front, Polish striker Patryk Klimala has been leading the way with 14 goals, just one behind Yago Cariello of Ulsan for the league lead, and winger Jeong Seung-won had contributed eight goals and six assists.

Goalkeeper Gu Sung-yun has been a steady force as the last line of defense, with FC Seoul having recorded 13 clean sheets, the second most in the league behind Gangwon FC's 14.

Head coach Kim Gi-dong is finally enjoying the kind of success FC Seoul first envisioned when they appointed him before the 2024 season. FC Seoul finished fourth in Kim's first season and dropped to sixth place in 2025, leading some frustrated fans to boo Kim at times. But the 55-year-old tactician now has FC Seoul on the cusp of a long-awaited title.

FC Seoul head coach Kim Gi-dong watches his team play Jeju SK FC during the clubs' K League 1 match at Seoul World Cup Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 10, 2026, in this photo provided by the Korea Professional Football League. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

(END)

title: Ilocos Region health officials make push for improved stroke care coordination
summary: HEALTH officials and medical professionals in the Ilocos Region are seeking better coordination among hospitals and health care facilities to address delays in stroke treatment, particularly for patients in remote communities, as stroke rem
content:
HEALTH officials and medical professionals in the Ilocos Region are seeking better coordination among hospitals and health care facilities to address delays in stroke treatment, particularly for patients in remote communities, as stroke remains the region’s leading cause of death.

The issue was discussed during a multi-stakeholder roundtable organized by UHC Watch and supported by Boehringer Ingelheim, where participants examined ways to improve stroke prevention, emergency treatment, referrals and rehabilitation across Region 1.

In La Union, stroke has remained among the causes of death over the past three years, according to Dr. Ivy Ico of the Provincial Department of Health Office in La Union.

*   [Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

“Stroke is not only a major health problem. It also places a significant financial burden on patients, families and communities,” Ico said.

[![Image 1: FACEBOOK/UHC WATCH](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260041.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260041.jpg)
FACEBOOK/UHC WATCH

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

She cited the need to improve referral pathways, specialist availability, public awareness and coordination among health care providers.

For patients in remote municipalities, traveling to facilities equipped to provide specialized stroke care can take two to four hours, potentially exceeding the 4.5-hour treatment window for certain interventions.

*   ![Image 2: Arroyo hails Nobel Peace Prize winner](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259931.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Arroyo hails Nobel Peace Prize winner](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/news/national/arroyo-hails-nobel-peace-prize-winner/2445857)

Dr. Mary Grace Fabia-Mistica, stroke program head of the Ilocos Training and Regional Medical Center Brain and Spine Center and the La Union Medical Center, said delays in recognizing symptoms and coordinating referrals contribute to patients arriving at hospitals beyond the critical treatment window.

“Some families still mistake stroke symptoms as a temporary episode of high blood pressure or initially seek treatment at home. Every delay can affect a patient’s chances of survival and recovery,” Mistica said.

Health care professionals also cited uneven access to neurologists, rehabilitation providers and long-term follow-up services, particularly in geographically isolated communities.

To address referral delays, stakeholders are advancing StrokeLiNCS LU, or Stroke Linking Institutions for Network Care, toward a Stronger La Union. The initiative aims to connect health care facilities through a hub-and-spoke system.

*   ![Image 3: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260179.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/news/our-soldiers-are-not-troublemakers/2445870)

Under the proposed model, designated hospitals, including the Ilocos Training and Regional Medical Center and the La Union Medical Center, would provide specialized stroke services, while smaller facilities would focus on recognizing symptoms, stabilizing patients and arranging referrals.

The proposed system would also use standardized protocols, hospital pre-notification, workforce training, telemedicine support and a shared stroke registry to improve coordination from emergency treatment through rehabilitation.

“The model does more than move patients,” Mistica said. “It helps bring expertise closer to where patients are.” The initiative is aligned with the Department of Health’s National Policy Framework on the Prevention, Control and Management of Acute Stroke, which seeks to establish coordinated stroke care under the Universal Health Care Act.

Ico said the framework covers prevention, acute treatment, rehabilitation and long-term recovery, supported by stronger health care networks, data systems, training and financing.

*   ![Image 4: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

At the provincial level, the La Union government and local stakeholders are working to incorporate dedicated stroke referral pathways into the next version of the province’s health care provider network referral manual.

Plans for a Level II general hospital and a neurological rehabilitation center have also been included in the proposed La Union Medical Hub.

Alvin Manalansan, co-convenor of UHC Watch, said improving stroke care requires cooperation among government agencies, hospitals, health care professionals, civil society groups and private organizations.

Participants called for continued coordination across the full range of stroke care, from public awareness and emergency response to treatment, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up.

很多人健身後，會喝無糖豆漿來補充蛋白質，看似少負擔，不過，營養師蔡正亮表示，無糖豆漿的脂肪含量其實不低，若與低脂鮮奶相比，特濃無糖豆漿的脂肪含量，約是低脂鮮奶的2至3倍。

蔡正亮在臉書粉專[「蔡正亮營養師專欄教室」](https://www.facebook.com/nutrition12345/posts/pfbid0URBtHzNVH1Z9unF6MsoTBZnUuKWS1opyeVtV5wK6xdw4Vqev7ZpKgKd6nFVJ9mACl)發文指出，說到豆漿，大家想到的通常就是高蛋白、低熱量、沒有膽固醇，但真相是無糖豆漿的脂肪含量，沒有大家想像中那麼低，甚至有些高蛋白濃豆漿，脂肪含量已接近全脂鮮奶。

蔡正亮指出，一般全脂鮮奶，每100c.c大約含3至4公克脂肪；低脂鮮奶約1至1.5公克，一般市售無糖豆漿，每100c.c大約含1.5至2.5公克脂肪，部分濃無糖豆漿甚至達3公克以上，如果跟低脂鮮奶相比，濃無糖豆漿的脂肪含量，反而是低脂鮮奶的2至3倍。

蔡正亮表示，濃無糖豆漿深受健身族青睞，因為使用更多黃豆原料，但蛋白質增加的同時，脂肪含量也會跟著提高。舉例來說，一瓶400c.c的濃無糖豆漿，如果每100c.c含有2.5公克脂肪，整瓶喝完就攝取了10公克脂肪，光是脂肪就提供90大卡熱量，這還不包括蛋白質及碳水化合物的熱量。

蔡正亮表示，黃豆本身沒有膽固醇，能提供植物性蛋白質，對於想增加植物性食物攝取的人來說，是不錯的選擇。但豆漿裡面的脂肪，每公克仍有9大卡熱量，如果正在減脂，且平時三餐攝取已相當充足，一天喝好幾瓶濃豆漿，仍可能導致全天總熱量超出需求，影響減脂成效。

**Heather Liu**

# Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case

(中文版見後）What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）(Charlotte and me in 2003)In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。） Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States. （多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。） (drawing by Charlotte)Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。） (drawing by Charlotte)Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。） (drawing by Charlotte)The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。） (Charlotte drawing)With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community. （您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese: （以下是部分有關此案的中文文章：）https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole廖亦武：《魏京生DNA認親案》(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641齊家貞：《我認識的劉懷昭和魏京生》(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears o

content:
## Details

Come learn all about hiking the Highlands and how you can join us on the trails in Glencoe in 2027!
 Join us for an info session designed for women who are ready to hike the [rugged trails of Scotland's Highlands in 2027.](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours)
 This is a detailed look at the solo trips for women we offer through Bold Spirit Travel.
 All are welcome, you do not need to be signed up for a trip with us to attend.

1.   Learn about the Highlands and what the trails are like in this area.
2.   Ask questions about gear, logistics, and training.
3.   Consider flights and transportation.
4.   Think about packing.

**This is for solo women travelers who are ready to get exploring again and need the details to feel prepared and ready to go.**
 We will cover the following topics:

*   _Gear_
*   _Food considerations_
*   _How to get there/get home_
*   _Hotels_
*   _Group numbers (small group)_
*   _Luggage and van assist_
*   _Miles to walk each day / elevation_
*   _Prep/training_
*   _Roommates_
*   _And more_

**Costs and Journeys:**

1.   This is a **free** event and all are welcome.
2.   All our guided trips are small-group, all-women journeys perfect for solo female travelers who want to make some new friends.

**Hike with Us in Scotland in 2027**

*   [Hiking Scotland for Solo Female Travelers September 2027](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours)

**Considerations:**

*   You do not need to be signed up to go with us on [this hiking trip](http://%5Bhttps//%5Bwww.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours%5D%5D(www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours%5D)(%5Bhttps://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours%5D(https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours)) "[[https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours)](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys-1/hiking-highlands-scotland-2027-solo-female-tours)") to attend the info session.
*   Come learn. Become inspired.
*   We want you to walk YOUR trail in Scotland, whether that is with us or on your own.
*   Learn more about who we are and our all-women tours here: [https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys](http://%5Bhttps//%5Bwww.boldspirittravel.com/journeys%5D%5D(www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys%5D)(%5Bhttps://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys%5D(https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys)) "[[https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys)](https://www.boldspirittravel.com/journeys)")

**Tickets:**

content:
ONLINE Sheng Zhen Gong Classes, Thursdays at 7:00 PM

In each class, we focus on a standing form and a seated form. These forms are an excellent remedy to calm our nervous system in challenging times. The practice is an opportunity to restore and nurture your energy reserves, to find relief from tension and stress, and to cultivate open-heartedness.

YES! Everyone is welcome, beginners and experienced practitioners.

Register here: [https://lastmaskcenter.pages.ontraport.net/qigongonline](https://lastmaskcenter.pages.ontraport.net/qigongonline)

Every season, or new quarter, we start a new series of classes that include a seated form and a standing form from the Sheng Zhen forms of Master Li Junfeng. (For more Sheng Zhen info click here. ([http://shengzhen.org](http://shengzhen.org/))) The practice creates a deep state of inner peace and a feeling of Love and harmony with the universe. It opens the heart, strengthening the body while calming the mind and emotions naturally. It can inspire a new sense of joy and compassion for others, and a deeper understanding of life.

**Vangie Villa**

Donation protected

Dear family and friends,

As many of you know, I’m Vangie, Ricky Villa’s daughter. I’m reaching out to you all today to explain why I’m raising money for my dad. As you know, he’s been incarcerated for quite some time now and is almost home with all of us! Please keep in mind I don’t want the donation number to intimidate anyone this is the goal we have set to get started as we all know getting a hold of a good attorney is costly! From the bottom of our hearts we greatly appreciate all the help that can be given!

Today, April 22, 2026, my dad reached out to his closest loved ones: me, my grandma Diana, my brother Ricky, my sister Ashley, and all his siblings, as well as his fiancée Irma. He had some news to share with us. He’s been withholding some information, but he finally worked up the courage to tell us that they plan to charge him with another offense. This would only prolong his incarceration, even though he’s already served a significant portion of his sentence.

His cases have been completely unfair, and he hasn’t received justice. My dad hasn’t seen me or my siblings out of prison, and he hasn’t seen his granddaughter out of prison either! For those of you who know my dad, you know where his heart is at and how true he is. He’ll go through anything to make sure his family and friends are taken care of before anything else.

Despite being in prison for a long time, that has never deterred us away from my dad and no one ever turned their back on him . We all have a lot of love for my dad. Every person or friend who has spoken with him or about him has never said anything negative about him. Everything has always been positive and reflective of how he truly is my dad is a jokester a prankster and one person you will love to have around you just simply because of his character family friends who haven’t seen my dad in years still show him love and respect just because of the person he is so full of energy and joy! He has so much love for his family and friends. He’s always ready to support and help his family and friends any way he can even while being incarcerated.

All I’m asking is if everyone can please share or donate anything possible to help my dad get an attorney who can help get him the justice he deserves. He deserves one who’s willing to fight for him and prioritize him and his case. Most importantly, he deserves a lawyer who’s going to hopefully free him and bring him home where he belongs, where he’s loved and respected, and not where he’s being treated unfairly.

My dad has had numerous health and mental health issues, and the problems he’s facing are only going to worsen due to the poor medical care he’s received. I hope to have my dad home soon so I can help him with all his medical needs.

Thank you all for your consideration and support. It truly means a lot to me and my family thank you all once again and god bless you all

Sincerely,

Vangelina Villa and the whole Villa family

# Support Cecilia’s Over Seas Detention Release

Help Bring Cecilia Home: Urgent Legal Support for US Citizen Detained in China My name is I. Denise Torres, and I'm reaching out with an urgent request to help my daughter Cecilia, a US-born citizen currently detained in China. Our family faces mounting legal expenses that are far beyond our financial means, and time is critical. Our Immediate Need Following the guidance of the US Consulate, we must retain specialized legal representation in China who is specifically an English speaking attorney that can navigate the Chinese legal system on Cecilia's behalf. Legal representation for international clients in criminal matters in China can range from several thousand to hundreds of thousands of yuan China Legal Experts depending on case complexity and duration. For families like ours, working-class Americans with limited resources, these costs are insurmountable without help. The US Consulate has recommended a qualified law firm experienced in representing foreign nationals. Cecilia has not been formally charged at this time and the funds are intended solely to support the current legal process related to her detention. However, we need to secure their services immediately, which requires: Attorney retainer and representation fees for an English-speaking Chinese defense lawyer Communication and translation services to facilitate family contact Personal care expenses for Cecilia during detention, including medical necessities Ongoing legal advocacy through the completion of her case Why Legal Representation Is Critical Cecilia is alone in a detention facility with severely limited communication rights and no phone calls, no family visitation, and no direct contact with us. The US Consulate has been extraordinarily supportive, but they can only conduct welfare checks once per month and cannot intervene in China's legal proceedings. A private attorney is her only opportunity for: Regular advocacy visits (every two weeks, as permitted) Direct communication link between Cecilia and our family Professional legal representation through required proceedings Monitoring of her wellbeing and medical needs The Medical Urgency Cecilia manages diabetes requiring three insulin injections daily. She experiences related complications including severe stomach issues and pain. Ensuring she receives proper medical care during detention is essential, and legal representation is critical to advocating for her health needs. The Process and Timeline Under guidance from the US Consulate, I cannot share specific details about the circumstances of Cecilia's detention, as doing so could compromise the legal process. What I can share is that we're working through official channels and following all recommended procedures to bring her home safely. Both Cecilia and I are US-born citizens. She is a compassionate, selfless young woman who would help anyone in need. Now she needs us to help her. Our goal is to cover estimated attorney fees for legal representation, communication services that allow us to stay connected with our daughter, and personal care expenses during her detention. Legal fees in China vary significantly based on lawyer experience, case complexity, and whether specialized English-language services are required Lawzana. International representation for US citizens detained abroad requires substantial financial resources that our working-class family simply doesn't have. Every Day Counts Without proper legal representation, Cecilia faces this situation alone—unable to communicate with her family, uncertain about the process ahead, and managing a serious medical condition in a foreign country. Every contribution, no matter the size, brings us closer to securing the legal help she desperately needs. How You Can Help Donate any amount you can afford—every dollar helps Share this campaign widely across your networks Keep Cecilia in your thoughts—this support means everything to our family The US Consulate continues monitoring her welfare, but only an attorney can advocate for her case, facilitate our communication, and work toward her safe return home. Our Gratitude Thank you for taking time to read Cecilia's story. Your generosity during this incredibly difficult time gives us hope. As a mother watching my daughter face this ordeal from thousands of miles away, your support is a lifeline. With deep gratitude and hope, Irma Denise Torres

# Help 88-year old Veteran Keep His Home After Marriage Fraud

UPDATE 9/8: Our retainer is gone and we are in need of funds to replenish the trust account with the attorney. We are in the middle of the discovery process, and while the wife continues to hide assets, we are forced to subpoena her bank and investment accounts which costs more money. The lawyer will ask the court that she pay our attorney fees, it likely won’t be granted until the trial in February. By then we may be out a lawyer because we can’t pay him. UPDATE 6/25: We have retained an attorney! We are continuing to seek donations for when the retainer runs out. Due to family donations, we need to raise less money than originally anticipated, so we’ve lowered our fundraiser from $15,000 to $10,000. My 88-year-old father is a victim of elder abuse and marriage fraud that may leave him homeless and destitute. I am setting up this GoFundMe to pay for his legal representation, likely the only way he will be able to keep his home of 23 years. Please hear our story: About six years ago, my father was pursued through an online dating site by a woman named Candy. In a matter of days and through very limited communication, she convinced my father she was in love with him, asked for his address, hopped on a Greyhound, and moved into his small home. Within two weeks they were married at the courthouse. Candy is a citizen of the People’s Republic of China, had been in and out of the country on a B2 tourist visa, and is 22 years younger than my father. Immediately after the marriage, Candy began the US citizenship process with my father's sponsorship. Upon her demand, my father took out a series of small loans to hire her an immigration attorney even though she started working. She began to receive social security spousal support, and was also receiving money from her Chinese pension. In spite of her income, my father continued to pay all their bills himself, including the mortgage and utilities. When Candy took a trip to Hawaii (with her friends and her own income), my father disclosed to me that he did not feel safe with her. I learned she had become increasingly hostile towards him, calling him fat, denying him food, referring to him as “the sickly old man” behind his back, and at times being aggressive enough that he would choose to sleep and/or sit in his car until she left the house. Her favorite insult was "garbage husband." It became increasingly clear that Candy was exploiting my father. At one point she approached him with a Quit Claim deed to transmute his sole property into community property. In the throes of an abusive relationship, my father felt like he had no choice but to sign the deed. Now my father's home of 23 years - and its equity - belongs to her as well. About a year ago, Candy started stealing money from my father, and he found himself overwhelmed with not being able to pay the bills that supported them both. By this time, my father had long been beaten down from the abuse, but in a last ditch effort he built up the nerve to ask Candy to return the stolen money and sign a quit claim to give back his house - she said only if he gave her $80,000! My brother and I were relieved when my father made the decision to file for divorce, and we become increasingly involved on his behalf. We prepared court paperwork for him as he cannot identify the correct documents. My father can't type and his handwriting is slow, so filling out forms is also challenging. He is a poor communicator. He often nods off at court. Recognizing that my father cannot represent himself in court, a judge ordered a settlement conference, which went nowhere fast because Candy still demands $80,000. My father does not have any money laying around, and is leveraged to the hilt with debt from the marriage (all in his name), so he couldn't borrow money to pay her even if he wanted. As a National Guard veteran, senior, and low-income individual, my father is eligible for free legal advice three times over, but what he needs is representation. Because of his advanced age and the complexity of his case, he does not have the mental capacity to represent himself. He has long been unable to organize and process decent amounts of detailed information without assistance. He is overwhelmed at the thought of losing his house, which flusters him even more. If he loses his house, not only does he face homelessness, but more importantly he loses the property's equity that was intended to cover his long-term nursing care, care that he is starting to need, and the emotional toll of being forced to sell and move out of his house would surely be the end for him. We appreciate every donation, big and small. The money raised will go directly to his legal representation. Please feel free to contact me with questions or more details.

# HELP BRING MY SON BACK HOME

My name is Nelson Wells, Sr. and I write to you on behalf of my wife, Cynthia Wells, and our family, asking for your assistance in our fight to bring home our son, Nelson Wells, Jr., who has been unjustly imprisoned in China for more than eight years. We are natives of Louisiana, who have served our country for decades. I served in the United States Army for more than 20 years, and Cynthia, served at the Department of Defense for nearly 28 years. We’ve traveled all over the United States and world and have a host of extended family and friends, who join us in the fight for our son. This includes Nelson’s wife and three children, who are desperate to have him returned to our family unit. Like us, Nelson, Jr. loved to travel, and it was this love of travel that inspired him to live in Japan and visit China. Unfortunately, it was on one of these visits there that Nelson was arrested and later convicted on a drug charge with little evidence of his guilt, opportunity to defend himself, or due process prior to this conviction and incarceration. He was stripped of his freedom without the opportunity to tell his story. Indeed, it took months for us to learn what happened to him. We’ve fought for years to help our son, working behind the scenes with advocates, lawyers and diplomatic officials in the United States and China. We were told that this quiet strategy was the best strategy to keep him safe, but after nearly a decade with little progress, we’ve decided to tell our story, Nelson’s story. It breaks our heart to say it, but Nelson is now sick. The weight of incarceration has taken a toll on his physical and mental health. As you can see from the photos, our child has gone from a healthy man to an emaciated one, who has lost more than 100lbs and is in poor health. He is suffering from life-threatening medical problems in a prison in Chongqing Southwest China far from us, far from his wife and children. Indeed, we have not seen him during these eight long years. We are sustained by periodic calls from him, and for that, we are thankful to God, the United States State Department, and the Chinese government and prison officials. Still, we fear that he will not last much longer. It is time to bring Nelson home, perhaps through medical parole. Whatever the pathway, getting help for him is more urgent now than ever and so we are turning to the public for help with legal fees and welfare support on his behalf. No amount is too small, and we promise that your donations will only be used to directly secure the release and return of our son. We also invite you to leave a comment alongside your donation with a note of inspiration that we can share with Nelson, a personal reflection about Nelson for those who know him, or a testimonial about why you are deciding to join our fight. Thank you for considering this request. Thank you for your thoughts and prayers for Nelson. Thank you, in advance, for your generosity. Even the act of creating this go fund me page and sharing our story publicly has given us – including Nelson – purpose and hope for the future when we can be reunited. Until then we are heartbroken, but we fight on. Mr. Nelson Wells, Sr. and Mrs. Cynthia Wells Louisiana

Like us, Nelson, Jr. loved to travel, and it was this love of travel that inspired him to live in Japan and visit China. Unfortunately, it was on one of these visits there that Nelson was arrested and later convicted on a drug charge with little evidence of his guilt, opportunity to defend himself, or due process prior to this conviction and incarceration. He was stripped of his freedom without the opportunity to tell his story. Indeed, it took months for us to learn what happened to him. We’ve fought for years to help our son, working behind the scenes with advocates, lawyers and diplomatic officials in the United States and China. We were told that this quiet strategy was the best strategy to keep him safe, but after nearly a decade with little progress, we’ve decided to tell our story, Nelson’s story. It breaks our heart to say it, but Nelson is now sick. The weight of incarceration has taken a toll on his physical and mental health. As you can see from the photos, our child has gone from a healthy man to an emaciated one, who has lost more than 100lbs and is in poor health. He is suffering from life-threatening medical problems in a prison in Chongqing Southwest China far from us, far from his wife and children. Indeed, we have not seen him during these eight long years. We are sustained by periodic calls from him, and for that, we are thankful to God, the United States State Department, and the Chinese government and prison officials. Still, we fear that he will not last much longer. It is time to bring Nelson home, perhaps through medical parole. Whatever the pathway, getting help for him is more urgent now than ever and so we are turning to the public for help with legal fees and welfare support on his behalf. No amount is too small, and we promise that your donations will only be used to directly secure the release and return of our son. We also invite you to leave a comment alongside your donation with a note of inspiration that we can share with Nelson, a personal reflection about Nelson for those who know him, or a testimonial about why you are deciding to join our fight. Thank you for considering this request. Thank you for your thoughts and prayers for Nelson. Thank you, in advance, for your generosity. Even the act of creating this go fund me page and sharing our story publicly has given us – including Nelson – purpose and hope for the future when we can be reunited. Until then we are heartbroken, but we fight on. M

summary: Wrongly Accused Abroad Help Me Afford Legal Defense and Survival. Hi to everyone, my name is Julian! I'm an Italian and American national, I used to work as a substitute teacher in an Italian high school. On 26th of August I went to China t
content:
Wrongly Accused Abroad Help Me Afford Legal Defense and Survival.

Hi to everyone, my name is Julian! I'm an Italian and American national, I used to work as a substitute teacher in an Italian high school.

On 26th of August I went to China to start traveling. Some weeks later, on September 28th, I arrived in Thailand. Since then, I had been traveling mostly in northern Thailand.

It was an incredible experience — honestly, probably the best of my life.

But then… something completely unexpected happened to me.

On Wednesday, November 26th, very early in the morning around 5:30 a.m., I booked a Grab taxi from where I was staying, in Nothanburi (a province northwest of Bangkok), to go to Suvarnabhumi Airport. I had a flight with Etihad Airways at 8:55 a.m. to Italy, where I live.

I arrived at the airport two hours before departure, as recommended by the airline. The check-in process went smoothly, and everything seemed normal until I reached immigration.

There were two sections: one with officers and one automatic lane. The automatic lane was moving faster, so I chose that. When it was my turn, I tapped my passport on the scanner, but a red message appeared. I tried again—same result.

A security guard came to help me and tried scanning my passport himself, but it still didn’t work. He then told me to go to the manual lane.

The immigration officer took my passport, typed something on her computer, smiled, and said, “Sorry, just wait here for a moment.” She left and returned a few minutes later with another officer who looked serious. They escorted me to the immigration desk and told me to wait.

At that moment I started to feel anxious. I thought maybe I had overstayed my visa. My visa was expiring that same day, November 26th, so I was worried I might be in trouble.

After about 15 minutes, I approached the desk to ask what was happening, but they just told me to sit down and wait. Ten minutes later, another officer came with a paper showing a photocopy of my passport and asked me to confirm that it was mine. I said yes.

Most of the staff did not speak English, which made everything more frightening.

Then, using a translation app on his phone, the officer showed me a message saying that I was being charged with possession of indecent content and distribution of that material on websites accessible to the public.

I was completely shocked and confused. I thought there must be a mistake.

There was no opportunity to explain anything. Two immigration officers escorted me to another office inside the airport.

Inside, I was told to sign many documents, all in Thai. No one explained them to me in English. They took photos of me with officers behind me. Later, they took more photos from the front, left, and right. That’s when I realized: they were taking a mugshot.

Everything felt surreal. I was exhausted because I hadn’t slept much the night before. It felt like a nightmare.

“Did you tell your family that you have been arrested?”

That was the moment it truly hit me. I had never imagined being arrested in my life, especially not in a foreign country. I was terrified and confused.

I called my embassy, but it was still closed. Later, they contacted me and explained the situation. The embassy told me that creating and distributing certain types of videos can be a crime in Thailand, as in many countries, and that if I believed I was innocent, the Thai legal process would take its course.

They asked me for two emergency contacts and sent me a list of lawyers, advising me to find legal representation.

Eventually, we arrived at a police station in Samut Prakan province, in a town called Khlong Dan.

At that point, I was officially placed under arrest and faced the risk of jail if I was unable to pay bail.

My Italian passport was confiscated by the police and is currently being held by them. This happened on November 26th.

I am writing this today, February 24, 2026. I am creating a YouTube channel to explain in more detail what is happening to me. I am currently safe and living in a hostel in Bangkok. The last three months have been the most stressful of my life.

In December, I struggled to obtain a visa extension, which I was finally able to secure on January 8, 2026. This visa must be renewed every 45 days.

I am asking for your help to raise funds for legal fees, living expenses, and possible bail that may be requested by the judge if the case goes to court. I cannot legally work in Thailand because that requires a work visa. My family is helping me at the moment, but they cannot sustain these expenses for much longer. I do not know when I will be able to return to my country, as I must wait for the Thai legal process to run its course.

**I want to state clearly that I have never uploaded any indecent content on the internet. The accuser, a woman, has claimed to provide “evidence” of this. At the police station, I was shown the alleged evidence, which consisted of screenshots from an OnlyFans profile belonging to a couple: a Thai woman and a Caucasian man. The man’s face was blurred, and I was accused of being that person.**

The case will soon be handed over to the prosecutor, and according to police officers at Khlong Dan Police Station, it will most likely proceed to court (that's what they said). This is extremely distressing, especially because my lawyer has told me that cases with weak evidence are usually dropped by the police or the prosecutor.

Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Any help or support during this very difficult time would mean a great deal to me.

Julian

title: Can We Still Talk Across Our Differences? The Future of Dialogue, Tue, Oct 27, 2026, 5:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: [Skip to content](https://meetup.com/ideas-exchange-portland/events/316855203/#main) ## Details Welcome to this fascinating global debate, held simultaneously across cities and countries. Join thoughtful people from around the world for a s
content:
[Skip to content](https://meetup.com/ideas-exchange-portland/events/316855203/#main)

## Details

Welcome to this fascinating global debate, held simultaneously across cities and countries. Join thoughtful people from around the world for a structured conversation where disagreement is welcome and curiosity matters more than winning.
**Reserve your place:**[https://ideas-exchange.info/en/online-debate/can-we-still-talk-across-our-differences/](https://ideas-exchange.info/en/online-debate/can-we-still-talk-across-our-differences/)
 Public conversation increasingly rewards certainty, outrage and performance. Political identity can shape whom we trust before a discussion even begins, while fragmented media make it difficult to agree on basic facts. Yet dialogue remains one of the few tools available when people must share workplaces, families, cities and democracies despite deep disagreement.
 This final English debate in the Meetup series asks when dialogue changes minds, when it merely manages coexistence, and when refusing conversation is justified. We will examine empathy without endorsement, the role of power and bad faith, and the habits and institutions that make disagreement productive.

## **Key topics we will discuss**

1.   Why people change—or defend—their beliefs
2.   Understanding, persuasion, compromise and coexistence as different goals
3.   Empathy without agreement or endorsement
4.   Identity, dignity and emotional safety
5.   Shared facts in a fragmented information environment
6.   Bad faith, propaganda and the limits of dialogue
7.   Online incentives that turn conversation into performance
8.   Practices and institutions that help people disagree better

You do not need to arrive with a fixed position. Bring experiences, questions and a willingness to listen. People of all ages, professions, countries and political viewpoints are welcome.

## **Practical information**

**When?** Tuesday, October 27, 2026
**What time?** 8:00 PM New York · 7:00 PM Chicago · 5:00 PM Los Angeles
**How does it work?** Online on Zoom · International groups · Maximum 9 participants per group
**How much?** US$6 contribution · First participation free on request · Full refund if it is not for you
**Do I need to prepare?** You do not have to prepare. The optional Food for Thought videos below offer contrasting perspectives and useful questions.
**How do I connect?** You will receive the Zoom link by email no later than 24 hours after payment.
**Register now:**[https://ideas-exchange.info/en/online-debate/can-we-still-talk-across-our-differences/](https://ideas-exchange.info/en/online-debate/can-we-still-talk-across-our-differences/)
