How do today’s autocratic governments maintain power, and what challenges do they pose for democracies?

In Autocracy, Inc., Anne Applebaum argues that modern autocratic governments are not necessarily united by a single ideology. Instead, she describes networks connected by shared interests in maintaining power, wealth, and political impunity.

The book examines why traditional responses such as international condemnation, economic sanctions, and popular opposition may struggle against these networks. Applebaum also makes the case that democracies need to reconsider how they respond.

About CPL Book Club:

This monthly gathering's mission is simple: to explore profound opinions
 and accounts of our nation’s and the world’s most critical issues
 through in-depth books. But it’s not just about reading - it’s about
 embracing diverse perspectives, sparking discussions, and sharing
 thoughts with fellow explorers of knowledge.

What you’ll get out of book club: our hope is for you to dare to dive
 deep, analyzing topics and navigating the twists and turns of politics
 together. If you share a passion for continuous learning and want to
 explore the intricacies of our world’s challenges, then this club is
 your intellectual haven (or entry) into finding out more.

title: Does Politics Have to be so Antagonistic?, Sun, Oct 18, 2026, 5:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: ▶ To attend, register on Member Hub — an RSVP here does NOT give you the Zoom link. Registration takes a moment, and the Zoom link is emailed to you and shown there: [https://members.crossingpartylines.net/events/cmuge0hqq00ay8pio0os1tc80?s
content:
▶ To attend, register on Member Hub — an RSVP here does NOT give you the Zoom link. Registration takes a moment, and the Zoom link is emailed to you and shown there:
[https://members.crossingpartylines.net/events/cmuge0hqq00ay8pio0os1tc80?src=meetup](https://members.crossingpartylines.net/events/cmuge0hqq00ay8pio0os1tc80?src=meetup)

When one political party takes an action the other strongly opposes, there can be pressure to respond in kind—or go even further. Over time, political disagreements can become a cycle in which each side sees its actions as necessary responses to what the other side has proposed.

At this meeting, we’ll explore how we experience this dynamic, what we want from political leaders when the stakes feel high, and whether there are times when not being antagonistic is possible—or even desirable.

We’ll ask questions such as:

• Have you ever found yourself wanting your side to push harder because of something the other side had done? What felt at stake for you?
 • Have you ever thought your own side went too far in responding to the other? What made it feel different that time?
 • Can you think of a political leader who chose not to respond in kind—or who worked with the other side when there was pressure not to? How did you react?
 • What might make you support a leader who chooses to not fight the other side’s proposal, even when other people on your side wanted them to?

This will be an opportunity to explore how political actions and reactions shape one another and consider what we want from our leaders when political differences and pressures increase.

title: Songwriter Support Group - Zoom Edition, Wed, Oct 21, 2026, 7:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: Hello songwriters! We are continuing our Songwriter Support Group over Zoom and hope you will join us! This is a great chance to connect with fellow songwriters and hear what others are creating. And, as we have discovered over the past yea
content:
Hello songwriters!

We are continuing our Songwriter Support Group over Zoom and hope you will join us! This is a great chance to connect with fellow songwriters and hear what others are creating. And, as we have discovered over the past year, you can log in and share from almost anywhere!

The Zoom room will open at 6:50pm and we will start promptly at 7:00pm. Plan to login at least a couple minutes early to make sure you are there for the start of the meeting. We will post the Zoom link a day or two before the meeting.

Please read the "Virtual Rules" below as there are some minor and important requirements in order for you to participate and for this to be effective. Also, if you are new, please make certain your meetup setting allows you to receive private messages as that is how I communicate initially. If you have it turned off, you WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RECEIVE MESSAGES AND I WILL REMOVE YOU FROM THE LIST TO ALLOW A WAITLISTED MEMBER TO ATTEND.

Looking forward to hearing your beautiful songs.

The requirements for your song:

A) Have your lyrics ready to share with the group. This can be done by sharing your computer screen or pasting your lyrics into the chat. If you have any questions, please send us a note and we'll be happy to help out.

B) You need to be able to perform it live OR have a recording of it that you can play over Zoom. If you have questions about this please contact me at least 48 hours ahead of the meeting.

Also…

Tell us what you’d like critiques of and we’ll verbally discuss only what each writer would like to hear about. It's not up to anyone in the group to make value judgements on anyone's work (it's good, it's not good). We're here to consider our songs from where they're at, with respect to the artistic work we're helping to nurture and grow.

The event is limited to 11 people. You must stay for the duration of the event as you would if you came in person. After 11 have signed up, a ‘yes’ rsvp goes on a wait list, so please don't RSVP yes to hold a spot if it's only a 50-50 chance you'll make it. NO SHOWS AND LAST MINUTE CANCELS WILL NOT HAVE PRIORITY FOR FUTURE CIRCLES.

New people and all genres and levels of music are welcome!

content:
【大紀元2026年10月15日訊】（大紀元記者夏楚君澳洲悉尼編譯報導）一項調查發現，兩個涉嫌與中共間諜有關的領英（LinkedIn）帳戶，在全球累積了數千名人脈，並以有償諮詢服務為誘餌，主動聯繫了數十名在澳洲政府、警務及貿易領域任職的人士。

澳廣（ABC）的調查發現，這些涉嫌間諜偽裝成智庫員工，向目標提供具競爭力的報酬，以換取「有價值的建議」。

2016年至2025年間，超過100名與澳洲有關的人士被列為接觸目標，包括前昆州州長、現任反對黨領袖史蒂文·邁爾斯（Steven Miles）、一名澳洲聯邦警察（AFP）指揮官，以及多名聯邦政府高級官員。他們的個人資訊出現在自稱代表智庫的兩個LinkedIn帳戶的聯絡人記錄中。被指控的外國特工聯繫了其中的58位聯絡人，部分收件人也提供了個人聯絡資訊。

澳廣披露，這些澳洲人是被同一中共間諜網絡鎖定，該網絡曾招募澳洲商人亞歷山大·切爾戈（Alexander Csergo）。切爾戈已因「魯莽外國干預罪」入獄，成為首名依此罪名被定罪者。

澳洲聯邦警方在調查切爾戈期間獲得的LinkedIn記錄顯示，這些帳戶曾聯繫過其他澳洲人，其中包括在政府機構和州貿易投資機構工作的人員。聯邦警方稱，這項行動由中共國家安全部（MSS）策劃。聯邦警方表示，中共國家安全部使用虛假的LinkedIn帳戶，聯繫並培養潛在的外國線人，然後向他們索取資訊。

但中共駐堪培拉大使館否認相關指控，稱澳洲聯邦警方的說法「毫無根據」。

今年6月，由美國、英國、澳洲、加拿大和新西蘭組成的五眼聯盟發出罕見聯合警告，指中共情報機構利用線上求職平台進行招募，藉此取得對五眼聯盟國家具有戰略及戰術優勢的情報。

## 以高薪顧問工作為誘餌 接觸政府及貿易部門人士

2021年11月，當時居住在上海的切爾戈收到一個名為Vera Su的LinkedIn帳戶發出的兼職工作邀請。對方自稱來自Nesa Consulting，表示該機構希望聘請專家，就中國與澳洲之間的貿易提供建議。澳廣對Vera Su的通訊記錄進行分析後發現，同樣的LinkedIn帳號也在尋找其他擁有相關專業知識和人脈的人。

被直接接觸的人士包括曾任職於澳洲貿易投資委員會（Austrade）、澳洲外交貿易部（DFAT）、新州投資局（Investment NSW）、維州投資局（Invest Victoria）及澳洲旅遊局（Tourism Australia）的人員。

部分訊息更直接探詢對方能否接觸政府內部人士。其中一則訊息寫道：「我想知道您是否有特殊的資訊來源……例如：來自政府重要人物的資訊。」

一位澳洲貿易投資委員會的員工表示，他不能接受金錢，因為他為澳洲政府工作，但他表示願意介紹自己職業網絡中的人脈。

前昆州州長邁爾斯在2021年4月擔任副州長期間，也與Vera Su的LinkedIn帳戶有聯繫。據澳廣了解，邁爾斯沒有回覆Vera Su發出的任何訊息。

## 商業顧問：警惕網上接觸及美人計

澳廣檢視的數據顯示，部分與澳洲有關的目標分享了聯絡方式，或討論改以LinkedIn以外的方式繼續交流，包括通過微信、電話或會面。

商業顧問尼克·科伊爾（Nick Coyle）在處理其前伴侶成蕾在中國被捕一事時，也遭涉嫌中共間諜的接觸。

「那段時間我收到很多奇怪的接近」，他說。有些是「美人計」，有人試圖線上或線下成為「朋友」。

「我採取的做法是——如果我之前不認識他們，就會回避」，他說。

澳洲人生教練（life coach）阿德里安·卡希爾（Adrian Cahill）也在2021年與Vera Su交換了聯絡方式。他懷疑自己前軍人的背景使他成為更具吸引力的目標。

「我經常收到這類訊息」，他說。「有人寫信給我說『我們有工作、有錢、有預算』。」

他說，過去接受的訓練有助他辨識這類手法，但缺乏安全及情報經驗的人會逐漸被誘入陷阱，提供「越來越多的信息」。

## 專家：情報搜集手法出現根本轉變

中國情報問題專家尼古拉斯·埃夫蒂米亞迪斯（Nicholas Eftimiades）形容這類國家支持的「撒網」行動是情報搜集手法的「根本轉變」。他表示，中國日益增長的AI能力可能發揮了作用，使中共情報人員能夠更有效率、更安全地進行大規模招募。

「他們可以一次接觸數十萬人，招募人員為他們工作的成本更低」，他說。

曾為美國政府處理涉及中共情報行動案件的美國前聯邦檢察官維卡斯·迪德瓦尼亞（Vikas Didwania）表示，LinkedIn是情報收集的「金礦」。

「我們在LinkedIn上看到有人公開自己能接觸到什麼機密資訊、擁有什麼等級的安全許可。」

迪德瓦尼亞表示，從LinkedIn招募對象取得的資訊可能並非機密，甚至不實用，但可能只是培養消息來源過程的一部分。

「在關係發展過程中，你可以開始再推進一步。」

## 與中國往來的澳洲人面臨的微妙平衡

近年來，澳洲安全情報局（ASIO）局長邁克·伯傑斯（Mike Burgess）警告稱，外國干預澳洲的威脅已達到「極端級別」，並且很可能會加劇。

在切爾戈的審判中，法庭獲悉他沒有洩漏任何機密資訊，他的報告均來自公開信息。克雷格·史密斯（Judge Craig Smith）法官判處切爾戈三年六個月監禁。他表示，阻止人們參與可能危害澳洲國家安全的活動「至關重要」。

對於與中國合作的澳洲人來說，這項判決也重新界定了與外國實體進行合法合作與國家支持的干預之間的危險界線。

中國約有2,000家智庫，這些機構與中共及政府的關係各不相同，而且往往不透明。此外，中共2017年實施的《國家情報法》要求組織及公民支持國家情報工作。一些專家認為，這項法律在實際運作中的影響，也可能波及在中國經營的外國企業。

迪德瓦尼亞表示，應對中共間諜活動的努力需要權衡利弊，避免產生寒蟬效應。

他表示，「如何區分真正意義上的合作和實際上是國家安全部招募人員的合作，確實是一個挑戰。」

title: 外长街头拉票时评价中国留学生英语欠佳，引发争议
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻

content: 才学了两个月英语而已 “她的英语说得不太好。” 近日，新西兰外交部长Winston Peters街头竞选时，对一名中国留学生英语水平的评价引发争议。 而就在今年7月，这位外长还曾因对一名中国出生的华人议员说“回你自己的国家”而遭到抨击。 据新西兰当地媒体报道，随着新西兰大选临近，新西兰外交部长、优先党（NZ First）领袖Winston Peters带领工作人员走上街头，希望通过与选民面对面交流，为自己的政党争取支持。 10月6日上午约11点，Peters去了奥克兰北岸的Takapuna进行街头拉票。 不过，当时街上的行人寥寥无几，Peters和一众工作人员走了很长一段路都没碰到一个人。 他甚至看了看手表调侃说“我们来早了一个小时”，还询问身边记者：“人都去哪儿了？” 随后，他继续沿街寻找愿意交流的民众，并遇到了几名正在英语学校学习的留学生。 现场视频显示，Peters主动走近几名留学生，与她们聊天。 交流开始后，他先询问其中一名女生来自哪个国家。 女生回答，她来自中国。 他又问道：“中国哪里”（Where about China？） 但女生听成了“best China”，于是回答了一句“yes”。 随后，Peters又询问她学习英语多久了。 女生回答：“两个月。” 得知这一情况后，Peters提到了一句英语学习中非常经典的句子： “The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.” 这句话包含英语字母表中的全部26个字母，因此经常被用于英语打字练习、字体展示以及键盘测试。 不过，从现场画面来看，双方交流过程中似乎存在一定语言障碍，对话并没有持续多久就结束了。 Peters转身向身边人员评价：“She couldn't speak English very well.”（她英语说得不太好。） 这段对话随后被现场媒体记录，并出现在当地媒体对其街头竞选活动的报道中。 事件曝光后，在新西兰华人社区引发争议。 一些观点认为，一名刚学习英语两个月的留学生，在日常交流中出现表达困难并不令人意外，公众人物面对年轻留学生时，可以给予更多鼓励。 但也有人认为，Peters的表述只是客观评论当时的交流情况，并不是嘲讽。 这件事争议的焦点在于，作为新西兰外交部长，同时也是长期活跃在政坛的政治人物，在面对语言能力仍处于学习阶段的移民群体时，公开评价其英语水平差是否合适。 其实，这并不是Winston Peters第一次因涉及华人群体的言论受到关注。 今年7月，在新西兰议会的一场辩论中，Green Party议员Lawrence Xu-Nan与Peters发生言语交锋。 在争论过程中，Peters对Xu说：“Go back to your own country.”（回你自己的国家去。） 随后，他还补充了一句：“Go back to where you've come from, you loudmouth.”（回你来的地方去，你这个大嘴巴。） 据报道，Xu-Nan出生于中国天津，后来移居新西兰，并在新西兰政坛担任议员。 Peters的相关言论随后引发华人群体的不满。 新西兰总理Christopher Luxon也公开指责，这样的表达“是种族歧视”、“很冒犯”。 中国驻新西兰大使馆也就相关言论提出交涉。 Lawrence Xu-Nan则表示，这类言论让移民社区感到不舒服。 Peters随后回应称，自己是在表达政治观点，并强调言论自由的重要性。 Winston Peters长期以强调新西兰利益、对移民问题立场强硬闻名。他领导的NZ First党目前也是新西兰政府联盟成员之一。 从今年7月的议会风波，到此次街头竞选活动中的留学生交流事件，涉及华人群体的言论接连引发关注。 在新西兰多元文化社会背景下，政治人物如何讨论移民、语言和文化差异，也成为当地社会持续讨论的话题。

# 台灣採購阿拉斯加天然氣 美學者：強化能源韌性縮減貿易順差

2026/10/15 09:26

[](javascript:)[](javascript:)[](javascript:)[](javascript:)[](javascript:)[![Image 17](https://imgcdn.cna.com.tw/www/website/img/support.svg)](https://cna.com.tw/donate/)

（中央社記者[侯姿瑩](https://cna.com.tw/author/0193/)華盛頓14日專電）美國總統川普稱台灣已同意在未來20年內採購阿拉斯加液化天然氣管線計畫30%天然氣。美學者今天向中央社記者分析，這有助強化台灣能源韌性、縮減對美貿易順差；台灣在美國出口市場的地位越重要，華府就越有意確保台灣安全。

川普（Donald Trump）昨天在阿拉斯加一場造勢集會上表示，台灣同意在未來20年內採購阿拉斯加液化天然氣管線計畫30%天然氣，還將額外投資44億美元用於該項計畫。他今天又在自家社群媒體「真實社群」（Truth Social）發文重申此事。

台灣經濟部指出，中油去年3月簽署「阿拉斯加液化天然氣買賣暨投資意向書」後，已與美方開發商協商取得重大進展，依目前規劃，開採後每年採購600萬噸液化天然氣，以及參與專案開發，預估投資金額最高44億美元。

針對這項天然氣採購及投資計畫，華府智庫「史汀生中心」（The Stimson Center）資深研究員孔明尚（Michael Cunningham）以電子郵件回覆記者詢問表示，這對台灣、美國及台美關係而言，都是有利的發展。若協議落實，將有助強化台灣能源韌性，同時也有助縮減台灣對美貿易順差，「這是華府非常在意的事項」。

根據台灣財政部統計，2025年台灣對美貿易順差約為1501億美元。

孔明尚指出，最重要的是，這類採購協議能提升台灣作為美國客戶的重要性。「台灣在美國出口市場的地位越重要，美國就越有意確保台灣維持安全」。

他認為，有鑑於阿拉斯加天然氣計畫預計2031年才會開始出口，川普所提及的20年採購時程意味著，至少就這項天然氣計畫而言，「台灣直到2050年代都將維持關鍵地位」。

另一方面，華府智庫哈德遜研究所資深研究員華特斯（Riley Walters）受訪表示，這項宣布意義重大，特別是在韓國對阿拉斯加液化天然氣計畫是否能獲利表達疑慮後。

華特斯分析，台灣承諾採購約1/3的產量，將有助確保這條天然氣管線的獲利能力。就美台關係而言，這項宣布也有助台灣朝向達成擴大對美投資承諾的目標邁進。

[![Image 18](https://imgcdn.cna.com.tw/www/website/img/ad300x223.jpg)](https://lin.ee/tPtHlLQ)

川普表示，韓國將投資500億美元推動阿拉斯加液化天然氣計畫。不過，外媒報導，韓國方面則說，唯有在這項計畫具備商業可行性的情況下才會推進。

經濟部表示，透過長期能源採購及專案投資，有助於增加天然氣供應來源，進一步強化台灣能源韌性。阿拉斯加液化天然氣計畫可透過太平洋航線直達台灣，有助分散天然氣運輸路線及地緣政治風險；若計畫順利推進，最快2032年可挹注國內天然氣供應。（編輯：田瑞華）1151015

# 病患進診間整疊「AI診斷」砸上桌要求照著治療 醫傻眼：當我得來速？

01:07 2026/10/15

中時新聞網

醫師徐國峰表示，日前有病患帶著整疊AI診斷，要求照上面進行診治，讓他傻眼到不行。（示意圖：shutterstock／達志）

人工智慧世代到來，許多人遇到疑難雜症時，第一時間都是求助AI，但也有人把AI的話當成聖旨，甚至要求專業人士照AI做。近日專精於椎間盤突出與坐骨神經痛的醫師徐國峰分享自己遇到的奇葩案例，有位病患上門時，把整疊AI診斷砸到桌上，要求按照上面進行治療，讓他傻眼「當我得來速嗎」。

徐國峰日前在[臉書粉專發文](https://www.facebook.com/msnhsu/posts/pfbid0UfGzg8jR2zwEynjw41LHuz2ZQbNGKBd4HG3dSmMhzXw4QhKcxy1Ur2VLWrKTQF4Al?locale=zh_TW)「資料印了整整十五頁，結果只准林北回答一個好字？」表示近來有位初診患者一坐下來，就把整疊比論文還厚的A4紙砸到桌上，除了MRI報告外，還有10幾頁的ChatGPT對話紀錄，上面甚至用螢光筆與紅筆標好重點，讓他一時以為是大學指考衝刺筆記。

患者開口說「AI說我腳麻是因為椎間盤突出、椎管狹窄，加上第二級滑脫害的，你照這個方向處理就好」，當他詢問是小腿哪邊、走幾步會麻？下樓梯會不會踩空時，患者竟露出不耐表情，「上面不都寫了嗎，就是神經壓迫啊」，徐國峰解釋，需要敲反射、測肌力，確認症狀跟片子有沒有對上，話音未落，患者就不客氣打斷詢問「AI都交叉比對完了，你照上面處置很難嗎」。

徐國峰形容，當下心裡真的是有1萬隻「草泥馬」狂奔而過，花貴鬆鬆的掛號費進來是來看病還是點得來速的？直言真的很賭爛，對連人長什麼樣都不知道的伺服器代碼虔誠得像在拜北港媽祖，卻百般質疑眼前的活人醫師。徐國峰強調，自己也天天用AI，但脊椎這檔事從來就不是報告有名詞就代表抓到病因，感嘆AI很會說，但隔著螢幕有辦法檢測到患者肌肉萎縮嗎？敲得出膝反射嗎？連患者坐在診間翹二郎腿都看不到。

文末徐國峰表示，患者可以帶十頁資料來考試，也可以帶一百個問題來抬槓，但走進診間，請留一點空間縫隙，讓檢查跟專業說話，「身上的病痛，真的不會因為你辯贏了就自己痊癒，相信醫生，相信專業好嗎」，並貼出一張告示「已經在GPT獲得診斷的患者，請勿再向我們尋求意見，請改向Google查詢，但Threads真的不建議」。

title: Ancient love poems show romance timeless across millennia
zh_title: 古老的爱情诗展现了跨越千年的永恒浪漫
summary: 香港大学的一位学者强调，古代美索不达米亚和埃及的爱情诗揭示了从神圣的仪式到世俗的崇拜，浪漫的渴望在 4000 多年来一直没有改变。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 00:05 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 远在现代之前浪漫，在古代近东，人心剧烈跳动。穿越美索不达米亚肥沃的平原和埃及阳光普照的沙滩
content:
香港
香港大学的一位学者强调，古代美索不达米亚和埃及的爱情诗揭示了从神圣的仪式到世俗的崇拜，浪漫的渴望在 4000 多年来一直没有改变。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 15 日 00:05 香港时间 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

早在现代浪漫之前，古代近东的人们的心跳就剧烈。香港大学阿拉伯语项目主任阿姆贾德·雷法伊 (Amjad Refai) 表示，穿过美索不达米亚肥沃的平原和埃及阳光普照的沙滩，早期文明将他们最深切的渴望刻在粘土和纸莎草上，证明爱是一种永恒的、通用的语言。

在古代美索不达米亚，浪漫的渴望与神圣的传统交织在一起。几个世纪以来，圣经中的《所罗门之歌》被认为是历史上最古老的情诗，直到考古学家发现了写于公元前 2000 年左右的《舒辛情歌》。拉法伊于 2026 年 10 月 15 日在《标准》专栏中写道，虽然最初是由一位女祭司在神圣的生育仪式上背诵的，以确保土地的繁荣，但这块泥板却揭示了女性原始、热情和世俗的奉献。
这首诗是一位被国王迷住的新娘深深的个人忏悔：“新郎，让我爱抚你，我珍贵的爱抚比蜂蜜更美味，在充满蜂蜜的卧室里，让我享受你的美丽，狮子，让我爱抚你，我珍贵的爱抚比蜂蜜更美味。”

几个世纪后，大约公元前 1300 年，古埃及人捕捉到了一种不同但同样迷人的浪漫色彩。新王国的世俗诗歌读起来就像艺术家欣赏杰作，呼应了法老拉美西斯二世对其心爱的王后奈菲尔塔丽的传奇般的热爱。在这些现存的诗歌中，情人怀着幻想般的钦佩崇敬着心上人独特的美丽，将她比作最稀有的宝石和太阳：“最美丽的！”像晨星一样升起，在快乐的一年开始时，闪闪发亮，皮肤白皙，她的眼睛可爱，她的嘴唇甜美，她没有说太多的话。

雷法伊写道，这些文本并排放置，编织出一幅人类情感的挂毯。美索不达米亚歌曲充满了肉体渴望的颤抖温暖，而埃及诗歌则呈现出对灵魂伴侣深深浪漫的崇拜。数千年来，他们共同耳语着一个令人欣慰的真理：帝国衰落，但坠入爱河的惊心动魄的体验却从未改变。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
A University of Hong Kong academic highlights how ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian love poems reveal that romantic longing has remained unchanged for over 4,000 years, from sacred rituals to secular adoration.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 00:05 HKT · 2 min read

Long before modern romance, the human heart beat fiercely in the ancient Near East. Across the fertile plains of Mesopotamia and the sun-drenched sands of Egypt, early civilizations etched their deepest desires onto clay and papyrus, proving that love is a timeless, universal language, according to Amjad Refai, director of the Arabic Programme at the University of Hong Kong.

In ancient Mesopotamia, romantic longing was intertwined with sacred traditions. For centuries, the biblical Song of Solomon was considered history’s oldest love poem, until archaeologists discovered the Love Song for Shu-Sin, written around 2000 BCE. Although originally recited by a priestess during sacred fertility rituals to ensure the land’s prosperity, the clay tablet reveals a woman’s raw, passionate, and earthly devotion, Refai wrote in a column for _The Standard_ on 15 October 2026.

The poem is a deeply personal confession of a bride captivated by her king: 'Bridegroom, let me caress you, My precious caress is more savory than honey, In the bedchamber, honey-filled, Let me enjoy your goodly beauty, Lion, let me caress you, My precious caress is more savory than honey.'

Centuries later, around 1300 BCE, the ancient Egyptians captured a different, yet equally enchanting, shade of romance. Echoing the legendary devotion Pharaoh Ramses II held for his beloved Queen Nefertari, secular poetry from the New Kingdom reads like an artist admiring a masterpiece. In these surviving poems, the lover reveres his sweetheart's unique beauty with starry-eyed admiration, comparing her to the rarest precious gems and the sun: 'Most beautiful of all! Rising like the morning star, At the start of happy year, Shining bright, fair of skin, Lovely the look of her eyes, Sweet the speech of her lips, She has not a word too much.'

Placed side by side, these texts weave a tapestry of human emotion, Refai wrote. While the Mesopotamian song pulses with the trembling warmth of physical longing, the Egyptian poem presents a deeply romantic adoration of a soulmate. Together, they whisper a comforting truth across millennia: empires fall, but the breathtaking experience of falling in love remains unchanged.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

Editor in Chief

title: Impeachment as democracy’s necessary check
summary: THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and
content:
THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and fitness for public office can travel in opposite directions.

A survey measures preference. It cannot certify honesty, reconcile financial records or absolve constitutional violations. Yet Duterte’s defenders treat her continuing popularity as though millions of supporters could collectively erase questions that demand documentary answers. When loyalty becomes a substitute for accountability, democracy risks becoming an elaborate mechanism for rewarding impunity.

This is why impeachment matters. It provides a constitutional means of protecting the republic when electoral judgment fails. The Senate can prevent irrational political allegiance from returning a demonstrably unfit official to power, provided it establishes impeachable wrongdoing through a fair examination of evidence. Popularity must never become immunity.

*   [Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Political theory gives us reasons to question the comforting assumption that voters reliably make informed, rational choices. Anthony Downs’ concept of rational ignorance explains why people may invest little effort in learning about politics. Acquiring information takes time, while one individual’s vote has an exceedingly small chance of deciding an election.

What makes sense for an individual can produce disastrous collective consequences. A citizen may find it easier to repeat a slogan than understand a financial disclosure. Multiply that shortcut across millions and an election can reward the candidate with the strongest emotional appeal rather than the strongest record of honesty.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Bryan Caplan goes further in “The Myth of the Rational Voter.” His concept of rational irrationality explains how voters can indulge comforting political beliefs because the personal cost of doing so appears negligible. People gain emotional satisfaction from believing what they want, while the consequences of misguided choices are shared by society.

Caplan’s principal evidence concerns economic policy. Applying his framework to unconditional loyalty toward a political personality is therefore an interpretation, rather than a finding about Duterte’s supporters. Nevertheless, the mechanism is recognizable. Admitting that one’s political idol has failed can be emotionally expensive. Dismissing inconvenient evidence can feel reassuringly cheap.

The resulting harm extends beyond the loyalist. Citizens who never supported that politician must also live under the administration that electoral devotion helps produce. Irrational voting carries a public cost. The satisfaction of defending an idol is privately enjoyed; the damage from installing an unfit leader is collectively endured.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

Geoffrey Brennan and Loren Lomasky’s theory of expressive voting adds another explanation. Voting can function as an expression of identity, belonging, resentment or solidarity. A ballot may resemble cheering for a team. Supporting the candidate communicates who the voter is and which community the voter considers home.

This helps explain why damaging information can fail to weaken political allegiance. A supporter who experiences criticism of Duterte as an attack on personal identity may defend her more fiercely. The question shifts from whether she has answered the evidence to whether one’s political camp will be humiliated by conceding anything.

Christopher Achen and Larry Bartels, in “Democracy for Realists,” likewise challenge the picture of citizens calmly comparing policies before choosing leaders. They emphasize social identities and partisan attachments. Political loyalties can shape how people perceive facts, enabling the same conduct to appear unforgivable in an opponent and excusable in an ally.

These theories cannot establish that every Duterte supporter is irrational. Nor does one survey reveal what each respondent knows or believes. They do explain why counting preferences cannot settle questions of competence and integrity. Persistent refusal to confront substantiated wrongdoing deserves criticism, regardless of how numerous or enthusiastic its defenders become.

*   ![Image 2: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260179.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/news/our-soldiers-are-not-troublemakers/2445870)

The argument for impeachment becomes stronger when supporters openly declare that no revelation could change their minds. Such loyalty abandons democratic scrutiny. It turns public office into a personal entitlement and makes constitutional accountability indispensable to the republic.

Constitutional democracy anticipates that popular judgment may falter. It distributes authority among institutions and imposes obligations that public enthusiasm cannot cancel. Article XI declares public office a public trust and identifies grounds for impeachment, including culpable constitutional violations, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust.

Impeachment is political because it addresses the abuse of public power through constitutionally designated political institutions. Its political character binds it to the protection of the republic. Alexander Hamilton’s discussion in “Federalist No. 65” links impeachment to violations of public trust and injuries to society, while warning against decisions governed by factional strength.

That warning applies directly to senators who might confuse Duterte’s survey numbers with a reason to excuse proven misconduct. Their obligation is to examine the charges, hear the defense and decide whether the evidence establishes constitutional grounds for conviction. Electoral calculations cannot discharge that obligation.

*   ![Image 3: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

Questions about asset declarations, unexplained wealth or the misuse of public funds require answers on their merits. If the evidence establishes impeachable wrongdoing, senators must act despite the respondent’s popularity. If it fails, they must decline to convict. The integrity of this check depends on principled judgment.

The Constitution permits impeachment judgments extending to removal and disqualification from public office. That power has a protective purpose: An official found culpable need not remain available for another electoral rehabilitation. Voters retain the right to choose among qualified candidates. Public support cannot compel institutions to disregard constitutionally established disqualification.

Senators are also vulnerable to irrationality, ambition and partisan attachment. Their election does not confer monopoly on wisdom. Robinhood Padilla is exhibit No. 1. This makes their conduct under oath especially consequential. They must demonstrate that constitutional responsibility can prevail over personal loyalty, anticipated electoral rewards and fear of offending a powerful political following.

The Senate can save irrational voters from making a mockery of democracy by enforcing accountability against proven abuses of public trust. Refusing that duty because an accused official remains popular would surrender constitutional government to political fandom.

Democracy deserves citizens willing to reconsider their loyalties and institutions willing to uphold their obligations. When voters will not confront proven unfitness, impeachment becomes a necessary check. Senators must have the courage to use it.

The author is a professor at the University of the Philippines Los Baños and vice chairman of the board of the People’s Television Network Inc.

title: BARMM coalition gets majority with 46 MPs
summary: **DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that br
content:
**DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that bridges political divisions and serves all BARMM communities.

In a press briefing in this city, Macacua said the coalition would prioritize unity among the Bangsamoro people after the region’s first parliamentary elections, stressing that the incoming government must serve constituents regardless of their political affiliations or electoral choices.

“After the formal assumption of the Government of the Day, we will pursue a program for the unity of all Bangsamoro,” Macacua said.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Macacua described the coalition as broad and inclusive, reflecting the diversity of the region and the need for political leaders to work together beyond the divisions created during the election campaign.

Macacua emphasized that the responsibility of the new government would extend beyond those who voted for its members, encompassing every community, province and sector across the Bangsamoro region.

According to Macacua, the coalition would reach out to other groups, heal divisions and build a government capable of responding to the needs of the entire Bangsamoro population.

The commitment to inclusive governance comes as the newly elected Parliament prepares to organize the region’s first fully elected parliamentary government, marking a significant stage in BARMM’s transition from an interim administration.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

[![Image 2: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)

The 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament emerged from the Sept. 14 elections, in which no single political party secured the 41 seats needed to command a majority. The coalition arrangement is therefore central to efforts to establish a working parliamentary majority. The 46 lawmakers who signed the coalition documents exceed the 41-member threshold required for a majority in the 80-seat Parliament, providing the coalition with a numerical basis to organize the incoming government.

The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), chaired by Macacua, emerged as the largest party in the elections, securing 31 seats when party and district seats were combined, according to election reporting. The United Bangsamoro Justice Party and the BARMM Grand Coalition also secured substantial representation in the new legislature.

Macacua thanked the 46 elected lawmakers for their trust and commitment, as well as the national government for respecting BARMM’s institutions and political processes.

*   ![Image 3: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

He said the coalition was prepared to move forward once Parliament convenes, with its members united by the objective of serving the Bangsamoro people.

The coalition’s formation comes at a crucial point in the region’s political transition, as elected lawmakers prepare to assume their responsibilities and determine the leadership and direction of the incoming parliamentary government.

The 80 newly elected members are scheduled to assume office on Oct. 30, when Parliament is expected to organize the new government and elect a chief minister.

title: Haze worsens air quality in Singapore, East Timor
summary: **SINGAPORE** — Air pollution in one part of Singapore hit the city-state’s “very high” band on Wednesday while East Timor shut schools, as haze from forest fires in Indonesia is causing a regional crisis. The blazes have burned through hun
content:
**SINGAPORE** — Air pollution in one part of Singapore hit the city-state’s “very high” band on Wednesday while East Timor shut schools, as haze from forest fires in Indonesia is causing a regional crisis.

The blazes have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest and plantations on the Borneo and Sumatra islands, sickened residents in Indonesia and sent thick haze across Southeast Asia.

Air pollution in western Singapore on Wednesday hit “very high” — the country’s top level — the National Environment Agency said.

*   [Japan’s PM: Household duties make me busier](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/world/asia-oceania/japans-pm-household-duties-make-me-busier/2445488)

It recorded levels of tiny particulates capable of penetrating the bloodstream and lungs, known as PM2.5, at 288 micrograms per cubic meter, vastly exceeding the World Health Organization’s recommended average annual exposure of five micrograms.

Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, but has seen stronger-than-usual blazes this year as a powerful El Niño cycle brings drought.

Experts also point to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape of Sumatra and Borneo.

The haze has drifted into neighboring Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor, which said it would shut schools nationwide for three days from Thursday, and as far afield as the Philippines.

The closures in East Timor were necessary “as a preventive measure to protect the health of students, teachers and other members of the educational community, given current air quality conditions,” the government said.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

It urged families to keep children indoors and to use “respiratory protection” if going outside.

Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment from Monday, a measure last activated in 2015, when similar blazes in Indonesia cloaked Southeast Asia in toxic smoke for weeks.

The city-state has also begun distributing N95 masks to eligible residents when pollution reaches very unhealthy levels.

Singapore’s National Trades Union Congress said on Monday that public transport workers and delivery riders could receive free N95 masks, but Agence France-Presse (AFP) found that uptake was slow.

*   ![Image 2: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

“It’s a little bit uncomfortable to wear a mask, and some orders we have to walk around blocks, or park outside,” a delivery rider, who gave his name only as Daniel, told AFP.

“With the mask, I will have to breathe heavier,” the 27-year-old said.

AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)

Homes razed,

diplomatic calls

Ong Kwang Wei, 57, who has asthma, said he wore an N95 mask outdoors and carried his inhaler and medication with him at all times.

He was accompanying his 88-year-old mother — also masked — for a health checkup after a recent bout of the flu.

“Once the flu kicks in, my asthma is exacerbated ... I get breathless, I cough, I get phlegm, so I need to use my inhaler,” Ong said.

In Indonesia, tens of thousands of people have sought treatment for respiratory illness linked to haze from fires burning in Borneo, South Sumatra and Papua regions.

On Sumatra island, a fire razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said on Tuesday.

Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps.

But the fire continued to smolder underground in peatland, and when the wind shifted, the flames moved toward their homes.

The local disaster agency said nearly 1,000 people fled the village.

“My house is gone,” Leni, a 55-year-old villager now staying at a shelter with her family, told AFP.

“There’s nothing left. I could only save myself and take my kids with me ... I panicked and didn’t have the time to grab anything,” said Leni, who, like many Indonesians, has one name.

President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilize maximum efforts, with officials saying more than 60,000 personnel had been deployed to combat fires on the ground.

But efforts so far, including cloud seeding and water-bombing, have had limited success.

The haze has prompted Malaysia to request a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), and on Tuesday Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Rahman urged a “diplomatic protest.”

“We must send a diplomatic protest note, not just on behalf of Malaysia, but the Asean. You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” he said.

title: The 'Small Power Forward'
summary: As we continue to fantasize about building twin towers for our national team, successful teams in the NBA are redefining positions to fit the modern game. The Golden State Warriors redefined the game in 2015 and made it a shooting league, a
content:
As we continue to fantasize about building twin towers for our national team, successful teams in the NBA are redefining positions to fit the modern game. The Golden State Warriors redefined the game in 2015 and made it a shooting league, and the paradigm of the typical starting five has changed drastically.

**Height Not Might?**

The adage of “height is might” has been floated since basketball began. After all, it is clearly a vertical sport with a 10-foot rim. Being tall allowed one to reach the goal quicker and easier. Thus, the early dominant players in the sport were centers, and the best example is George Mikan of the Minneapolis Lakers.

*   [Rising Spanish tennis star handed code violation for swearing at ballboy](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/sports/rising-spanish-tennis-star-handed-code-violation-for-swearing-at-ballboy/2445568)

After Mikan, new generations of big men emerged like the rivalry of Bill Russell and Wilt Chamberlain. The 1980s saw Patrick Ewing, Hakeem Olajuwon, and David Robinson. Up until the 1990s, being tall pretty much guaranteed a ticket to the NBA.

Nowadays, being tall is no longer much of an advantage, and it’s not just in the NBA. As seen in the recent Asian games, the tallest team (China) got walloped by Akatsuki Japan, a team well-entrenched in the modern style of play.

**Skillset Over Positional Size**

It’s ironic to brush off height these days now that Victor Wembanyama has become a dominant force. Having a unicorn type center still matters, and more Wemby-types are on the way. Teams still need a center, but the traditional frontcourt mate has evolved.

In the recent NBA Finals, the starting power forwards were OG Anunoby and Julian Champagnie. Both were 6’7, and were more attuned as small forwards rather than the traditional power forward. LeBron James, Pascal Siakam, Jayson Tatum, Kevin Durant were former All-Stars as small forwards.

*   ![Image 1: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

That doesn’t mean there is no more space for tall power forwards. Chet Holmgren is the power forward in the OKC Thunder’s twin tower starting combo. But Holmgren is the modern big–mobile, with three-point shooting range and able to play facing the basket.

The game has changed and there are less post-up plays and more three-point shots. That results in long rebounds and more fastbreak attempts. Even tall players need to be quick and run back on defense.

It can be recalled that Anthony Davis famously complained about being played as a center, and demanded a trade. He can’t avoid that now, as it would be considered a waste of a position to place him with a big bruiser. Fortunately, young starter Alex Sarr has European-developed skills.

Athleticism, lateral quickness, and strength override height. For the international game, that’s what Gilas should look for, more than seeking someone who’s simply 6’10. Younger players with those skills like Scottie Barnes and Jalen Johnson started as small forwards, but are now converted. For Gilas, players like Carl Tamayo and Zavier Lucero could play that role.

Here is a list of the realistic prospects which PBA teams could choose from. This is by no means final since the deadline to declare is still far off. title: N. Korea could bolster drone capabilities through workers at Russian factory: report
zh_title: 报告：朝鲜可以通过俄罗斯工厂的工人增强无人机能力
summary: 华盛顿，10 月 14 日（韩联社）——美国智库周三的一份报告显示，朝鲜可以通过部署到俄罗斯主要无人机生产设施的工人获得技术专长来增强其军用无人机能力，这可能对韩国和该地区的美军构成新的安全威胁。该报告由战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）和乔治·W·布什研究所联合发布，研究了朝鲜参与俄罗斯无人机制造行业的安全影响，以及朝鲜在其中扮演的角色。
content:
作者：张东宇

华盛顿，10 月 14 日（韩联社）——美国智库周三的一份报告显示，朝鲜可以通过部署到俄罗斯主要无人机生产设施的工人获得技术专长来加强其军用无人机能力，这可能对韩国和该地区的美军构成新的安全威胁。

这份由战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）和乔治·W·布什研究所联合发布的报告探讨了朝鲜参与俄罗斯无人机制造业的安全影响，以及中国和伊朗在支持莫斯科对乌克兰战争中的作用。

根据多边制裁监测小组 (MSMT) 9 月发布的另一份报告，截至 2025 年底，俄罗斯接待了估计 15,000 至 30,000 名朝鲜工人，其中一些人参与制造军用无人机。报道还称，莫斯科制定了一项学生签证计划，将朝鲜工人伪装成学生。

报告称：“朝鲜劳动力还转让技术知识。被派往阿拉布加的技术人员将在观察俄罗斯对不断改进的杰兰无人机的改进后返回平壤，获得在大规模生产无人机装配线工作的宝贵经验。”报告指的是俄罗斯的阿拉布加无人机生产基地。

Geran 是俄罗斯生产、伊朗设计的攻击无人机，莫斯科在对乌克兰的战争中广泛使用。
报告补充说：“朝鲜拥有更加复杂和不断发展的无人机计划，这对印太地区的韩国、日本和美国军队构成了新的军事挑战。”

该报告由战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）韩国主席车维克多（Victor Cha）和布什研究所项目经理约瑟夫·金（Joseph Kim）撰写，援引乌克兰军事情报部门的估计，多达 12,000 名朝鲜工人被派往阿拉布加工厂。

报告还强调了平壤从海外劳工业务中获得的经济利益，并指出该政权扣留了工人工资的 70% 至 90%。

报告称：“朝鲜工人赚取的工资最终会流回平壤以及强迫劳工的政权。”

据MSMT称，在俄罗斯的每名朝鲜工人估计平均年薪为7,500美元，每月收入可能高达在中国朝鲜工人的五倍，具体取决于行业。

该图描绘了联合国对朝鲜及其海外劳工计划的制裁。 （韩联社）

odissy@yna.co.kr
（完）

【原文 English Original】
By Chang Dong-woo

WASHINGTON, Oct. 14 (Yonhap) -- North Korea could strengthen its military drone capabilities by gaining technical expertise through workers deployed to a major Russian drone production facility, potentially posing a new security threat to South Korea and U.S. forces in the region, a U.S. think tank report showed Wednesday.

The report, jointly published by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and the George W. Bush Institute, examined the security implications of North Korea's involvement in Russia's drone manufacturing industry, as well as the roles of China and Iran in supporting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

According to a separate report issued by the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) in September, Russia hosted an estimated 15,000 to 30,000 North Korean workers as of the end of 2025, some of whom were involved in manufacturing military drones. The report also said Moscow had established a student visa scheme to disguise North Korean workers as students.

"North Korean labor also transfers technical know-how. Technicians sent to Alabuga will return to Pyongyang with invaluable lessons from working at a mass-production drone assembly line, having observed Russian refinements to the constantly improving Geran drones," the report said, referring to Russia's Alabuga drone production complex.

The Geran is a Russian-produced, Iranian-designed attack drone widely used by Moscow in its war against Ukraine.

"A North Korea with a more sophisticated and growing drone program poses a new order of military challenge for South Korea, Japan, and U.S. forces in the Indo-Pacific," it added.

The report, authored by Victor Cha, Korea Chair at CSIS, and Joseph Kim, program manager at the Bush Institute, cited Ukrainian military intelligence estimates that up to 12,000 North Korean workers had been assigned to the Alabuga complex.

It also highlighted the financial benefits Pyongyang derives from its overseas labor operations, noting that the regime withholds 70 to 90 percent of workers' wages.

"Wages earned by North Korean workers ultimately flow back to Pyongyang and the same regime that compels the labor," it said.

According to the MSMT, each North Korean worker in Russia generates an estimated average of US$7,500 in annual wages, with monthly earnings potentially reaching up to five times those of North Korean workers in China, depending on the industry.

This graphic illustration depicts U.N. sanctions against North Korea and its overseas labor program. (Yonhap)

odissy@yna.co.kr
(END)

title: IRRI-BASF project probes rice methane emissions
summary: **LOS BAÑOS, Philippines** — Cutting methane emissions from rice fields is possible. But what does it do to the soil that farmers depend on for the next planting? That is the question now being asked by the International Rice Research Insti
content:
**LOS BAÑOS, Philippines** — Cutting methane emissions from rice fields is possible. But what does it do to the soil that farmers depend on for the next planting?

That is the question now being asked by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), based here, as it starts the second phase of its joint research with German agricultural company BASF.

IRRI and BASF formally launched on Oct. 1, 2026 Phase 2 of Optima, short for Optimizing Management for Reduction of GHG in Rice, according to IRRI.

*   [BSP: ‘Prepare for the worst’Amid El Niño threat on prices, supplies](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/business/top-business/bsp-prepare-for-the-worstamid-el-nio-threat-on-prices-supplies/2445893)

Optima Phase 1, IRRI said, showed that three practices combined — direct-seeded rice instead of transplanted, better fertilizer management, and alternate wetting and drying (AWD) — can reduce water use and methane emissions without lowering yield. Under AWD, a rice field is left dry for a few days in between flooding, instead of keeping it flooded all season.

IRRI also tested its computer model for rice growth, called Otyza — named after Oryza sativa, the scientific name for rice — and found it can track how water moves in the field and predict how much methane will be released. IRRI said this makes the model useful for counting greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions and for future carbon farming programs.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

**Looking deeper into the issue**

Phase 2, IRRI said, looks deeper into the issue.

IRRI explained that soil organic carbon — the organic matter that makes soil fertile — changes depending on how often farmers plant, how they manage rice straw, and whether they add organic materials.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

When a flooded field is dried, soil microbes get oxygen and become more active. They break down organic matter faster and release carbon dioxide. Over many seasons, IRRI noted, this could mean soil carbon built up over years might slowly be lost.

[![Image 2: IRRI and BASF have launched the second phase of a project to advance low-emission rice technologies including direct-seeded rice, improved nutrient management, and alternate wetting and drying. IRRI PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259000.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259000.jpg)
IRRI and BASF have launched the second phase of a project to advance low-emission rice technologies including direct-seeded rice, improved nutrient management, and alternate wetting and drying. IRRI PHOTO

That trade-off matters, IRRI said, because methane reduction can be seen quickly, but soil carbon loss is slow and hard to notice — yet it affects fertility and long-term harvests.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

"Optima 1 has established that the Oryza model is a useful tool to quantify climate benefits of AWD. Our next step is to understand what its effect is in the long term on the system's long-term sustainability, particularly for soil health and soil carbon dynamics,” said Ligia Bacchereti Azevedo, Senior Sustainability Manager for Agricultural Solutions of BASF, during the kickoff meeting for the joint initiative.

“Optima 2 will help us examine whether low emissions practices can support long-term sustainability, while considering potential trade-offs," the BASF official said.

IRRI said the new two-year study will compare different ways of doing AWD and see how straw management and biochar — charcoal-like material added to soil — interact with it to affect yield and carbon storage.

The institute said it will also improve the Oryza model so it can simulate these effects over the short, medium, and long term. To do this, IRRI will use data from its Long-Term Continuous Cropping Experiment in Los Baños, one of Asia's longest-running rice experiments that has tracked soil changes for decades.

*   ![Image 4: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

"The continuation of this partnership is a testimony of the alignment of BASF and IRRI vision in ensuring transformation of rice systems towards low-emissions systems are supported by science-based evidence and farmers will be equipped with the best combinations of technologies optimized for productivity, profitability and sustainability," said Virender Kumar, Research Director of IRRI's Sustainable Impact through Rice-based Systems Department.

IRRI said Optima 2 starts this wet season of 2026. The goal, according to IRRI, is to give clearer, field-based evidence on how to lower GHG emissions, especially methane, without harming the soil that sustains rice farming — so that low-emission practices can be promoted at scale with confidence for both climate and farmers.

title: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’
summary: DEFENSE Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. blasted Vice President Sara Duterte for saying the Philippines is “becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia,” and made clear that the source of all troubles in the region is China. “Can you say that
content:
DEFENSE Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. blasted Vice President Sara Duterte for saying the Philippines is “becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia,” and made clear that the source of all troubles in the region is China.

“Can you say that our soldiers who sacrifice there [in the West Philippine Sea] are troublemakers, when we are only fighting for our rights over the sea that is the future of our country’s sustainability?” Teodoro said in Filipino.

Duterte had made the comment after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called alleged remittances from a Chinese state-owned firm into a company linked to the vice president’s husband a potential national security issue.

*   [44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

“Is doing business with China really prohibited because it’s a national security risk?” Duterte had said in Filipino. ”We are becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia.” Teodoro made it clear that engaging with the Chinese in business is not prohibited. What’s in question rather is how a public official is allowed to enter into such transactions.

“Filipinos are not prohibited from doing business with China, but the question is, is a public official, first and foremost, allowed to have any business transactions on a certain level? Some are not, some are. That is a question which has to be determined by the proper investigative authorities,” Teodoro said.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Teodoro cited as an example China-owned or linked businesses in the Philippines that were proven to be illegal or flawed such as the alleged substandard steel, illegal mining and the offshore gaming operations which he said “did not benefit the overall integrity of the Philippines.” “If you are a public official, you have a voice in the stability of our national territory and integrity; if you have transactions with China, these should be studied to determine if they are, above all, legitimate and proper,” the Defense chief said.

Teodoro emphasized that it is China who is the troublemaker and not the Philippines, citing as proof the intention of the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (Asean) member countries to finalize a long-awaited South China Sea Code of Conduct with China.

“China is clearly the troublemaker here, crystal clear, and I will not accept any other narrative on that. It’s obvious; nobody can say that the Philippines is the one causing trouble,” Teodoro said.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

**Chinese talking point**

Vice President Duterte’s use of the word “troublemaker” mirrors Chinese talking points against the Philippines.

China has repeatedly used the label “troublemaker” against the Philippines over the years to describe Manila’s actions in the West Philippine Sea.

In July 2026, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian labeled the Philippines a “troublemaker” in the South China Sea after Manila embedded journalists on resupply missions and patrols, accusing the Philippines of provoking maritime confrontations to “stir up tensions.” In July 2015, following the Philippines’ legal challenge against China’s expansive maritime claims at the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued an official statement explicitly referring to the Philippines as the “real troublemaker in the region.”* China accused Manila of deliberately escalating tensions and violating bilateral agreements.

*   ![Image 2: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

During early disputes following the Scarborough Shoal standoff in July 2013, Maj. Gen. Luo Yuan of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army publicly stated: “The role of the Philippines in the South China Sea is actually, in my view, a troublemaker.” Beijing routinely uses this narrative whenever the Philippines asserts its sovereign rights or brings international visibility to maritime disputes, portraying Manila’s defense measures and joint security partnerships as disruptive to regional peace.

title: Oligarcho-political urbanism: How wealth and power hijack our cities
summary: OLIGARCHO-POLITICAL urbanism as a self-reinforcing cycle in which economic and political actors shape urban development priorities, increasing land values and private profits while producing significant social and spatial consequences. I us
content:
OLIGARCHO-POLITICAL urbanism as a self-reinforcing cycle in which economic and political actors shape urban development priorities, increasing land values and private profits while producing significant social and spatial consequences.

I used to think that urban planners were the dominant shapers of cities. I would read about land use planning, transportation and other infrastructure planning. I also would study the strategic environmental assessment and public consultation processes. All of this gave me the impression that there were processes and structures for planning in a democratic state.

However, the more I practiced architecture and urban design, the more I became uncertain about the process of urban planning. Important urban planning decisions are made a long time before any consultation processes. By the time the public is allowed to give their opinions, important planning decisions have already been made. The public is rarely consulted in a process that gives them real decision-making power.

*   [39 impeachment days: Takeaways](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/opinion/columns/39-impeachment-days-takeaways/2445742)

This realization led me to an uncomfortable question: “Who are the real urban planners?”

[![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259972.png)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259972.png)

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Textbooks lead us to believe urban planning is a collaborative effort to integrate planning and design with the goals and objectives of the state and citizens. The projects that really influence the region and shape the metropolis are usually the result of big business, political clout and planning integration.

Jane Jacobs’ thesis is that the rapid growth and expansion of cities is organic. Cities should be designed with and for the people who inhabit them, so they may have the means to lead a productive life. Healthy cities should not be designed from above, but grow from the bottom up.

*   ![Image 2: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

When looking at the Philippines’ cities, it’s difficult to see the impact the average person has on their urban environment.

Let’s think about how cities grow. The government creates a big plan to improve city infrastructure. The price of land goes up. Developers buy land. Businesses open. More improvements to city infrastructure are needed. Sometimes, the growth of a city seems natural, but it can be a series of investments by a few people that leads to a change in infrastructure.

Of course, a city needs businesses and a thriving economy. The problem is when a small group of people is able to control and change the goals of the public.

This is what I call “oligarch urbanism.” It doesn’t include illegal activities. It occurs when a small group of people, usually in the economy, is able to control the ways in which a city changes and grows. In our case, some of the largest businesses of the country are part of the real estate, toll ways, logistics, construction and commercial businesses of the nation.

*   ![Image 3: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

Oligarch urbanism doesn’t focus on the illegal activities that business people and political families do. Instead, it is about how the goals of improving cities are determined and changed by these people.

This has certainly advantaged some cities in the country to become more productive, but at the expense of others, especially the middle income and the poor, to become more competitive, particularly in infrastructure that favors the market and the economy. Roads are constructed at the expense of parks. Spaces are planned and developed to commercially facilitate the free flow of capital and goods to the detriment of the free flow of people, especially the poor and the vulnerable. The building of houses is giving way to the construction of malls and other commercial and financial centers to the point that providing facilities for the basic needs of the poor is quite a challenge, and it is difficult for the poor to access public services and use public spaces.

It is sad to say that leisure, sports and social activities have been relegated to shopping malls and commercial centers. Privately owned commercial space has largely replaced, and even absorbed, the functions and services once provided by, and located in, civic and public spaces. Fun and games have been privatized and commercialized. Mall owners even charge an entrance fee just to use their commercial space!

The city, and especially commercial and financial centers, should provide places where children play, people relax, gather, and enjoy the city and its public spaces.

*   ![Image 4: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

As an urban planner and architect, I evaluate the success of urban areas differently than most. I focus on the quality of life of the people living in an urban area instead of the monetary worth of the land or the cost of the infrastructure.

Jane Jacobs noted that urban areas provide a wide range of opportunities and benefits for the population because of the diversity and choices offered by a large urban center. However, the existence of abundant choices in a large urban area depends on the participation of the entire population.

Are the largest and most prominent urban areas in the Philippines still designed for the participation of the majority, or are they designed by the upper class and the elite?

If decisions that affect the design of a city are made by an exclusive few, the city will eventually be planned and designed for the few and unjustly privileged. In the process, it will lose its ability to offer various possibilities and choices for the majority and will ultimately fail to serve the urban population.

Louwie Gan is the first Filipino architect and urban planner to be accredited by international green building institutions. He is an award-winning designer and internationally accredited sustainability expert who advocates for care-centric urbanism and regenerative development. He has worked as a sustainability and urban planning consultant for the government and international organizations.

title: Inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged
summary: **_Dear PAO,_** **_I filed a data privacy case before the National Privacy Commission (NPC), and the said office ruled in my favor. However, the appellate court overturned the NPC’s decision, stating that the text messages I attached to my
content:
**_Dear PAO,_**

**_I filed a data privacy case before the National Privacy Commission (NPC), and the said office ruled in my favor. However, the appellate court overturned the NPC’s decision, stating that the text messages I attached to my complaint were unauthenticated and thus inadmissible. This is surprising because the respondent did not even contest the admissibility of the text messages. Can I still elevate the case to the higher court?_**

**_Syl_**

*   [The ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/legal-advice/the-captain-of-the-ship-doctrine/2444935)

Dear Syl,

Yes, you may still elevate the case in the higher court, subject to the prescription period provided for by the Rules of Court.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

As ruled in the case of Trimillos v. Fcash Global Lending Inc., GR 271360, Aug. 13, 2025, penned by Associate Justice Henri Jean Paul Inting, inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged at the proper time, and such issue may not be raised for the first time on appeal, saying:

“However, in the same case, the Court also recognized that inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged at the proper time and such issue may not be raised for the first time on appeal, viz.:

“In any case, it bears pointing out that petitioner failed to raise his objection to the admissibility of the photos during the proceedings in the RTC. Basic is the rule that in order to exclude evidence, the objection to admissibility of evidence must be made at the proper time, and the grounds therefore be specified. Objection to evidence must be made at the time it is formally offered. In case of documentary evidence, offer is made after all the witnesses of the party making the offer have testified, specifying the purpose for which the evidence is being offered. It is only at this time, and not at any other, that objection to the documentary evidence may be made. When a party failed to interpose a timely objection to evidence at the time they were offered in evidence, such objection shall be considered as waived. This is true even if by its nature the evidence is inadmissible and would have surely been rejected if it had been challenged at the proper time.

*   ![Image 1: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

“As a complimentary principle, it is well-settled that no question will be entertained on appeal unless it has been raised in the proceedings below. Points of law, theories, issues and arguments not brought to the attention of the lower court, administrative agency or quasi-judicial body, need not be considered by a reviewing court, as they cannot be raised for the first time at that late stage. Basic considerations of fairness and due process impel this rule. Any issue raised for the first time on appeal is barred by estoppel.”

In your case, the respondents did not even contest, in any stage of the proceeding, the admissibility of your evidence. Thus, you can argue before the higher court that by failing to timely raise any objection to the admissibility of the text messages you have attached, the respondent is deemed to have already waived the same. Hence, the text messages are admissible in evidence by virtue of estoppel.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice was solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

*   ![Image 2: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

title: Two lives, one Constitution: Rethinking the abortion debate
summary: EVERY Oct. 15, the Philippines observes National Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day, established under Proclamation 700, Series of 2024. It is an occasion to remember children lost through miscarriage, stillbirth and infant death, an
content:
EVERY Oct. 15, the Philippines observes National Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day, established under Proclamation 700, Series of 2024. It is an occasion to remember children lost through miscarriage, stillbirth and infant death, and to recognize the grief of families whose children never had the opportunity to grow up.

This observance comes amid renewed advocacy for the decriminalization of abortion, including proposals to amend Articles 256 to 259 of the Revised Penal Code. Although congressional discussions on revising penal laws have recently taken place, the reported hearing on abortion decriminalization and the status of a specific bill in the present Congress still require confirmation.

The debate nevertheless raises a fundamental question: Can the State protect women by withdrawing legal protection from unborn children?

*   [39 impeachment days: Takeaways](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/opinion/columns/39-impeachment-days-takeaways/2445742)

**The Constitution protects two lives**

Article II, Section 12 of the Constitution commands the State to “equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception.”

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The language is unmistakable in recognizing both lives. In Imbong v. Ochoa (2014), the Supreme Court also interpreted conception as fertilization in resolving challenges to the Reproductive Health Law. While this does not conclusively decide every proposed amendment to abortion laws, it establishes a serious constitutional question that Congress cannot ignore.

Supporters of decriminalization raise legitimate concerns: unsafe abortions, maternal deaths, rape, poverty and bodily autonomy. These deserve serious answers, not condemnation.

But do these problems necessarily justify the proposed solution?

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

**Answering the arguments**

First, proponents argue that criminalization drives women toward unsafe abortions. Medical evidence confirms that unsafe procedures can cause grave harm. However, proving that a problem exists does not establish that every proposed remedy is constitutionally permissible or practically sufficient.

Republic Act 10354 already requires humane, nonjudgmental treatment of women suffering post-abortion complications. Government must ensure that emergency treatment is never withheld because of stigma or fear. Clear medical protocols, accessible obstetric care and accountability for negligent facilities are urgently needed.

Second, poverty and unintended pregnancy are cited as reasons for abortion. But poverty is fundamentally a failure of economic opportunity and social protection. If a mother fears she cannot afford to raise her child, should society respond by making it easier to end the pregnancy, or by making it possible for mother and child to survive and flourish?

*   ![Image 2: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

We need accessible prenatal health care, maternity assistance, employment protection, childcare and financial support for struggling families.

Third, proponents invoke rape and incest. These are profoundly difficult cases requiring compassion, trauma-informed care, protection from perpetrators and appropriate medical treatment. No victim should be blamed for the violence committed against her. Neither should serious medical emergencies be reduced to slogans. The State must provide lawful, timely, life-saving treatment and clarify medical standards where uncertainty endangers patients.

Finally, the argument of bodily autonomy deserves examination. A woman unquestionably possesses dignity, bodily integrity and rights to health care. Yet pregnancy also involves a developing human organism with its own biological identity, dependent upon the mother. Science establishes that human embryonic development ordinarily begins at fertilization, although science alone cannot settle legal personhood or moral status.

The constitutional challenge is precisely how to protect both.

*   ![Image 3: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

**Life is more than comfort**

Scripture provides a deeper foundation for the dignity of life.

Genesis 1:26–27 teaches that humanity is created in God’s image, the Imago Dei. Human worth does not depend upon wealth, health, independence or usefulness.

God told Jeremiah, “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you” (Jeremiah 1:5). David declared that God knitted him together in his mother’s womb (Psalm 139:13–16). Jeremiah’s passage specifically concerns his prophetic calling, yet both passages reveal God’s knowledge and purpose extending beyond birth.

The ancient Israelites were forbidden to sacrifice children to Molech (Leviticus 18:21). Such practices were associated with attempts to secure divine favor or prosperity. Modern crisis pregnancies are not identical to ancient child sacrifice, and we must never presume that every woman seeking abortion acts from selfishness. Nevertheless, the moral question remains: Should one human life be surrendered to secure another person’s comfort or prospects?

Christianity presents a radically different picture of sacrifice.

God gave His Son so humanity might receive eternal life (John 3:16). Jesus voluntarily laid down His life (John 10:17-18), offering the abundant life described in John 10:10. The Greek word zoē speaks of life, which John’s Gospel presents in its fullest meaning through Christ.

The Christian ideal is not children sacrificing their lives for parental comfort, but parents sacrificially loving and caring for their children.

**The blood of the innocent**

When Cain murdered Abel, God declared that Abel’s blood cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:10). Proverbs 6:16-17 identifies hands that shed innocent blood among the things the Lord hates.

For Christians who understand unborn human life as deserving protection, these passages carry a solemn warning against intentionally destroying innocent life.

The familiar slogan “My body, my choice” expresses a concern for personal autonomy. Christian teaching adds another consideration: The child in the womb is also a life entrusted to God’s purposes.

But conviction must never become cruelty toward frightened mothers.

Psalm 82:3–4 commands God’s people to defend the weak and needy. Jesus welcomed children when others sought to turn them away (Mark 10:13–16).

That responsibility extends to vulnerable unborn children and to mothers confronting abandonment, violence, poverty or fear.

**Protecting life requires more than prohibition**

A genuinely compassionate response must offer practical help.

Government, churches, families and civil society should establish pregnancy-support services, temporary shelters, prenatal assistance, counseling, support for single mothers,and accessible adoption and foster-care pathways under Republic Act 11642.

Women facing dangerous pregnancies need competent medical care. Survivors of sexual violence need protection and justice. Those who have experienced abortion deserve compassionate care, not humiliation.

The debate must therefore go beyond criminal penalties to ask whether our institutions are doing enough to protect the lives already entrusted to their care.

As we observe Oct. 15, let us remember that the value of life is not measured by its convenience, productivity or material circumstances.

A society that truly values life must protect the unborn without abandoning the mother.

The Constitution calls us to protect both. Scripture calls us to defend the vulnerable. And the Gospel reminds us that genuine love is measured not by whose life we are willing to sacrifice for our comfort, but by what we are willing to sacrifice so that others may live.
