content:
该地区专家告诉自由亚洲电台，北京的腐败和影响力行动不仅限于斐济，其他太平洋岛国也可能存在类似的行动。

该分析是在华盛顿指控斐济国民赵富刚担任苏瓦华侨服务中心负责人腐败后不久发表的。

美国国务院发言人托马斯·皮戈特在一份声明中表示，“赵滥用其公共地位，向斐济公民行贿，以促进中国政府、企业和犯罪利益。” “他的行为构成了严重腐败，并对美国在斐济的利益产生了不利影响。”

总部位于华盛顿的联盟期货倡议智库执行主任格雷戈里·布朗对自由亚洲电台表示，尽管赵现在被禁止进入美国，但可能有更多的人参与了他被指控的腐败行为——不仅在斐济，而且在整个太平洋地区。

布朗表示：“我严重怀疑北京在斐济建立了腐败和影响力行动，然后决定不在斐济其他任何地方复制这种做法，因为该地区在基础设施上花费了数十亿美元，签署了安全协议，并且每天都在争夺政治影响力。” “这违背了逻辑，也违背了我们对中共海外影响力活动的了解。没有理由类似的行动在霍尼亚拉、莫尔兹比港、努库阿洛法或维拉港行不通。”
斐济地图 显示斐济在太平洋地区位置的地图。 （法新社）

华盛顿战略与国际研究中心澳大利亚主席副主任凯瑟琳·派克 (Kathryn Paik) 告诉自由亚洲电台，促进中国利益的非法活动也发生在太平洋其他地区。

白南准表示：“有许多记录在案的中国行为者在其他太平洋国家和地区从事贩毒、非法捕鱼、洗钱等非法活动的案例。” “关键是，虽然这些行为者中的大多数（如果不是全部）可能不是中国官方特工，但他们正在进行的活动要么受到北京的鼓励，要么得到北京的协助。”

**非法干扰者**

新西兰坎特伯雷大学的何塞·苏萨-桑托斯 (José Sousa-Santos) 在“未来”项目[小战争杂志](https://smallwarsjournal.com/2026/08/28/china-criminal-networks-and-gray-zone-competition/)上发表的一篇文章中写道，赵是中国利用“国家纵容的非法破坏者作为太平洋灰色地带活动形式”的一个例子亚利桑那州立大学的安全倡议。

这篇文章写于美国制裁赵（澳大利亚执法部门已认定其与有组织犯罪有联系）几个月前，详细介绍了北京如何容忍和保护犯罪分子和网络以服务于国家目标。
苏萨-桑托斯写道：“这并不要求中国政府与有组织犯罪之间存在简单的指挥关系。也不意味着海外的每个中国犯罪行为者都是北京的代理人。” “更重要的一点是，某些非法行为者在扩大影响力、培养当地精英、产生可否认的经济影响力、支持爱国言论以及在正式国家权力会招致阻力的空间运作时，可以在战略上变得有用。”

文章称，像赵这样的演员很有价值，因为北京可以否认与他们的非法活动有任何联系，同时又能从中受益。

“赵的价值在于他代表

【原文 English Original】
Beijing’s corruption and influence operations are not limited to Fiji, and similar operations likely exist in other Pacific island countries, experts on the region told Radio Free Asia.

The analysis came shortly after Washington accused Fijian national Zhao Fugang of corruption as head of the Overseas Chinese Service Center in Suva.

“Zhao abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests,” U.S. State Department spokesman Thomas Pigott said in a statement. “His actions constituted significant corruption and adversely affected U.S. interests in Fiji.”

Though Zhao is now barred from entering the United States, there are probably more people involved in the type of corruption he is accused of – not just in Fiji, but across the entire Pacific region, Gregory Brown, executive director of the Washington-based Alliance Futures Initiative think tank, told RFA.

“I seriously doubt that Beijing set up a corruption and influence operation in Fiji and then decided not to replicate it anywhere else in a region where it’s spending billions on infrastructure, signing security agreements, and competing every day for political influence,” said Brown. “That defies logic and everything we know about the CCP’s overseas influence campaigns. There is no reason similar operations wouldn’t work in Honiara, Port Moresby, Nuku’alofa, or Port Vila.”

fiji map A map showing the location of Fiji within the Pacific region. (AFP)

Illicit activities that advance Chinese interests occur elsewhere in the Pacific, Kathryn Paik, deputy director of the Australia Chair at the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies, told RFA.

“There have been many documented cases of Chinese actors in other Pacific countries and territories conducting illegal activities such as drug trafficking, illegal fishing, money laundering, and more,” said Paik. “What is key is that while most if not all of these actors may not be an official Chinese agent, they are conducting activity that is either encouraged by or facilitated by Beijing.”

**Illicit disruptors**

Zhao is an example of China’s use of “state-condoned illicit disruptors as a form of gray zone activity in the Pacific,” José Sousa-Santos, of the University of Canterbury in New Zealand, wrote in an essay published in [Small Wars Journal](https://smallwarsjournal.com/2026/08/28/china-criminal-networks-and-gray-zone-competition/), a project by the Future Security Initiative at Arizona State University.

Written months before the U.S. sanctioned Zhao – who Australian law enforcement had already identified as having connections to organized crime – the essay detailed how Beijing tolerates and protects criminal figures and networks to serve objectives of the state.

“This does not require a simple command relationship between the Chinese state and organized crime. Nor does it mean that every Chinese criminal actor abroad is an agent of Beijing,” wrote Sousa-Santos. “The more important point is that certain illicit actors can become strategically useful when they extend influence, cultivate local elites, generate deniable economic leverage, support patriotic narratives, and operate in spaces where formal state power would attract resistance.”

Actors like Zhao are valuable in that Beijing can deny all connections of involvement in their illegal activities, all while benefiting from them, the essay said.

“Zhao’s value is that he represents the kind of high-risk intermediary who can move money, cultivate elites, open doors, normalize Chinese influence, and generate dependency while remaining formally outside the state,” it said.

After the U.S. sanctioned Zhao, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference she had no knowledge of his case.

“We oppose vilification and smears against China,” she said.

**Cooperation needed**

In a Facebook post, the Fijian government asked Washington to provide evidence of the allegations against Zhao, and affirmed Suva’s commitment to work with international partners to crack down on transnational crime.

The U.S. and its allies should coordinate with each other to stop illicit activities, Paik said.

“Working collaboratively to identify illegal activity and name specific actors is certainly a start,” she said. “But of course Pacific countries are sovereign nations and the next step will ideally be to take action against these individuals in whichever country they are acting.”

Brown said that the U.S. should not stop with its sanctions on Zhao, but should name other individuals in the region to demonstrate how widespread the problem is.

“If we see three or four more across different Pacific countries in the next six months, the signal becomes a pattern,” he said.

Brown also called for the U.S. and its allies to support Pacific governments in building their own anti-corruption and counter-intelligence capacity, urged Pacific governments to make foreign-linked community organizations more accountable by requiring them to register, and work together to protect Chinese diaspora communities in the region.

“My big question now is whether this designation is a one-off or a campaign,” he said. “If it’s a one-off, Beijing will absorb the hit and move on. If it’s a campaign, it’s a chance to change calculus for every Chinese operative and every compromised Pacific official in the region.”

Key Points

*   Chinese Commerce Ministry Spokesperson He Yadong said that China is willing to continue approving rare earth licenses to Europe.
*   He was responding to a CNBC question about the impact of a January deadline for the U.S.-China trade truce.
*   European trade commissioner Maroš Sefčovič met with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing last week.

European Union flags flutter outside the EU Commission headquarters in Brussels, Belgium, on Feb. 1, 2023

Yves Herman | Reuters

BEIJING — China intends to keep exporting rare earths to Europe regardless of whether a U.S. trade deal with Beijing gets extended past January.

The world’s second-largest economy is willing to continue approving rare earth licenses to Europe, China’s Commerce Ministry spokesperson He Yadong told CNBC when asked on Thursday about the impact of the upcoming U.S. deadline.

Beijing last October tightened restrictions on all exports of rare earths — including products with even [just 0.1% of China-sourced rare earths](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/09/china-expands-rare-earth-export-restrictions-ahead-of-possible-trump-xi-meeting.html). The move followed a new U.S. rule that [expanded an American blacklist](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/department-commerce-expands-entity-list-cover-affiliates-listed-entities) to the majority-owned subsidiaries of Chinese companies on an entity list, potentially affecting some[20,000 Chinese entities.](https://wirescreen.ai/press/wirescreen-bis-50-affiliates-rule)

However, both the U.S. and China agreed to [suspend those measures for one year](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/trump-xi-south-korea-rare-earth-tariff-trade-war-nvidia.html) at a meeting in late October 2025 between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. Ahead of the leaders’ latest summit last month, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the truce was extended by two months to January.

Trade tensions between the EU and Beijing cooled last week after European trade commissioner Maroš [Sefčovič met with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/09/china-europe-hybrid-vehicle-exports-deal.html) Wentao [in Beijing](https://audiovisual.ec.europa.eu/en/media/video/I-295803). China said it was willing to use a [“green channel” mechanism](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/xwfb/bldhd/art/2026/art_870aab913b204c278dc2c42b51174cb1.html) to keep rare earths flowing to Europe, while asking for the bloc to support China’s imports of certain products in dual-use sectors.

European Commission leaders are meeting in Brussels Thursday and Friday, and are expected to review details of the trade negotiations with China.

# Taiwan Plans to Invest $4.4B in Alaska LNG, Subject to Negotiations

The proposed Alaska LNG liquefaction plant on Cook Inlet (Alaska LNG)

By **[The Maritime Executive](https://maritime-executive.com/author/marex)** 2026-10-14 20:15:36

On Wednesday, Taiwan's government confirmed that it currently plans to buy six million tonnes per annum of LNG from the Alaska LNG megaproject, and it intends to make a $4.4 billion investment in the construction of the system, subject to further negotiations.

In a statement on his social media platform on Wednesday, President Donald Trump confirmed that Taiwan had agreed to an "offtake commitment" equaling 30 percent of the plant's output "because this is now a U.S. federal government project." New York-based investment company Glenfarne Group and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation are the project's sole owners, holding equity stakes of 75 percent and 25 percent respectively.

Taiwan's energy ministry couched its commitment in terms of an ongoing negotiating process, pledging "an estimated maximum" investment amount only after further study and budgeting. "Specific investment arrangements, shareholding ratios, and related conditions will be handled according to subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures," the ministry said.

Alaska LNG is a longstanding proposal for an infrastructure network to pipe abundant North Slope gas resources across the state to Cook Inlet for liquefaction and export. It would require construction of an 800-mile line connecting gas fields on the Artic tundra to an LNG plant rated at 20 million tonnes per annum.

At one time, Alaska LNG had support from BP, ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips and was advancing steadily as a private-sector venture. All three oil majors backed out in 2016 following an independent assessment of the [project's economics](https://www.offshore-energy.biz/2016/08/30/exxonmobil-bp-conocophilips-back-out-of-alaska-lng). At present, a New York-based investment company and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation own the equity in Alaska LNG.

With the need to construct a $9 billion gas treatment plant at the Arctic northern side, then build an 800-mile overland supply pipeline through rugged wilderness, the megaproject is expected to cost $45-55 billion for 20 mtpa of capacity. This works out to as much as $2.7 billion per mtpa, much higher than the $1.6 billion per mtpa capex cost for the LNG Canada Phase 2 project in Kitimat, British Columbia. About 900 nautical miles apart, the two sites are natural competitors: they target the same East Asian market, and at similar scale. Two weeks ago, LNG Canada got the green light from private investors for its $23 billion Phase 2 expansion, which will double its capacity to 28 mtpa.

华盛顿——在习近平 9 月访问华盛顿之前，自由亚洲电台 (RFA) 在国会山召开了一场闭门两党圆桌会议，题为“中国的跨国镇压 (TNR)：三个社区、三个阶段、一个不断发展的体系”，探讨了针对藏人、维吾尔人和香港侨民社区和群体的趋势和发展。 RFA 拥有独特的主办圆桌会议的地位，它既记录了 TNR 的崛起，也成为了目标。

根据与国会工作人员、政策制定者、权利倡导者、学者和记者的讨论，RFA 报告了关于 TNR 的发展、成长和成熟度的[一系列建议和想法](https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf)。提出的问题包括保护记者和倡导者的方式、北京利用 TNR 作为操纵全球叙事的策略、人工智能在扩大其范围方面的作用、其[在美国领土上日益增长的影响力](https://radiofreeasia-radio-free-asia-prod.web.arc-cdn.net/english/special-reports/nyc-police-chinese/)，包括大学和侨民社区，以及北京在国际刑警组织等国际机构协助其努力。
**“从自由亚洲电台对西藏限制宗教自由、新疆强迫劳动和侵犯人权行为的独家报道，到当局颁布第 23 条并将我们列为‘外国势力’后关闭我们在香港的实体分社，自由亚洲电台和我们的记者经历了旨在让我们保持沉默并限制透明度的每一次 TNR，”**自由亚洲电台总裁兼首席执行官方方 (Bay Fang) 表示。

美国国会及行政当局中国委员会 (CECC) 前主席参议员杰夫·默克利 (D-OR) 在圆桌会议上致开幕词，他去年提出了两党跨国镇压政策法案 (S.2525)，该法案由现任 CECC 主席参议员丹·沙利文 (R-AK) 共同发起。此次对话由 RFA 首席通讯官 Rohit Mahajan 主持，深入探讨了上述问题，着眼于促进更大的跨部门合作、理解和解决方案。

RFA 计划继续与这一关键领域的合作伙伴、政策制定者、当局、技术专家、自由倡导者、记者和专家就这一问题进行合作。

请在此处阅读 RFA 会议的主要要点：[https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf](https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf)。

【原文 English Original】
WASHINGTON—Ahead of Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington, D.C. in September, Radio Free Asia (RFA) convened a closed, bipartisan roundtable on Capitol Hill, “China’s Transnational Repression (TNR): Three Communities, Three Phases, One Evolving System”—examining trends and developments regarding the targeting of Tibetan, Uyghur, and Hong Kong diaspora communities and groups. RFA, uniquely positioned to host the roundtable, has both documented TNR’s rise and has been a target.

From that discussion with Congressional staff, policymakers, rights advocates, academics, and journalists, RFA is reporting out [a set of recommendations and ideas](https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf) regarding TNR’s development, growth, and sophistication. Issues raised were ways of protecting journalists and advocates, TNR’s use by Beijing as a tactic aimed at manipulating global narratives, artificial intelligence’s role in expanding its scope, its [growing presence on U.S. soil](https://radiofreeasia-radio-free-asia-prod.web.arc-cdn.net/english/special-reports/nyc-police-chinese/), including universities and diaspora communities, and Beijing’s growing influence with international institutions, such as Interpol, to aid its efforts.

**“From RFA’s exclusive reporting on restrictions of religious freedom in Tibet and forced labor and human rights abuses in Xinjiang, to closing our physical bureau in Hong Kong after authorities enacted Article 23 and named us a ‘foreign force,’ RFA and our journalists have endured every iteration of TNR designed to silence us and inhibit transparency,”**RFA President and CEO Bay Fang said.

Delivering opening remarks at the roundtable was Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR), former Chair of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC), who introduced the bipartisan Transnational Repression Policy Act (S.2525) last year, co-sponsored by current CECC Chair Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK). The conversation, moderated by RFA’s Chief Communications Officer Rohit Mahajan, delved into the issues outlined above, with an eye on fostering greater cross-sector cooperation, understanding, and solutions.

RFA plans to continue engaging on this issue with partners, policymakers, authorities, technologists, freedom advocates, journalists, and experts in this critical space.

Read the chief takeaways from RFA’s session here: [https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf](https://docs.rfa.org/english/docs/RFA_TNR_Roundtable_Sept.2026.pdf).

**Gulnisa Nazarova**

Donation protected

My name is Gulnisa Nazarova, and I have been an Uyghur language instructor for over 20 years. This year, as I turn 60, instead of gifts I am asking for something much closer to my heart.

My dear mother taught me how to cook. Through her hands, I learned patience, generosity, and how food carries memory. Many of the dishes she passed on come from the Uyghur tradition, a cuisine rich in history, flavor, and storytelling, yet still too little known and increasingly at risk of being forgotten.

This fundraiser supports a lifelong dream of mine: creating a cookbook dedicated to Uyghur cuisine and cultural heritage.

My connection to Uyghur culture begins with my family and upbringing. My parents and ancestors came from the Uyghur Autonomous Region, known as Eastern Turkistan to Soviet Central Asia in the mid-20th century, carrying with them their traditions, food, language, history, and stories. I grew up learning not only recipes, but also their deeper meaning — meals that bring families together, celebrations filled with memory, and dishes that carry history from one generation to the next.

Over the years, I have worked professionally to support Uyghur language and culture through teaching, writing, and sharing my knowledge with others around the world. This cookbook, however, is different. It comes directly from the heart — from meals shared with my family and from a deep desire to preserve the taste of home for future generations.

This is a personal initiative, and the funds raised will help cover:

*   Research and documentation of recipes and food stories
*   Photography and image use for the book
*   Writing and editing
*   Professional design
*   Initial publication costs

Whether you give a little or a lot, you are helping keep a culinary heritage alive.

Thank you for celebrating my 60th birthday by honoring my mother’s legacy with me.

Hi, I'm Mehmet Utku ÖZTÜRK, and I'm reaching out to you to support the vital work of the Uyghur Human Rights Project (UHRP).

As many of you may know, the Uyghurs in East Turkistan face severe human rights challenges, torture, forced labor, child labor and cultural repression (I linked some articles and publications upon this matter at the end, you can check)

UHRP is dedicated to advocating for their civil, political, social, cultural, and economic rights through extensive research and reports.

Your donations will directly impact this important mission by:

*   Funding vital research and publications that raise awareness about the plight of the Uyghurs.
*   Supporting advocacy efforts that push for international accountability and protection of human rights in East Turkistan.

Together, we can help amplify the voices of those who need it most. Please consider donating to support UHRP's ongoing efforts. Every contribution makes a difference. Thank you!

title: Donate to Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children, organized by Yangkey Gangshar
summary: Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Taman
content:
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.

Who We Are & Our Connection

We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.

“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.

A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family

At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.

Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.

He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.

The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.

Our Family’s Connection to This Community

Our connection to this region goes back generations.

Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.

Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.

The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.

Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.

The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.

Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.

What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.

We Are Grieving Many Losses

Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.

His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.

We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.

Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.

How the Funds Will Be Used

We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.

The funds will be used specifically for:

*   Food and daily necessities
*   Shelter, rent, and household expenses
*   Clothing and essential supplies
*   School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
*   Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
*   Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives

100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.

Bringing the Help Directly to Nepal

Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.

We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.

Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.

If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.

Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.

From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.

With gratitude,

Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

— His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama

title: TSMC raises 2026 sales growth forecast to 44%, leaves capex unchanged - Focus Taiwan

summary: 中新社台北 10 月 15 日电 台积电 (TSMC) 周四表示，已将 2026 年以美元计算的销售增长预测上调至 44%，同时保持资本支出 (capex) 预算不变。台积电首席执行官 C.C. 在投资者会议上发表讲话魏哲家表示，对该公司先进工艺的需求预计将保持强劲，从而推动使用其 2 纳米工艺制造的芯片的出货量，这是该芯片制造商投入商业化生产的最新技术。魏总表示，台积电在领先的技术开发上领先于同行，有强大的支持
content:
中新社台北 10 月 15 日电 台积电 (TSMC) 周四表示，已将 2026 年以美元计算的销售增长预测上调至 44%，同时保持资本支出 (capex) 预算不变。

台积电首席执行官 C.C. 在投资者会议上发表讲话魏哲家表示，对该公司先进工艺的需求预计将保持强劲，从而推动使用其 2 纳米工艺制造的芯片的出货量，这是该芯片制造商投入商业化生产的最新技术。

魏表示，台积电在领先技术开发方面领先于同行，以及客户的大力支持，预计将确保其2026年的业绩。

44% 的预测是对 7 月份预测的升级，当时 Wei 预计 2026 年以美元计算的销售额增长将略高于 40%。

会前，台积电发布了第三季度业绩，每股收益创纪录新台币29.43元，而去年同期为新台币17.44元，一季度为新台币27.25元。

第三季度，采用2nm工艺制造的芯片占总销售额的8%，高于第二季度的3%。

台积电首席财务官黄仁昭对第四季度表示乐观，预计第四季度营收在523亿美元至543亿美元之间，中值同比增长58%，环比增长14%。
黄说，台积电第四季度的毛利率（收入与销售成本之间的差额）预计为 65-67%，而第三季度为 66.4%。

他表示，第四季度的营业利润率（扣除运营费用）预计为 56.5-58.5%，而第三季度为 58.7%。

黄仁勋表示，台积电将 2026 年资本支出预算维持在 600 亿美元至 640 亿美元不变。

他表示，高资本支出反映了公司对未来几年客户需求强劲的预期，包括新兴的代理人工智能（AI）应用程序。

黄仁勋表示，台积电2026年至2028年的资本支出将比前三年更多，预计支出将根据客户需求持续增长。

【●台积电Q3净利润创季度新高】(https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610150009)

他补充说，台积电将继续投资，同时努力为股东带来更高的回报，并支付有吸引力的现金股息。

黄说，对台积电广泛应用于人工智能应用的晶圆上芯片（CoWoS）封装技术的需求仍然强劲。

黄说，台积电将继续与客户密切合作，确保有足够的 CoWoS 产能来满足他们的需求。
魏回应黄，表示CoWoS仍然是客户集成电路组装的首选，并且台积电在该技术方面拥有令人满意的良率记录。

（张建中、钟荣峰、黄芳芳撰文）

Enditem/sfj

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) said Thursday that it has raised its 2026 sales growth forecast to 44 percent in U.S. dollar terms, while leaving its capital expenditure (capex) budget unchanged.

Speaking at an investor conference, TSMC CEO C.C. Wei (魏哲家) said demand for the company's advanced processes is expected to stay strong, driving shipments of chips made using its 2-nanometer process, the most recent technology the chipmaker has put into commercial production.

Wei said TSMC's lead over its peers in leading-edge technology development and strong support from its customers are expected to ensure its performance in 2026.

The 44 percent estimate is an upgrade from the forecast made in July, when Wei predicted sales growth in U.S. dollar terms would be slightly more than 40 percent in 2026.

Before the conference, TSMC released its third-quarter results, reporting record earnings per share of NT$29.43, compared with NT$17.44 a year earlier and NT$27.25 a quarter earlier.

In the third quarter, chips made using the 2nm process accounted for 8 percent of total sales, up from 3 percent in the second quarter.

Expressing optimism about the fourth quarter, TSMC Chief Financial Officer Wendell Huang (黃仁昭) said the company expects fourth-quarter revenue of between US$52.3 billion and US$54.3 billion, with the midpoint representing a 58 percent increase from a year earlier and a 14 percent rise from the previous quarter.

Huang said TSMC's gross margin -- the difference between revenue and the cost of goods sold -- is forecast at 65-67 percent in the fourth quarter, compared with 66.4 percent in the third quarter.

Its operating margin -- which also deducts operating expenses -- is estimated at 56.5-58.5 percent in the fourth quarter, compared with 58.7 percent in the third quarter, he said.

Huang said TSMC has kept its 2026 capex budget unchanged at US$60 billion to US$64.0 billion.

The high capex reflects the company's expectations of strong demand from its customers over the next few years, including from emerging agentic artificial intelligence (AI) applications, he said.

TSMC will spend more on capex from 2026 to 2028 than in the previous three years, and spending is expected to keep rising in line with customer demand, Huang said.

[●TSMC's Q3 net profit hits new quarterly high](https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610150009)

While TSMC will continue to invest, the company will work hard to deliver higher returns to shareholders and pay attractive cash dividends, he added.

Huang said demand for TSMC's Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) packaging technology, which is widely used in AI applications, remained strong.

TSMC will continue to work closely with customers and ensure sufficient CoWoS capacity to meet their demand, Huang said.

Echoing Huang, Wei said CoWoS remained customers' top choice for integrated circuit assembly and that TSMC had a record of satisfactory yield rates for the technology.

(By Chang Chien-chung, Chung Jung-feng and Frances Huang)

Enditem/sfj

# Typhoon Champi unlikely to hit Hong Kong, Observatory says

China's weather agency says a tropical depression east of Guam is set to become Typhoon Champi within 24 hours, possibly reaching super typhoon strength. The Hong Kong Observatory says a direct hit on the city is unlikely, with tropical cyclones not expected to affect Hong Kong for the rest of Octob

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 17:54 HKT · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "X")[](https://clb.org.hk/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Email")

China's National Meteorological Center said a tropical depression east of Guam is forecast to become this year's 30th typhoon, Champi, within 24 hours, and it could develop into a super typhoon as it moves west-northwest.

The Hong Kong Observatory said the city is less likely to be hit directly, and tropical cyclones are unlikely to affect Hong Kong for the rest of October. The storm may move toward waters east of Luzon early to mid next week. Its later track remains uncertain, but there is a higher chance it will turn north and pass through waters east of Taiwan.

AI weather models all show Champi making a 90-degree northward turn near eastern Taiwan. Model Pangu forecasts the storm will cross Japan on October 26, while Fuxi and Fengwu show it passing near Tokyo between October 25 and 26.

Separately, Typhoon Koguma in the western North Pacific weakened into an extratropical cyclone on October 14.

Locally, the Observatory said a fresh easterly airstream will bring stronger winds and one or two showers to the Guangdong coast over the next two or three days. As an upper-air anticyclone strengthens, the South China coast should be generally sunny and dry early to mid next week, with hot daytime weather. A northeast monsoon is expected to affect southern China late next week.

The Observatory predicted mostly sunny weather over the next nine days. Saturday will be mostly cloudy with one or two showers, and Sunday will start mostly cloudy with one or two light showers. Next week will be cooler, with the lowest temperature on October 23 dropping to 25 degrees, with sunny periods and dry daytime conditions.

## Details

I have lived in 6 countries, traveled to 45 and all 7 continents, and checked everything off my very extensive travel bucket list by the age of 36.

Ask me anything.

Whether you would like to travel more, are itching to live the digital nomad life, or just want to hear some cool stories from around the globe, join me to chat about life, travel, and the pursuit of happiness.

If you’d like to know more about me and my story in the meantime, check out [https://www.nicoleelysejourneys.com](https://www.nicoleelysejourneys.com/) and my talk on “Why getting robbed at gunpoint in Colombia is the best thing that’s ever happened to me.”

This is not a sales pitch. I do do travel coaching if you want more targeted help getting started, but that’s not what we’re here to talk about. I just like meeting fellow travelers and wannabe travelers.

# Group urges candidates to address four women's rights priorities

10/15/2026 06:43 PM

The Garden of Hope Foundation held a press event on Sunday to call for greater social support for female survivors of domestic violence.CNA photo Aug. 11, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) A women's rights group on Thursday urged candidates running for top local government positions to address four priorities: housing for survivors of domestic violence, action against workplace sexual harassment, childcare and caregiver training.

The Garden of Hope Foundation, a charity that campaigns for gender equality, put forward eight demands under the four categories to 81 candidates running for magistrate or mayor in Taiwan's 22 counties and cities in the local elections on Nov. 28.

The foundation said in a news release that it hoped to turn needs identified by frontline social workers into concrete proposals that local governments can put into practice. "Gender-responsive policies should be part of local governance," it said.

Citing a 2025 survey showing that 52 percent of survivors of domestic violence struggled to find housing after fleeing their homes, the foundation called for more housing options that meet survivors' needs while keeping them close to work, school and their daily routines.

It also called for giving survivors priority in public housing allocations and for setting up shelters within such housing that offer childcare and other support services.

On workplace sexual harassment, the foundation called on local labor authorities to hold at least two legal advice sessions a month to help employers handle cases and access outside support.

Many companies, particularly small and medium-sized businesses, still struggle to follow central government guidelines on workplace sexual harassment because they lack dedicated staff, the foundation said.

On childcare, the foundation called for more drop-in childcare services to meet parents' occasional needs, including at least one daytime center and one nighttime center open until 10 p.m. in each district.

It also urged more flexible working hours to help parents manage childcare drop-offs and pickups, and called for easing eligibility rules for public childcare so more families can use the services.

On caregiver training, the foundation called for home-based childcare providers to receive at least three hours of gender equality training every two years, matching the mandatory requirement for workers at childcare institutions.

The foundation is awaiting a response from candidates, as of press time.

(By Wu Hsin-yun and Shih Hsiu-chuan)

content:
中新社台北10月15日电 交易商称，台湾股市周四遭遇第六大单日跌幅，暴跌逾1,600点，因华盛顿隔夜公布高于预期的通胀数据后，科技股受到美联储加息担忧的打击。

台湾证券交易所基准指数在 46,795.38 点至 48,382.75 点之间波动，最终下跌 1,655.96 点，至 46,969.87 点，跌幅为 3.41%。成交总额为新台币 1.32 万亿（409.8 亿美元），而周三为新台币 9,781.4 亿。

“看看成交量的扩大。我认为投资者在恐慌中争相减持，”华南证券分析师Kevin Su表示。 “他们对美国9月份通胀数据感到失望，引发了对鹰派美联储的担忧。”

周三，美国9月消费者价格指数(CPI)数据显示，通胀上涨3.7%，高于市场预期的3.6%。

“利率上升将提高人工智能公司的融资成本，”苏说。 “在科技股估值较高的时期，这种负面影响被放大，导致其股价陷入混乱。”

苏表示，东京和首尔市场半导体股票的下跌增加了台北市场的抛售。
在美国存托凭证下跌3.40%后，占总市值超过40%的台积电(TSMC)下跌2.01%，收于新台币2,440.00元，带动电子指数下跌3.84%。

IC封装测试公司日月光跌10%，创单日最大跌幅，收于新台币673.00元；智能手机IC设计公司联发科跌6.93%，收于新台币4,165.00元。

同样在科技板块，电源管理解决方案提供商台达电子股价下跌 8.68%，收于新台币 1,630.00 元；iPhone 组装商和人工智能服务器制造商鸿海精密工业股份有限公司 (Hon Hai Precision Industry Co.) 收盘下跌 1.44%，收于新台币 239.50 元。

“从科技股的损失来看，我怀疑外国机构投资者继续站在卖方一边，并将资金撤出本地市场，”苏说。

据台湾证券交易所称，周四外国机构投资者在主板净售出新台币3025.6亿美元的股票。

苏表示，随着科技股暴跌，投资者希望将资金投入防御性股票。

中华电信上涨2.69%，收于新台币152.50元；台湾大哥大收涨3.65%，收于新台币131.00元；远传电信上涨4.63%，收于新台币113.00元。

此外，食品品牌统一企业收涨1.66%，至新台币79.50元；味全食品收涨0.44%，至新台币11.50元。
轮动买盘提振金融板块上涨0.73%。玉山金控涨3.17%，报48.80元新台币；兆丰金控涨2.74%，报52.50新台币。

“台交所跌破20日移动平均线48,041点，技术面变得脆弱，”苏说。 “我预计，在指数接近 46,000 点之前，未来还会出现更多损失。”

（弗兰西斯·黄）

结局/ASG

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan suffered their sixth-steepest single-day point loss on Thursday, plunging over 1,600 points as tech stocks were hammered by fears of a Federal Reserve rate hike after Washington released higher-than-expected inflation data overnight, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 1,655.96 points, or 3.41 percent, at 46,969.87 after moving between 46,795.38 and 48,382.75. Turnover totaled NT$1.32 trillion (US$40.98 billion), compared with NT$978.14 billion Wednesday.

"Look at the expanded turnover. I think investors scrambled to trim their holdings in panic," Hua Nan Securities analyst Kevin Su said. "They were disappointed with the U.S. September inflation data, raising concerns over a hawkish Fed."

On Wednesday, the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data for September showed that inflation rose 3.7 percent, higher than the market forecast of 3.6 percent.

"Rising interest rates will raise fundraising costs for AI companies," Su said. "At a time of high valuations of tech stocks, such negative leads were amplified, sending their stock prices into a tailspin."

Su said losses for semiconductor stocks in the Tokyo and Seoul markets added selling in Taipei.

After its American depositary receipts lost 3.40 percent, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for over 40 percent of total market value, lost 2.01 percent to close at NT$2,440.00, sending the electronics index down 3.84 percent.

IC packaging and testing firm ASE Technology Holding Co. tumbled 10 percent, the maximum daily decline, to end at NT$673.00, and smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. slid 6.93 percent to close at NT$4,165.00.

Also in the tech sector, power management solution provider Delta Electronics Inc. shed 8.68 percent to end at NT$1,630.00, while iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. closed down 1.44 percent at NT$239.50.

"Judging from the tech losses, I suspect foreign institutional investors continued to stand on the sell side and move their funds out of the local market," Su said.

According to the Taiwan Stock Exchange, foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$302.56 billion of shares on the main board Thursday.

Su said that with tech stocks plunging, investors looked to park their money in defensive stocks.

Chunghwa Telecom Co. rose 2.69 percent to end at NT$152.50 and Taiwan Mobile Co. closed up 3.65 percent at NT$131.00, and Far EasTone Telecommunications Co. ended up 4.63 percent at NT$113.00.

In addition, food brand Uni-President Enterprises Corp. closed up 1.66 percent at NT$79.50, and Wei Chuan Foods Corp. ended 0.44 percent higher at NT$11.50.

Rotational buying lifted the financial sector 0.73 percent. E. Sun Financial Holding Co. closed up 3.17 percent at NT$48.80 and Mega Financial Holding Co. ended up 2.74 percent at NT$52.50.

"The Taiex fell below the 20-day moving average of 48,041 points and became technically fragile," Su said. "I expect more losses ahead until the index gets closer to 46,000 points."

(By Frances Huang)

Despite China’s close ties with Russia, Chinese solar energy technology is giving Ukraine badly needed energy resilience.

By **Hao Tan**

October 15, 2026

A worker on a cherry picker installs solar panels on a building in Kyiv, Ukraine, May 9, 2026.

Credit: [Shutterstock](https://www.shutterstock.com/image-photo/kyiv-ukraine-may-9-2026-editorial-2778680709?trackingId=106fc2f5-479f-4bb0-adae-654795817c83&listId=searchResults)

Ad

Russia’s war against Ukraine has shown that energy security is no longer just about access to fuels, pipelines, and large power stations. It also depends on solar panels, batteries, and other distributed energy equipment that can keep homes, businesses, and critical services operating when the electricity grid is under attack.

Ironically, most of the equipment helping Ukraine keep the lights on comes from China.

Beijing has maintained close strategic ties with Russia. Yet through trade and global supply chains, Chinese-made clean energy technologies are helping Ukraine reduce the vulnerability created by Russian attacks on its energy system.

Russia’s attacks exposed the vulnerability of Ukraine’s highly centralized power system. The International Energy Agency (IEA) [estimated](https://www.iea.org/reports/ukraines-energy-security-and-the-coming-winter) that around half of Ukraine’s generation capacity was occupied, damaged or destroyed during 2022-23, while around half of its large network substations were damaged by missiles and drones. After another wave of attacks in spring 2024, Ukraine [lost](https://www.iea.org/reports/ukraines-energy-security-and-the-coming-winter) a further 9 GW of generation capacity, leaving it with only around one-third of its pre-war capacity. On January 20, 2026, another [major Russian attack](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3340587/almost-half-kyiv-without-heat-and-power-after-massive-russian-drone-strike)on energy infrastructure left almost half of Kyiv without heat and power.

Such attacks turned Ukraine’s large, fixed energy assets into major points of vulnerability, making energy [decentralization](https://www.csis.org/analysis/striving-access-security-and-sustainability) an increasingly important source of resilience. Consequently, there has been a resurgence of solar power in Ukraine.

The country was already a significant solar market before Russia’s full-scale invasion, [ranking](https://www.ren21.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/gsr_2020_full_report_en.pdf) ninth globally for new solar capacity addition in 2019. But deployment and trade collapsed after February 2022. Chinese module exports to Ukraine [fell](https://www.infolink-group.com/energy-article/tw/solar-topic-solar-energy-ukraine) from 83.9 MW in February 2022 to just 7.5 MW in March, and totaled only 15.8 MW in 2023.

Since then, the market has recovered. The Solar Energy Association of Ukraine [estimated](https://aseu.org.ua/en/in-2025-almost-twice-as-many-solar-power-plants-were-installed-in-ukraine-as-in-the-previous-year/) that around 800 MW of solar was installed in 2024 and 1.5 GW in 2025. Businesses and households have been installing solar power to reduce their dependence on the grid. Distributed solar PV, often combined with battery storage, has therefore [become](https://www.iea.org/reports/policy-options-to-accelerate-distributed-solar-pv-in-ukraine) an important part of Ukraine’s wartime energy security.

International organizations, such as the [IEA](https://www.iea.org/reports/empowering-ukraine-through-a-decentralised-electricity-system) and the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://www.csis.org/analysis/striving-access-security-and-sustainability), have recently examined Ukraine’s energy reconstruction, covering aspects such as decentralization, solar power, battery storage, financing, and electricity-market reform. However, these reports tell us remarkably little about the sources of the equipment needed for this transition.

In particular, the role of Chinese-made equipment in this shift has received much less attention. According to the IEA, China [accounts](https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-technology-perspectives-2026) for around 85 percent of global solar supply-chain production capacity and around 80 percent of lithium-ion battery production capacity. Its share in some specific segments is even higher – for example, China supplies around 95 percent of global PV wafer capacity.

# TSMC evaluating Texas production, cooperation with Terafab

A TSMC fab in Arizona. CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) C. C. Wei (魏哲家), Chairman and CEO of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), said Thursday that the chipmaker is evaluating the possibility of collaborating with Elon Musk's Terafab project in Texas.

Speaking at an investor conference, Wei said that while cooperation with Terafab was possible, any fab should be run by TSMC to control production.

[●TSMC raises 2026 sales growth forecast to 44%, leaves capex unchanged](https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610150018)

He emphasized that the possible cooperation with the Terafab project was at the discussion stage.

Wei's remarks came after Musk said on social media that it was possible TSMC could sublease part of Terafab "but nothing more than that."

Wei said TSMC is working hard to expand its capacity in the United States and the expansion is necessary as its major American clients have asked the chipmaker to raise production to meet their demand. He added that the U.S. government has provided necessary assistance to TSMC for expansion.

He added that on the back of strong demand for smartphones, high-performance computing devices and artificial intelligence applications, TSMC's production capacity using its latest-generation 2-nanometer process will more than double from a year earlier in 2027.

CNA graph

Meanwhile, Wei said TSMC is developing the A14 process and trial production is slated for 2027 before mass production is scheduled to begin in 2028.

Compared with the 2nm process, the A14 process is expected to offer a 10-15 percent speed improvement at the same power, or a 25-30 percent power reduction at the same speed, while the new process is expected to boost logic density by almost 20 percent, according to TSMC.

According to Wei, nearly 20 fab projects worldwide are currently underway, including three new 3nm fabs.

In Taiwan, a 3nm fab in Tainan is expected to begin mass production in the first half of 2027, while another 3nm fab is also planned in Tainan and will start commercial production in the first half of 2028, Wei said.

In Arizona, a second fab using the 2nm process will start mass production in the third quarter of 2027, he added.

(By Chang Chien-chung and Frances Huang)

content:
中新社台南10月15日电 台南台南地下列车将于周六开始运行，标志着台南城市景观重塑迈出了重要一步，也为台南百年火车站作为了解当地历史文化的门户开辟了新的可能性。

几代人以来，这条铁路一直是贯穿台湾最古老城市台南的重要南北交通走廊。但其轨道、平交路口、地下通道和立交桥也将城市分割开来，使得东部和西部地区之间的交通更加困难。

据交通部称，全长8.23公里的地下路段将取消23个铁路道口及相关建筑物，改善行人和骑自行车者的通行，同时缓解交通瓶颈。

该项目于2009年9月获得内阁批准，由铁路局牵头，历时约17年才实现第一阶段通车。据该局称，在此期间，成本从预计的 330 亿新台币增加到 412.6 亿新台币（13 亿美元），整个项目目前计划于 2031 年 3 月完工。

转型将不仅仅限于交通运输。交通部表示，一旦现有轨道被拆除，计划将原来的铁路走廊变成一条约30米宽的绿道，并设有步行道、自行车道和景观区，连接新车站、社区、学校和公共设施。
## 历史车站的新角色

国立成功大学建筑学荣休教授、车站修复和再利用计划审查委员会成员傅朝卿表示，该项目还提供了一个重新思考台南车站角色的机会，台南车站是该市最知名的地标之一。

该车站的历史建筑于 1936 年重建，并于 1998 年被指定为国家纪念碑。该车站于 1900 年日本殖民统治期间（1895-1945 年）首次开放。它将保留在新地铁站旁边，而不是被新地铁站取代。

傅说，车站与台南的城市布局紧密相关。它面向车站环岛和历史悠久的市中心的位置决定了人们进入和游览城市的方式。

铁路规划者最初考虑在更北的地方建造一个新车站，将历史建筑抛在后面，傅反对这一提议，因为这可能会切断车站与市中心的长期关系。

采用的设计将新车站置于地下并毗邻历史建筑，使两者共存。其低矮的水平轮廓和宽阔的天篷使旧车站在视觉上更加突出，而下沉的广场和连接的走道将两个设施连接起来。
台铁表示，旧车站还可以发挥更重要的文化和商业作用，并补充说，正在讨论的计划包括咖啡馆、便餐选择、当地纪念品、阅读空间和展览。

## 连接交通和遗产

成大城市规划系特聘教授陈彦仲表示，铁路迁入地下也为保留和诠释车站周围的历史风貌提供了机会。

台南已有400多年的历史，曾是台湾的省会，保留了历史悠久的铁路设施和车站周围的其他历史遗迹，包括站台、转盘、仓库和车站等。

【原文 English Original】
Tainan, Oct. 15 (CNA) Trains are set to begin running underground in Tainan on Saturday, marking a major step in reshaping the southern Taiwan city's urban landscape and opening up new possibilities for its century-old railway station to serve as a gateway to local history and culture.

For generations, the railway has served as a vital north-south transportation corridor through Tainan, Taiwan's oldest city. But its tracks, level crossings, underpasses and overpasses have also divided the city, making travel between its eastern and western districts more difficult.

According to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), the 8.23-kilometer underground section will eliminate 23 railway crossings and related structures, improving access for pedestrians and cyclists while easing traffic bottlenecks.

Approved by the Cabinet in September 2009 and led by the Railway Bureau, the project will have taken about 17 years to reach its first-stage opening. In that period the cost rose from a projected NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion (US$1.3 billion), with the full project now scheduled for completion in March 2031, according to the bureau.

The transformation will extend beyond transportation. Once the existing tracks are removed, there are plans to turn the former railway corridor into a greenway about 30 meters wide, with walking and cycling paths and landscaped areas linking new stations, neighborhoods, schools and public facilities, the MOTC said.

## A new role for a historic station

The project also offers an opportunity to rethink the role of Tainan Station, one of the city's most recognizable landmarks, said Fu Chao-ching (傅朝卿), an emeritus professor of architecture at National Cheng Kung University (NCKU) and a member of the review committee for the station's restoration and reuse plan.

First opened in 1900 during Japanese colonial rule (1895-1945), the station's historic building was rebuilt in 1936 and designated a national monument in 1998. It will remain in place alongside the new underground station rather than be replaced by it.

Fu said the station is closely tied to Tainan's urban layout. Its position facing the station roundabout and the historic city center has shaped how people enter and navigate the city.

Railway planners initially considered building a new station further north, leaving the historic building behind, a proposal Fu opposed because it risked severing the station's long-standing relationship with the city center.

The adopted design instead places the new station underground and next to the historic building, allowing the two to coexist. Its low, horizontal profile and broad canopy give visual prominence to the old station, while a sunken plaza and connecting walkways link the two facilities.

The old station could also take on a more prominent cultural and commercial role, Taiwan Railway Corp. said, adding that plans under discussion include cafes, light meals options, local souvenirs, reading spaces and exhibitions.

## Connecting transport and heritage

The railway's relocation underground also presents an opportunity to preserve and interpret the historic features around the station, said Chen Yen-chung (陳彥仲), a distinguished professor in NCKU's Department of Urban Planning.

With a history of more than 400 years, Tainan was once the capital of Taiwan and retains historic railway facilities and other remnants of the past around the station, including platforms, a turntable, warehouses and sections of the old city wall.

Chen said future development should balance preservation with new uses, allowing the station to serve as a starting point for understanding Tainan's history and culture.

He said rather than simply passing through the station to transfer to other forms of transportation, visitors could encounter the city's past there before continuing to historic areas such as the old city center and Anping.

"Restrictions should not be seen as limitations. They can instead become opportunities to create a distinctive urban character," Chen said.

The project has also revealed traces of Tainan's earlier history beneath the modern city. According to the city's Cultural Affairs Bureau, construction teams uncovered 20 archaeological sites containing remains dating from prehistoric times to the Qing dynasty and Japanese colonial period.

The discoveries directly impacted the project's construction schedule, with archaeological investigations and preservation work adding about two years to the original timetable, the Railway Bureau said.

According to the Tainan City government, there were also design changes to preserve archaeological remains, either by relocating them for safekeeping or reinforcing them in place.

However, the transformation will take time. After trains begin running underground, the existing tracks and structures still need to be removed, roads restored and pedestrian facilities improved before the full benefits can be realized.

Two additional underground commuter stations, Linsen and South Tainan, are scheduled to open in 2029 and 2030, respectively.

The longer-term challenge will be to ensure that the land freed up by the project becomes useful public space, encourages renewal along the corridor and helps reconnect communities, Chen said.

For Tainan, the railway's move underground could ultimately reshape more than the city's transport network. Whether the former railway corridor becomes a meaningful public space, and whether the historic station can draw visitors into the city's wider cultural landscape, will help determine how far the project succeeds in reconnecting Tainan with its past as well as its future.

(By Chiu Chu-yin, Chang Jung-hsiang, Huang Chiao-wen and Lee Hsin-Yin)

title: Leave forms, bags of cash link Hawks member to alleged ‘crime syndicate’
summary: Last year, a member of the Hawks allegedly booked leave on two occasions to travel to Nelson Mandela Bay so he could join other members of a kidnapping syndicate to abduct two women for ransom. Around the same time, he spent his share of th
content:
Last year, a member of the Hawks allegedly booked leave on two occasions to travel to Nelson Mandela Bay so he could join other members of a kidnapping syndicate to abduct two women for ransom.

Around the same time, he spent his share of the ransom money on a luxury car, which was parked at a house in Motherwell where the police found close to R200,000 in marked bills used to pay the ransom, as well as a firearm that was used in the [assassination of Gqeberha prosecutor Tracy Brown](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-08-02-gqeberha-prosecutor-gunned-down-outside-her-home-in-planned-hit-emphasises-high-stakes/).

These were among allegations levelled against Xolani Busakwe at the Gqeberha Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, where State advocate Marius Stander led evidence opposing his formal bail application.

Busakwe, a member of the Hawks’ Digital Forensic Investigation Unit, sat in the dock with slumped shoulders as Stander outlined the State’s case that he is allegedly linked to a criminal syndicate responsible for Brown’s death and at least two kidnappings for ransom – all in the space of three months last year.

He faces a string of charges including kidnapping, human trafficking, extortion and robbery with aggravating circumstances, as well as charges under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act.

His co-accused, Simthembile Xungu, David Mthembu, Buhle Mbini, Andile Mathumbu, Unathi Mayi and his brother Ayabulela Busakwe face similar charges, while some have also been charged with murder and conspiracy to commit murder in relation to the hit on Brown.

 Ayabulela Busakwe (left) and Simthembile Xungu will remain behind bars until the start of the trial. (Photo: Riaan Marais)

According to an affidavit prepared by the Hawks and read into the court record by Stander, Busakwe was a police officer stationed at the Gqeberha Local Criminal Records Centre before he was transferred to the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (Hawks) head office in Pretoria, where he was assigned to the Digital Forensic Investigations Unit in 2024.

In June 2025, Busakwe submitted a leave request and planned to visit his home in Motherwell. It was during this time that cellphone records place him in the vicinity of the Markman Fresh Produce Market where [Lindsay Knowlden was kidnapped](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-06-25-abducted-held-captive-for-4-days-lindsay-knowlden-reunited-with-family/).

Cellphone records also placed Mthembu, Mbini and Mathumbu in the same location and indicated continuous communication between the four men around the time of the kidnapping.

It was also revealed that the last known live location of Knowlden’s cellphone was Mathumbu’s home address in Motherwell.

Lindsay Knowlden was kidnapped from the Fresh Produce Market in Markman Industrial in June 2025. (Photo: Deon Ferreira / Facebook)

A ransom amount of R1.25-million was paid for Knowlden’s release. The following day, Busakwe and his brother contacted a used car dealership in George, Western Cape, to negotiate the cash purchase of a BMW to the tune of R155,000.

The two brothers, along with a friend, Lungile Jika, travelled to the dealership a few days later with a plastic bag full of cash to complete the transaction. However, the deal was delayed when the salesman became suspicious.

The car was subsequently purchased via an electronic fund transfer and registered in Jika’s name.

Stander said it was the State’s case that the Busakwes, along with Mthembu, Mbini and Mathumbu, orchestrated Knowlden’s kidnapping, and that the BMW was purchased with a portion of the ransom money.

Between 11 and 14 August 2025, Busakwe was scheduled to testify in a court case in Nelson Mandela Bay, and the police booked his flights between Pretoria and Gqeberha. The day after his flights were confirmed, he booked leave for the days leading up to the court dates, claiming he would be in Nelson Mandela Bay due to a family bereavement.

On 11 August, [Theresa Minnie was kidnapped outside her home in Kariega](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-08-12-hawks-mum-on-arrests-after-numerous-nelson-mandela-bay-kidnappings/). A ransom of R1.1-million was paid to secure her release. However, before the payment was made, the Hawks marked the cash with a fluorescent powder.

Theresa Minnie was kidnapped from her home in Kariega, Eastern Cape, on 11 August 2025. (Photo: Facebook)

The suspects were subsequently tracked, and in the week following the kidnapping, Ayabulela Busakwe and Mathumbu were arrested and found in possession of large sums of cash, including banknotes marked with the fluorescent powder.

Stander also indicated that during questioning, Ayabulela Busakwe made a partial confession that a “Xolani” was involved in the kidnapping, effectively fingering his brother as an accomplice.

Further investigation led the police to an address where the accused allegedly stashed some of their loot. The police found R197,000 marked with the fluorescent powder, as well as a firearm that has since been positively linked to the murder of prosecutor Tracy Brown.

Gqeberha prosecutor Tracy Brown was gunned down at her Young Park, Gqeberha home on 31 July, 2025. (Photo: Supplied / Facebook)

A witness also told the police that Ayabulela Busakwe parked a BMW at the address, but that his brother later came to fetch the vehicle.

Xolani Busakwe missed his flight from Gqeberha to Pretoria on 14 August. It is the State’s case that he waited in Nelson Mandela Bay until he was certain that Minnie’s ransom had been paid before driving the BMW, purchased with Knowlden’s ransom money, back to Pretoria.

The vehicle has since been located in Pretoria and is the subject of an asset forfeiture application.

Stander also indicated that Busakwe faces charges of theft and defeating the ends of justice in a separate case. During the search of his residence, police uncovered 12 dockets related to a 2022 investigation at the Local Criminal Record Centre at Mount Road police station in Gqeberha, where Busakwe had previously been stationed.

The State submitted that it would be in the interests of justice for the court to deny Busakwe bail, mainly because of his familiarity with police systems and some of the witnesses, and he could easily interfere with the investigation and possibly tamper with evidence.

The case was postponed until Friday for closing arguments by the State and defence. Busakwe is scheduled to return to court alongside his co-accused next week. **DM**

# China Spied on Taiwanese President’s Son – in the US

The incident shone a spotlight on China’s growing repertoire for transnational repression targeting Taiwanese leaders.

By [Brian Hioe](https://thediplomat.com/authors/brian-hioe/)

October 15, 2026

[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F&title=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US "Share on LinkedIn")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on Facebook")[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on Bluesky")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on X")

Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te

Credit: [Official Photo by Liu Shu fu / Office of the President, ROC (Taiwan)-8a90004bfc-k](https://www.flickr.com/photos/presidentialoffice/54502930988/in/dateposted/)

Ad

News broke earlier this month that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had arrested real estate agent Wanying “Heather” Zhang for spying on Lai Ting-yu, the eldest child of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te. Zhang lived in Irvine, California, where she worked as a real estate agent. She was originally from Changsha, China, before emigrating to the United States and naturalizing.

Lai Ting-yu is not a political figure – members of the Lai family tend to keep a low profile. Lai Ching-te’s wife, First Lady Wu Mei-ju, does not often make public appearances with her husband. Arguably, the most famous members of the Lai family outside of Lai Ching-te himself are the family dogs, Murphy, Banban, and Luke, though Luke has since [passed away](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E7%8B%97%E6%B4%BE-%E7%B8%BD%E7%B5%B1%E8%B3%B4%E6%B8%85%E5%BE%B7%E7%B1%B2%E9%A0%98%E9%A4%8A%E4%B8%8D%E6%A3%84%E9%A4%8A-%E6%9B%AC%E5%85%A8%E5%AE%B6%E7%A6%8F%E7%85%A7%E4%BB%8B%E7%B4%B9%E6%84%9B%E7%8A%ACmurphy-%E7%9B%BC%E7%8B%97%E7%8B%97%E9%83%BD%E8%83%BD%E5%9C%A8%E6%84%9B%E8%88%87%E7%90%86%E8%A7%A3%E4%B8%AD%E6%89%BE%E5%88%B0%E6%AD%B8%E5%B1%AC-075324709.html). Banban in particular [is best known](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/life/breakingnews/5422777) as a dog that had lost a leg to a wild boar trap before being adopted by the Lai family.

Lai Ting-yu, who [holds a doctorate](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/suspected-chinese-agent-taiwan-president-son-los-angeles-federal-court/) in bioengineering from the University of Washington, works for electronics company Philips and lives in Seattle with his wife and son.

The FBI alleged that Lai was being surveilled by Zhang, along with other accomplices, in September 2025. It is unclear what Zhang was attempting to accomplish, given Lai Ting-yu’s lack of a political background.

There could be a domestic political angle. Lai Ching-te has long been criticized by members of the pan-Blue camp over allegations that his son lives in the United States. The suggestion is that Lai is hypocritical in calling for Taiwan to increase defense spending to ward off Chinese threats, even as his own children live abroad.

Alternatively, China may have sought to project its reach, or possibly to threaten Lai Ting-yu in order to have leverage over Taiwan’s president. Indeed, the idea that China might seek to kidnap the children of influential government officials in the course of an invasion, so as to blackmail political leaders during the turmoil of armed conflict, has occasionally been raised. This sort of political kidnapping is a plot thread that comes up in several episodes of “[Zero Day Attack,](https://nomanisanis.land/zero-day-attack-overall-review/)” the hit 2025 television show dramatizing a Chinese invasion.

Whatever the motive, according to the FBI, Zhang was working in coordination with Chinese handlers and demonstrated [signs of tradecraft](https://udn.com/news/story/6656/9796629) to cover her tracks, such as renting vehicles for several hours then returning them, or booking short-range flights with little notice. It is unclear how evidence of her activities was detected, but Zhang was arrested in October 2026 while attempting to board a flight to Shanghai.

The FBI did not comment on when Zhang was recruited, or her motivations, seeing as she lived in [a $6 million home](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wanying-heather-zhang-china-surveillance-arrest-los-angeles/) and handled real estate transactions that were in the millions. Though there have been reports of China increasingly recruiting “disposable” agents that are used temporarily and then cast aside, tradecraft by Zhang may indicate professional training.

The Taiwanese government has criticized such actions as Chinese transnational repression. This is not the first case occurring in the United States. [Individuals](https://www.justice.gov/usao-cdca/pr/political-operative-sentenced-4-years-federal-prison-acting-covert-agent-peoples) allegedly working for China’s government were arrested for surveilling Taiwan’s then-President Tsai Ing-wen’s travels in California in 2023. Reports indicate that Taiwanese government officials such as Joseph Wu were [surveilled](https://newbloommag.net/2021/10/31/wu-european-visit/) during past trips to Europe.

Most famously, news broke in June 2025 of [an attempt](https://thediplomat.com/2025/07/china-car-crash-plan-targeting-hsiao-bi-khim-shocks-taiwan/) by the Chinese military attaché in Prague to ram a vehicle into the motorcad

content: 维权网 2026-10-15 特约评论员：楚江风 2026年10月14日，原湖北钟祥市税务局干部、独立作家周远志，因突发心脏病骤然离世，终年65岁。消息来得十分仓促，汉江故土之上，一位敢于直面现实、在重压下坚守至最后一刻的写作者，就此离开了这个世界。 前半生置身体制，周远志曾出任钟祥市城区税务局副局长，多年的税务工作让他真切触摸到基层社会的真实肌理。当不少亲历者选择将体制内的名利博弈与权力幽暗藏于心底时，他却不愿意附和世俗的圆滑。早在上世纪90年代，他就因向境外媒体投稿曝光体制积弊而被撤销官职；2008年，他又因撰写官员腐败与人权文章被国安局以“涉嫌煽动颠覆国家政权罪”抓捕。他用一生的起落证明，脱离公职之后的他，才真正找到了一支拒绝粉饰和虚美的、属于独立写作者的笔。 作为独立中文笔会会员，周远志的目光始终冰冷而炙热。一部分笔墨，他以“曾仁全”、“华梁兴”为笔名，剖析仕途之中的欲望沉浮与政治纠葛；另一部分，他则投向了社会的边缘与最底层，其最具代表性的长篇小说《浑浊的婉儿河》（又名《一个坐台小姐日记》）便是最具风骨的见证。在这部作品中，他正视了那些被主流目光漠视的弱势女性工作者角色的困顿与命运。他不去做道德上简单的评判，只是用如手术刀般的文字，忠实地记录下夹缝之中普通人的苦难与挣扎。 然而，秉笔直书的代价，是伴随他大半生的铁窗与高墙。2017年11月，他因参与维权及发表批判性文章再度遭遇抓捕。2019年6月，湖北荆门掇刀法院对他进行了秘密宣判：以“组织非法聚集罪”判刑2年、“网上寻衅滋事罪”判刑3年、“诽谤罪”判刑1年6个月，数罪并罚，强行合并执行有期徒刑4年6个月。在这场漫长的文字狱里，他被剥夺了本该属于公民的言论自由，甚至在2020年狱中病危、查出严重心脏瘤并面临生命危险时，家属为其申请的保外就医也遭到了无情的拒绝。 直至2022年5月刑满获释，漫长的铁窗岁月已将他的身体彻底摧残。出狱后的他陷入了贫病交加的绝境，甚至连本该享有的退休养老与医疗待遇也被全部剥夺。而就在2023年，仅因在网上转发了有关水灾的社会帖文，他再度遭遇国安强行带走并处以行政拘留。长期身处这种无孔不入的监控环境，他内心始终保持着一份警惕。平日里闭门在家专心致志制作视频的他，和朋友通电话、发语音时常常提心提吊胆，深感随时处于别人的注视之下。这份如影随形的戒备，与10月4日后他世界里那场突如其来的寂静，成为了横在他生命最后阶段最残残忍的枷锁。 现实生活里的周远志，自带一份侠气。很多普通群众在维权路上陷入困境，求助无门之时，总会通过各种渠道辗转找到他。只要确属弱者蒙冤，他便耗费自己的时间与心力帮普通人梳理事实、代为发声。他心里清楚，每一次站出来，都有可能给自己招来新的困扰，可内心的道义，让他没有办法选择回避。笔是他的武器，仗义，是他一生恪守的底色。 回望这一生，写作要抵御外界施加的压力，助人发声要承担额外的风险，个人的道路几经起落。纵然周遭风声不断，该写的文字，他没有搁置；该伸出的援手，他也不曾收回。 现在，陪伴他半生的那支笔，永远停下了。汉江水依旧滔滔不绝，郢中的市井烟火照常流转，只是这片土地上，少了这样一支敢于向现实发问的笔，少了一个愿意替沉默者说话的人。 “真的猛士，敢于直面惨淡的人生。”肉身终会归于尘土，但他用尽自己的方式，为底层的声音留下过印记。人们会记得，曾经有这样一个普通人，不趋时，不避祸，在没有任何恐惧、任何窃听的彼岸，他的风骨永存。 先生，安息。

content: 追光者  2026-10-15 【致不屈的靈魂｜《唯紅花綻放》作者馮哲芸專訪 感動港人在高壓下的堅定與韌性】 今年7月，香港兩間獨立書店「留下書舍」和「田園書屋」遭搜查，涉事 書籍包括《唯紅花綻放》。一本書，可以如何「煽動」？作者馮哲芸（Emily Feng）在2019年前往返北京和香港報道，接受《追光者》專訪時說：「去香港總像是進入了另一個世界」。看到書店遭查，她不諱言「真的不知道」書煽動了甚麼，但看到香港人關心書店和言論自由，就感慨「即使他們現時無法在公共空間聚集並定期公開表達，人們依然有一種韌性與堅定去維持本真、做他們自己」。 《唯紅花綻放：習近平時代的認同與歸屬》是一本關於身份認同的書，書中的人物歷經磨難，對自己的身份認同有掙扎過，也失落過。現任NPR（美國全國公共廣播電台）駐華府記者馮哲芸在書中寫道，幾年前往返中國與香港報道時，在機場遇到的海關人員跟她說，即使在海外長大，「本質」仍是中國人，應透過報道「說好中國故事」。隨後幾年，她被官方貼上「民族叛徒」標籤，被指勾結境外敵對勢力。她在2022年被中國拒絕入境後，就開始寫這本書。 一個維權律師、震驚社會的鐵鍊女、一個流亡異鄉的維吾爾父親，乃至「銅鑼灣書店」店長林榮基和流亡海外的香港人，在習近平治下的年代，人們到底如何生活，一個只容許紅花綻放的國度，不屈的生存着，已是一件不容易的事。哪怕只是有尊嚴地賣書、讀書，也成為了一種難以言喻的艱辛。 在中國報道多年，馮哲芸對這片土地上的人的身份認同最感興趣，「因為它是人們行為背後的核心原因，它塑造了社群，塑造了我們的動機，也塑造了政策」。她觀察到，人們往往透過身份認同進行反抗，建立屬於自己的社群和身份，而身份認同的定義相當廣泛，可以是政治身份、性別身份，或是民族與語言身份。 ｜採訪香港抗爭者：非常直接和敢言的社會 很欣賞 書中有幾個章節的人物，都是香港人，除了賣書的林榮基，還有2019年的抗爭者，和坐船離開香港的逃亡者。2019年，馮哲芸剛好在NPR擔任駐中國記者，頻繁往返北京和香港，每個周末都飛到香港報道，「去香港總像是進入了另一個世界」，她笑言不敢自稱是香港問題專家，沒有在香港工作或生活過，但認為香港是一個很有意思的對照，「讓人理解中國『是甚麼』或『不是甚麼』」。 書中其他章節都是獨立的人物，然而關於香港的三章，卻隱約有着互相串聯的地方，「因為香港的故事是全球性的，我在香港遇到的人最終可能去了台灣或美國」。她更說自己在中國採訪時，總有些被訪者是啟發自香港的抗爭運動，從而影響他們在中國的行動。 2019年的採訪已是7年前的事，跟進採訪也已過了4、5年，她對香港的印象，就是一個「非常直接和敢言的社會」，「這是我很欣賞的」。而報道香港時最令她感到衝擊的，是每當從北京到達香港，就是從一個言論受到極其嚴格控制的城巿，突然身處一個喧鬧的示威現場。那種對比令她相當震驚，這也是香港引人入勝的地方，「讓我如此熱愛報道這場示威的原因，就是想去理解是甚麼驅使這些人，這不是突然出現一條法例的草案把大家帶上街頭，背後必然有多年積怨的沉澱」。 ｜感動港人關心書籍：人們依然有一種韌性與堅定去維持本真 7年過去，她把那時遇到的人們寫下來，而這本書卻成為了「煽動刊物」，賣書的店員被捕、書店被迫關閉，到底對香港政府來說，這本書為何如此敏感？又煽動了甚麼？馮哲芸輕輕搖頭：「我真的不知道」。但她承認，此書不是對中國目前政治治理「歌功頌德」，但同時亦不認為它是一本特別激進或帶有強烈社運色彩的書，「我只是有話直說，不會迴避我發現的任何事實。但我當然知道關於維吾爾族、新疆以及香港示威的報道在中國大陸變得極其敏感」。 然而，書中探討的身份認同問題，或者正好揭開中共的傷疤。「他們認為如果操控（身份認同）得當能鞏固執政，但如果失去控制，對國家政權來說將會非常危險。」 2019年年底後，她再也沒有去過香港了，那是《國安法》實施前，也沒有跟被訪的香港人聯繫。幾個月前得悉書籍被港府查抄的消息，甚至成為針對獨立書店店主和店員的調查一部分時，她好像不得不重新審視過去在中國的報道，被拒絕入境已有4年，「當我在不自願的情況下離開中國時，我非常想回去，但我回不去了」。 不能回到中國和香港，但她依然想跟香港人說：「港人關心書籍、關心書店經營者，仍關心言論自由，讓我非常感動。」當看見書店店員被扣上手銬帶上警車時的昂首闊步，讓她更了解香港人有獨立思考能力，擁有自己的價值觀和想法，「即使他們現時無法在公共空間聚集並定期公開表達，人們依然有一種韌性與堅定去維持本真、做他們自己」。 她的新作《為故土焚心：敘利亞戰場上的維吾爾人》（Our Hearts Burned for Home: Uyghur Militants in Syria’s Civil War）已出版，描繪數千名維吾爾人，因在新疆被壓迫和敘利亞內戰，而遠赴他鄉，新書揭示北京的嚴密監視與文化抹殺，如何將整整一代人推向流亡，並影響中東局勢。

title: 中欧脱钩加速

content: 艾地声Edysen   X @KA594594 · Oct 11, 2026 中欧脱钩加速 德国联邦议院委托成立的“中国委员会”近日发布首份半年度报告，认为德国对华经济安全状况总体趋于恶化，供应链依赖仍在加深，并建议欧盟准备更有力的贸易政策工具，以应对中国在贸易争端中可能采取的升级措施。报告尤其引人注目的一句话，是将中国同时定位为“合作伙伴、竞争对手和制度性对手”的既有战略已经失败。 几乎与此同时，欧洲议会以454票赞成、86票反对、110票弃权，通过关于欧中关系的政策建议。决议一方面继续主张同中国保持对话，另一方面要求在关键原材料、医药、电池、电动汽车、通信、半导体等战略部门全面降低依赖，强化投资审查、技术保护和贸易反制。 德国报告与欧洲议会决议前后呼应，传递出一个越来越清楚的信号：中欧关系虽然还没有走向全面脱钩，却正在进入制度性、选择性脱钩加速的阶段。 一、德国转向具有风向标意义 欧洲对华政策的变化并非始于今日。2019年，欧盟已经用“合作伙伴、谈判伙伴、经济竞争者和制度性对手”几种不同身份定义中国；俄乌战争以后，“去风险”又逐渐成为布鲁塞尔的政策关键词。 但德国的变化仍然具有特殊意义。过去二十多年，德国是欧洲对华接触政策最重要的经济支柱。默克尔时代形成了一套看似互利的分工：中国向欧洲提供低成本商品、完整供应链和不断扩大的市场，德国则向中国出售汽车、机械设备和化工产品。德国企业在中国获得利润，中国也通过德国技术、资本和工业管理经验实现产业升级。 这套模式建立在两个假设之上：第一，经贸融合可以促使中国逐渐接受国际规则；第二，中国主要是德国工业的市场和生产基地，而不是足以替代德国制造的竞争者。 如今，这两个假设都在瓦解，中共并未因加入全球市场而走向政治开放。习近平时代的中国反而加强党对企业、资本和社会的控制，并越来越多地把经贸关系、市场准入和关键原材料转化为国家战略工具。与此同时，中国已不再满足于承接欧洲产业转移，而是在电动车、机械、化工、光伏、电池、轨道交通和数字技术等领域直接进入德国工业腹地。 德国面对的因而不再只是“如何在中国赚钱”，而是德国工业是否可能被中国制造逐步替代。联邦议院成立审查德中安全相关经济关系的专门委员会，意味着德国已经把对华经贸从企业利润问题提升为国家安全问题。未来，价值链、能源、原材料、港口、物流和关键基础设施，都可能接受更严格的政治与安全审查。 需要说明的是，专家委员会的报告不等于德国政府已经正式废除对华“三重定位”。但它正在为德国下一阶段的政策转向提供知识准备和立法依据。当欧洲最依赖中国市场、也最信奉自由贸易的工业大国开始讨论反制能力，中欧关系的性质便已经发生改变。 二、“去风险”正在产生脱钩效果 欧盟仍然反复强调，对华政策是“去风险，而不是脱钩”。这一表述既反映了现实约束，也是一种政治修辞。中欧年贸易规模巨大，中国是欧洲重要商品来源地，欧洲则是中国最重要的出口市场之一。欧洲需要中国的稀土、永磁材料、电池、光伏组件和工业中间品；中国也需要欧洲的高端设备、技术、资本和消费市场。像冷战时期美苏那样全面切断经济联系，既不现实，也会造成双方难以承受的成本。 问题在于，“去风险”涵盖的范围正在不断扩大。最初被列入安全审查的主要是5G、电信设备和军民两用技术，后来扩展到芯片、人工智能、数据、港口和基础设施，如今又延伸到电动车、电池、光伏、医药、钢铁、化工、关键矿产乃至政府采购。当一个经济体最具战略价值和增长潜力的产业都被纳入安全边界，“去风险”在累积效果上就会越来越接近局部脱钩。 过去的欧盟主要针对某一种中国商品进行反倾销调查；现在则开始建立包括反补贴关税、外国补贴审查、外资审查、出口管制、政府采购限制、强迫劳动产品禁令、本地成分要求和反经济胁迫工具在内的完整经济安全体系。 这意味着欧洲不再只是判断某一批中国商品是否构成倾销，而是在重新规定中国资本、企业、技术和产品进入欧洲经济体系的条件。可以说，欧洲在语言上仍然拒绝脱钩，在制度上却正在建设脱钩能力。 三、从产业互补走向正面竞争 中欧矛盾迅速加深的根本原因，是双方的产业关系已经从互补转向竞争。第一次“中国冲击”主要冲击欧洲的纺织、鞋类和低端消费品制造。欧洲能够接受这种代价，因为中国生产廉价商品，德国、法国和意大利则向中国出售汽车、飞机、机械、奢侈品和化工产品。欧洲消费者得到低价商品，欧洲大型企业获得中国市场，经济全球化因而具备广泛的利益联盟。 如今的“第二次中国冲击”完全不同。中国出口的不再只是衬衫、玩具和日用品，而是电动车、电池、工业机器人、工程机械、化工产品和新能源设备。这些产品直接挑战欧洲最重要的工业部门。特别是在美国不断提高对华关税、限制中国商品进入之后，中国庞大的工业产能更多转向欧洲，使欧洲成为承受中国产能外溢压力的主要市场。 中国2025年的全球贸易顺差已经超过1.2万亿美元。2026年第二季度，欧盟对华贸易逆差达到1033亿欧元。问题不只是逆差规模，而是欧洲出口中国的传统优势产品正在失去市场，中国对欧洲出口却迅速向高技术、高附加值领域升级。 对德国而言，这几乎是一场工业模式危机。德国过去依靠俄罗斯廉价能源、中国巨大市场和美国安全保护维持繁荣。俄乌战争切断了第一项条件，中美战略竞争动摇了第二项条件，美国政策的不确定性又削弱了第三项条件。如今中国企业在汽车和机械领域迎头赶上，德国工业赖以生存的外部环境已经不复存在。 因此，欧洲政策转硬既有地缘政治因素，也有十分现实的产业自救成分。所谓“经济安全”，背后首先是就业、工厂、税收以及欧洲能否继续保持工业文明的问题。 四、中共也在推动脱钩 中欧关系恶化不能仅仅归因于欧洲保护主义。事实上，中共同样在主动建设一套对西方的“去风险”体系。从“中国制造2025”到科技自立自强，从国产替代到关键技术攻关，从数据安全审查到稀土和关键材料出口管制，中国一直在降低对西方技术和市场的脆弱性。中国要求外国企业转让技术、扩大本地生产，同时通过补贴、信贷和政府采购扶植本国企业；一旦本土企业具备替代能力，外国企业原有的市场空间便会受到挤压。 换言之，欧洲担忧中国把经济依赖武器化，中共也担忧美国及其盟友利用技术、金融和市场优势实施封锁。双方都在以国家安全名义重组经济体系。这形成了一个自我强化的循环：欧洲越担心中国控制供应链，就越加强审查和限制；中共越担心西方围堵，就越推进自主替代和资源管制；中共的反制又进一步证明欧洲关于依赖风险的判断。“去风险”于是从单方面政策变成双向行为，最终推动两个经济体系逐步分层。 五、脱钩不是直线，也不等于断交 就在欧洲议会通过强硬决议、德国专家委员会发出警告之际，中欧贸易代表又达成一项初步安排：中国可能在未来数年减少对欧洲的电动及插电式混合动力汽车出口，欧方则争取中国改善稀土出口许可，并降低部分欧洲商品进入中国市场的门槛。这一安排仍需欧盟成员国认可，但至少说明双方都希望避免贸易战完全失控。 这恰恰揭示了未来中欧关系的基本形态：不是简单地从合作走向断交，而是在施压、谈判、交换和继续设防之间反复摆动。欧洲不会放弃中国市场，却会努力降低关键依赖；不会禁止所有中国投资，却会把中国资本排除在部分核心基础设施之外；不会停止政治对话，却会降低通过对话改变中国的期待；不会在所有问题上追随美国，却会在科技、安全和供应链领域逐渐向美国靠拢。 中共则会继续利用欧洲对美国战略自主的追求，尽量防止欧美形成完全一致的对华阵线；同时以稀土、市场准入和在华投资作为谈判筹码，争取为中国企业保留欧洲市场。中欧贸易总额可能在相当长时间内仍然庞大，甚至在某些年份继续增长。但是，贸易规模已经不足以说明关系是否健康。即使商品仍在流动，技术体系、投资规则、数据网络、供应链和战略产业也可能已经开始分离。 六、从接触时代进入“冷和平经济” 过去四十年的中欧关系，基本建立在一个自由主义信念之上：经济相互依赖能够抑制政治冲突，全球市场最终会使不同制度趋同。如今，欧洲正在放弃这种乐观主义。它越来越相信，相互依赖不仅能够创造和平，也可能制造脆弱；贸易不仅能够增加财富，也可能成为权力工具；市场无法自动消解制度冲突，反而可能被强大的国家机器利用。这也是德国报告所谓“三重定位失败”的真正含义。失败的不是一句外交术语，是一整套通过经贸接触改变中国的历史设想。中国仍然可以在气候、贸易和全球治理方面成为合作伙伴，但“伙伴”已经不足以平衡“竞争者”和“制度性对手”所带来的压力。 未来三至五年，中欧大概不会全面脱钩，却会形成一种新的“冷和平经济”：有贸易而少信任，有谈判而多防备，有局部合作，也始终为冲突预留工具。如果台海维持和平，这一过程仍可能被控制在产业与技术层面；一旦台海发生战争或封锁，今天正在准备的投资审查、出口管制、金融制裁和供应链替代机制，就可能迅速转化为真正的经济脱钩。 所以，中欧脱钩不是未来才会到来的一个事件，是已经展开的一段过程。它不会以一纸宣言突然完成，而会通过一次次产业审查、一项项贸易限制、一条条供应链转移和一轮轮企业撤资逐步累积。 中欧经济全球化的黄金时代已经结束。双方尚未进入冷战，却已走出接触时代。德国的转向表明，这一变化不再只是布鲁塞尔的政治表态，而正在深入欧洲最核心的工业国家，进入立法、产业和国家安全体系。值得关注的，已不是欧洲是否仍然使用“脱钩”这个词，是被纳入“安全”名义的领域还会扩大到什么程度。当安全边界不断扩张，所谓去风险，最终就可能成为一场没有正式宣布的脱钩。

title: 一真溅雪：廿世纪改变人类历史进程的伟人

content: 重发前言：本文已写就一十五年了，今天重读此文，仍深感该文对当今的世界，和当今的中国大陆仍具现实意义，故决定重发。 在人类有文字记载的将近七千年的漫漫历史长河中，廿世纪是最值得历史学家浓墨重彩地大书特书一翻的一个世纪。这是一个各种思潮、思想风起云涌的世纪;这是一个各式各样的革命此起彼伏的世纪；这是一个各种大、小战乱频乃(其中包括两次在规模上和给人类造成的破坏和伤亡上都堪称史无前例的世界大战)的世纪;这是一个科学技术、生产力和社会财富飞速发展的世纪(这一个世纪所取得的科学技术成就、生产力的巨大进步和所创造的社会财富，都超过了人类社会在此之前在这些方面所取得的成就总和的数百乃至数千倍);这 是一个科学技术的进步带来的生产力和生产方式的改变和迅猛发展，给人类的思想、生活方式、社会结构、人与人、国家与国家之间的关系带来无法逆料的巨大变化的世纪；这是一个由科学技术的突飞猛进和生产方式、生产能力的高速而巨大的发展，给人类走向更加美好的未来带来了巨大的希望、同时又把人类带进由环保灾难和可能发生可怕的核大战、核泄漏而使人类陷入自我毁灭的深渊的世纪;这是一个给人类带来无穷苦难的乱世枭雄和引导人类走向和平、民主、繁荣昌盛的历史伟人同时登上历史舞台的世纪。前者如列宁、斯大林、毛泽东、希特勒……这些给世界和本国人民精神上、肉体上、生活上带来史无前例的巨大灾难的独裁暴君(本文暂不谈这些人渣)。后者如独具远见卓识的丘吉尔、撒切尔夫人、罗斯福、英年早逝的肯尼迪、里根以及最近的戈尔巴乔夫等。 首先来看一下丘吉尔，他在给廿世纪人类带来深重灾难的两场政治运动:一九一七年发生的俄国十月革命建立的苏维埃极权政权，和上世纪廿年代末德国希特勒领导的纳粹主义运动的兴起之初，便以其敏锐、深邃的政治眼光，准确地预见到这两场政治运动(或称之为“革命”)将给全世界带来的无穷无尽的巨大灾难。 是他在苏联十月革命建立苏维埃政权之初，便向英国议会也是向全世界大声疾呼:“要将苏维埃政权扼杀在襁褓之中”；是他在上世纪三十年代初，希特勒纳粹党上台之初，又向英国议会和全世界大声疾呼:“希特勒的纳粹德国将给全世界带来战争和灾难”。极力反对张伯伦(英国首相)和达拉第(法国总理)对纳粹德国采取的绥靖政策；是他主张英、法联合对纳粹德国采取强硬态度。 世界局势的发展不幸都被他言中。是他在极其困难的条件下上台，以他的睿智和坚忍不拔的顽强精神领导英国人民联合世界反法西斯同盟国，战胜德、意、日法西斯，把世界从德、意、日法西斯的铁蹄之下拯救出来。 美国的富兰克林．罗斯福总统也是后者之中的杰出代表，他在迄今为止全世界最大的经济危机期间的一九三二年当选美国总统，上台后，立即实施一系列的振兴美国经济的计划(世人称之为罗斯福新政)。在全国大力开展基础设施的建设(如兴修铁路、公路、高速公路、水坝……等)，以带动美国的钢铁、运输、建材、汽车、采矿、冶金、化工等行业的快速发展，成功地解决了大批失业工人的就业问题，迅速带领美国走出世界最大经济危机的阴影，使美国迅速走向复兴和高速发展的道路，为二次世界大战战胜德、意、日法西斯奠定了强大的物质基础。 二次世界大战暴发后，他预见到德、意、日法西斯危害的不仅仅是欧洲、亚洲、非洲而是全世界，就连远隔大西洋、太平洋的美国和美洲国家都不能幸免。他以极其巧妙的手法，引导美国人民摆脱“孤立主义”的束缚，领导美国人民投入世界反法西斯战争，以美国举世无双的巨大的政治、经济、军事、科学和技术实力为世界反法西斯战争的胜利做出了无与伦比的巨大贡献。
