title: Takaichi’s history remarks aim to smooth the path to a meeting with Xi, Taiwanese expert says
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory sig
content:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory signal to Beijing as Tokyo seeks a meeting between Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) in November.
**Murayama Statement**

Asked about her views on history at a House of Councillors Budget Committee meeting on Oct. 16, Takaichi [said](https://tchina.kyodonews.net/articles/-/14976?words=%E6%9D%91%E5%B1%B1%E8%AB%87%E8%A9%B1) that, as stated in the 70th-anniversary statement marking the end of World War II, the positions of successive Japanese Cabinets would remain unchanged under her administration.

She said this included the 1995 Murayama Statement, issued on Aug. 15 that year by then Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama.

The statement was the first in which the Japanese government officially acknowledged that Japan’s wartime aggression and colonial rule caused great damage and suffering in Asian countries, and expressed deep remorse and heartfelt apology.

 Chinese President Xi Jinping meets Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, on the afternoon of Oct. 31, 2025. (Ministry of Foreign Affairs PRC)

**A conciliatory signal?**
This year’s APEC summit will be held in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18–19. Whether Xi and Takaichi will meet during the summit has drawn attention.

Takaichi [confirmed](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/10/18/japan/politics/takaichi-china-apec-parliament/) plans to attend the China-hosted APEC leaders' summit pending Diet clearance, signaling a readiness to engage Beijing in person despite deeply strained bilateral ties.

Kuo

Yu~~-~~jen (郭育仁), director of the Institute of China and Asia-Pacific Studies at National Sun Yat-sen University, told TCN that Japan was working to arrange a meeting between the two leaders. Takaichi’s pledge to uphold the Murayama Statement ahead of APEC, he said, was a gesture of goodwill toward Beijing.
Given Beijing’s recent posture, a formal bilateral meeting remains improbable, Kuo said, suggesting that any encounter would likely be choreographed as a "chance meeting" in the corridors.

Should no interaction take place at all, he said, it would signal that already strained Tokyo-Beijing relations are continuing to deteriorate.

**A Taiwan contingency is a Japan contingency**

In November 2025, Takaichi told Japan’s House of Representatives that a Chinese armed assault on Taiwan—such as a naval blockade enforced with military force—could be deemed a "survival-threatening situation" under Japanese security laws. Such a determination, she noted, could legally permit the Self-Defense Forces to exercise limited collective self-defense, provided other legal requirements were met.

Beijing responded with retaliatory measures, cooling cultural exchanges, dampening outbound tourism to Japan, re-imposing a ban on Japanese seafood, and restricting exports of dual-use goods to Japanese military users and for military uses, including uses that contribute to Japan’s military capabilities. China’s dual-use control list covers roughly 1,100 items, including critical minerals such as rare earths, gallium, and germanium.

Kuo said Takaichi’s commitment to the Murayama Statement did not mean she was retracting her “Taiwan contingency, Japan contingency” remarks, adding that the two issues were unrelated.

Pointing to enduring structural rifts over history, the disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) Islands, and cross-strait issues, Kuo noted that Takaichi previously stated in parliament that Tokyo refrains from commenting on Taiwan's status under international law because Japan has renounced sovereignty over the island.

Kuo said the remarks indirectly touched on the “undetermined status of Taiwan” theory, which Beijing opposes, but should not be conflated with Takaichi’s earlier comments about a Taiwan contingency.

 A China Coast Guard officer observes the Diaoyu Islands from aboard a patrol vessel. (CCG)

**Xi-Takaichi meeting could signal easing tensions**
Kuo said a meeting between Xi and Takaichi at APEC was unlikely, but that Beijing also had an interest in easing tensions with Tokyo amid the current international environment.

Kuo pointed out that,ahead of Japan’s year-end revisions to its National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program, the Japan Innovation Party has called for the blueprints to endorse nuclear-powered submarines and create an exception to Tokyo's Three Non-Nuclear Principles to permit US nuclear-armed assets entry during contingencies.

Pointing out that the APEC summit coincides with coalition-level preparations to deliver defense recommendations to Takaichi, Kuo noted that Tokyo could deploy flexible terminology like "consider" in the revised security documents to retain strategic room for maneuver.

While such defense debates risk antagonizing Beijing, they could paradoxically create openings for renewed bilateral dialogue, Kuo argued. Tokyo’s public discourse on nuclear-powered submarines and potential exemptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles may function as a calculated form of strategic signaling toward China, he added.

Beyond the defense document updates, Kuo noted, Takaichi has set her sights on a major constitutional overhaul next year. The four-point reform agenda targets enshrining the legal status of the Self-Defense Forces in pacifist Article 9, creating executive emergency authorities during national crises, ending merged House of Councillors constituencies to ensure representation for each prefecture, and improving educational access.

Kuo said China would not want Japan to revise Article 9 and might therefore seek to coordinate with Tokyo on the matter.

**Japan-Taiwan security cooperation**

Regardless of whether Tokyo and Beijing break the ice on the sidelines of APEC, the direct military threat China poses to Japan remains fundamentally unaltered, Kuo said.

Looking ahead, he predicted that Japan’s updated security documents, due by year-end, will define its stance on security cooperation with Taiwan with unprecedented clarity.

Even if Japan-China relations ease temporarily, Kuo said, Takaichi is unlikely to change her policy toward Taiwan and remains strongly inclined to advance security cooperation with the island.

 In April 2025, Japanese lawmaker Sanae Takaichi led a delegation to visit Taiwan and posed for a photo with Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍). (MOFA Facebook)

**Taiwan should proceed cautiously**
Kuo said a substantive improvement in Japan-China relations would be difficult under Takaichi’s administration.

Since November last year, he said, China has restricted group travel to Japan and rare-earth supplies, sought to court Japanese opposition parties and factions outside the mainstream of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, and criticized Takaichi in international forums, putting pressure on her.

Despite Takaichi’s push to deepen economic, technological, and defense alignment with Taiwan, Kuo noted she remains constrained at home by pushback from career diplomats, business interests, opposition parties, and rival ruling-party factions.

Takaichi remains exceedingly unlikely to walk back her statements regarding a Taiwan contingency, Kuo noted. Given the resulting pressure from Beijing and domestic critics, cultivating a close, steadfast rapport with US President Donald Trump has become paramount to underwriting her security agenda, Kuo added.

Kuo urged Taipei to recognize the practical constraints shaping Japan’s cross-strait policy, noting that bilateral cooperation has traditionally advanced most effectively out of the public eye.

Taiwan should respect Tokyo’s appetite for discretion rather than pressing for high-profile diplomatic milestones, allowing practical partnerships to develop steadily beneath the political radar, Kuo added.

title: South Africa’s digital ID system and green book phase-out
summary: _“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://ww
content:
_“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-05-28-digital-dispatch-from-estonia-the-egovernance-capital-of-the-world/)_is card-based ... what we are doing is now made in a purely digital format that’s on your smartphone.”_

That was the explanation Lohan Spies, founder of DIDx, gave when Daily Maverick asked his views on the cooperation between Estonia and South Africa in this digital public infrastructure (DPI) journey.

You can trust him because DIDx is, by its own admission in the bio the company’s PR sent over ahead of our meeting in Techno Park, “a technology-based business that builds Africa’s trusted digital identity and payments infrastructure”.

Spies, a cybersecurity veteran who was building with blockchain before it was cool, founded the company in 2019 and established it as the continent’s most experienced builder of decentralised identity infrastructure.

He also shares Communications Minister Solly Malatsi’s sentiment that Estonia is “a reference point for a lot of DPI development that is happening, and there’s nothing wrong with observing best practice and how it can be useful for our context”.

Spies independently confirmed the minister’s claims that what we are building in South Africa is “not just a cut and paste … because the environments are different, and societal digital skills proficiency is also different”.

Someone [owes the Estonian ambassador an apology](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-23-estonian-echoes-sas-digital-public-infrastructure-looks-like-it-was-made-in-estonia/).

### **Show, don’t tell**

South Africa is undergoing a comprehensive digital migration designed to overhaul how civil registration, national security and public service delivery function. It’s anchored by the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) strategy for 2025-2030, with the primary objective of transitioning from an inefficient, paper-heavy legacy system into a digital-first organisation under the banner of “Home Affairs @ home”.

This transformation leverages the DPI infrastructure of a secure digital identity framework, an automated risk engine, data-exchange channels and mobile credentials to grant every South African secure identity authentication from smartphone devices or partner facilities.

According to Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber, “digital IDs enable instant, paperless processing for banking, work visas and business registrations through an automated risk engine, eliminating months of administrative delays”.

That DHA Strategic Plan reveals that attracting highly skilled workers and streamlining access to work visas can significantly boost economic output; bringing in 11,000 skilled workers annually adds 1.2% to annual GDP growth, while a 10% increase in tourism (through a digitised travel visa system) adds 0.6% to GDP.

And before we start marching (and marching), a digitally authenticated population register linked to the automated biometric identification system prevents illicit entries, fraudulent citizenship acquisition and internal collusion.

When demonstrating the live working prototype using his personal record on the population register, Schreiber emphasised that digital credentials would restore transparency and dignity.

He also confirmed that “on the 31st of March 2028 the Green ID book will officially cease to be recognised as a valid form of identification in terms of section 251B of the Identification Act”.

### **All the pieces clicking together**

Addressing GovTech on behalf of the Presidency’s Digital Services Unit within Operation Vulindlela, Kule Duma detailed the foundational mechanics of South Africa’s Digital Transformation Roadmap.

> “The experience of someone going to a government office is often layered by bureaucracy... They often must borrow money as a first stop, or they must use the very grants that we pay them ... jump on two or three taxis ... get into that long line and at the end they’re told you don’t have the sufficient documentation... We know that we can bring digital services to the tip of people’s fingers.”

He also articulated the central solution: “How should one person experience this one government and one government service ... if I provide government my information once, you shouldn’t have to ask me for that information ... that is the way that we drive it through the data exchange.”

Kule Duma on stage at GovTech 2026. (Photo: Lindsey Schutters)

Spies explained the details as best he understands them – DIDx is doing work in an SA Revenue Service skunkworks project, but his experience of these systems bridges the gap.erv

“DHA will be an issuer, and DHA will issue me with my verifiable credential in [mDoc format](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/digital-identities-getting-know-verifiable-digital-credential-0),” he says. “Once I then issue that credential to the holder, which is me, the citizen, that then lives in my mobile device, and on the mobile device we make use of the secure enclave on the device. So we make use of what the OEM manufacturer provides us ... to protect the private keys.”

It’s simple, actually, and Schreiber’s demo, erm … demonstrated it perfectly. “In that demo, the reality is they actually move the data by Bluetooth phone to phone,” Spies points out.

“So there’s no third party involved in that at all ... the security there is literally in proximity. It’s directly Bluetooth phone to phone ... you can be completely offline and I can share my credentials.”

### **Goodbye, green mamba**

The paper-based green ID book lacks modern cryptographic security and embedded biometrics. It is easily forged, altered, or duplicated by criminal syndicates, making it the primary vehicle for identity theft and impersonation.

Green ID books also cannot support automated online authentication, remote Know-Your-Customer checks for banks, or digital wallet credentials required for e-commerce and integrated public services.

The solutions being built like Schreiber’s Home Affairs @ home and the Presidency’s MyMzansi app propose a world where citizens can request, renew or authenticate civic identity products (IDs, birth/marriage certificates, passports) online using facial recognition on a mobile phone or computer, with physical cards delivered directly to their doorstep.

The green South African ID book is being phased out in favour of a digital ID system. (Photo: trying2 [adult.com](http://adult.com/) / Wikipedia)

By transferring routine transactions to digital self-service channels, we no longer lose full working days or pay transport costs standing in the queue at Home Affairs offices.

And all that is built on the foundation of a digital ID that anchors the experience with state platforms, including tax compliance with the SA Revenue Service, social grant distribution through Sassa, healthcare records and digital payment systems.

And the future is being built by South Africans. **DM**

title: Taiwan security agency flags rise in Chinese disinformation ahead of local elections
zh_title: 台湾安全机构在地方选举前警告中国虚假信息增多
summary: 这张插图中可以看到中国和台湾国旗，摄于 2022 年 8 月 6 日。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration [购买许可权，打开新的选项卡](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/illustration-shows-chinese-and-taiwanese-flags/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjI6bmV3c21sX1JDMjFSVjlIMlpBQw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead) *摘要* 台湾将于下个月底举行地方选举 * 中国否认干涉台湾选举 * 台湾称中国对其使用“灰色地带”策略 台北，10 月 21 日（路透社） - 中国散布超过 250 万条争议
content:
这张插图中可以看到中国和台湾国旗，摄于 2022 年 8 月 6 日。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration [购买许可权，打开新的标签](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/illustration-shows-chinese-and-taiwanese-flags/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjI6bmV3c21sX1JDMjFSVjlIMlpBQw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

* 总结

* 台湾下月底举行地方选举
* 中国否认干预台湾选举
* 台湾称中国对其使用“灰色地带”策略

路透台北 10 月 21 日 - 台湾最高情报机构表示，今年前 9 个月，中国在网上传播了超过 250 万条针对台湾的有争议或虚假的网络信息，指责北京在地方选举前加强行动。

台湾国家安全局在本周向立法者提交的一份报告中表示，此类信息在 2026 年前 9 个月增加了约 48%，从一年前的超过 169 万条增至超过 250 万条。

《错误信息监测》时事通讯汇集了国际错误信息叙述，并以“真还是假？”为主题。每个版本都有测验。 [此处注册。](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fbusiness%2Fmedia-telecom%2Ftaiwan-security-agency-flags-rise-chinese-disinformation-ahead-local-elections-2026-10-21%2F)
声明称，源自中国的内容重点关注能源、食品安全和国防政策，以及特定候选人的政纲和形象，试图影响台湾11月的市长和县长选举。

中国台湾事务办公室没有立即回应置评请求。北京不顾台湾的反对，将台湾视为自己的领土，此前曾否认干涉台湾选举或散布虚假信息。

台湾一再抱怨中国的“灰色地带”策略——从日常军事演习到网络攻击——而此时北京正在加大军事和政治压力，迫使台北接受其主权主张。

报告称，北京经常通过官方媒体编造故事，然后通过“网络巨魔大军”和公关公司放大这些故事，在台湾民众中挑拨离间。该公司表示，这些策略包括内容农场、人工智能生成的视频、虚假账户和协调一致的评论泛滥。

报告称：“中国扩大了人工智能技术的使用来操纵信息，试图影响选民的支持和选举结果。”

该局表示，中国正在利用人工智能技术收集有关台湾时事、候选人政策和民调数据的信息，以影响行动并扩大人工智能驱动的信息操纵，旨在“影响选民偏好和选举结果”。
该公司表示，这些消息主要在 Facebook、Threads、YouTube 和在线论坛等社交媒体平台上传播。

路透社与台北研究组织 IORG 进行的一项调查发现，中国官方媒体在信息战中越来越多地放大了台湾对执政的民进党的批评，其中包括与反对派国民党有联系的影响者和政客。

中国对台湾政府机构的网络攻击平均为 258 万次

【原文 English Original】
Chinese and Taiwanese flags are seen in this illustration, August 6, 2022. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/illustration-shows-chinese-and-taiwanese-flags/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjI6bmV3c21sX1JDMjFSVjlIMlpBQw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Taiwan to hold local elections late next month
*   China has denied interfering in Taiwan's elections
*   Taiwan says China using 'grey-zone' tactics against it

TAIPEI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - China spread more than 2.5 million pieces of disputed or false online ​information targeting Taiwan in the first nine months of this year, the island's top intelligence ‌agency said, accusing Beijing of stepping up operations ahead of local elections.

In a report to lawmakers this week, Taiwan's National Security Bureau said such information rose by about 48% in the first nine months of 2026 to more than 2.5 million ​items from more than 1.69 million a year earlier.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fbusiness%2Fmedia-telecom%2Ftaiwan-security-agency-flags-rise-chinese-disinformation-ahead-local-elections-2026-10-21%2F)

It said the China-originated content focused on energy, ​food security and defence policy, as well as the platforms and images of specific ⁠candidates, in an effort to influence Taiwan's elections for city mayors and county magistrates in November.

China's Taiwan Affairs ​Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Beijing, which views Taiwan as its own territory ​over the island's objections, has previously denied interfering in Taiwanese elections or spreading disinformation.

Taiwan has repeatedly complained about what it sees as China's "grey-zone" tactics - from daily military drills to cyberattacks - at a time when Beijing is ramping up military and political pressure ​to force Taipei to accept its sovereignty claims.

The report said Beijing often created narratives through official media ​outlets before amplifying them through "online troll armies" and public relations firms to sow discord among Taiwanese people. It said the tactics ‌included ⁠content farms, AI-generated videos, fake accounts and coordinated comment flooding.

"China has expanded the use of AI technology to manipulate information, seeking to influence voter support and election results," the report said.

China was using AI technology to gather information on Taiwanese current affairs, candidates' policies and polling data to shape influence operations and expand AI-driven information ​manipulation aimed at "affecting voter ​preferences and election outcomes," ⁠the bureau said.

It said the messages were mainly distributed on social media platforms including Facebook, Threads, YouTube and online forums.

Chinese state media have increasingly amplified Taiwanese critics of ​the ruling Democratic Progressive Party in an information war, including influencers and politicians ​linked to ⁠the opposition Kuomintang, a [Reuters investigation](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-turns-taiwans-own-voices-against-it-information-war-2026-04-17/) conducted with Taipei-based research group IORG found.

Chinese cyberattacks on Taiwanese government agencies averaged 2.58 million a day in the first nine months of 2026, with detected threats surging from June and reaching 185.6 ⁠million in ​July and 106.4 million in August, data from the National Security ​Bureau showed.

"It cannot be ruled out that this was advance intelligence-gathering and harassment preparation aimed at interfering in Taiwan's year-end 'nine-in-one' elections," the ​report said.

Reporting By Yimou Lee; Additional reporting by Ben Blanchard and Liz Lee in Beijing; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Yimou Lee is a Senior Correspondent for Reuters covering everything from Taiwan, including sensitive Taiwan-China relations, China's military aggression and Taiwan's key role as a global semiconductor powerhouse. A three-time SOPA award winner, his reporting from Hong Kong, China, Myanmar and Taiwan over the past decade includes Myanmar's crackdown on Rohingya Muslims, Hong Kong protests and Taiwan's battle against China's multifront campaigns to absorb the island.

# 亚太经合财长会议在港闭幕 共识是增协调以加强财金系统韧性 保区域稳定

一连两日的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）财长会议今(21日)午在港闭幕，主持会议的中国财长蓝佛安表示，各成员经济体在坦诚丶深入丶富有建设性的交流下，核准及发布今年APEC财长联合声明等文件，为亚太经济体深化财经合作明确方向和提供指引。他在一天半的会议期间，多次强调地缘冲突影响外溢扩散，各成员经济体应通过开放合作，共同应对挑战。

发表时间： 21/10/2026 - 10:34

 8 分钟 浏览时间

 APEC财长会议首次在香港举行，中国强调各与会者应加强合作应对经济挑战。 © 麦燕庭提供(政府新闻处图片)

 作者： [香港特约记者 麦燕庭](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%89%B9%E7%BA%A6%E8%AE%B0%E8%80%85-%E9%BA%A6%E7%87%95%E5%BA%AD/ "香港特约记者 麦燕庭")

广告

继续浏览后续

中国是今年亚太经合组织（APEC）的轮任主办国，首次在香港举行的APEC财长会议亦由中国财政部主办。蓝佛安今午在会议闭幕后联同财政部副部长廖岷丶APEC秘书处执行主任爱德华多·佩罗萨出席记者会，公布今年财长会议的成果。他表示，在各与会方共同努力下，会议顺利结束，取得一系列成果，圆满成功。

蓝佛安表示，各方在加强宏观经济政策沟通协调丶携手应对外部风险挑战等方面进一步凝聚共识，并在一天半的会议期间，形成两份专业领域成果文件，包括支持民生发展丶以投资於人推动亚太地区可持续增长的财政政策报告，以及亚太地区普惠金融创新实践案例，并总结APEC青年财经人才交流合作项目。他认为，项目获各与会方的高度肯定和支持。

他表示，各与会方均认同，要加强宏观经济政策的沟通和协调，增强财政金融系统的韧性，更好应对经济增长中的不确定性和不稳定性因素，维护区域经济金融稳定。他又提到，当前世界百年变局加速演进，国际形势变乱交织，APEC作为亚太地区主要经济合作平台，各与会方都认同，人工智能等新兴技术，有提升生产力和培育新增长动能的潜力，为亚太经济增长注入新的动力。

**会议共识：投资於人 提振内需**

在支持民生发展的财政政策方面，各方强调支持民生发展与投资於人，在促进家庭消费丶提振内需丶提高生产力方面发挥重要作用，同时亦要加强财经纪律，确保财政可持续性。

蓝佛安早于昨（20日）午的财长会议开幕致词时，已强调各经济体合作的重要。他指出，当前国际形势变乱交织，地缘冲突影响外溢，世界经济增长面临多重挑战，亚太作为全球经济增长引擎，肩负更大责任。

他又说，今年的APEC财经合作机制，中方提出四大议题，包括支持民生发展的财政政策丶数字基础设施融资丶因地制宜促进普惠金融发展丶促进APEC青年财经人才交流合作等，希望在相关议题取得共识。同时，面对人工智能等新一轮科技革命，各成员经济体应加强经济政策对话丶沟通与协调，防范负面外溢效应，维护区域经济金融稳定。

香港特首李家超和蓝佛安为APEC财长会欢迎晚宴主礼。李家超致辞时表示，APEC通过对话与合作，促进区域经济增长，改善人民生活，财长会在这一使命下扮演关键角色。他又说，APEC各成员就扩大金融服务普及性丶帮助年轻人在全球经济中成长等议题，寻求共同解决方案，建设更创新丶包容和有韧性的经济体，有关愿景亦与香港的发展目标不谋而合。

港府表示，香港会趁财长会议举办的机会，向各经济体充分彰显作为「超级联系人」的角色，并向与会者展示香港的发展成果，亦期望与会代表能亲身感受香港的独特魅力丶活力和发展机遇。

# 中国纪念台湾光复81周年与孙文160周年诞辰 被指企图操作两岸叙事

北京当局近年扩大对台统战，不仅将「台湾光复」立法化，中共领导人习近平更将亲自出席11月12日的孙文诞辰160周年大会，定调「孙文一生为促统」。国安官员分析，中国一系列活动主要在建构三大意图目标。

北京当局近年扩大对台统战，不仅将「台湾光复」立法化，中共领导人习近平更将亲自出席11月12日的孙文诞辰160周年大会，定调「孙文一生为促统」。

10月25日是台湾光复81周年，也是设立台湾光复纪念日一周年。国台办发言人张晗21日在记者会上介绍有关举办纪念活动，共同回顾全体中华儿女前仆后继，浴血奋战，实现抗战胜利和台湾光复的历史，凝聚推进祖国完全统一，实现中华民族伟大复兴的奋进力量。

另外，中国也将于11月举办孙中山先生诞辰160周年纪念活动，以此继承和发扬他维护国家统一、致力民族振兴的崇高精神风范。团结包括台湾同胞在内的全体中华儿女，坚决打击台独分裂，反对外来干涉，促进两岸交流融合。

《自由时报》报导，国安官员示警，北京正透过历史修正主义强行拼接二战史料，企图藉由「尊孙」伪造继承中华民国法统的假象，借此争夺历史诠释权、补强并吞台湾的法理叙事，为扩大第一岛链战略优势铺路。中国将透过有规模的庆祝活动及各种官宣认知操作来满足这样的企图。

国安官员分析，中国一系列活动主要在建构三大意图目标。首先是「补强法理叙事」，中国全国人大去年通过将10月25日定为法定「光复纪念日」，借此展现坚持一个中国原则、反击「台湾地位未定论」。第二是「争夺历史诠释权」，活动由习近平亲定，「光复纪念」与「孙文诞辰」两件事相互串联，强化涉台话语权。

第三个目标是「塑造继承者假象」，国安官员表示，中华人民共和国成立于1949年10月1日，并未参与二战过程及后续国际条约的签署，主要参与的是内战，却试图创造「国体继承」的想像，以塑造「亚洲民主先行者」继承者的形象。

title: 欧洲中间派政党为何正在失去民心
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 中间派政党在欧洲最大、最重要的国家正陷入困境。经济增长低迷、通胀高企、政府债台高筑以及年轻人前景黯淡所引发的愤怒正在催生抗议，带来极右翼和极左翼民粹主义政党的崛起。 最初只是抗议学校经费不足的[法国大规模骚乱](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/world/europe/france-protests-riots.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/world/europe/fran
content:
中间派政党在欧洲最大、最重要的国家正陷入困境。经济增长低迷、通胀高企、政府债台高筑以及年轻人前景黯淡所引发的愤怒正在催生抗议，带来极右翼和极左翼民粹主义政党的崛起。

最初只是抗议学校经费不足的[法国大规模骚乱](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/world/europe/france-protests-riots.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/world/europe/france-protests-riots.html")就是一个令人震惊的例证。但这一现象已酝酿多年：自由民主制被认为未能兑现创造更美好未来的承诺，对年轻人和受薪工人阶级而言尤其如此。

许多欧洲人日益感到，中左和中右的传统政党并未提供真正的替代选项，且由受过教育的精英领导，这些人已与穷人、工人和年轻人脱节。面对不断上升的赤字、开支和利率，各国政府在回应举措上感到束手束脚。

于是，许多人转而支持玛丽娜·勒庞的国民联盟——该党作为极右翼在法国总统民调中领先——以及让-吕克·梅朗雄的不屈法国党，后者作为极左翼排名第二。在德国，选民转向极右翼的德国选择党和极左翼的左翼党。

明年，欧洲四个人口最多的国家——西班牙、法国、意大利和波兰——都将迎来重大选举，来自更极端政党的重大挑战正在逼近。甚至在意大利，周末也爆发了抗议，右翼总理乔治娅·梅洛尼要面对立场更靠右的前将军罗伯托·万纳奇的挑战。

利摩日市政厅于周六遭焚毁。Pascal Lachenaud/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

巴黎高等商学院欧洲法教授阿尔贝托·阿莱曼诺最近[指出](https://albertoalemanno.substack.com/p/can-the-eu-survive-a-hard-right-takeover?r=3wazw&utm_medium=ios)，极右翼政党还进入了捷克、芬兰、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚的政府，而斯洛文尼亚政府则依赖一个此类政党的外部支持。来自更右翼的竞争已在推动其中一些政党强化立场。

皮尤研究中心的定期[民意调查](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/06/10/americans-are-more-dissatisfied-with-how-their-democracy-is-working-than-people-in-other-high-income-countries/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Link: https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/06/10/americans-are-more-dissatisfied-with-how-their-democracy-is-working-than-people-in-other-high-income-countries/?utm_source=chatgpt.com")显示，民众对民主运作的满意度一直在急剧下降。皮尤今年发现，法国有69%的人口对民主不满意，西班牙为68%，意大利为62%。经历多年苏联占领后成为最新民主国家 的波兰，不满意比例为47%。美国则为69%。

对于乐观情绪和对中间派政治的信念为何下降，人们提出了许多解释。但诺贝尔经济学奖得主达龙·阿杰姆奥卢说得直白：“我们开始把民主视为理所当然。”

自由民主制未能对普通公民守信，对更广大的工人阶级尤其如此。“如果自由主义要再次崛起，它必须以工人阶级为核心，”他说。

**共享繁荣**

法国抗议活动迅速蔓延全国，工人和退休人员也加入其中，他们对通胀和高利率感到愤怒，尤其是能源价格和借贷成本不断上升，这指向总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙的中间偏右政府乃至整个自由民主制的更大失败。

在许多城市，抗议演变为骚乱，其暴力预计只会进一步助长勒庞的声势，以及她关于移民和治安失序的反自由主义抱怨。

麻省理工学院教授阿杰姆奥卢在[新书](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/815318/what-happened-to-liberal-democracy-by-daron-acemoglu/)《自由民主 怎么了？》(What Happened to Liberal Democracy?)中试图同时提供分析和处方。他在书中概括了过去半个世纪的“两个广泛的失败”，这些失败导致了普遍的疏离感和反建制情绪。

第一条是他所称的未能兑现共享繁荣，受打击最重的是受薪工人阶级，他们受到自动化、全球化和急剧恶化的不平等的冲击，如今又对人工智能深感焦虑。

他说，领导人忘记了他们与选民契约的一个关键部分是“管好下水道”，即确保日常生活基础设施的良好运转，从道路到教育再到医疗保健。

周一，一名市政工作人员在里昂特雷奥广场的巴托尔迪喷泉清理涂鸦。Olivier Chassignole/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

阿杰姆奥卢在采访中表示，第二条是“自上而下的文化政治的兴起”。在此进程中，一个受过大学教育的精英群体如今主导着整个西方世界甚至传统的社会党和工人阶级政党，在他看来，这些人对那些传统上支持他们的人所关切的问题摆出居高临下的姿态，或不予理会。

结果，工人阶级选民正转向极左、极右翼的民粹主义政党——后者尤甚，法国和德国的情况即是如此。这威胁到传统价值观，使历史上作为中间派“大帐篷”的政党不断萎缩，并威胁到议会民主的运作。

在英国2024年大选中，两个长期主导的政党——工党和保守党——合计得票率创下一个多世纪以来的最低水平。极右翼的英国改革党去年在民调中抬头，尽管此后有所回落。

美国德国协会主席史蒂文·E·索科尔表示，中间派政党需要重新赢得选民的信任，让选民相信他们不仅听到了自己的声音，而且同情自己的处境。“所有这些国家的一个不变因素是那些感到被落下的人，他们觉得自己与周围所见的繁荣和安全毫无关系，”他说。

**承压的中心**

德国提供了另一个中间派疲惫和分裂的例子。

中右和中左的Volksparteien，即“人民党”——基督教民主联盟（及其伙伴基督教社会联盟）和社会民主党——自二战以来交替执掌民主化的德国。但索科尔表示，它们正在被掏空，工人和年轻人正转向更极端的政党，如德国选择党和左翼党。

鉴于如今组建稳固联盟的难度，两个人民党被锁在一个争吵不断的联盟中，该联盟日益不受欢迎，并被外界认为未能带来经济增长和安全。

在前总理安格拉·默克尔领导下，基民盟向中间靠拢，但步伐谨慎，“即使面对明显的挑战也绝对不冒险，”该党著名议员诺贝特·勒特根说。

这些挑战包括移民增加、对华出口市场下滑、与俄罗斯紧张关系加剧以及经济增长缓慢。勒特根说，向中间靠拢以及默克尔对大规模移民的接纳疏远了许多该党的传统保守选民。

勒特根表示，这给右翼留下了空间，被德国选择党填补，该党如今正在吸引工人阶级中的传统基民盟选民。“但要认真解决我们的问题需要多数支持，而这，”他说，“就是我们的悖论。”

上个月，民众在德国施韦林市中心参加极右翼德国选择党集会。Lisi Niesner/Reuters

至于社会民主党，勒特根说，他们走了阿杰姆奥卢所描述的许多左翼政党的道路：知识精英和左翼学者“征服了党，并使其与传统的选民脱节”。

德国[当前民调的平均值](https://www.alleumfragen.de/ "Link: https://www.alleumfragen.de/")显示了构建一个可行的中间派联盟有多么困难。

德国选择党是最受欢迎的政党，支持率约28%，其次是基民盟/基社盟，为19.8%。绿党有15%，社会民主党仅13.1%，勉强领先于左翼党的11.3%。

两个主流政党内部都在如何推进上存在分歧：对基民盟而言，是靠近德国选择党而不只是复制其部分政策；对社会民主党而言，是进一步左转以同时抵御绿党和左翼党。

**分裂的欧洲**

保加利亚自由主义战略中心主席、维也纳人文科学研究所研究员伊万·克拉斯特夫表示，随着这四场重要选举以及极右翼在其中表现出的号召力，“我们将迎来一场重大转型，”政府将趋于碎片化。

右翼联盟很可能包含小型极右政党，“这将使主流极右政党成为人质，并可能阻止它们向中间移动。”

他说，如果它们表现良好，“那么你很快就会试图将它们正常化，因为否则欧盟无法运转，而这并不会让人们感到更安全。”

明年春天的法国总统选举将是关键。勒庞的胜利可能对布鲁塞尔、欧元、北约以及欧洲对乌克兰的支持产生重大影响。

极右翼国民联盟领导人玛丽娜·勒庞，她在法国总统民调中领先，极左翼不屈法国党领导人让-吕克·梅朗雄位居第二。Nicolas Tucat/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

阿杰姆奥卢主张“一个大帐篷式的民粹主义”，以包容性的名义引导选民的愤怒。

“核心必须是为没有大学学位和多元技能的人创造就业、工资增长和职业路径，”他说。“必须有一个共享繁荣的议程，这就是为什么人工智能及其使用方式至关重要。”

# 民進黨：中共涉假車禍跨國鎮壓 暴行令人髮指

2026-10-21 17:23 中央社／ 台北21日電  中共  車禍  民進黨

關閉

民進黨發言人吳崢。聯合報系資料照

[](https://udn.com/news/story/6656/9829080# "分享FB")[](https://udn.com/news/story/6656/9829080# "分享Line")[](https://www.threads.com/intent/post?text=%E6%B0%91%E9%80%B2%E9%BB%A8%EF%BC%9A%E4%B8%AD%E5%85%B1%E6%B6%89%E5%81%87%E8%BB%8A%E7%A6%8D%E8%B7%A8%E5%9C%8B%E9%8E%AE%E5%A3%93+%E6%9A%B4%E8%A1%8C%E4%BB%A4%E4%BA%BA%E9%AB%AE%E6%8C%87&url=https%3A%2F%2Fudn.com%2Fnews%2Fstory%2F6656%2F9829080%3Futm_source%3Dthreads%26utm_medium%3Dudnnews%26utm_campaign%3Dthreadspost "分享Threads")

[**中共**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E5%85%B1)涉跨國鎮壓買凶攻擊相聲演員黃逸豪，檢方起訴5嫌建請法院重判。[**民進黨**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%B0%91%E9%80%B2%E9%BB%A8)發言人[**吳崢**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%90%B3%E5%B4%A2)今天表示，中共干預、介入台灣的力道越來越殘暴，嚴重踩到台灣民主法治紅線，台灣不分黨派的政治工作者，應齊聲譴責中共這種令人髮指的暴行。

相聲演員黃逸豪9月演出前遭車撞受傷，新北地檢署查出中共涉跨國鎮壓教唆國內人士阻止其演出，且嫌犯原要讓黃逸豪斷手斷腳，因聽到慘叫才停止，最後依重傷害未遂等罪起訴5人並求處重刑。

[Video 18](https://content1.avplayer.com/5b59760c073ef46a2e6b8f13/videos/69d8bed5fc5b3e8a960d2c4e/hls/video.m3u8?AV_TAGID=6814930766b0cc5c3d0ead4d&pid=615ac1a77d20d4235b6a596a&cid=68149208c94d744b4a057116&AV_TEMPID=681494bbf2ab4be52e0614da&AV_PUBLISHERID=615ac1a77d20d4235b6a596a&av_qd1=6818a0d1ee249970a60232b2&videoId=69d8bed5fc5b3e8a960d2c4e)

針對上述案件，吳崢在民進黨中執會後記者會表示，相信民眾看到這件事情都會非常震驚，此事的本質已近乎恐怖主義的跨國鎮壓，且這位演員不是公職人員、從政者，只是一位在台灣享受言論自由的台灣人民。

吳崢指出，中國竟然連台灣人在台灣的言論也要管、甚至買凶進行這種極度殘暴的行為，相信所有台灣人民絕對不能接受，這已嚴重踩到台灣的國安、治安以及民主法治的紅線。

吳崢說，中國對台灣不論是介選、認知作戰，到現在直接買凶攻擊，意圖使民眾的人身安全受到損傷，這都凸顯中共對台灣干預及介入的力道越來越加強、殘暴。

吳崢認為，台灣不分黨派、支持台灣自由民主的政治工作者，都應齊聲、同聲譴責中共這種令人髮指的暴行，也拜託民眾參與選舉活動、行使自由民主的權利時，一定要多加留意，保護自己的人身安全，行政團隊也會盡全力做好相關因應與應變。

民進黨中國部於臉書撰文，嚴厲譴責中共當局毫不遮掩的流氓行徑，並正告北京當局，立即停止各項跨國鎮壓與對台灣人民威脅的惡劣行徑，台灣人民的生命安全與言論自由，絕不容許任何境外勢力任意侵犯。

此外，陸劇「逐玉」男主角張凌赫申請來台被拒，中國國台辦發言人張晗稱，大陸演藝人員赴台開展文化交流，是「兩岸民眾樂見並期盼的民間往來，有利於增進兩岸民眾相互了解」。民進黨政府拒不同意有關大陸演藝人員赴台交流，這有損兩岸文化交流，應摒棄政治操弄，取消不合理限制。

吳崢說，陸委會已清楚說明此事。出入境管理本來就是國家主權的象徵，例如他10幾年前參加完學運，跟青年夥伴申請港簽時也是直接被拒絕，這都是各國會有的管理作為。

吳崢指出，國台辦希望台灣行政團隊重視台灣粉絲心願，看來國台辦現在也感受到「民主是個好東西」，中國人民在網路上也表達希望中國民主化等心願，值得國台辦參考。

title: 刘军宁 | 从分赃到逃生：中国官场的腐败转型
summary: 刘军宁 X @liujunning · Oct 19 从分赃到逃生 江胡两朝的腐败是有价目表的。允你分利，换你听话。脏是真脏，但两头都认这笔账。官僚因此成了这家中国共产党股份有限公司的股东——有份子可拿，自然有理由替它续命。 十八大以后，股东一夜之间变成随时可以被清算的雇员。 雇员不会为公司拼命。雇员会把能搬的往外搬。 《决定》标题里“持之以恒”四个字，等于把话说死：这事没有终点。一个官员读懂这四个字，剩下的心思就只有一样。下一轮轮到我之前，怎么把人和钱弄到安全的地方。 贪腐
content: 刘军宁  X @liujunning · Oct 19 从分赃到逃生 江胡两朝的腐败是有价目表的。允你分利，换你听话。脏是真脏，但两头都认这笔账。官僚因此成了这家中国共产党股份有限公司的股东——有份子可拿，自然有理由替它续命。 十八大以后，股东一夜之间变成随时可以被清算的雇员。 雇员不会为公司拼命。雇员会把能搬的往外搬。 《决定》标题里“持之以恒”四个字，等于把话说死：这事没有终点。一个官员读懂这四个字，剩下的心思就只有一样。下一轮轮到我之前，怎么把人和钱弄到安全的地方。 贪腐于是改了形态。从前捞钱是为了置产、过日子、送儿子出去读书，那是奔着未来去的。现在捞钱是为了买一张随时能走的票。 从希望到绝望 十八大之前蛋糕在长。官商同盟里有一种真实的乐观：真能升官真会发财。多数人相信经济还会好，位子和票子一直呈正相关。 十八大之后，“刑不一再上常委”。党政官僚队伍里再没有一个人知道自己离危险有多远。 绝望不来自高压。熬得过去的叫运动，熬不过去的叫常态。《决定》把高压钉成了常态，后面再接上二十一大继续掌权，等于当着全党的面通知：你们这辈子就这样了。洗洗睡吧！ 上级疑下级不忠，下级防上级整肃。谁也不敢把真话说出口，于是谁也不知道别人在想什么。这是新常态。 从进取到躺平 从前一个干部的眼光能放到五年十年。守住基本的政治正确，按部就班往上走；帮企业冲一冲旧规矩，自己在增量里分一块。规矩虽然是暗的，但它存在，可以照着办。 现在他能看多远？下一轮还能不能平安落地？ 最划算的做法跟着就变了。别把事做大，先把手里的东西变现、挪走。少拍板、少签字、少留痕。做成一件事换不来什么，做错一件事可以要命。 躺平不是懒。那是一个人在没有法、随时可能被清算的地方，自己算出来的最优解。 从合作到对抗 交易还在的时候，上下之间至少有一样东西是真的：彼此有用。上面要稳定，下面要份子，各取所需，双方依从无形的约定。 现在《决定》给出的办法叫“一岗双责”：下属出事，上级连坐。名义是监督，做法是扣人质。后果可以提前写出来，上级从此不想知道下面的事，知道了就得担责；下级从此不敢往上报，报上去先挨处分的是自己。 一份想解决信息问题的文件，办法却是加重知情者的责任。这条路往下走只有一个结局：上面越来越看不见。 对抗不会以叛变的形式出现。它安静得多：不作为、不表态、不把身家押在这条船上。末日的王朝之船还在往前走，只是负责划桨的人已经一个一个把手松开了。 （@baodiantimes） 背景资料： 爆点周刊（BaodianTimes） @baodiantimes   · Oct 19, 2026 独家解密：五中全会《关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》稿 爆点周刊 纽约 10月19日讯 记者保罗 10月15日，《求是》杂志刊发习近平《以更高标准、更实举措推进全面从严治党》一文，引发海内外广泛关注。外界有观点认为，这是习近平在为即将召开的中共二十届五中全会提前释放政策信号，甚至可能成为即将出台的《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》（以下简称《全面从严治党决定》）的重要政策依据。然而，这篇文章实际上只是习近平2026年1月12日在二十届中央纪委五次全会上讲话的主要部分，并非专门为五中全会发表的新讲话。 值得注意的是，《求是》此时刊发这篇讲话，客观上容易使外界将其视为五中全会全面从严治党议题的主要政策信号。然而，根据本刊获得的《从严治党决定》稿，习近平试图推动的政治安排，远不止公开讲话所呈现的内容。 据本刊掌握的信息，该决定讨论稿此前已在部分省部级官员范围内征求意见。本刊获得文件后，已通过交叉核验确认其真实性。为了避免公众被误导和帮助公众更加全面地了解这一重大政治动向，《爆点周刊》决定提前披露该决定讨论稿的主体框架及核心内容，并对其背后的政治意图与可能产生的影响进行分析。 据不愿透露姓名的一位中共高级官员向本刊介绍：“《全面从严治党决定》的背景是，习近平中央已经充分意识到，自党的十八大以来的反腐整肃路线所引发巨大争议和党内分裂，只是大家敢怒不敢言而已。习近平想通过这种‘若干重大问题决定’的方式，以党中央的名义，肯定其反腐路线的正当性，从而对自己的既往路线进行盖棺定论的同时，宣誓继续将该路线贯彻到底，进而为其二十一大继续掌握最高权力铺平道路。其官方表述为：充分彰显了以习近平同志为核心的党中央强党强国的历史主动和深入推进从严治党的自我革命的坚强意志和坚定决心” 本刊通过研究该决定的讨论稿发现，除了对习近平18大以来的全面从严治党路线的肯定。决定的第一部分是“加强党的建设、确定并维护习近平的核心地位”，其方法论是：要求全体党员要严守党的政治纪律和政治规矩，不折不扣落实党中央决策部署，深刻领悟“两个确立“的决定性意义，坚决做到“两个维护”。持之以恒用党的创新理论凝心铸魂，深学细悟习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，深入系统学习近平党建思想，用以武装头脑、指导实践、推动工作等。 决定的第二部分是：强化组织建设。其具体方法论是：要深入贯彻新时代党的组织路线，着力增强各级党组织政治功能和组织功能，持续打造忠诚干净担当的高素质专业化干部队伍。 决定的第三部分是继续保持反腐高压态势。其主要方法论是：加大对权力集中、资金密集、资源富集等重点领域、关键岗位的监督。加强对既往反腐败案件经验的总结，围绕填补制度空白和机制漏洞为抓手，有针对性做好建章立制，完善反腐败体制机制建设。加强以案示警，一体推进不敢腐、不能腐、不想腐。 决定的第四部分是推进党的作风建设，要从严从实落实中央八项规定及实施细则精神，巩固拓展树立践行正确政绩观学习教育成果，推动作风建设长效化。 决定的第五部分是压实各级党委主体责任，各级党委（党组）要切实扛牢全面从严治党主体责任，主要负责同志要担负起“第一责任人”责任，班子成员要履行好“一岗双责”。 决定的第六部分是压实各级纪委责任，决定要求各级纪委要履行好监督责任，以更高标准、更严举措推动全面从严治党各项工作落到实处。 上述六个方面，是本刊记者根据《爆点周刊》透明度计划独家获得的《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》讨论稿原文，进行梳理、归纳和提炼后形成的主要内容。出于保护信息来源及相关人员安全的考虑，本刊暂不公开文件全文及其他可能暴露信息源的细节。我们对所披露信息的真实性负责，并愿意接受本月底中共五中全会正式文件及相关官方信息的公开检验。 纵观中共百余年历史，中央先后通过了三份具有特殊政治地位的历史决议。第一份是1945年4月20日中共六届七中全会通过的《关于若干历史问题的决议》，通过总结和批判党内历次错误路线，确立了毛泽东政治路线的权威，为毛泽东思想在中共七大上被确立为党的指导思想奠定了基础。第二份是1981年6月27日中共十一届六中全会通过的《关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议》，由邓小平主导，在全面否定文化大革命、承认毛泽东晚年严重错误的同时，维护毛泽东的历史地位，为改革开放确立了政治和思想基础。第三份是2021年11月11日中共十九届六中全会通过的《关于党的百年奋斗重大成就和历史经验的决议》，由习近平主导，以总结中共百年成就为主，突出十八大以来的所谓历史性成就，进一步强化习近平的核心地位。从政治权力的角度看，这三份历史决议虽然产生于不同年代，政治背景和历史任务各不相同，但都具有一个鲜明的共同特征：通过对历史的权威解释，重新确认现实政治路线，为最高领导人的政治权威提供历史依据。毛泽东通过总结历史确立权威，邓小平通过纠正历史错误推动政治转型，习近平则通过肯定历史成就巩固自身权力。历史决议表面上是总结过去，实际上深刻影响着中共未来的政治方向与权力格局。 值得注意的是，习近平执政以来，尤其热衷于通过具有宏大政治叙事特征的中央重大决定，确立自己的执政路线和政治权威。例如，2013年十八届三中全会通过《关于全面深化改革若干重大问题的决定》，2014年十八届四中全会通过《关于全面推进依法治国若干重大问题的决定》，2019年十九届四中全会通过《关于坚持和完善中国特色社会主义制度、推进国家治理体系和治理能力现代化若干重大问题的决定》。这些文件虽然与三份历史决议在性质和历史地位上有所不同，但都体现了中共政治运作中的一个重要特点：通过中央委员会的集体决定，将最高领导人的政治主张上升为全党的政治意志，并以制度化、权威化的形式要求全党贯彻执行。 在本刊看来，习近平如今试图推出的《关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》，正是这一政治逻辑的延续。如果该文件最终获得通过，它将成为习近平执政以来主导出台的又一份重要中央决定，其政治意义显然不止于反腐败本身。习近平试图通过这份文件，以党中央的名义，对十八大以来持续十余年的反腐整肃路线作出系统性肯定，将原本充满争议的政治实践转化为不容轻易否定的中央政治结论，并以此进一步强化全党对其个人权威和政治路线的服从。更值得警惕的是，这种安排不仅着眼于总结过去，更指向未来的权力延续：通过对既往执政路线的制度性确认，为其在二十一大继续掌握最高权力创造政治条件。说到底，这份决定真正值得关注的，不仅是习近平准备如何继续反腐，而是他试图如何通过中央集体决定，为自己的执政历史作出有利于自身的政治定性，并将个人权力意志转化为全党的政治纪律。这种借助宏大政治叙事进行自我辩护、权力巩固和政治延续的操作，值得国际社会高度关注与警惕。

title: 陈小平：你不支持我无期限任期，你就要被腐败，把你“长期关下去”
summary: 陈小平 @xchen156 X 2026年10月20日 我们现在看到的一个公认的事实是，谁是习近平的接班人？现在连个影子都没有。如果他想盖棺定论，应该不是这种玩法。习总目前最忙的应该是确保无限任期。 爆点周刊披露了全会要讨论通过的《从严治党决定》，---全称是《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》中的六方面的内容。并推出本周爆点话题：习近平要忙于给自己盖棺定论？ 习近平低调上位，高调掌权，2012年登位以来，争议不绝。最大的争议无疑是他无限任期。如果是以往
content: 陈小平 @xchen156  X 2026年10月20日 我们现在看到的一个公认的事实是，谁是习近平的接班人？现在连个影子都没有。如果他想盖棺定论，应该不是这种玩法。习总目前最忙的应该是确保无限任期。 爆点周刊披露了全会要讨论通过的《从严治党决定》，---全称是《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》中的六方面的内容。并推出本周爆点话题：习近平要忙于给自己盖棺定论？ 习近平低调上位，高调掌权，2012年登位以来，争议不绝。最大的争议无疑是他无限任期。如果是以往，台上的干10年就走人，台下政客和野心家心情会好些，多少还有个盼头嘛。 记得与陶杰先生做节目谈军中反腐，他说：茅台酒一喝，老习这个不好，那个不好就来了，这“新时代”十几年，权术一流，政绩如何？这非议自是如滔滔江河。。。。。。 共产党的朝廷，造反没戏，军委委员、上将、司令都快抓完了，你听说过谁想造反？但谁也挡不住矮嘴茅台开喝牢骚满腹呀。但“新时代”特色是处处隔墙有耳，这些非议自然是络绎不绝进了习总办公桌。 这些年，我们听惯了“定于一尊”、“不尊妄议”、“忠诚不绝对，绝对不忠诚“这些东东，无论它叫什么，目的就是一个：防堵官家之口。 无奈习总占位不走，这非议如何能绝？于是，“定于一尊”、“不尊妄议”之外，还有监狱。任志强先生就是这样被判刑18年的。这还算轻的，判无期徒刑的是一抓一大把的。 我看BBC 在2017年采访曾经的毛泽东秘书李锐，当年李锐非议毛泽东，结果被逐出共产党加8年单人监禁，他自己说：“我关在秦城我就发现了，好像要长期关下去。” 今天的习总也好这一手。被他关进监狱的，很多都是无期徒刑，这就是李锐说的“好像要长期关下去”。 我觉得习总现在最忙的是要确保自己无限任期。我们现在看到的一个公认的事实是，谁是习近平的接班人？现在连个影子都没有。如果他想让位，不是这种玩法。 爆点周刊披露的《从严治党决定》的第一部分是“加强党的建设、确定并维护习近平的核心地位”，其方法论是：要求全体党员要严守党的政治纪律和政治规矩，不折不扣落实党中央决策部署，深刻领悟“两个确立“的决定性意义，坚决做到“两个维护”。持之以恒用党的创新理论凝心铸魂，深学细悟习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，深入系统学习近平党建思想，用以武装头脑、指导实践、推动工作等。 他打算继续占位不走，自然就会继续面临党内批评与高压。但他预备了后手：这就是五中全会《从严治党决定》的第三部分：继续保持反腐高压态势。 你不支持我无期限任期，你就要被腐败，把你“长期关下去。” @baodiantimes

title: Defence, debt, diplomacy: Takaichi’s first year as Japanese prime minister
zh_title: 国防、债务、外交：高市担任日本首相的第一年
summary: 周三是日本首相高市早苗上任一周年，她疏远了中国，以其庞大的支出扰乱了市场，并将自己塑造为一个工作狂领导人。日本首相高市早苗于 2026 年 10 月 5 日在东京国民议会众议院全体会议上发表讲话。照片：Yuichi Yamazaki/法新社。以下是关于日本第一位女首相及其迄今为止的执政时期需要了解的五件事。与中国发生争执的高一上台后不久，就提出了
content:
周三是日本首相高市早苗上任一周年，她疏远了中国，以其庞大的支出扰乱了市场，并将自己塑造为一个工作狂领导人。日本首相高市早苗于 2026 年 10 月 5 日在东京国民议会众议院全体会议上发表讲话。照片：Yuichi Yamazaki/法新社。以下是关于日本第一位女首相及其迄今为止的执政时期需要了解的五件事。与中国发生争执高一上台后不久，就建议日本可以在台湾遭到袭击时进行军事干预，此举激怒了中国。北京声称台湾是自己的领土。她的言论引发了一场外交争端，导致中国警告其公民不要前往日本并实施贸易限制。高市将国防置于其议程的首要位置，日本一直在加强亚洲的军费开支和安全合作，在外岛部署导弹发射器，努力获得“反击”能力，并放宽武器出口规则。尽管如此，高市在最近的一份施政报告中仍称北京为“重要邻居”，并承诺在敌对国家之间建立稳定的关系。一面台湾国旗。照片：总统府台湾，来自 Flickr。
这位极端保守派领导人还表现出足够务实的态度，没有亲自参拜一座供奉战死者（包括被定罪的战犯）的有争议的东京神社，这一举动可能会激起中国和韩国的愤怒。 高市政府的巨额政府支出计划和日本央行相对低调的利率令市场感到不安，并将日本基准债券收益率推升至三十年来的最高水平。这位领导人重申了对积极和负责任的财政政策的承诺，但她还寻求从明年开始削减食品消费税，尽管市场担心日本不断增加的债务是年经济产出的两倍多。到目前为止，她未能确定每年需要大约 5 万亿日元（320 亿美元）为其提供资金。外国人政策 尽管亚洲第二大经济体正面临劳动力短缺和人口萎缩的问题，但对过度旅游和与外国投资相关的土地价格飙升的抱怨促使高市推动加强对移民的控制。在她的指导下，日本本月收紧了永久居留权的规定，要求外国人拥有更高的年收入和更高的日语流利程度。宝藏门，日本东京著名的旅游景点。照片：维基共享资源。
除了一些游客的签证费近 50 年来首次大幅上涨之外，对商务经理签证持有者的资本要求也变得更加严格。 工作道德 自称是工作狂的高一在当选保守派执政党主席后宣称，她“应该工作、工作、工作、工作、工作”。她在一篇被广泛嘲笑为“炫耀”的 X 帖子中透露，她每晚的睡眠时间在零到三个小时之间，从而强化了这一形象。她还表示，有时她会安排凌晨 3 点举行员工会议。她喜欢在深夜独自阅读下班回家的大量文件，这意味着她花在喝酒和吃饭上的时间比她的男性前任要少得多——这打破了日本传统的“夜间政治”。接下来是什么？饰演 高一

【原文 English Original】
Wednesday marks the first anniversary of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s leadership that has seen her alienate China, rattle markets with her expansive spending and establish herself as a workaholic leader. Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi delivers a speech during a plenary session of the House of Representatives at the National Diet in Tokyo on October 5, 2026. Photo: Yuichi Yamazaki/AFP. Here are five things to know about Japan’s first woman prime minister and her time in power so far. Spat with China Soon after coming to power, Takaichi incurred China’s wrath by suggesting that Japan could intervene militarily in the event of an attack on Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own territory. Her comment triggered a diplomatic spat that led to China warning its citizens against travelling to Japan and imposing trade restrictions. Takaichi has placed national defence at the top of her agenda and Japan has been beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire “counterstrike” capabilities and easing rules on weapons exports. Still, Takaichi called Beijing an “important neighbour” in a recent policy address and pledged to build a stable relationship between the rival nations. A Taiwan flag. Photo: Taiwan Office of the President, via Flickr. The ultraconservative leader also proved pragmatic enough to refrain from visiting a controversial Tokyo shrine honouring war dead, including convicted war criminals, in person — a gesture that would have provoked fury in China and South Korea. Expansive government spending Takaichi’s programme of big government spending and the Bank of Japan’s relatively low-key interest rate have unnerved the markets and pushed Japan’s benchmark bond yield to its highest level in three decades. The leader has reiterated her commitment to a proactive and responsible fiscal policy, but she is also pursuing a consumption tax cut on food starting next year, despite market concerns about Japan’s mounting debts more than double annual economic output. So far, she has failed to identify around five trillion yen ($32 billion) needed annually to fund it. Foreigner policy Complaints of overtourism and soaring land prices linked to foreign investment sparked Takaichi’s push for tighter control on immigration, despite Asia’s number two economy grappling with labour shortages and a shrinking population. Under her tutelage, Japan toughened rules for permanent residency this month, with foreigners required to have higher annual incomes and greater fluency in Japanese. The Hozomon Gate, a popular tourist attraction in Tokyo, Japan. Photo: Wikicommons. Capital requirements for business manager visa holders were also stiffened on top of a sharp increase in visa fees for some tourists for the first time in nearly 50 years. Work ethic A self-proclaimed workaholic, Takaichi declared she “shall work, work, work, work and work” upon being elected the president of her conservative ruling party. She has reinforced that image by revealing in an X post — that was widely derided for “showing off” — that she sleeps between zero and three hours a night. She also said she sometimes schedules 3 am staff meetings. Her penchant for solitary, late-night perusal of reams of documents brought home from work means she has spent far less time than her male predecessors wining and dining — a break with Japan’s traditional “nighttime politics”. What’s next? As Takaichi faces another Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election next year, and with her lone-wolf tendency costing her intraparty support, the longevity of her government hinges for now on public backing. The latest opinion polls have suggested a slight dent in her popularity due in part to the resignation of her scandal-hit farm minister, but overall, her approval rates remain fairly strong at around 40 to 60 percent.

title: China says COP31 should focus on tariffs against its clean tech
zh_title: 中国称COP31应重点讨论对其清洁技术征收关税
summary: 中国 中国敦促下个月在土耳其举行的COP31峰会解决其所谓的全球气候行动的新问题：对其清洁技术征收关税。李高副部长批评单边主义和保护主义，并表示北京将对袭击事件作出坚决回应。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 21 日香港时间 14:45 · 2 分钟阅读中国已致电下个月在土耳其举行的 COP31 峰会将重点讨论所谓的新问题
content:
中国
中国敦促下个月在土耳其举行的第三十一届联合国气候变化框架公约(COP31)峰会解决其所谓的全球气候行动的新问题：对其清洁技术征收关税。李高副部长批评单边主义和保护主义，并表示北京将对袭击事件作出坚决回应。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 21 日 14:45 香港时间 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

中国呼吁下个月在土耳其举行的 COP31 峰会重点讨论全球气候行动的一个新问题：针对其清洁技术的关税。

生态环境部副部长李高周三在新闻发布会上表示，将于下个月在安塔利亚举行的第31届缔约方大会（COP）应讨论发展中国家的气候融资等问题，以及单边主义和保护主义的“新问题”，这是对美国和欧盟贸易政策的常见间接批评。

他说：“我们认为，这次会议应深入讨论发达国家减排不足、资金支持不足的老问题，以及单边主义和保护主义破坏全球集体努力的新问题。”
中国是迄今为止世界上最大的减排所需太阳能电池板、风力涡轮机、电池和电动汽车生产国。然而，对于担心对其当地产业产生竞争影响的国家来说，这项技术越来越被视为威胁，而不是机遇。

美国对中国太阳能和电动汽车征收高额关税，欧盟对汽车也采取了同样的做法，对一些太阳能零部件实施了限制，并正在调查中国一家大型风电公司的不公平贸易行为。

李说，在地缘政治冲突“加剧”的背景下，会议应讨论绿色技术的自由流动，并补充说，中国将对针对绿色技术的抹黑或攻击给予“坚决回应”。

李说，会议的其他优先事项应包括在 2024 年承诺每年为发展中国家提供 3000 亿美元气候融资的路线图。当被问及中国是否支持土耳其推动全球电气化协议时，李表示，这一目标符合中国政策，但没有明确支持这一推动。 “我们建议主席继续充分听取各方意见，寻求最大公约数，争取最广泛支持，”他说。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
China
China urges next month's COP31 summit in Turkey to address what it calls a new problem for global climate action: tariffs on its clean technology. Vice minister Li Gao criticised unilateralism and protectionism, and said Beijing would give a firm response to attacks.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

21 Oct 2026 at 14:45 HKT · 2 min read

China has called on the COP31 summit in Turkey next month to focus on what it described as a new problem for global climate action: tariffs against its clean technology.

The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP) meeting, which begins in Antalya next month, should address issues such as climate finance for the developing world as well as the “new problem” of unilateralism and protectionism, a common indirect criticism of US and EU trade policy, Li Gao, vice minister of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, told a press conference on Wednesday.

“We believe the conference should discuss in depth the old problems of developed countries’ insufficient emission reductions and insufficient financial support, as well as the new problem of unilateralism and protectionism undermining global collective efforts,” he said.

China is by far the world’s largest producer of solar panels, wind turbines, batteries and electric cars needed to cut emissions. However, that technology is increasingly seen as a threat, rather than an opportunity, for countries concerned about the competitive impact on their local industries.

The United States has imposed steep tariffs on Chinese solar and electric cars, while the European Union has done the same for autos, imposed restrictions on some solar components and is investigating a major Chinese wind company for unfair trade.

Against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts, the conference should discuss the free flow of green technology, said Li, who added that China would give a “firm response” to smears or attacks against it.

Other priorities for the conference should include a roadmap for a pledge made in 2024 to marshal US$300 billion of climate finance a year for the developing world, Li said. Asked whether China supported Turkey’s push for a global agreement on electrification, Li said the objective was in line with Chinese policy but stopped short of explicitly supporting the push. “We suggest the presidency continue to listen fully to views from all sides, seek the greatest common denominator, and work to win the broadest possible support,” he said.

# MPF confidence hits 15-year high; 28% of HK workers target HK$8m retirement

Hong Kong's MPF Confidence Index reached a 15-year high of 5.1 out of 10. A GUM survey found 28% of respondents expect to need at least HK$8 million for retirement, up from 21% in 2025. The average retirement target rose 12% to HK$6.48 million.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Hong Kong employees' confidence in the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) system has reached a 15-year high, while the proportion expecting to need at least HK$8 million for retirement has risen sharply, according to a survey by MPF consulting firm GUM.

The MPF Confidence Index rose to 5.1 out of 10 in October, up from 4.0 in 2025 and rebounding from a record low of 2.8 in 2022, GUM said. The firm surveyed 808 Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 64 who participate in the MPF system between 13 and 15 August.

GUM attributed the improved confidence to better market returns in recent years, greater member engagement, and an enhanced digital experience on the eMPF platform. Michael Chan, managing director of GUM, said: “As confidence improves, members are placing greater emphasis on retirement savings adequacy, fund performance and investment choices, signaling a shift from passive participation to more active management of retirement assets.”

The survey found that 75 per cent of respondents review their MPF performance at least once a year, and about 30 per cent had switched funds in the past six months. The proportion expecting to need HK$8 million or more for retirement rose from 21 per cent in 2025 to 28 per cent in 2026. The average retirement savings target increased 12 per cent year on year, from HK$5.79 million in 2025 to HK$6.48 million in 2026.

GUM also noted growing demand for decision-making support. Among respondents, 51 per cent expressed interest in artificial intelligence-empowered investment analysis and fund selection tools, and an equal proportion said regular market updates would be most valuable. A further 35 per cent hoped for tools to assess their risk tolerance, highlighting members' increasing desire for guidance in retirement investment decisions, GUM said.

## Modi government’s defence comes amid reported mass detentions, assembly restrictions and arrests of protest organisers

i

[![Image 3: google_preferred_badge](https://images.assettype.com/nationalherald/2026-06-11/gv2jpi8h/googlepreferredbadge.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=nationalheraldindia.com)

Follow us on:

*   _India rejected what it called selective targeting at the UN, as international scrutiny of the response to youth-led protests intensified_

*   _UN experts have sought an independent investigation into reported police excesses, with rights groups also documenting restrictions and detentions_

*   _INDIA bloc leaders and the CJP have condemned the arrests and restrictions as an assault on the right to peaceful protest_

India has pushed back against criticism of its human rights record at the United Nations, arguing that unverified allegations should not be used to portray the country negatively, amid [growing international concern over the police response to youth-led protests](https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/opinion/let-jantar-mantar-speak).

The government’s defence comes against a backdrop of reported mass detentions, restrictions on public assembly and arrests of protest organisers that have drawn criticism from UN experts, rights organisations and opposition parties.

Addressing the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee on Tuesday during a discussion concerning the Working Group on Enforced Disappearances, Ministry of External Affairs deputy secretary Barkha Tamrakar said human rights must not become a means of exerting political pressure or selectively targeting countries.

She said India remained willing to address specific, properly documented cases through established mechanisms, but opposed attempts to draw sweeping conclusions from allegations, incomplete statistics or a report containing no country observation on India.

“We call on delegations to cite the report faithfully, not to inflate a humanitarian communication into a verdict,” she said.

Tamrakar maintained that engagement with international human rights mechanisms should rest on dialogue, cooperation, transparency and non-selectivity.

Her remarks coincided with a call from more than 20 UN human rights experts for an independent investigation into the authorities’ handling of recent demonstrations. The experts raised concerns about excessive force, restrictions on assembly and the treatment of protesters, and urged accountability for reported abuses.

The criticism extends beyond UN mechanisms. Amnesty International has called for the release of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, detained after attempting to protest at Jantar Mantar. Human Rights Watch has also urged the government to end arbitrary detentions and ensure that security forces respect international standards governing protests.

At home, INDIA bloc leaders have been challenging the government’s handling of the demonstrations. Rahul Gandhi has led opposition allies in condemning the custody of Das and Ranka, as the opposition pledged to defend the right to protest at Jantar Mantar.

Trinamool Congress leader Mamata Banerjee described the restrictions and detentions as a “super Emergency”. Her criticism followed the police operation in which CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained after arriving in Delhi by air on 10 October.

The CJP has questioned why the government has deployed such extensive restrictions against people demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Dipke argued that the Centre had brought Delhi to a standstill to shield the election chief from public pressure.

The movement and opposition parties have challenged the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, saying it risks disenfranchising eligible voters. Their demonstrations have increasingly focused on the freedom to assemble and the continued detention of organisers.

Das and Ranka have approached the Delhi High Court against the extension of their custody. Their petition challenges the rejection of their sureties and argues that their continued detention violates their constitutional right to liberty. CJP legal head Ratna Singh has criticised the extension as unjustified.

Indian authorities have defended the police response as lawful and rejected international criticism as interference in domestic affairs. The government has also maintained that the electoral revision targets ineligible entries and provides an appeals process.

New Delhi had earlier dismissed a UN expert’s observations as hearsay and described the UN human rights office’s concern over mass detentions as unwarranted interference. The latest statement reiterates that position as demands grow for scrutiny of the arrests, restrictions and use of force.

title: U.S. Curb on Chinese Drones Hurts American Users

content:
Foreign tourists select handheld photography equipment at a DJI flagship store in Shenzhen. (PHOTO: XINHUA)
U.S. restrictions on Chinese-made drones are hurting cash-strapped American police departments, forcing some to scramble for ways to afford the more expensive American-made alternatives, according to an October 12 report by NPR.

The report quoted Jon Beal, head of the Law Enforcement Drone Association (LEDA), as saying Chinese-made drones are "light years ahead of what our American drones are able to do."

Beal said Chinese company DJI offers a drone with an impressive high-resolution thermal camera that costs less than 10,000 USD. In comparison, American-made drones have lower flight-time capabilities, thermal imaging and zoom. They usually cost between 20,000 USD and 50,000 USD, depending on the type and the model.

In recent years, the U.S. has steadily erected barriers to the import and sale of Chinese drones. In December 2025, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) added foreign-produced unmanned aircraft systems and critical components to its "Covered List," restricting the authorization of new models for import and sale. In July 2026, the FCC sought to label civilian drones as "military-grade," expanding the scope of restrictions. In addition, several other U.S. government agencies have repeatedly used their regulatory powers to target Chinese drones.

The difficulties facing U.S. police departments are just one example of the wider consequences of these restrictions. Similar problems are emerging across multiple industries.

According to Construction Executive, a U.S. construction industry news outlet, 36 percent of American contractors are using drones, and nearly all of them rely on Chinese products. The U.S. government's prohibition on the use of Chinese drones by contractors working on government projects has put these businesses under pressure.

Sales of new agricultural spray drones in the U.S. fell by 60 percent in 2025, largely because of U.S. Customs and Border Protection interventions in DJI shipments, U.S. agricultural news website AgFunderNews reported.

Eric Ringer, president of the American Spray Drone Coalition, described the industry as "very much in flux," with some U.S. spray drone operators buying up any existing DJI models that are not enmeshed in the ban.

The performance advantage of Chinese drones is a major reason many American users would rather continue using older Chinese models than switch to domestic alternatives.

Last year, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's National Urban Security Technology Laboratory evaluated drones in Manhattan, New York City. As the surrounding highrises interfered with control signals, three drones were unable to fly reliably: one could not determine its position, another failed to take off, and a third temporarily lost contact.

By contrast, the two DJI drones tested at the same time operated normally, according to a report by U.S. drone industry news outlet DroneXL.

However, the U.S. government's test report mentioned only the scores of the American drones while deliberately concealing the test results of the Chinese drones. The U.S. government appears unwilling to let the public fully understand the performance advantages of Chinese drones, nor does it want to face the reality of its own products lagging behind.

However, if police officers and firefighters in New York are forced to use substandard American drones to carry out missions in the densely built and heavily populated Manhattan, it has the potential of creating enormous public safety risks.

At present, drone technology is still undergoing iterative development. Restrictions on Chinese drones will prevent the American public and various institutions from using the latest Chinese drone products, effectively creating an artificial technological divide — and this time, it is the U.S. that will be losing.

Reports indicate that DJI is about to launch a new generation of drones and drone stations that can quickly swap batteries without waiting for recharging. DroneXL lamented in its report that this clearly demonstrates the losses caused to the U.S. by the "Covered List," as law enforcement agencies in other countries no longer have to endure a 27-minute charging time.

As for the so-called security issues of Chinese drones that the U.S. has repeatedly hyped, facts have proven them to be a fabricated pretext for trying to suppress China's related industries and engaging in trade protectionism. From October last year to March this year, American cybersecurity firm OnDefend conducted an independent security review of multiple DJI drone models. The results found no backdoors, no data flowing out of the U.S., and no viable network hijacking pathways.

Drones are becoming increasingly integrated into economic development, public safety, urban governance, agricultural production and everyday life. Restricting Chinese drones will not serve as a "protective shield" for the development of the U.S. drone industry. Instead, it will create a range of unnecessary problems across different applications.

The U.S. government should listen to drone users across industries. Persisting with its current course could ultimately result in even greater losses.

title: US Grapples With China-Linked Critical Minerals Shortfall Left Unresolved By Trump-Xi Summit
summary: WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals e
content:
WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals export restrictions that have roiled Pentagon and commercial supply chains alike.

Trump and Xi agreed to extend a trade truce -- set to expire on November 10 -- by two months. But the extension doesn’t address Washington’s core concerns about inadequate minerals exports from China.

During testimony in July before the Senate Finance Committee, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that China’s mineral exports are “not as much as we would want. It’s not at the pace we would want.”

#### SEE ALSO:

[Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict](https://www.rferl.org/a/trump-xi-summit-iran-war-china-hormuz-nuclear-trade/33757431.html "SEE ALSO: Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict")

China dominates global production and refining of critical minerals and rare earth permanent magnets, which retain their magnetic properties indefinitely without the need for external power. Rare earth permanent magnets are essential for the functionality of everything from electrical vehicle motors and wind turbines to fighter jets and missile guidance systems.

The International Energy Agency (IEA), an autonomous intergovernmental organization based in Paris, estimates that China is the top refiner for 19 out of 20 key strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent.

China has an even tighter grip on permanent magnets with a 94 percent global market share, according to the IEA.

Beijing has weaponized its critical minerals dominance to counter US sanctions on its semiconductor sector and the Trump administration’s tariffs. It has calibrated the export controls to inflict maximum pressure on Pentagon supply chains while avoiding large-scale disruption to consumer industries, which would risk escalation with Washington that China’s ruling Communist Party (CCP) does not want.

Overall, China exported 512 metric tons of rare-earth permanent magnets to the US in August, down 21 percent from July and 13 percent from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data.

Heading into the summit, Xi sought to leverage China’s strategic metals dominance to secure a lasting trade truce with the United States, says Tomasz Nadrowski, portfolio manager at the New York-based Amvest Terraden Critical Minerals Fund.

“China has this spigot that it can turn on and off -- which determines the flow of critical minerals to the US and other countries,” he told RFE/RL in an interview.

“Extending the trade truce two years would have given this tool additional value,” further locking in US dependency on China’s critical mineral supply chains.

The Trump administration was concerned that with a two-year truce, “everyone [both commercial and defense manufacturers] would relax and think, 'We don’t need to build any new capacity,” he says.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

“The US cannot afford to accept strategic chokepoint dependencies for inputs that are essential to our defense industrial base and foundational industries like automotive,” Mahnaz Khan, vice president of policy for critical supply chains at the Silverado Policy Accelerator in Washington, said in an interview.

The two-month truce agreed to by Trump and Xi “buys the United States time, but it doesn’t eliminate the underlying vulnerability,” she said

## **Partnering With Central Asia**

As it works to reduce critical minerals dependence on China, the Trump administration has cast a wide net. In an August [**fact sheet**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-announces-billions-in-new-deals-and-investments-to-power-american-mining/), the White House said it has signed or approved more than 160 mineral deals since January 2025, totaling about $40 billion.

While the administration prioritizes domestic minerals production, in some cases, overseas projects are more feasible. This holds true for tungsten, which the United States has not produced at home since 2015. Tungsten is a crucial input for military-grade steel, aerospace components, munitions, and ground vehicle armor. Given its high density, the metal is used for stabilization and control in missiles and aircraft.

Tungsten’s importance for defense led the Trump administration to throw its support behind a $1.1 billion project in Kazakhstan. Under an agreement signed in November 2025 between US-based Cove Capital (now known as the Cove Kaz Capital Group) and the state-run Kazakh mining company Tau-Ken Samruk, the two parties will jointly develop one of the world’s largest tungsten resources.

“Kazakhstan made a conscious political choice to make an award to a US company, though rumor has it that China was also bidding for the same project,” Akbota Karibayeva Meyer, a research fellow at the Caspian Policy Center in Washington, told RFE/RL. The decision exemplifies Kazakhstan’s multi-vector foreign policy, which aims to preserve strategic autonomy by balancing ties with major powers, she explains.

#### SEE ALSO:

[US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise](https://www.rferl.org/a/us-georgia-black-sea-iran-trump-trade/33727854.html "SEE ALSO: US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise ")

Drilling, feasibility studies, and site preparation began after the agreement’s formal closing. Yet full commercial production is several years away.

“Are these projects in Kazakhstan viable? Sure, they’re viable. The economics are very hard to pencil out without a subsidy, though,” Ian Lange, a professor at the Colorado School of Mines and deputy director of its Critical Materials Innovation Hub, said in an interview.

“Ideally, I might want to do something [in terms of a mining investment] that limits the government’s expenditure and provides for some competition,” he says.

The Trump administration is also working with Uzbekistan to source critical minerals.

In February, the US commodities firm Traxys signed a $1 billion deal with the Uzbek government focused on the exploration and extraction of tungsten, molybdenum, and copper. This agreement aligns with a separate critical minerals pact reached between the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Uzbekistan.

Elsewhere in Central Asia, the potential for cooperation with the US exists. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan both have major reserves of antimony, a critical mineral used as a flame retardant, an alloying agent for lead, and a compound in semiconductors.

During a September visit to Bishkek, US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor and US Senator Steve Daines, chairman of the Senate Central Asia Caucus, discussed mining cooperation with Kyrgyz officials.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

During their trip, they also met with the presidents of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikstan.

While the US continues to make progress sourcing critical minerals from Central Asia, “it is important to recognize the limiting factor of geography,” Karibayeva Meyer says.

Given its proximity to Central Asia, “it is much easier for China to be involved in the region.”

## **Short And Long-Term Challenges**

In the short term, the US faces a key hurdle in its critical minerals diversification push: from January 1, 2027, the Pentagon will prohibit the use of certain metals sourced from the “foreign adversary countries” of China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran.

The ban, outlined in [**Executive Order 14415**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/07/securing-americas-defense-supply-chains-and-ensuring-domestic-acquisition-of-critical-materials/), sharply narrows the possibility of receiving waivers for the use of rare-earth magnets, tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum from those four nations. Defense firms can no longer be granted a waiver based on cost or convenience reasons. To receive one, they must show that compliant materials are completely unavailable despite exhaustive efforts to source them.

The Aerospace Industries Association (AIA), a Washington-based trade association, said in a [**recent report**](https://www.aia-aerospace.org/publications/strengthening-critical-minerals-supply-chains/) that some of its member companies expect to achieve compliance for certain applications by January 1. Others may need until 2028 or later, given the paucity of compliant aerospace-grade material for several covered materials.

AIA recommends that the Trump administration align compliance requirements with supply chain readiness and preserve flexible waiver authorities.

Lange of the Colorado School of Mines says that the administration may offer defense firms some additional leeway.

In the longer term, analysts say that the United States must focus greater effort on critical minerals processing. Decades of outsourcing production to China have resulted in high regulatory costs, a shortage of specialized metallurgical expertise and a dearth of commercial-scale downstream facilities.

**“**I do see processing as the top, most enduring impediment to large-scale diversification away from China,” Cory Combs, head of critical mineral and supply chain research at the consultancy Trivium China, told RFE/RL.

“Mining is generally much less technologically complex. Processing is where the most critical know-how bottlenecks lie. China's own experience, with decades spent building its processing capabilities, reflects the challenge,” he says.

He further notes that the US lacks strong demand signals in the parts of the production chain between processed minerals and end uses, which limits the scale of offtake agreements necessary to properly fund processing expansions.

Given long project lead times, permitting bottlenecks and capital constraints, analysts expect that Washington will need more than a decade to develop a midstream critical minerals supply chain not dependent on China.

In the meantime, Beijing will aim to exploit that continued dependency to deter the US from imposing further curbs on its development of advanced technologies integral to semiconductors and artificial intelligence.

So far, it has been successful.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration delayed adding more than 100 Chinese firms to the Commerce Department Entity List -- a trade and export blacklist -- because of concern over how Beijing might further throttle rare earth shipments.

China’s continuing dominance of critical minerals could also constrain Washington’s ability to intervene in a Taiwan Strait crisis.

A [**Heritage Foundation report**](https://www.heritage.org/tidalwave/chapters/chapter-6-assessing-the-us-indo-pacific-munitions-system)published in January warns that if China fully weaponizes its export restrictions at the onset of a war, the US could deplete existing stockpiles of minerals needed to produce new advanced munitions in under 90 days.

summary: **[Wake Up Together](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)**[](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)is an online meditation community that was established in 2020 by Trina Truong and partners. Our mission is to help support individu
content:
**[Wake Up Together](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)**[](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)is an online meditation community that was established in 2020 by Trina Truong and partners. Our mission is to help support individuals in maintaining a solid meditation practice through practicing in an accessible and open-minded community. We meet every day, virtually. While we are rooted in the Vipassana-Insight tradition, our approach is also inclusive to all Buddhist meditation practices such as anapanasati (mindfulness of the breath), Metta (loving-kindness), body scans, Zen, ton glen, and others.

The space that our meditators come to know is one that expresses itself as welcoming and embodying all views and interpretations of spirituality.

We hold the commitment to remain humble and vulnerable in our role as the door openers to the individual's inner journey. We aspire to shape the experience for participants to experience serenity, clear-seeing and profound understanding of the mind, and the [no] self through the practices, the guidance, the teachings, and the reflections offered in group sharing.

To solidify this spiritual aspiration is to make a commitment to sit in community with a predetermined frequency or as often as you can.
 We welcome you to join our beloved community!
**[Register to Join](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdJF26i6aTbMKLzw53MiwlehbsGaJG5qmVBPQEWwQ6WCOirKg/viewform)**

These guided meditations are offered daily and given freely. There
 are no up-front fees. Wake Up Together is 100% donation based,
 relying on your support and generosity.
**[100% Donation Base](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/giving)**

KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.

Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.

Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:

• Namgyal Higher Secondary School

• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School

• Namgyal Middle Boarding School

• Marshyangdi Boarding High School

• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School

We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.

We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.

For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.

Funds raised will help provide:

• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities

• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses

• Ongoing living and caregiving support

• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers

Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.

You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.

Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.

【周日下午活动】｜牛腾宇妈妈 作品展

🕟 4:30–6:30 PM

现场将展出牛腾宇妈妈的画作，并邀请她和大家交流。我们将有机会听她亲自讲述牛腾宇案的相关情况及狱中生活近况，也听她分享作品背后的故事，以及一路走来面对困境、坚持抗争的经历与心声。

这不仅是一次作品的展示，也是两场关于人生选择、女性成长、困境与坚持、爱与生命力量的真诚交流。

有人经历风雨，依然选择热爱生活；

有人身处困境，依然选择坚持和发声。

期待这个周末与大家在Los Altos Public Library相见。一起看作品、听故事、聊人生，在真实的生命经历中，看见彼此，也获得一些温暖与力量。

summary: 想一想本世纪最经典的喜剧电影：《老学究》、《赌球风云》、《婚礼傲客》、《王牌播音员》。它们有什么共同点吗？ 如果你猜到了文斯·沃恩，那你猜对了。（如果你把他未露面的客串也算在内，还可以加上《超级名模》。） 在乔恩·费儒的独立电影《舞出我人生》中成名后，沃恩找到了自己的定位，主演了一系列至今仍备受喜爱的票房大片，总票房超过 20 亿美元。 多年来，沃恩一直是极具票房号召力的巨星，所以，为了不过分夸大其词，到底发生了什么？这位曾被《新闻周刊》称为“无敌”（懂了吗？）的好莱坞黄金男
content: 想一想本世纪最经典的喜剧电影：《老学究》、《赌球风云》、《婚礼傲客》、《王牌播音员》。它们有什么共同点吗？ 如果你猜到了文斯·沃恩，那你猜对了。（如果你把他未露面的客串也算在内，还可以加上《超级名模》。） 在乔恩·费儒的独立电影《舞出我人生》中成名后，沃恩找到了自己的定位，主演了一系列至今仍备受喜爱的票房大片，总票房超过 20 亿美元。 多年来，沃恩一直是极具票房号召力的巨星，所以，为了不过分夸大其词，到底发生了什么？这位曾被《新闻周刊》称为“无敌”（懂了吗？）的好莱坞黄金男孩，是如何从杂志封面、充满赞誉的采访和卖座电影，变成了一系列票房惨败、低预算作品，甚至最近主演一部与猴子合作的电视剧，并与唐纳德·特朗普合影的？ 欧文·威尔逊和文斯·沃恩在 2005 年电影《婚礼傲客》中共同主演。 故事是这样的。沃恩出生于明尼阿波利斯，18 岁时拍完一部大型汽车广告后，搬到了洛杉矶，希望立刻被发掘。然而，他在试镜路上走了七年，直到最终在备受赞誉的《舞出我人生》中担任主角。随后他出演了一系列角色，包括《侏罗纪公园：失落的世界》和与詹妮弗·洛佩兹合作的《移魂女郎》，直到 2003 年的《舞出我人生》让他迎来了事业的巅峰。这部 R 级喜剧让他成为喜剧明星，随后他又主演了《霹雳游侠》、《赌球风云》、《婚礼傲客》、《分手信》和《爱在旅途》，并在《史密斯夫妇》和获得奥斯卡提名的《荒野生存》中出演角色。 文斯·沃恩在 2004 年热门电影《赌球风云》中。 2005 年，沃恩在报道中被誉为“喜剧之王”，《纽约时报》报道说，由于他“炙手可热”，各大制片厂为他的下一个项目《分手信》展开了竞价。出价最高者支付了 1700 万美元，相当于今天的 3000 万美元。证明他星途多亮的是，詹妮弗·安妮斯顿也签约与他共同主演，两人后来还开始约会。 文斯·沃恩和詹妮弗·安妮斯顿在电影《分手信》中的一个场景。他们在现实生活中后来也开始了约会。 在这一时期的某本杂志专访中，这位演员被问及约会建议，并非常谦虚地说：“我对单身男士的唯一建议是：出去拍几部电影。这让事情容易多了。” 当时做文斯·沃恩真是太棒了。 他的星途第一个打击来自 2011 年的《致命约会》，该片耗资 1 亿美元制作，上映首周仅收获 2500 万美元。随后，他又主演了一系列预算同样巨大的作品，如《监视者》、《实习生》和《送货员》，结果都惨败。 2015 年，他的职业生涯遭遇了最糟糕的开局，电影《未了情》上映首周末仅收获 670 万美元，尽管耗资 5000 万美元。观众并不友好，该片在烂番茄上的评分仅为 10%，评论家称其为“愚蠢”、“绝望”和“无趣、荒谬且毫无目的”。 文斯·沃恩在电影《送货员》中的一个场景。 2015 年，沃恩尝试了一次人们希望他能借此重振旗鼓的举措，主演了《真探》第二季。这部黑暗犯罪惊悚剧的第一季让马修·麦康纳从浪漫喜剧男神转变为备受尊敬的演员，而沃恩作为职业罪犯出演第二季，似乎也是为了同样的目的。 读者：并没有。虽然沃恩的表演获得了一定程度的赞誉，但整个季度广受批评，未能吸引观众的关注。 随后，他主演了一系列真正令人遗忘的 B 级和 C 级项目，如《99 号牢房暴乱》、《拖过混凝土》、《与我的家人搏斗》和《瑟伯格》。 文斯·沃恩在《真探》第二季中的一个场景。 唯一的亮点是他在 2016 年的《血战钢锯岭》中担任配角，以及在 2020 年的讽刺恐怖电影《怪诞》中担任主角，该片现在在 Tubi 流媒体上播出，在烂番茄上的评分为 86%，并为他赢得了多年来的最佳评价。 然而， complicating 他的公众形象的是他直言不讳的持枪立场，包括错误地声称在《GQ》杂志上，大规模枪击事件“只发生在不允许枪支的地方”，如校园。他还表示，他认为应该在学校鼓励持有枪支。 “我支持人们在公共场所持有枪支，而不仅仅是家中。” 他在采访中还抨击了当代的好莱坞，2024 年告诉《纽约时报》，对于电影制作人和制片厂来说，“目标不是被解雇”。同年，他告诉《综艺》，“负责任的”喜剧是“无聊透顶的”。 今年在为 Theo Von 做播客时，他谈到好莱坞的政治氛围时说：“确实有一种文化，如果你不同意这些观点，就会被视为坏人。” 2020 年，他被拍到与唐纳德·特朗普握手，并作为嘉宾参加了特朗普 2025 年的就职典礼舞会。去年 4 月，白宫官方社交媒体账号发布了一张照片，显示沃恩和特朗普在椭圆形办公室合影，配文是一张恶搞版的《婚礼傲客》海报。 2024 年，沃恩多年来的第一部电视剧《坏猴子》在 Apple 播出，一位评论家说它“并不差”，第二季将于今年晚些时候上映。 尽管如此，今天的沃恩与我们记忆中那个令人印象深刻的男主角相去甚远，那个机智、举止随意的魅力人物。在 2024 年《时代》杂志的一篇专访中，作家描述与他交谈的经历是“最奇怪的明星采访之一”，并说这位演员将对话变成了“自助指南”。其中也有点老派沃恩的影子。他开玩笑地对《好莱坞报道者》说，关于他的《坏猴子》中与他合作的猴子，“我们合不来”和“我再也不会和它合作了”。 文斯·沃恩在 AppleTV+ 喜剧剧《坏猴子》中的一个场景。 还没有人问过猴子她是什么感觉。 还没有人问过猴子她是什么感觉。
