title: China protests after Japanese premier sends monetary offering to war-linked Yasukuni shrine
summary: Aamir Latif and Riyaz ul Khaliq 19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a monetary offering Monday to the war-linked Yasukuni shrine in Tokyo, prompting “strong protests” from China, according to
content:
Aamir Latif and Riyaz ul Khaliq

19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a monetary offering Monday to the war-linked Yasukuni shrine in Tokyo, prompting “strong protests” from China, according to local media.

The shrine has long been a source of diplomatic friction between Japan and its neighbors, including China.

Takaichi sent the offering out of her own pocket for the shrine’s autumn festival, Kyodo News reported.

Takaichi, as the leader of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, also sent a "masakaki" ritual offering of evergreen twigs on Saturday.

Land Minister Tatsunori Ibayashi and the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's Election Strategy Committee Chairperson Nishimura Yasutoshi separately visited the shrine, which honors "convicted war criminals" along with millions of war dead.

Previous visits to the shrine by Japanese leaders have prompted strong criticism from China and South Korea. Japan occupied a wide area of China by the end of World War II, and South Korea was under Japanese colonial rule between 1910 and 1945.

China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Beijing “firmly opposes and strongly condemns” the “negative moves” by Japan.

Beijing has “lodged serious and strong protests with the Japanese side,” Mao told reporters in Beijing.

“The war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarist war of aggression,” Mao said, recalling that it “honors 14 convicted Class A war criminals responsible for Japan's aggression.”

“Japanese leaders and politicians, despite knowing this quite well, still pay respect to the war shrine. This reveals their deep-seated wrong view on historical issues and malicious intention to erase the criminal record of those war criminals, reverse the verdict on aggression and clear the path for remilitarization,” Mao alleged.

Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Mao said Beijing calls on Japan to “recognize history, repent for historical crimes, stop the retrogressive moves on historical issues and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the wider world with concrete actions.”

Ties between Tokyo and Beijing have been strained since last November following Takaichi's comments suggesting that an attack on Taiwan could prompt a response by Japan's Self-Defense Forces in support of the US.

China considers Taiwan its breakaway province to be unified with the country, while Taiwan insists on its independence.

title: Madagascar Marks One Year Since Uprising As Russia's Influence Grows
summary: _Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through
content:
_Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through closer military ties and weapons deliveries, while researchers have identified Moscow's interest in a strategic Indian Ocean port. Many of the political reforms demanded by protesters, however, remain unfinished._

Randrianirina was sworn in as president of the Refoundation of Madagascar on 17 October 2025, after a month of Gen Z protests demanding water, electricity, justice and transparency culminated in the ousting of Rajoelina.

[Russia](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/russia/) was quick to engage with the new leadership. Just four days after taking office, Randrianirina met the Russian ambassador in the Malagasy capital, [Antananarivo](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/antananarivo/).

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/) for the latest headlines

What followed was a rapid expansion of Moscow's presence on the island, researchers say.

An investigation published last month by [All Eyes On Wagner](https://alleyesonwagner.org/), a project that tracks Russian influence and security operations, traced the development of military, political and economic networks in [Madagascar](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/madagascar/) in the months after Randrianirina's inauguration.

"Madagascar has historical ties with Russia," explained Lou Osborn, co-author of the report.

"And Russia has had a discreet foothold on the island since the 2018 elections. But what is very striking is the speed with which the GRU [Russian military intelligence] has extended its networks in the country, through Africa Corps, African Initiative and various other activities."

[A year after Madagascar's Gen Z protests and Rajoelina's ouster, little promised change](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20261012-a-year-after-madagascar-s-gen-z-protests-and-rajoelina-s-ouster-little-promised-change)

A lightning offensive

The Russian presence soon became more concrete.

On 20 December 2025, two months after Randrianirina took office, a flight carrying 40 men led by Russian intelligence general [Andrey Averyanov](https://www.opensanctions.org/entities/Q100742758/) landed in Madagascar.

The investigation cites information collected by the Russian investigative unit of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. Averyanov is described by the researchers as the suspected supervisor of Africa Corps, the Russian paramilitary organisation that succeeded the Wagner group.

Malagasy authorities confirmed that same month that Africa Corps instructors were in the country training its military.

Then came the equipment. Helicopters, tanks, trucks, drones and rifles arrived in multiple shipments presented as donations, with deliveries continuing until April, the researchers said.

Averyanov also appeared at increasingly senior levels of the relationship.

In February, he was seen at a meeting in [Moscow](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/moscow/) between Russia's deputy prime minister and Madagascar's armed forces minister. Two weeks later, he was part of the delegation that welcomed Randrianirina on an official visit to the Russian capital.

The push has gone beyond military cooperation. Alongside Africa Corps, the researchers point to African Initiative, a Russian news agency with links to the state, as a key part of Moscow's influence campaign in Madagascar.

The agency has sought to reach young people through prizes and sporting events. It has also supported local media in exchange for coverage of Russian-Malagasy relations and organised trips to Moscow for media figures and influencers.

[Madagascar's wave of disappearances exposes 'deeper institutional failings'](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260720-madagascar-s-wave-of-disappearances-exposes-deeper-institutional-failings)

Influence at the top

Russia has also developed ties with senior Malagasy figures, including members of the political establishment who have remained influential despite last year's change of power, the investigation found.

"We are seeing figures from the old guard return," Osborn said. "These people have gained influence. And for some of them there is a kind of opportunism in playing the Russian card."

Among them is National Assembly speaker Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko, whom the investigation identifies as Moscow's most prominent supporter in Madagascar.

His connections with Russia have been fostered through his role as president of the African Judo Union. He confirmed the arrival of Africa Corps personnel and has spoken frequently about cooperation between the two countries.

Prime Minister Mamitiana Rajaonarison is also described as pro-Russian. A former head of Samifin, Madagascar's financial intelligence unit, he was involved in negotiations with Sber, Russia's main bank, which is under international sanctions, the investigation said.

Ny Hasina Andriamanjato, meanwhile, is a Russian-speaking former foreign minister whom the investigation places in former president Rajoelina's circle. He was appointed Madagascar's ambassador to Russia in May.

[Madagascar charts new course with France, after meeting Putin in Moscow](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260225-madagascar-charts-a-new-course-with-france-after-putin-meeting-in-moscow)

Gateway to the Indian Ocean

Sitting at the entrance to the Mozambique Channel, Madagascar offers access to shipping routes linking southern Africa, the [Middle East](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/middle-east/) and the [Indian Ocean](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/indian-ocean/).

"Madagascar can give the Russians a sought-after access point to the Indian Ocean," Osborn said. "Potential access for their shadow fleet [of ships used to evade Western sanctions]."

Much of the attention has centred on the port of Antsiranana, also known as Diego-Suarez, at Madagascar's northern tip. A Russian delegation visited in April, and the following month Madagascar and Russia announced a joint economic zone, with fuel storage as its first project.

The authors of the investigation say the port's potential goes much further. They compare Diego-Suarez with Tartus, Russia's naval base in [Syria](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/syria/), arguing that its location could eventually make it a major military and economic logistics hub.

But the interest is not only military. "They are building a logistics platform and an information platform in Madagascar, but also setting up financial infrastructure, which is developing as in [Togo](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/togo/), with the A7 system," Osborn said.

A7 is a Russian cross-border payments network designed to allow international transactions outside conventional Western banking channels. The investigation says such a system could be used in Madagascar to finance arms deliveries, economic projects, security services and other areas of Russian cooperation.

Osborn sees a pattern in which Africa Corps and Russian military intelligence establish a foothold first, with the financial infrastructure following close behind to support business, potential arms sales and payments to Russian personnel.

"It didn't happen like that in [Mali](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/mali/), [Burkina Faso](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/burkina-faso/) or [Niger](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/niger/)," she said. "In fact, we hadn't seen Russia so firmly rooted since the [Central African Republic](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/central-african-republic/)."

[How Moscow is reinventing its influence machine across Africa](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20250819-how-moscow-is-reinventing-its-influence-machine-across-africa)

New words, old practices

Meanwhile, questions remain over how much has changed for the people of Madagascar. The authorities that emerged from last year's uprising have themselves faced accusations of repressing Gen Z activists, six of whom were arrested in April.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

"There has certainly been a political break since the previous regime fell," political scientist Ketakandriana Rafitoson, vice-chair of anti-corruption organisation Transparency International, told RFI. "But I would say the vocabulary has changed more than the practices."

Randrianirina's administration has promised to overhaul the state, strengthen national sovereignty and forge a new relationship with citizens. But Rafitoson argues that the concentration of power, weak checks and balances, impunity and a lack of transparency persist.

"That is why today I would speak of a real political revolution, but an institutional 'refoundation' that remains largely unfinished."

[Africa's Gen Z unrest shows 'generational divide' between people and politicians](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20251205-africa-s-gen-z-unrest-shows-generational-divide-between-people-and-politicians)

While changing political practices built up over decades can take time, Rafitoson said this could not justify a lack of progress. "The victims of last year's violence are still waiting for justice," she said.

For [the young people who drove the protests](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20251101-madagascar-s-gen-z-uprising-as-told-by-three-young-protesters), there has been one significant shift. Gen Z has established itself as a political force capable of mobilising, shaping its own message and putting issues on the national agenda, Rafitoson said.

"But being heard does not yet mean having power."

Some young activists now speak of betrayal as they see practices they fought against beginning to reappear. That frustration is also rooted in how little influence they have gained since helping force political change, Rafitoson said.

"They were powerful enough to help bring down a regime, but they have not gained the same influence over decision-making in the transition."

_This article draws on reporting from [this story](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260924-madagascar-comment-la-russie-cherche-%C3%A0-s-imposer-dans-l-oc%C3%A9an-indien) and [this interview](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-afrique-midi/20260925-un-an-apr%C3%A8s-l-insurrection-%C3%A0-madagascar-une-r%C3%A9volution-r%C3%A9elle-mais-une-refondation-institutionnelle-inachev%C3%A9e) by RFI's French service._

BEIJING (Reuters) -- China's Commerce Ministry said on Monday it would set export controls on tunnel boring machines, a key piece of equipment for construction in neighboring India.

India remains heavily dependent on imported tunnel boring machines, underscoring the country's long-standing struggle to build domestic manufacturing capacity. China is among the key suppliers of tunneling and other boring equipment used in metro rail and highway construction.

China's Commerce Ministry said export operators would need to apply for a license in accordance with provisions of export control law and regulations on the export control of dual-use items.

Advertisement

The restrictions go into effect on Nov. 18.

It also said it would adjust export control measures for drone-related items and dredgers, part of updates to the country's dual-use items exports list.

# 中国经济增速高于预期 国内仍面临棘手难题

3 小时前 3 小时前
今年夏季，中国经济增速略有回升：第三季度同比增长4.5%。这主要归功于外贸。中国国内则继续面临巨大的问题，特别是房地产危机的持续。

高科技产品出口强劲的同时，中国国内消费持续疲弱 图像来源: Imaginechina/Sipa USA/picture alliance

广告

（德国之声中文网）中国国家统计局周一（10月19日）宣布，第三季度，世界第二大经济体GDP同比增长4.5%。这一增速略高于此前外界预期。

第二季度，中国的GDP增长还仅为4.3%，是三年来最低水平。中国今年的官方增长目标是4.5-5%。去年，中国官方数据显示，达到了5%的预设目标。德新社指出，世界三分之一的经济增长来自于中国，但中国国内状况却面临[棘手的难题](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%87%BA%E5%8F%A3%E6%9A%B4%E5%A2%9E%E6%B6%88%E8%B4%B9%E7%96%B2%E8%BD%AF-%E7%BB%8F%E6%B5%8E%E9%9A%90%E5%BF%A7%E9%9A%BE%E5%8C%96%E8%A7%A3/a-79659242)。

中国国家统计局发言人毛盛勇对实现今年的增长目标表示乐观。对于第二季度增长乏力，他给出的解释是中东局势带来的油价状况。他同时预期第四季度会有改善。

毛盛勇表示：“也要看到，国际环境复杂多变，国内需求不足问题仍较突出，经济稳中向好基础尚需巩固。”

## 出口加速 贸易关系紧张的担忧加剧

中国经济发展仍十分不平衡。[外贸保持繁荣](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%BE%B7%E8%AF%AD%E5%AA%92%E4%BD%93%E5%87%BA%E5%8F%A3%E6%BF%80%E5%A2%9E%E4%B9%9F%E6%98%AF%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E8%BD%AF%E8%82%8B/a-79682218)：今年前九个月，中国海关数据显示，出口同比增长21.3%。9月的增长率甚至达到36.3%。特别是科技产品如半导体及人工智能电子产品的国际需求强劲，推动了贸易增长。

ITC市场分析师Andy Ji向路透社表示：“高科技产品、芯片、电动汽车及其出口价值反映出工业现代化的竞争实力。这一竞争力是真实存在的，并且持续增长。”

专家表示，国外需求继续支撑着中国经济。今年前九个月，中国的贸易顺差约9380亿美元（约合8340亿欧元）。巨额贸易顺差导致中国与重要贸易伙伴关系紧张。特别是欧洲对于中国廉价商品冲击本土制造商的担忧加剧。

工业也仍是经济的一个重要支柱。9月较大型企业的工业增加值同比上升5.5%，8月为5.2%。

## 房地产危机持续

中国国内状况则仍十分困难。尽管9月零售同比增长1.1%，高于预期，消费仍十分疲弱。许多消费者继续捂紧腰包。

投资方面显示出更为明显的疲软。对于新工厂、新设备、新建筑和基础设施的投资低于去年。1-9月，固定资产投资同比下滑7.2%。对于房地产开发的投资更是下跌20.6%。

房地产危机对经济带来多层次的冲击。许多住房价值缩水，房主因此不愿消费。建筑公司的新项目减少，外包工程也减少。与此同时，许多城市财政吃紧。

政府试图推动内需。10月起，中国实施对个人首套住房贷款提供财政贴息。中国官方媒体称，这是国家层面首次为个人房贷贴息。

[国际货币基金组织近日对中国增长预期略有下调](https://dw.com/zh/imf%E6%9C%80%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E9%95%BF%E9%A2%84%E6%9C%9F%E4%B8%8B%E8%B0%83%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E8%87%B345%E4%B8%8A%E8%B0%83%E5%8F%B0%E6%B9%BE%E8%87%B3107/a-79649497)。今年的预测是4.5%，2027年则仅为4%。国际货币基金组织警告中国国内需求疲弱的后果，呼吁加强对消费的扶持。原因是，长期而言，通过推高出口平衡经济所面临的问题，其难度将进一步加大。

（德新社、路透社、法新社）

（ 德国之声中文网）《华尔街日报》周日（10月18日）援引知情人士报道称，克里姆林宫提议在11月18日至19日于中国深圳举行亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会期间，与[特朗普](https://dw.com/zh/%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE/t-69234616)习近平举行对话。

克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）向该报证实，各方正在讨论举行会晤的可能性。他表示：“目前，对于会议本身或其可能的议程，还没有明确的设想。不过，三方都承认，举行这样一场会晤在理论上是有可能的。”

一名美国高级政府官员表示，特朗普尚未同意举行这场峰会，但考虑到特朗普希望兑现[结束战争](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BF%84%E7%BD%97%E6%96%AF%E5%85%A5%E4%BE%B5%E4%B9%8C%E5%85%8B%E5%85%B0/t-60868685)的竞选承诺，他可能对这一提议持开放态度。特朗普曾在竞选时承诺，要在新任期的“第一日”结束战争。

该报援引知情人士透露的信息称，[俄罗斯](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BF%84%E7%BD%97%E6%96%AF/t-40351655)官员已通过外交渠道向中方提出这一想法。中方表示若特朗普同意，自己不会反对。

## 潜在三方峰会对北京而言利弊共存

研究中国问题的分析人士对《华尔街日报》指出，若三方对话在中国举行，对习近平而言，将是提升中国作为外交斡旋力量地位迈出的一大步。华盛顿智库史汀生中心中国项目主任孙韵对该报表示：“中国希望被视为大国之间的枢纽，并有可能成为美国与俄罗斯之间的调解方。”

但也有分析人士认为，三方对话对北京而言也并非毫无弊处：若三国对话在APEC峰会期间举行，中国方面也担心，这场会谈可能喧宾夺主，冲淡北京借助峰会展示自身在亚太地区影响力的计划。分析人士还称习近平正试图在支持普京与维护对欧洲关之间维持谨慎平衡。此种三方会晤也可能使中国更直接地卷入乌克兰战争，并引发欧洲国家的反弹

## 美国中期选举在即 与莫斯科关系出现转向

该报随后援引一名了解相关情况的俄罗斯前情报官员的话报道称，普京是在10月9日与特朗普的一次电话交谈中提出了这一想法。[两国之间的柴油交易](https://dw.com/zh/%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE%E5%86%8D%E6%AC%A1%E9%80%86%E8%BD%AC%E5%AF%B9%E4%BF%84%E5%88%B6%E8%A3%81-%E5%AE%A3%E5%B8%83%E4%B8%8E%E6%99%AE%E4%BA%AC%E8%BE%BE%E6%88%90%E6%9F%B4%E6%B2%B9%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE/a-79626933)也是在此次通话中达成的。

特朗普决定豁免对俄制裁之际，距离他宣布美俄达成柴油交易也仅过去一周 图像来源: Dmitry Azarov/Kommersant Photo/Sipa USA/picture alliance

特朗普于同一日宣布同意俄罗斯向美国和全球市场供应俄罗斯柴油，以期降低全球能源价格。

分析人士对路透社指出，美国中期选举临近，且美国民众已因美以对伊战争等因素导致的生活成本上升而承压。若对俄制裁生效，可能进一步推高油价，从而对共和党中期选举的选情造成不利影响。

一周后，特朗普再以国家利益为由签署豁免令，[暂缓实施国会此前通过的新一轮对俄制裁措施](https://dw.com/zh/%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE%E7%AD%BE%E7%BD%B2%E8%B1%81%E5%85%8D%E4%BB%A4-%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E5%AF%B9%E4%BF%84%E5%A4%9A%E9%A1%B9%E5%88%B6%E8%A3%81%E9%99%90%E5%88%B6%E5%8F%8A%E5%85%B3%E7%A8%8E/a-79686658)。此举被批评者称是在向普京让步，背弃乌克兰及欧洲盟友。

## 特朗普对泽连斯基不满

上周日（10月18日）俄罗斯当局发布消息称[圣彼得堡遭到大规模乌克兰无人机袭击](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BF%84%E4%B9%8C%E6%88%98%E5%86%B5%E5%9C%A3%E5%BD%BC%E5%BE%97%E5%A0%A1%E6%B2%B9%E5%BA%93%E9%81%AD%E6%97%A0%E4%BA%BA%E6%9C%BA%E5%87%BB%E4%B8%AD%E8%B5%B7%E7%81%AB/a-79692325)。袭击发生后，特朗普在社交媒体平台Truth Social上发文[批评泽连斯基将俄罗斯柴油炼油厂作为打击目标](https://dw.com/zh/%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE%E4%BF%83%E4%B9%8C%E5%85%8B%E5%85%B0%E6%8D%A2%E6%80%BB%E7%BB%9F%E6%B3%BD%E8%BF%9E%E6%96%AF%E5%9F%BA%E5%BC%80%E5%87%BA%E5%AF%B9%E7%AD%89%E5%81%9C%E7%81%AB%E6%9D%A1%E4%BB%B6/a-79633849)“他很清楚这些袭击严重损害了全球柴油市场，也波及到了美国”，特朗普称其“根本不想结束这场战争，而且他可能从一开始就不想结束”。

特朗普还为其暂缓制裁俄罗斯的决定解释缘由，称“不希望采取任何可能导致俄罗斯愚蠢地退出谈判桌的行动”。

## 特朗普和泽连斯基赞扬谈判取得进展

[Video 6](https://hlsvod.dw.com/i/vps/webvideos/CHI/2025/DWVG/DWVGCHI251229_TrumpUkraineWIDE_01SMW_,AVC_480x270,AVC_512x288,AVC_640x360,AVC_960x540,AVC_1280x720,AVC_1920x1080,.mp4.csmil/master.m3u8)

01:55

《华尔街日报》分析称，莫斯科认为潜在的美中俄三方对话有助于巩固俄罗斯作为全球大国俱乐部成员的地位。这种会谈形式还将欧洲排除在外，克里姆林宫视欧洲为俄罗斯在乌克兰取得胜利的主要障碍。该报引述俄罗斯前情报官员的话写道，普京对这种三方会谈机制抱有宏大、但并不现实的设想，希望将其打造为第二次“雅尔塔会议”。

## 将乌克兰排除在外或为台海问题释放信号

《华尔街日报》进一步分析若美中俄三国领导人共同商讨乌克兰问题，会谈却不邀请乌克兰参加，将开创前所未有的先例，并引发欧洲及其他地区的警觉，比如人们可能加剧这样一种担忧，即[台湾](https://dw.com/zh/2026%E5%B9%B4%E5%8F%B0%E6%B9%BE%E5%9C%B0%E6%96%B9%E9%80%89%E4%B8%BE/t-79656866)有朝一日，尤其是中国未放弃武统的背景下，也可能在类似的场合被拿来谈判。

title: Workers rally in Taipei for pension reform, profit-sharing rules - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 台北工人集会要求养老金改革和利润分享规则 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月19日电 在台湾最近一波罢工和罢工授权投票浪潮中，数百名工人周一在总统府外集会，要求提高工资、增加雇主养老金缴款和更明确的利润分享规则。代表台湾各地数十个工会的参与者聚集在凯达格兰大道上，然后穿过附近的街道经过立法院，在午后的阳光下返回大道。 ##年金改革 台湾团结会主席何政家在集会前向记者发表讲话
content:
中新社台北10月19日电 在台湾最近一波罢工和罢工授权投票浪潮中，数百名工人周一在总统府外集会，要求提高工资、增加雇主养老金缴款和更明确的利润分享规则。

代表台湾各地数十个工会的参与者聚集在凯达格兰大道上，然后穿过附近的街道经过立法院，在午后的阳光下返回大道。

## 养老金改革

台联主席何政家在集会前对记者发表讲话时特别谈到了他认为过时的劳工养老金制度。

2005年7月推出的新劳动养老金制度由个人职工退休金账户组成，要求雇主每月向该账户缴存不少于雇员工资的6%。

员工可以自愿额外缴纳 6% 以增加储蓄金额。只要缴费至少15年，基金的累积总额就可以在退休时一次性领取或作为每月年金领取。

Ho 认为，现在是提高雇主 6% 最低义务的时候了，他说这个义务太低，无法确保足够的退休储蓄，而增加义务将有助于弥补 21 年来缴款不足的情况。
他说：“我们希望先提高到9%，然后逐步提高到15%。”他指出，在旧养老金制度下，雇主每名工人的年度退休费用估计约为工资的12%。

政府数据显示，截至 2026 年 7 月，约有 787 万名工人在新制度下缴款，而截至 2025 年 12 月，估计有 115,000 人完全在旧制度下缴款。

新的劳工养老金制度是台湾大多数工人有资格享受的两项退休计划之一。

另一个是劳动保险制度下的“养老待遇”。目前劳保费为工资的11.5%，每月上限为新台币45,800元，雇主缴纳70%。

由于工资上限相对较低，保险制度下的退休金一般限制在每月900美元以下。

这两个系统均由劳动部劳动保险局负责管理。

何先生还敦促修改《劳动标准法》第29条，为向员工分配公司利润制定更明确的要求，并表示经济收益应该惠及科技行业以外的工人。

## 劳工骚乱中的罢工投票

此前，玻璃制造商旭硝子和零食生产商快快公司的罢工最近结束，中华电信和美国存储芯片制造商美光科技公司桃园工厂的工会也进行了罢工授权投票。
中华电信工会主席邓克廉表示，桃园及高雄分公司已通过罢工授权投票，其他分公司将陆续举行投票。

该工会在滕称公司利润创纪录的情况下发起了要求加薪的投票，该工会在 26 个分支机构拥有约 20,000 名会员，几乎代表了公司所有员工。

滕说：“罢工只是一种手段，不是我们的目标。”他敦促管理层“积极回应”工人的要求，同时指出年底前不太可能发生罢工。

Paul Chen，中华电话

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) Hundreds of workers rallied outside the Presidential Office on Monday, demanding higher wages, increased employer pension contributions and clearer profit-sharing rules, amid a recent wave of strikes and strike authorization votes across Taiwan.

Participants representing dozens of labor unions from across Taiwan gathered on Ketagalan Boulevard before marching through nearby streets past the Legislative Yuan and returning to the boulevard under the afternoon sun.

## Pension reform

Speaking to reporters before the rally, Ho Cheng-chia (何政家), chairman of the Taiwan Solidarity Front Confederation of Trade Unions, focused specifically on what he felt was an outdated labor pension system.

Introduced in July 2005, the new labor pension system consists of retirement accounts for individual workers and requires employers to contribute at least 6 percent of an employee's salary to the account every month.

The employee can voluntarily contribute an additional 6 percent to increase the amount saved. The total built up in the fund can be collected in a lump sum or as a monthly annuity upon retirement as long as contributions have been made for at least 15 years.

Ho argued that it was time to increase the employer's minimum 6 percent obligation, saying it was too low to ensure adequate retirement savings and that an increase would help make up for 21 years of insufficient contributions.

"We hope to raise it to 9 percent first and then gradually to 15 percent," he said, noting that employers' annual retirement costs per worker under the old pension system were estimated at around 12 percent of wages.

Government figures show that about 7.87 million workers had contributions made under the new system as of July 2026, while an estimated 115,000 were exclusively under the old system as of December 2025.

The new labor pension system is one of two retirement plans that most workers in Taiwan qualify for.

The other is the "old-age benefits" under the labor insurance system. The current labor insurance premium is 11.5 percent of salaries, capped at NT$45,800 per month, with employers paying 70 percent.

Because of the relatively low salary cap, retirement benefits under the insurance system are generally limited to under US$900 a month.

Both systems are run by the Bureau of Labor Insurance under the Ministry of Labor.

Ho also urged amendments to Article 29 of the Labor Standards Act to establish clearer requirements for distributing company profits to employees, saying that economic gains should benefit workers beyond the technology sector.

## Strike votes amid labor unrest

The rally followed recently concluded strikes at glassmaker AGC Display Glass Taiwan Inc. and snack producer Kuai Kuai Co., as well as strike authorization votes by unions at Chunghwa Telecom and the Taoyuan operations of U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology Inc.

Chunghwa Telecom Workers' Union Chairman Teng Ke-lien (鄧克亷) said its Taoyuan and Kaohsiung branches had passed strike authorization votes, with other branches set to hold votes in succession.

The union, which launched the vote to demand higher pay amid what Teng described as record company profits, has approximately 20,000 members across 26 branches, representing nearly all company employees.

"Striking is just a means, not our goal," Teng said, urging management to "respond positively" to workers' demands, while noting that a walkout was unlikely before year-end.

Paul Chen, a Chunghwa Telecom engineer with more than five years' service, said he took leave to join the protest despite concerns about possible retaliation.

"I'm still a little worried, but I think we need to fight for our demands and let the company hear our real voices," Chen, who spoke under a pseudonym, told CNA.

Under Article 35 of Taiwan's Labor Union Act, employers are barred from retaliating against workers for participating in union activities or labor disputes.

## General strike call

Speaking at the rally, Taoyuan Confederation of Trade Unions Chairwoman Shih Shu-hua (施淑華) called for a nationwide general strike ahead of the 2028 elections if pension reform remained stalled.

"We must show these political parties that workers cannot be pushed around," she said.

Responding to the protest, the Ministry of Labor said it remained "open" to raising employer pension contributions but stressed that changes required "careful evaluation."

It also highlighted environmental, social and governance (ESG) assessment incentives for listed companies that voluntarily increase their contribution rates.

The ministry also pointed to minimum wage reviews and collective bargaining incentives to promote pay raises and profit-sharing, urging employers to consider raising existing employees' salaries as the monthly minimum wage increases from NT$29,500 (US$908.05) this year to NT$30,900 in 2027.

(By Sunny Lai)

# Typhoon Champi to turn away from Taiwan, will still bring heavy rain

10/19/2026 07:53 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

CNA graphic

Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) Typhoon Champi will turn northward earlier than previously forecast, sparing Taiwan a direct hit but still bringing heavy rain to the north of the country on Friday and Saturday, according to the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

CWA forecaster Cheng Chieh-jen (鄭傑仁) told CNA Typhoon Champi had strengthened and increased in size over the past 12 hours, and as of Monday afternoon was packing sustained winds of 198 kilometers per hour near its center.

Due to the weakening of a Pacific high-pressure system, however, the storm is now expected to turn northward earlier than initially forecast, likely around Japan's Ishigaki Island, Cheng said.

As Champi brushes past northeastern Taiwan, it will likely be a strong "moderate" typhoon or weak "intense" typhoon per the CWA's classification system, which defines the latter as having sustained winds above 184 kph, Cheng said.

Based on current forecasts, the CWA could issue a sea warning on Wednesday night or Thursday at the earliest, and a land warning on Thursday evening or Friday, Cheng said.

The warning will likely apply to northern and eastern Taiwan, with the north and Yilan, in particular, facing possible heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, he added.

As for this week's weather, Cheng said the CWA forecast mostly cloudy to clear skies on Tuesday, with high temperatures of 30-32 degrees Celsius in the eastern half of the country and 31-34 degrees in the west.

On Wednesday, a northeasterly wind system will bring slightly cooler temperatures to the north, with daytime highs reaching 27-30 degrees and a chance of scattered showers in Yilan and areas north of Hsinchu, Cheng said.

As the typhoon approaches on Thursday, there will continue to be scattered rain showers in Yilan and northern Taiwan. Those areas could see heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, while scattered showers are forecast for other regions, Cheng said.

As Typhoon Champi weakens and moves away from Taiwan on Sunday, cloudy to clear weather conditions will prevail in most regions, with the exception of lingering rain showers in the east and on the Hengchun Peninsula in the south, Cheng said.

(By Chang Hsiung-feng and Matthew Mazzetta)

title: Australia gets the ball rolling on medium-range air defense
zh_title: 澳大利亚在中程防空方面取得进展
summary: 澳大利亚珀斯——为了保护整个大陆，澳大利亚只有一个团的 NASAMS 短程防空系统。堪培拉认识到这还不够，因此为澳大利亚陆军启动了中程陆基防空解决方案的正式招标。国防部于 10 月 13 日启动了该项目的行业招标，命名为 Project Land 6504。这一潜在交易已经引起了全球的兴趣，来自欧洲、以色列、韩国、土耳其和美国的供应商都关注着澳大利亚的需求。一个主要动机
content:
澳大利亚珀斯——为了保护整个大陆，澳大利亚只有一个团的 NASAMS 短程防空系统。堪培拉认识到这还不够，因此为澳大利亚陆军启动了中程陆基防空解决方案的正式招标。国防部于 10 月 13 日启动了该项目的行业招标，命名为 Project Land 6504。这一潜在交易已经引起了全球的兴趣，来自欧洲、以色列、韩国、土耳其和美国的供应商都关注着澳大利亚的需求。填补澳大利亚国防缺口的一个主要动机是中国不断增强的军事实力。令许多人震惊的是，中国人民解放军于 2025 年初派出海军特混舰队绕行澳大利亚，然后中国于今年 7 月向南太平洋发射了一枚洲际弹道导弹。由于中国拥有世界上最多样化的导弹库，澳大利亚知道它需要更好的防御。因此，Land 6504 正在寻找一种防御系统，能够在飞行末期击落弹道导弹，并应对亚音速吸气威胁。
《2026 年国防战略》将导弹防御列为优先事项，呼吁“通过投资导弹发射器和弹药，并将其与澳大利亚国防军的指挥和控制系统集成，加速引入中程、陆基、主动导弹防御。”招标书中写道，这个设想的现成系统预计将具有“经过验证的能力”，为国家综合系统做出贡献。然而，资金是一个长期存在的问题，因为 AUKUS 核动力潜艇吸收了可用的国防资金。但也许最大的风险是这个澳大利亚项目的进展速度之快。供应商的最终选择将于 2027 年底完成。解决方案是在 2029 年中期在护身军刀演习中进行实弹射击，并在 2030 年代初期实现初步作战能力。重要的是，远征防空系统必须与 CEA Technologies 的雷达以及澳大利亚洛克希德·马丁公司正在开发的联合空战管理系统集成。由于时间限制，堪培拉正在同时寻求直接商业销售和美国对外军售（FMS）途径。招标的时机可能会增加非美国导弹供应商的机会，因为美国在与伊朗的冲突中消耗了大量导弹后，正在努力解决弹匣耗尽的问题。国会研究服务部最近的一份报告警告说：“有限的美国
工业基础产能需要在满足 FMS 订单和补充美国库存之间进行权衡。 FMS 交付延迟可能会导致取消，从而可能影响美国和合作伙伴的互操作性和集成。”不过，还有其他选择。例如，澳大利亚可以在其现有的 NASAMS 中添加 AMRAAM-ER 增程导弹。康斯伯格澳大利亚公司董事总经理约翰·弗莱告诉《防务新闻》：“我们肯定对该计划感兴趣。我认为 NASAMS 架构的伟大之处在于康斯伯格和雷神公司正在将其发展为全谱防空系统。”在其他地方，澳大利亚洛克希德·马丁公司于 6 月利用“宙斯盾”作战系统和 CEA 雷达从拖车发射器发射了一枚 SM-2 导弹。这展示了混合防空系统如何利用澳大利亚现有的组件。

【原文 English Original】
PERTH, Australia — To protect a whole continent, Australia has only a regiment’s worth of NASAMS short-range air defense systems. Recognizing this is not nearly enough, Canberra has launched a formal tender for a medium-range, ground-based air defense solution for the Australian Army. The Department of Defence launched an industry solicitation for the project, christened Project Land 6504, on Oct. 13. The potential deal has already attracted interest globally, with vendors from Europe, Israel, South Korea, Turkey and the United States eying the requirement Down Under. A primary motivation for filling the gaping hole in Australian defenses is China’s rising military prowess. Alarming many, the People’s Liberation Army sent a naval task group to circumnavigate Australia in early 2025, and then China fired an intercontinental ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July this year. With China possessing the world’s most diverse missile arsenal, Australia knows it needs better defenses. Land 6504 is therefore looking for a defensive system capable of shooting down ballistic missiles in their terminal phase of flight, as well as address subsonic air-breathing threats. The National Defence Strategy 2026 prioritized missile defense, calling for “accelerated introduction of medium-range, ground-based, active missile defense through investment in missile launchers and munitions and integrating them with the Australian Defence Force’s command-and-control systems.” This envisioned off-the-shelf system is expected to be a “proven capability,” contributing to a national, integrated system, the solicitation reads. Money is a perennial problem, however, as AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines soak up available defense funds. But perhaps the greatest risk is the lightning speed at which this Australian project is moving. Final selection of the vendor is to occur by the end of 2027. The solution is to perform live-firing in Exercise Talisman Saber in mid-2029, and an initial operational capability achieved in the early 2030s. Importantly, the expeditionary air-defense system must integrate with radars from CEA Technologies and the Joint Air Battle Management System being developed by Lockheed Martin Australia. Because of the time constraints, Canberra is pursuing direct commercial sale and U.S. Foreign Military Sales (FMS) avenues simultaneously. The timing of the tender may boost the chances of non-American missile suppliers, as the U.S. grapples with depleted magazines after expending large amounts of missiles in its conflict with Iran. A recent Congressional Research Service report warned , “Finite U.S. industrial base capacity introduces trade-offs between filling FMS orders and replenishing U.S. stockpiles. FMS delivery delays may result in cancellations, potentially affecting U.S. and partner interoperability and integration.” Other options are available, however. For example, Australia could add AMRAAM-ER extended-range missiles to its existing NASAMS. John Fry, managing director of Kongsberg Australia, told Defense News : “We’re definitely interested in that program. I think the great thing with the NASAMS architecture is Kongsberg and Raytheon are evolving that into full-spectrum air defense.” Elsewhere, Lockheed Martin Australia fired an SM-2 missile from a trailer launcher in June, utilizing the Aegis combat system and a CEA radar. This demonstrated how a hybrid air defense system can make use of components already available in Australia.

title: Volta doubles Springer rare earths, eyes 2027 study
zh_title: Volta 将 Springer 稀土产量翻倍，着眼 2027 年研究
summary: Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) 已将其位于安大略省的 Springer 矿床的指示稀土资源量增加了一倍多，随着 2027 年经济评估的进展，该项目按测量和指示资源吨位跻身北美五个最大的项目之列。更新后的矿产资源估算将指示资源量增加了 116%，达到 1.224 亿吨，总稀土氧化物 (TREO) 品位为 0.59%。另外 1.975 亿吨品位 0.53% TREO 被归类为推断。独立准备的估算还包括该项目的第一次镓资源评估。 “我们相信
content:
Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) 已将其位于安大略省的 Springer 矿床的指示稀土资源量增加了一倍多，随着 2027 年经济评估的进展，该项目按测量和指示资源吨位跻身北美五个最大的项目之列。更新后的矿产资源估算将指示资源量增加了 116%，达到 1.224 亿吨，总稀土氧化物 (TREO) 品位为 0.59%。另外 1.975 亿吨品位 0.53% TREO 被归类为推断。独立准备的估算还包括该项目的第一次镓资源评估。 Volta 总裁兼首席执行官凯雷姆·乌斯梅兹 (Kerem Usenmez) 在一份声明中表示：“我们相信，在市场为中国以外的供应支付溢价之际，斯普林格正在成为北美少数几个大型、可通过公路获取的磁铁稀土和潜在镓来源之一。”萨德伯里首席执行官表示，萨德伯里在“披萨外卖区”举办了大型稀土项目，此次扩张正值西方政府寻求减少对中国的依赖，中国在全球稀土加工和镓生产中占据主导地位。这两种商品都具有重要的战略意义，稀土用于电动汽车和风力涡轮机的永磁体，而镓对于某些半导体技术至关重要。
高品位扩张 Springer 表示，高品位核心产量增长了 140%，达到 2,760 万吨，TREO 品位为 1%，预计金属净收入为每吨 384 加元（272 美元），相当于原地金属总价值 106 亿加元（75 亿美元）。推断的高品位核心产量增加了九倍，达到 2,670 万吨，TREO 品位为 0.94%，估计金属净收入为每吨 333 加元（236 美元），或原地总价值 89 亿加元（63 亿美元）。该区域仍然开放以进行扩张。该矿床在其指示资源范围内还含有估计 4,427 吨原位镓，其中包括 1,480 万吨的高品位区域，平均每吨 56 克。镓可以提供额外的收入来源，尽管 Volta 尚未确定这种金属是否可以经济地回收。该公司正在进行冶金研究，以评估回收方法和潜在的商业可行性。磁铁稀土（钕、镨、镝和铽）约占指定资源稀土氧化物总含量的 22.4%，Volta 表示这一比例是北美最高的之一。北美稀土项目按测量和指示吨位排名，包括报告的储量。推断吨位单独显示以供上下文参考，不用于排名。 （标普全球市场情报数据库，2025 年 5 月；施普林格于 2026 年 9 月 30 日 MRE。
根据该公司引用的标准普尔全球市场情报数据，按实测和指示资源吨位计算，施普林格在北美稀土项目中排名第五。不过，该排名衡量的是资源规模而不是经济潜力，也没有考虑品位、冶金、开发成本或项目成熟度的差异。发展前景 Springer 位于萨德伯里以东约 70 公里处，受益于直接的高速公路、现场电力以及附近的天然气和铁路基础设施。该矿床的低剥采率也可以支持未来的矿山开发，尽管该项目的经济性尚未经过测试。 Volta 计划进行额外钻探以扩大和提炼资源，同时推进稀土冶金工作

【原文 English Original】
Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) has more than doubled the indicated rare earth resource at its Springer deposit in Ontario, placing the project among North America’s five largest by measured and indicated resource tonnage as it advances toward an economic assessment in 2027. The updated mineral resource estimate increased indicated resources by 116% to 122.4 million tonnes grading 0.59% total rare earth oxides (TREO). A further 197.5 million tonnes grading 0.53% TREO are classified as inferred. The independently prepared estimate also includes the project’s first gallium resource assessment. “We believe Springer is shaping up as one of the few large, road-accessible sources of magnet rare earths, and potentially gallium, in North America, at a time when the market is paying a premium for supply from outside China,” Volta president and CEO Kerem Usenmez said in a statement. Sudbury hosts major rare earth project ‘in a pizza delivery zone,’ CEO says The expansion comes as Western governments seek to reduce their dependence on China, which dominates global rare earth processing and gallium production. Both commodities are strategically important, with rare earths used in permanent magnets for electric vehicles and wind turbines, while gallium is essential to certain semiconductor technologies. High-grade expansion Springer’s indicated high-grade core grew 140% to 27.6 million tonnes grading 1% TREO, with an estimated net metal revenue of C$384 ($272) per tonne, equivalent to C$10.6 billion ($7.5 billion) in gross in-situ metal value. The inferred high-grade core increased ninefold to 26.7 million tonnes grading 0.94% TREO, with an estimated net metal revenue of C$333 per tonne ($236), or C$8.9 billion ($6.3 billion) in gross in-situ value. The zone remains open for expansion. The deposit also contains an estimated 4,427 tonnes of in-situ gallium within its indicated resource, including a higher-grade zone of 14.8 million tonnes averaging 56 grams per tonne. Gallium could provide an additional revenue stream, although Volta has yet to establish whether the metal can be economically recovered. The company is conducting metallurgical studies to assess recovery methods and potential commercial viability. Magnet rare earths — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — account for about 22.4% of the indicated resource’s total rare earth oxide content, a proportion Volta says is among the highest in North America. North American rare earth projects ranked by Measured and Indicated tonnage, including Reserves where reported. Inferred tonnage is shown separately for context and is not used in the ranking. ( S&P Global Market Intelligence database, May 2025; Springer at the September 30, 2026 MRE. ) Springer ranks fifth among North American rare earth projects by combined measured and indicated resource tonnage, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data cited by the company. However, the ranking measures resource size rather than economic potential and does not account for differences in grade, metallurgy, development costs or project maturity. Development outlook Located about 70 km east of Sudbury, Springer benefits from direct highway access, on-site power and nearby natural gas and rail infrastructure. The deposit’s low strip ratio could also support future mine development, although the project’s economics remain untested. Volta plans additional drilling to expand and refine the resource while advancing metallurgical work on rare earth and gallium recovery. The company is targeting a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) in the first half of 2027, which would provide an initial evaluation of potential mining costs, processing requirements and project economics.

title: How Corruption Got This Bad
zh_title: 腐败为何如此严重
summary: “这不是违法的吗？”作为一名前联邦检察官，我经常被问到这个问题。唐纳德·特朗普、他的家人和他的政府成员往往是灵感的源泉。去年，卡塔尔人向美国国防部赠送了一架价值4亿美元的豪华大型喷气式飞机供总统使用，总统计划在离任时将其带到总统图书馆。随后特朗普向卡塔尔提供了类似北约的安全保证。这听起来像是贿赂吗？就在特朗普第二次就职前四天，阿联酋人向特朗普家族的加密业务投资了 5 亿美元。
content:
“这不是违法的吗？”作为一名前联邦检察官，我经常被问到这个问题。唐纳德·特朗普、他的家人和他的政府成员往往是灵感的源泉。去年，卡塔尔人向美国国防部赠送了一架价值4亿美元的豪华大型喷气式飞机供总统使用，总统计划在离任时将其带到总统图书馆。随后特朗普向卡塔尔提供了类似北约的安全保证。这听起来像是贿赂吗？就在特朗普第二次就职前四天，阿联酋人向特朗普家族的加密业务投资了 5 亿美元。四个月后，特朗普批准向他们出售先进的人工智能芯片，但拜登政府因担心这些芯片会落入中国人手中而阻止了这些芯片。同样的问题。但即使我听到“这不是违法吗？”比以前要多得多，这不是一个新问题。前农业部长迈克·埃斯皮 (Mike Espy) 和前弗吉尼亚州州长罗伯特·麦克唐纳 (Robert McDonnell)（民主党和共和党）都从寻求帮助的个人和实体那里收受了丰厚的礼物，并在因此被起诉时成为全国新闻。这肯定是违法的吗？然而，尽管有常识，答案是否定的。埃斯皮和麦克唐纳都没有被追究责任，甚至特朗普看似令人震惊的不当行为也可能不会被起诉。
这是因为从 20 世纪 80 年代开始，最高法院对反腐败法的解释非常狭隘，以至于实际上使彻底的腐败合法化。这些判决使政客的所有行为都超出了检察官的能力范围。这是一个荒谬的结果。但我们生活在法院的世界里。 20 年来，我在美国司法部起诉白领犯罪。我的第一次刑事审判是安然公司。我的最后一位是亨特·拜登。在此期间，我以腐败罪名起诉了参谋长联席会议副主席；巴尔的摩市长；巴尔的摩警察局长；巴尔的摩市州检察官；以及其他数十名政治家、政府雇员、警察和狱警。我曾在司法部和国会山担任领导职务，重点关注腐败问题。我在位于华盛顿的司法部公共廉洁科结束了我在司法部的职业生涯，该部门是起诉全国各地公共腐败的专门部门，直到 2025 年 2 月该部门实际上被关闭。我是被要求驳回针对纽约市长埃里克·亚当斯案件的检察官之一。和公共诚信部的几乎所有同事一样，我拒绝这样做，并于当年离开了该部门。在那段时间里，我经历了最高法院在涉及公职人员的案件中如何限制检察官。
甚至在我职业生涯开始之前，法官们就已经开始削弱联邦反腐败法规，而这个项目在我任职期间加速了。当联邦调查局特工向我提供不当行为的证据时，我经常不得不驳回这些案件，因为我知道我永远无法让指控成立。我服务的时间越长，我的工作就变得越困难。 【亚当·塞尔维尔：特朗普的政治化起诉可能会遇到障碍】最高法院的第一个裁决是1987年判决的麦克纳利诉美国案。在该案中，肯塔基州州长内阁成员、当地商人、肯塔基州民主党前主席从一家与该州有业务往来的保险公司获得了数十万美元的回扣。检察官指控他们剥夺公众的权利

【原文 English Original】
“Isn’t that illegal?” That’s a question I get asked a lot as a former federal prosecutor. Donald Trump, his family, and members of his administration are most often the inspiration. Last year, the Qataris gave the U.S. Defense Department a $400 million luxury jumbo jet for the president’s use, which he plans to take with him to his presidential library when he leaves office. Then Trump gave Qatar NATO-like security guarantees. Does that sound like a bribe? Exactly four days before Trump was inaugurated for the second time, the Emiratis invested $500 million in the Trump-family crypto business. Four months later, Trump green-lighted selling them advanced AI chips, which the Biden administration had blocked out of fear that they would fall into the hands of the Chinese. Same question. But even though I hear “Isn’t that illegal?” a lot more than I used to, it isn’t a new question. Former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy and former Virginia Governor Robert McDonnell, a Democrat and a Republican, both took lavish gifts from individuals and entities seeking their help and made national news when they were prosecuted for it. Surely that was illegal? Common sense notwithstanding, however, the answer is no . Neither Espy nor McDonnell were held accountable, and even Trump’s seemingly egregious misbehavior likely can’t be prosecuted. That’s because starting in the 1980s, the Supreme Court has interpreted anti-corruption laws in ways so narrow as to effectively legalize flat-out corruption. These decisions put whole categories of politicians’ conduct beyond a prosecutor’s reach. It’s an absurd result. But we live in the Court’s world. For 20 years, I prosecuted white-collar crime at the U.S. Department of Justice. My first criminal trial was Enron. My last was Hunter Biden. In between, I prosecuted on corruption charges the vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff; the mayor of Baltimore; the Baltimore police commissioner; the Baltimore City state’s attorney; and dozens of other politicians, government employees, police officers, and prison guards. I served in leadership positions at the Justice Department and on Capitol Hill focused on corruption. I finished my DOJ career in the department’s Public Integrity Section in Washington, the specialized unit that prosecuted public corruption around the country—until February 2025, when it was effectively shut down. I was one of the prosecutors asked to dismiss the case against New York Mayor Eric Adams. Like nearly all my colleagues in Public Integrity, I declined to do so and left the department that year. In all that time, I experienced how the Supreme Court restrained prosecutors in cases involving public officials. Even before the start of my career, the justices had begun to chip away at federal anti-corruption statutes, and this project accelerated during my tenure. When FBI agents brought me evidence of misconduct, I often had to turn the cases away, knowing I’d never be able to make charges stick. The longer I served, the harder my job became. [ Adam Serwer: Trump’s politicized prosecutions may hit a roadblock ] The first of these Supreme Court rulings was McNally v. United States , decided in 1987. In that case, a member of the Kentucky governor’s Cabinet, a local businessman, and a former chair of the Kentucky Democratic Party received hundreds of thousands of dollars in kickbacks from an insurance company that did business with the state. Prosecutors charged them with depriving the public of its right to their “honest services,” a crime under the federal mail- and wire-fraud statutes. The Court reversed their convictions and declared that the public enjoyed no such right. Although federal courts had upheld similar convictions for more than 40 years, the Supreme Court ruled that all those courts had gotten it wrong: It declared that the mail-fraud—and, by implication, the wire-fraud—statute was limited to protecting money and property, not intangible rights such as citizens’ right to good government. Congress reacted swiftly. One year later, a broad bipartisan majority in Congress passed legislation effectively reversing the Court’s decision. But McNally is an outlier in that regard. In 1999, in United States v. Sun-Diamond Growers of California , the Supreme Court reversed the conviction of an agricultural trade association that gave gifts—tickets to the U.S. Open, expensive luggage, even a crystal bowl—to the U.S. secretary of agriculture in the Clinton administration. The Supreme Court held that giving a politician lavish gifts because of his official position was not illegal. Rather than focusing on the conduct at hand, Justice Antonin Scalia, writing for a unanimous Court, spun out a ridiculous hypothetical—that the government’s interpretation of the statute would allow the president to be prosecuted for accepting “replica jerseys given by championship sports teams.” What that claim ignored was the reality that no Justice Department would ever authorize such a prosecution. In Skilling v. United States , decided in 2010, the Supreme Court reversed the conviction of Jeffrey Skilling, a former CEO of Enron Corporation, for conspiring to commit honest-services fraud. I had been one of the prosecutors in Skilling’s trial. Although Skilling was the president of a publicly traded company, not a politician, he was charged with conspiracy to commit honest-services wire fraud for undisclosed self-dealing. Self-dealing is a problem whether the perpetrator is a corporate executive hiding a conflict of interest from shareholders or an elected official hiding one from voters. Except the Supreme Court held that it wasn’t illegal. Confronted with the fact that lower courts had for years upheld honest-services-fraud convictions for undisclosed self-dealing, Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg’s majority opinion noted the “infrequency” of those decisions and how they were not “models of clarity.” That, of course, didn’t mean those decisions were wrong. Remarkably, Ginsburg didn’t even say they were. Instead, she claimed that because bribery and kickbacks were the “basis of most honest-services prosecutions,” that’s what the statute’s application would be limited to. In place of legal analysis, the Court resorted to a game of numbers, and the practical effect was to restrict the number of corruption cases prosecutors could bring under this statute. In perhaps its grossest pro-corruption decision, the Supreme Court in 2016 reversed Robert McDonnell’s conviction. A jury had convicted the former governor on bribery charges for accepting $175,000 in loans and gifts from the CEO of a nutritional-supplement company that wanted Virginia’s public universities to run clinical trials on his product. The Court held that what McDonnell did for the CEO—setting up meetings, hosting events, talking to other elected officials, all to benefit his company—did not qualify as “official acts,” for which McDonnell could be bribed. Chief Justice John Roberts, writing for a unanimous Court, adopted the most restrictive of definitions of official acts , things such as voting in the Senate or in an official committee. The decision leads directly to the question Why would a CEO give a governor that much money if these weren’t official acts? The Supreme Court didn’t offer an answer. Then, in 2024, in Snyder v. United States , the Supreme Court reversed the conviction of the mayor of Portage, Indiana, for accepting $13,000 from a company that got more than $1 million in city contracts. Prosecutors charged him with violating a statute Congress had enacted to protect federal money administered by the states, called “666,” after its numbering in the United States Code. The indictment had charged these payments to the mayor as illegal gratuities, which is what the law calls “illegal gifts.” In reversing his conviction, the Court held that 666 covered only bribery, not gratuities. In that year alone, approximately $1 trillion in federal funds flowed to the states. As Justice Brett Kavanaugh noted in his majority opinion, as many as 19 million state and local officials administer this money. But according to the Supreme Court, there’s nothing wrong with giving them a little something extra for the effort. That same year, the Court decided Trump v. United States , announcing a sweeping and previously unrecognized doctrine of official-acts immunity for former presidents. Whereas the decisions discussed above left prosecutors room to pursue certain kinds of corruption, the Trump ruling means that presidents, alone among elected officials, can likely never be prosecuted for corruption. That’s because the Court, with Chief Justice Roberts writing for the majority, held that former presidents enjoy absolute immunity for actions within their “core” constitutional authority and presumptive immunity for all other official acts. And worse, unlike the earlier decisions that interpreted statutes and that therefore Congress can reverse by passing new legislation, the Court claimed that presidential immunity was required by the Constitution itself. So only a future Supreme Court that decided to reverse the Trump decision, or an amendment to the Constitution, could cancel the get-out-of-jail-free card the Court gave presidents. [ David Frum: The Trump presidency’s world-historical heist ] All but the last two decisions, Snyder and Trump , spanned the Court’s conservative-liberal divide. Sun-Diamond and McDonnell were even unanimous. This isn’t partisan politics; it’s political elites protecting political elites. The facts in these cases were egregious, but the Court purported to be saving hapless bureaucrats from overzealous prosecutors in the future. In any event, they haven’t. Instead they’ve told juries of ordinary Americans that what they concluded to be corruption was not. Perhaps to try to obscure what it was doing, the Court used technical rather than normative language, something the Fordham law professor Zephyr Teachout explored more broadly in her paper “Demoralizing Elite Fraud,” in The Yale Law Journal . But that technical language can’t obscure the underlying badness of the conduct that the Court blessed. Congress can undo much of what the Supreme Court has done: address Sun-Diamond by making it illegal to give a politician gifts because of his position; address Skilling by designating undisclosed conflicts of interest as honest-services fraud; address McDonnell by expanding the definition of official acts in the bribery statute to cover what politicians actually do all day; and address Snyder by amending 666 to cover gratuities. As noted above, Congress already reversed the Court’s decision in McNally , and prosecutors have brought hundreds of honest-services prosecutions ever since, albeit with the limitations the Skilling decision imposed. Addressing Trump v. United States is tougher, but options still exist: Congress could close off the avenues a president can use to enrich himself and try to build his legacy by, for example, prohibiting the U.S. government from accepting gifts such as the Qatari plane, or disqualifying companies that invest in a president’s businesses or donate to his library from bidding on government contracts. That would be a good first step, but more ambitious approaches are needed, such as Senator Elizabeth Warren’s Anti-Corruption and Public Integrity Act. Unfortunately, Congress, like the Supreme Court, has so far chosen to protect political elites—in Congress’s case, by doing nothing. This behavior should be illegal because corruption is poison to democracy. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote in dissent in Snyder , “Greed makes governments—at every level—less responsive, less efficient, and less trustworthy from the perspective of the communities they serve.” And Americans know it. Results of a Gallup survey announced last month show that Americans’ perceptions of government corruption are at their highest in 20 years: 89 percent of adults say it is widespread. That is a 10-percentage-point increase since 2025 and includes strong majorities of both Democrats and Republicans. Although the Court has placed politicians beyond the law’s reach, at least for now, the public gets it. Hopefully, a new Congress will too.

文莱政府宣布，律政司司长林定国周一下午启程前往文莱，出席第十六届中国-东盟检察长会议及相关区域会议。

林郑月娥作为中国官方代表团的一员出席此次高级别会议，并计划在一场致力于保护数字时代儿童的全体会议上发表讲话。他与东南亚国家联盟成员国代表的讨论将集中于加强国际合作，应对针对青少年的网络犯罪威胁。
此次访问之际，人们越来越担心影响全球年轻人的数字威胁。技术的快速进步为年轻人创造了广泛的发展机会，但同时也带来了前所未有的安全风险，特别是未经同意的亲密图像传播和深度换脸技术的滥用。由于针对儿童的非法在线活动很容易跨越国界，区域执法和司法机构认为跨境伙伴关系至关重要。

在会议期间，林郑月娥将介绍香港现有的旨在保护儿童免受网络伤害的法律架构，同时概述该市未来旨在应对新兴数字危险的政策措施和监管举措。除全体会议外，林郑月娥还将与中国代表团成员和东盟官员一起参加双边讨论，以扩大相互交流并促进跨司法管辖区更紧密的工作关系。

陪同林郑月娥正式出访的有刑事检控专员周天行及数名政府律师。律政司司长预计于10月23日结束任期返港。在他缺席期间，律政司副秘书长张国钧代理律政司司长。

He will discuss cross-border cooperation against cybercrime targeting youth and present Hong Kong's le

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 16:53 HKT · 2 min read

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok departed for Brunei on Monday afternoon to participate in the 16th China-ASEAN Prosecutors-General Conference and related regional meetings, the government announced.

Lam is attending the high-level gathering as part of the official Chinese delegation, where he is scheduled to address a plenary session dedicated to safeguarding children in the digital era. His discussions with representatives from member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations will centre on strengthening international collaboration to counter cybercrime threats directed at youth.

The visit comes amid growing concern over digital threats affecting young people globally. While rapid technological progress has created extensive developmental opportunities for youth, it has simultaneously introduced unprecedented safety risks, notably the non-consensual distribution of intimate images and the misuse of deepfake technology. Because illicit online activities targeting children easily cross national borders, regional law enforcement and judicial bodies view cross-border partnerships as critical.

During the conference, Lam will present Hong Kong's existing legal architecture designed to shield children from online harms, while outlining the city's future policy measures and regulatory initiatives aimed at tackling emerging digital dangers. In addition to the plenary sessions, Lam will join bilateral discussions alongside members of the Chinese delegation and ASEAN officials to broaden mutual exchanges and foster closer working relationships across legal jurisdictions.

Lam is accompanied on the official trip by Director of Public Prosecutions Anthony Chau Tin-hang and several government counsel. The justice secretary is scheduled to wrap up his engagements and return to Hong Kong on October 23. During his absence, Deputy Secretary for Justice Horace Cheung Kwok-kwan is assuming the role of acting secretary for justice.

# Filipina helper remanded over alleged assault on five-month-old baby

A 40-year-old Filipina domestic helper has been remanded in custody after appearing in court over allegations she assaulted a five-month-old baby girl on five occasions in a Hong Kong apartment. She faces five counts of willful assault and will return to court in November.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

A 40-year-old Filipina domestic helper accused of assaulting a five-month-old baby girl on five occasions was remanded in custody after appearing in court on Monday.

The defendant, Viesca Ferlyn Martinito, faces five counts of willfully assaulting a child or young person under the age of 16 in her custody between October 11 and 19 at an apartment on Chung Hau Street. The charge alleges she intentionally assaulted the baby in a manner likely to cause unnecessary suffering or injury to her health.

The defendant appeared in Tuen Mun Magistrates' Courts this morning and was not required to enter a plea. She did not apply for bail and was remanded in custody until her next hearing on November 30 at Kowloon City Magistrates' Courts, pending further police investigation and the receipt of the victim's medical report.

summary: 香港 下午 2 点至 4 点期间，约有 9,400 名旅客通过新皇岗口岸入境香港，是之前落马洲口岸平均人数的 3.5 倍多。当局开放了所有车道，实施了人群控制，并增加了公交车服务以应对激增的情况。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 19 日香港时间 18:07 · 2 分钟阅读《保安局》黄冈新口岸南下旅客流量开始增加
content:
香港
下午2点至4点期间，约有9,400名旅客通过新皇岗口岸入境香港，是之前落马洲口岸平均人数的3.5倍多。当局开放了所有车道，实施了人群控制，并增加了公交车服务以应对激增的情况。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 18:07 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

安全局表示，从下午 2 点起，新皇岗口岸南下的旅客流量开始增加。下午2时至4时期间，约有9,400名旅客经口岸入境，是过往落马洲口岸同期入境旅客人数的3.5倍多。该局预计，当天晚些时候南行流量将进一步增加。

皇岗口岸L4层入境大厅通关通道已全部开通。为加快疏散旅客，入境处将联同警方视实际情况实施L4及L2级别的人群分流及管制措施。如果人流持续增加，警方将安排旅客在通关后在指定排队区域等候，然后安全有序地搭乘公共交通工具。
入境事务处已透过保安局「口岸连线」平台公布最新轮候时间资料。旅客可在出发前查询皇岗口岸及其他口岸的最新出入境信息。

运输署已安排约120辆专营巴士、40辆专线小巴及130辆跨境巴士提供服务及后备支援，以应付入境高峰。在繁忙时段，专营巴士的班次可增加至每两至三分钟一班，而专线小巴和跨境巴士则可每三至四分钟一班。专营巴士营办商亦增设特别短途班次，以加快疏散抵港乘客及巴士周转时间。

服务大使及公共交通营办商工作人员将协助L2层及公共运输交汇处的乘客根据目的地选择合适的交通工具并有序登机。警察也在现场帮助维持秩序。
保安局表示，会继续联同入境处、警方、运输署及相关部门，实时监察检查站及旅客人流，并灵活调配人手及采取相应应对措施，确保通关安排及公共交通服务顺利。建议广大市民尽早规划出行，选择合适的口岸，尽可能错峰出行。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
About 9,400 travellers entered Hong Kong via the new Huanggang checkpoint between 2pm and 4pm, more than 3.5 times the previous average at the Lok Ma Chau control point. Authorities opened all lanes, implemented crowd control and boosted bus services to manage the surge.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 18:07 HKT · 2 min read

The Security Bureau said traveller flows heading south began increasing at the new Huanggang checkpoint from 2pm. Between 2pm and 4pm, about 9,400 travellers entered Hong Kong via the checkpoint, more than 3.5 times the figure recorded during the same period at the Lok Ma Chau control point in the past. The bureau predicted the southbound flow would rise further later in the day.

All clearance lanes on the L4 level arrival hall of the Huanggang checkpoint have been opened. To speed up the dispersal of travellers, the Immigration Department, together with police, will implement crowd diversion and control measures on the L4 and L2 levels depending on the actual situation. If the flow continues to increase, police will arrange for travellers to wait in designated queuing areas after clearance before boarding public transport in a safe and orderly manner, the bureau said.

The Immigration Department has published the latest waiting time information through the Security Bureau's "Port Connect" platform. Travellers can check the latest immigration information for the Huanggang checkpoint and other control points before departure.

The Transport Department has arranged about 120 franchised buses, 40 green minibuses and 130 cross-boundary coaches for service and backup support to cope with the inbound peak. During busy periods, franchised bus frequencies can be increased to one every two to three minutes, while green minibuses and cross-boundary coaches can run every three to four minutes. Franchised bus operators have also added special short-haul trips to speed up the dispersal of arriving passengers and bus turnaround.

Service ambassadors and public transport operators' staff will assist passengers on the L2 level and at the public transport interchange in choosing suitable transport according to their destinations and boarding in an orderly manner. Police officers are also on site to help maintain order.

The Security Bureau said it will continue to work with the Immigration Department, police, the Transport Department and related departments to monitor the checkpoint and traveller flow in real time, and flexibly deploy manpower and take corresponding response measures to ensure smooth clearance arrangements and public transport services. It urged citizens to plan their journeys early, choose suitable control points and, where possible, travel outside peak hours.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

title: Wary of instability, China calls for deeper security cooperation with Tajikistan
summary: BEIJING, Oct 19 (Reuters) - China's Premier Li Qiang called on Monday for deeper security and intelligence cooperation with Tajikistan to fight what Beijing ‌views as extremism and separatism, and said he hoped the country ‌would take "stro
content:
BEIJING, Oct 19 (Reuters) - China's Premier Li Qiang called on Monday for deeper security and intelligence cooperation with Tajikistan to fight what Beijing ‌views as extremism and separatism, and said he hoped the country ‌would take "strong measures" to protect Chinese citizens.

China has long feared violence in Central Asia could spill ​over into its far western region of Xinjiang, home to the mostly Muslim Uyghur people. China says Uyghur militants were behind a string of past attacks in Xinjiang.

Li told Tajik President Emomali Rahmon that the two countries should deepen cooperation on ‌law enforcement and security, and ⁠strengthen intelligence exchanges and sharing, China's official Xinhua news agency said.

China and Tajikistan should jointly fight the "three evil forces" — a ⁠term Beijing uses to describe terrorism, separatism, and extremism — and safeguard regional peace and stability, Li added.

Human rights groups say China has severely repressed the Uyghur people and ​curtailed their ​religious, cultural and linguistic rights. China denies ​any abuses have taken place.

Li ‌is not the only high-profile foreign official visiting resource-rich Central Asia this week, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio travelling on Sunday to Uzbekistan. Li was in Uzbekistan before going to Tajikistan.

China, which has a remote, mountainous border with Tajikistan, is a major investor in the country.

Late last year, five Chinese nationals ‌were killed in Tajikistan in attacks the ​authorities said were launched from neighbouring Afghanistan.

Tajikistan, a ​former Soviet republic of around 11 ​million people with a secular government, has tense relations with ‌the Taliban authorities in Afghanistan. It ​has previously warned of ​drug smugglers and illicit gold miners working along the frontier.

Tajikistan endured a brutal civil war in the 1990s after the Soviet Union broke apart, ​during which Rahmon initially ‌rose to power. The country is closely aligned with Russia, which ​maintains a military base there.

(Reporting by Liz Lee and Beijing newsroom; ​Editing by Christopher Cushing and Kate Mayberry)

# Koizumi Rejects Chinese Claims of 'New Militarism' in Japan

 Koizumi challenges Beijing's claims of renewed Japanese militarism as China reportedly takes its accusations directly to Trump.

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi responds to questions at a lower house Budget Committee session, October 14 at the Diet (©Sankei/Ataru Haruna).

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected China's accusations of a resurgence of Japanese militarism on October 14, questioning why a country with nuclear weapons and strategic bombers would level such criticism at one that possesses neither.

Speaking at a Lower House Budget Committee session in response to a question from Keishi Abe of Ishin no Kai, Koizumi said Beijing was attempting to promote its narrative of Japan's "new militarism" internationally, but that "hardly anyone sympathizes with that."

## **A Narrative Aimed at the World**

Koizumi said China keeps advancing new claims while concealing the opacity of its own military activities. Japan will rebut unfair criticism, he said, but it is "important to consistently maintain the stance that dialogue is always open."

The minister also pointed to China's expanding nuclear forces. Its stockpile is estimated at about 600 warheads, he noted, and is projected to exceed 1,000 after 2030.

## **Xi Raised the Issue With Trump**

Chinese President Xi Jinping brought up the same theme at his September 24 summit with US President Donald Trump.

Multiple Western intelligence sources told The Sankei Shimbun that Xi described Japan's higher defense spending as an "arms buildup" and urged the American side to be wary of Japanese "militarism." Trump reportedly did not engage with the point, calling Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi a good friend.

[![Image 6: The 8th RD20 Conference 2026](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2A-2.webp)](https://rd20.aist.go.jp/conference/)

## **Calm and Resolute Response**

Koizumi described China's military activities and lack of transparency as "a matter of serious concern for Japan and the international community." He added that the Defense Ministry and Self-Defense Forces would "respond calmly and resolutely."

### Moving Manufacturing From China to Mexico: The Complete Guide

When China's COVID-zero lockdowns and its aggression toward Taiwan started spooking foreign companies in 2022, the [international manufacturing lawyers](https://harris-sliwoski.com/practice-areas/international-manufacturing-law/) at my firm began getting a steady stream of calls and emails from companies looking to leave China. Most wanted to know about Mexico, and some of the companies calling us were themselves Chinese or Taiwanese. The tariff wars since then have given companies more reasons to look south. Mexico makes sense for many of them. But companies that go into Mexico expecting to find China with a shorter shipping route are in for an expensive education.

Starting in 2022, my good friend Andrew Hupert and I wrote a long series of posts for this blog on what leaving China for Mexico actually involves. Nobody was better suited to write about this than Andrew. I first met him in Shanghai in 2003, and over the following two decades I came to rely deeply on his practical business wisdom, especially about China. When my firm stepped up its China practice, he was one of my go-to people on all things China. He was a business school professor who taught negotiation around the world, and he spent more than 20 years in Asia, living and working in Shanghai, Taipei, Hong Kong, and Saigon. Though he had tied his career to China, he, like me, was an early believer in a post-China manufacturing world. He moved to Thailand and then Vietnam, and when Mexico began emerging as a leading replacement for China manufacturing, he moved to Monterrey and then Oaxaca, and became fluent in Spanish. He spent his last years there helping companies, especially companies leaving China, set up and run operations in Mexico. Few people had spent as much time thinking about how the two countries compared, and fewer still had Andrew's willingness to say exactly what he thought.

Andrew died of a heart attack in Oaxaca in October 2024, at 61. I wrote about him and our friendship in [Remembering Andrew Hupert](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/remembering-andrew-hupert-international-business-guru/). This guide brings our Mexico work together in one place and updates it for 2026. Most of the business and cultural observations are Andrew's, drawn from his years running and advising operations in both countries. The legal and trade analysis is mine, informed by my firm's [affiliated lawyers in Mexico City](https://harris-sliwoski.com/location/mexico-city/) and the United States, and by many of the conclusions Andrew and I reached together over the years. Andrew is no longer here to update his words, so I have done that as best I can. Where events have proved us right or wrong, I say so. When I quote him, the words are his as he wrote them. I want readers to understand where his observations came from and why I continue to think they matter.

### Why Companies Are Leaving China

In early 2023, Andrew and I wrote that running a supply chain entirely through China had become a bet against the house, the kind that ends with the gambler up a ton at midnight and borrowing bus fare home by morning. The trade numbers seemed to argue otherwise. U.S.-China trade had hit a record $690 billion in 2022, and plenty of companies took that as vindication of their decision to stay. Multinationals were reading the situation differently. Their supply chain planners, the Lean Production and Six Sigma people who treat unnecessary risk as a sin, were piling into Mexico, as Unilever's $400 million commitment to a new plant in Nuevo León showed that same month. When a Chinese surveillance balloon was shot down over the United States that February, we predicted that cooler heads would not prevail. Washington, we said, would keep changing the economics of China supply chains by every means available, and Beijing would answer each new U.S. restriction with its own. We saw little reason to expect either government to put the interests of companies caught in the middle ahead of its own political priorities.

We put governments at the top of the list of likely supply chain shocks and said the damage would most likely come through mistakes, meaning bad regulations written and enforced for non-economic goals. Would governments knowingly hurt their own economies for a good soundbite? "Yes. Of course they would. We expected U.S. customs to demand ever more detailed proof that your goods were not made with forced labor in Xinjiang. Complying would trap your China staff in a catch-22, because trying to trace the origin of your materials could get them "invited to tea" by the authorities. We also expected Beijing to retaliate, since, as we put it, "Beijing will not apologize; it will reply." China has a long record of using trade to punish countries that anger it, including Japan, Norway, Canada, South Korea, Australia, and Lithuania. And we warned that after the disruptions of 2021 and 2022, no owner or fiduciary could credibly claim a China supply chain disruption was impossible to foresee. Many of our clients already had China exit and evacuation plans, and we told readers they should too. That advice was based on what we were already seeing companies struggle with, long before the current tariff battles. See [Doing Business with China and Your Reputation Risks](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/doing-business-with-china-and-your-reputation-risks/) and [Repeat After Me: Trade Relations Between the United States and China Will Only Get Worse](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/repeat-after-me-trade-relations-between-the-united-states-and-china-will-only-get-worse/).

Tariffs and trade restrictions have since vindicated much of what we wrote. In 2023, Mexico overtook China as the top source of U.S. goods imports, at $475.6 billion to China's $427.2 billion, with China's total down 20 percent from 2022. Real U.S. imports from China fell 28 percent in 2025 alone, and by year-end the average U.S. tariff on Chinese goods was near 50 percent, up from 21 percent when the second Trump administration took office. Beijing retaliated most effectively with rare earth export controls. It suspended its expanded October 2025 controls for one year, until November 10, 2026, but its April 2025 controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths remain in force. The forced-labor scrutiny we predicted has also become a basis for tariffs. In July 2026, the U.S. Trade Representative imposed tariffs on goods from 60 economies, China and Mexico among them, after finding that they had failed to impose and effectively enforce bans on imports made with forced labor. Our biggest mistake was assuming North American trade would remain politically protected. We underestimated just how willing Washington would be to make life difficult for companies manufacturing in Mexico, a subject I discuss below.

Companies that left China early told us their decisions had paid off. In that same 2023 series, Andrew and I passed along what clients who had moved their manufacturing elsewhere were saying. One said he slept better, both because he worried less about his supply chain and because he felt better about no longer supporting such a brutal regime. Another had left before COVID, which let it avoid the China tariffs, underprice its competitors, and take a good chunk of market share while those competitors scrambled to catch up. Others said they were hiring people who chose them because they had nothing to do with China. Still others had customers choosing them because their products did not come from China, whether to reduce supply chain risk or reputational risk. These were business owners explaining what had happened to their companies, and their experiences were far more persuasive than another consultant's presentation about geopolitical risk. We also said the most unforgivable sin foreign companies committed in China was going there without an exit strategy. I still believe that, and I would build an exit strategy into any Mexico plan from the start as well.

**Which Manufacturing Risks Can You Actually Control?**

One of the most important differences between manufacturing in China and Mexico is how much control you have over the risks your business faces. Every country has problems. Factories lose power, employees leave, suppliers fail, and shipments get delayed. You can reduce many of these risks by investigating your suppliers, choosing your location carefully, and making sure you have alternative sources of supply. You can never eliminate every manufacturing risk, but there is a great deal you can do to keep ordinary business problems from becoming disasters.

Many of Mexico's biggest manufacturing risks fall into that category. Security is a serious concern, but you can investigate specific locations and arrange safer transportation. Labor laws are demanding, but you can hire Mexican employment lawyers and structure your operation to comply with them. Infrastructure varies considerably, but you can check whether a proposed site has reliable power and water before committing to it. None of these precautions guarantees that your operation will run smoothly. They do, however, give you meaningful ways to reduce your exposure.

China presents some risks that no amount of good management can bring under your control. You can investigate your suppliers and trace your materials, but you cannot eliminate the possibility that U.S. Customs will detain your goods over forced-labor concerns. You cannot prevent Beijing from imposing export restrictions or Washington from raising tariffs. You can prepare for a crisis involving Taiwan, but you cannot prevent one. A company can do everything right inside its Chinese factory and still find its business badly damaged by a political decision made thousands of miles away. That is what makes these risks especially troubling. The company has very little ability to influence the decisions that create them.

Mexico has political risks of its own, as the 2026 USMCA review and the latest tariffs demonstrate. A Mexican manufacturer cannot control what Washington decides about North American trade any more than a Chinese manufacturer can control U.S. policy toward China. I would never suggest otherwise. But when comparing countries, I would pay particular attention to which risks you can realistically manage and which ones can overwhelm your business regardless of how carefully you operate. That distinction is one of the strongest reasons many companies have decided they would rather manufacture in Mexico.

**Who Can Still Stay in China**

Andrew's test turned on what you make and who buys it. Several kinds of companies can probably stay in China: those that provide services to Chinese B2B markets, produce for sale in China and Asia, or specialize in multinational supply chains. Companies that depend on an end-to-end global presence, such as hotels, travel companies, and financial services firms, can also stay, as can those big enough to run separate supply chains for separate markets. Companies that need materials, components, technology, or processes available only in China are a maybe. Their position keeps deteriorating, and nobody should want to be the last international manufacturer in China. A company running a low-cost strategy built on small runs of pre-sold products, less-than-container-load shipping, probably cannot stay. The important question is whether your own business falls into one of the categories that still makes economic sense there.

### Is Mexico Right for Your Company?

Andrew's starting point, from the first post of our series, was that comparing China and Mexico is not comparing apples to apples. The same product may leave the factory gate in both countries, but setting up and running operations in them involves very different systems. China's economy is highly structured and centrally planned. Mexico's is decentralized and reactive, an

It’s clear from the increasingly bellicose actions of the People’s Republic of China that the PRC seeks to return to its self-appointed role as the “Middle Kingdom” at the center of the world. ### Why Taiwan May Need To Reconsider the Ultimate Deterrent

Lasse de Graaf• RealClearDefense• October 12, 2026

For decades, Taipei’s security has leaned on three pillars: its relationship with the United States, the Taiwanese armed forces, and the island’s renowned ‘silicon shield.’ However, as the global order shifts, the reliability of these safeguards is becoming increasingly uncertain. Decades after Taiwan ended its clandestine nuclear weapons program in 1988, the changing geopolitical environment raises questions on whether Taipei should reconsider nuclear deterrence.

The growing uncertainty surrounding U.S.-Taiwan relations is a clear warning sign for Taipei. Unlike South Korea and Japan, Taiwan lacks a formalized military alliance with Washington. Instead, U.S. policy toward Taiwan has traditionally rested on the Taiwan Relations Act of 1979 and a policy of strategic ambiguity. For Taipei this policy has been a double-edged sword, on the one hand serving as a potent deterrent by forcing China to weigh the high risk of a U.S. kinetic intervention without knowing the exact threshold or scale of that response, but simultaneously creating uncertainty for Taiwan’s strategic planning.

### Deterrence on Best Efforts: When Taiwan's Arms Come Without a Guaranteed Delivery Date

Hong-Yu Harper Chen• RealClearDefense• October 9, 2026

Taiwan’s arms contracts treat delivery dates as estimates, and Congress should require Washington to account for the major slips.

At a defense forum in Taipei in September, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey[said](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10879531)that the hold on a $14 billion Taiwan arms package is “definitely affecting the business,” and that “as long as that’s stuck, you don’t have continued forward progress in other areas.” He had raised it, he said, with the President. That is a hold before any sale. A different problem starts after Taiwan signs a sale agreement and waits for delivery. The standard terms in those agreements do not, as a rule, guarantee a delivery date, and if a date slips, any dispute over it goes to consultation between the two governments.

### Australia's Security Race in the South Pacific
