For much of my time as a journalist, the story of China’s rise has come with a familiar undertone of alarm. China is either becoming the next great global power, challenging the West, rewriting the rules of international politics or quietly building a parallel system that the rest of the world will eventually have to adapt to. All of these arguments have some basis. But I sometimes wonder whether we make the China story too simple, especially from Central Asia, where China is not some distant geopolitical competitor, but a country next door, a major trading partner and an increasingly visible part of our economic landscape.

Jiyang Dong. Photo credit: Nazarbayev University

So I wanted to ask a broader question: if China continues to gain economic and geopolitical weight over the next 10 years, what will that power actually look like by 2035, and what will it mean for Central Asia? I spoke to several experts and their answers were more nuanced than the usual China-versus-the-West narrative. The most interesting conclusion was not that China will necessarily replace the existing international order. It may not have to.

**China may reshape the order without replacing it**

Jiyang Dong, assistant professor at Nazarbayev University’s Graduate School of Business, made a point that immediately shifted the question for me. “Ironically, the key variables impacting China’s future role in the international system are not necessarily within China,” he said.

China’s policies, he said, are already laid out in successive five-year plans and implemented with consistency. What matters just as much is what happens elsewhere: whether the United States (U.S.) continues to retreat from multilateralism and whether institutions such as the World Bank and IMF continue to meet the development needs of the Global South.

If they do not, Dong believes, institutions in which China plays a central role could gradually become more important. He points to the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank as one example. That means China’s rise may not depend entirely on Beijing building a new system from scratch. It may also depend on whether existing institutions leave enough space for China and other emerging powers to build something alongside them.

> Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of the China Studies Center in Kazakhstan, sees the process in similar terms. “I would rather speak not about the creation by China of a completely alternative world order, but about an attempt to change the balance and rules within the existing international system,” she said.

By 2035, she expects a more polycentric system in which China becomes one of the key centers of economic, technological and political influence. The real question, she said, is not whether one world order will simply replace another, but which institutions and norms will adapt to the new balance of power.

Ken-Moriyasu-Hudson. Photo credit: nationalinterest.org

Deputy Chairman of the Institute of Foreign Policy Studies under Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs Amangeldy Tazhenov reaches a similar conclusion. China, he said, is not trying to “break” the existing system. It is pushing for its transformation and reform so that it better reflects current realities and the changing distribution of power.

But Ken Moriyasu, a senior fellow at Hudson Institute, offered a sharper interpretation of the same trend. For much of the post-Deng Xiaoping era, he noted, China largely adapted to an international system shaped by Western powers. Under Xi Jinping, the ambition is different.

“It is less about reforming China to fit the existing order and more about changing the order to fit China,” Moriyasu said.

At the same time, he cautions against assuming Beijing is confident it can simply build the order it wants. China also knows that its rise generates resistance and suspicion. That, he said, helps explain why Beijing continues to emphasize the UN and existing institutions while simultaneously promoting BRICS, the SCO and a more multipolar system.

> “Beijing will preserve institutions that reinforce China’s status, seek to reshape institutions where Western influence remains predominant, and simultaneously build organizations, relationships and economic networks that give Beijing alternatives,” he said.

I find that distinction more useful than the familiar question of whether China is trying to become “the next U.S.” Perhaps China does not need to replace the system. It may simply need to become powerful enough to change the way the system works around it.

**Central Asia is becoming more important for a different reason**

Amangeldy Tazhenov. Photo credit: sszi.kz

This is where the discussion becomes more interesting for Central Asia. For years, China’s relationship with the region was discussed largely through the familiar vocabulary of trade, energy, resources and transport corridors. Those things still matter. But the strategic logic appears to be changing. Moriyasu calls the emerging logic “strategic resilience.” Much of China’s trade and energy still moves through maritime routes exposed to American naval power. Central Asia gives Beijing something the South China Sea cannot: a vast continental hinterland connecting China westward across Eurasia. “Central Asia matters to Beijing not only because of the energy, minerals and markets within Central Asia, but increasingly because of what lies beyond it. It connects China westward across the Eurasian landmass,” he said.

His forecast is striking: “I would expect Central Asia to move from China’s economic periphery toward the strategic center of China’s relationship with Eurasia.”

That changes the question because Central Asia’s value for China is no longer simply what Beijing can obtain from the region. It is also what the region allows China to reach. Jiyang Dong approaches this from a more economic perspective. “Central Asia’s greatest strategic significance hinges on its potential as a connectivity hub in the heart of Eurasia,” he said.

Without sufficient connectivity infrastructure, he notes, trade volumes remain limited, and resources remain effectively locked in the region. That is why projects such as the[expansion](https://astanatimes.com/2026/07/kazakhstan-uzbekistan-expand-strategic-partnership-through-trade-transport-and-regional-agreements/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) of the Aktau container hub and the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway matter beyond their immediate economic purpose. They are helping turn Central Asia’s geography into an asset. Perhaps this is where we should stop thinking of infrastructure simply as infrastructure.

**Infrastructure may be the new geopolitics**

Moriyasu said something that stayed with me: “Infrastructure becomes the new hinge of geopolitics.”

> “Once trade routes, pipelines, power grids and supply chains are built around particular networks, they begin to shape the economic choices available to countries using them,” Moriyasu said.

That is a much more subtle form of power than the geopolitics I grew up reading about. There is no flag going up. No alliance is announced. No military base appears. But the network changes. And once a country’s trade, logistics, power systems, digital infrastructure or industrial supply chains are deeply embedded in a particular network, those connections can begin shaping the choices available to it. This is also where my own perception of China has changed.

It is difficult to ignore the efficiency of some of the infrastructure projects I see around me. The LRT in Astana is a very concrete example. Whatever one’s broader political view of China may be, a functioning project creates a different impression than a political speech or diplomatic statement. This is where infrastructure can begin to operate as soft power. Not necessarily because Beijing tells people to admire China, but because people encounter its capabilities in practical ways: a railway, a road or a technology. Over time, that can produce something harder to measure but politically significant: familiarity, respect and, potentially, a certain degree of loyalty.

Tazhenov described China’s approach in similarly long-term terms, noting that Beijing tends to think in much longer horizons than many other countries. He also pointed to the growing visibility of Chinese economic activity in Kazakhstan: from infrastructure and roads to new enterprises and resource projects. That matters because soft power is usually discussed in terms of culture, education or films. Perhaps in the next decade, we will have to add infrastructure to that list.

**The next phase may be about technology, not concrete**

This is where the forecasts become even more interesting. Shaimergenova believes the development most underestimated today is the transition from physical infrastructure connectivity to technological and institutional connectivity. A few years ago, the China conversation in Central Asia focused on roads, railways, pipelines and energy. Today, she notes, the agenda increasingly includes AI, digital infrastructure, green technologies and critical minerals.

> “Central Asia will be not only a territory through which flows between China and Europe pass, but increasingly a space where different technological, production and regulatory systems will intersect,” she said.

That is probably the part of the China story that deserves more attention. Dong sees another underestimated area: cooperation in non-fossil energy. Solar panels, wind turbines, energy storage, flexible grids and nuclear power could all become increasingly important as Central Asian economies grow and demand more electricity. In other words, China’s future role in Central Asia may be less about simply connecting the region to China and more about helping shape the systems through which the region itself develops.

**More China: more choices, or fewer?**

This is where the experts stop agreeing. Dong sees growing competition among major powers as potentially useful for Kazakhstan because it creates more room to advance national interests through different partners and financial systems.

Shaimergenova is more cautious. “The strengthening of competition among major powers provides Kazakhstan with additional opportunities for investment, technology, transport projects and access to different markets. But at the same time, the risk increases that economic, technological and even logistical decisions will increasingly be viewed through the prism of geopolitical choice,” she said.

> Tazhenov is even more direct: “My opinion is that an aggravation of geopolitical rivalry is certainly unfavorable for Kazakhstan. It actually narrows the field for foreign policy maneuver.”

This may be the real paradox of the next decade. China’s rise can give Kazakhstan access to more capital, infrastructure, technology and markets. But if rivalry between China and the U.S. continues to harden, those same economic choices may increasingly be interpreted as political choices. The more interconnected Kazakhstan becomes with major external powers, the more important it is to remain capable of deciding where each connection leads.

**What we may be underestimating**

One idea kept returning throughout these conversations, even when the experts approached it from very different directions. It is not simply that China is becoming more present in Central Asia. The region and China are becoming more mutually interested in one another. Tazhenov believes this growing mutual interest, connectivity and economic complementarity is one of the least appreciated trends. For China, Central Asia offers transport routes, resources, energy and stability. For Kazakhstan and its neighbors, China increasingly offers markets, investment and technology. The relationship is therefore becoming more complicated than a simple story of a rising power expanding into a neighboring region.

It is also becoming a story of mutual dependence which is not automatically goo

# Hong Kong prosecutes eateries for allowing dogs in unauthorised venues

Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department has filed 20 prosecutions against eateries that unlawfully allowed dogs inside, plus seven against pet owners who brought dogs into such venues. It also lodged four cases over untethered dogs in permitted premises, urging diners to check approval

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 18 Oct 2026 at 14:13 HKT · updated 19 Oct, 04:24 · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=Hong%20Kong%20prosecutes%20eateries%20for%20allowing%20dogs%20in%20unauthorised%20venues%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/government/Hong-Kong-prosecutes-eateries-for-allowing-dogs-in-unauthori-d67c34 "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/government/Hong-Kong-prosecutes-eateries-for-allowing-dogs-in-unauthori-d67c34&text=Hong%20Kong%20prosecutes%20eateries%20for%20allowing%20dogs%20in%20unauthorised%20venues "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/government/Hong-Kong-prosecutes-eateries-for-allowing-dogs-in-unauthori-d67c34 "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/government/Hong-Kong-prosecutes-eateries-for-allowing-dogs-in-unauthori-d67c34&text=Hong%20Kong%20prosecutes%20eateries%20for%20allowing%20dogs%20in%20unauthorised%20venues "X")[](mailto:?subject=Hong%20Kong%20prosecutes%20eateries%20for%20allowing%20dogs%20in%20unauthorised%20venues&body=Hong%20Kong%20prosecutes%20eateries%20for%20allowing%20dogs%20in%20unauthorised%20venues%0Ahttps%3A//clb.org.hk/en/government/Hong-Kong-prosecutes-eateries-for-allowing-dogs-in-unauthori-d67c34 "Email")

The [Food and Environmental Hygiene Department](https://clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Tuen-Mun-man-flees-FEHD-officers-after-dropping-cigarette-bu-89f771) (FEHD) said it has filed a total of 20 prosecutions against eateries that unlawfully allowed dogs to enter premises without the required permission. It has also brought seven prosecutions against individuals who took dogs into such unauthorised restaurants, the department said on Sunday.

In addition, the FEHD said it has taken strict action against serious violations by dog owners inside permitted eateries, including four prosecutions for failing to keep dogs securely leashed.

Ahead of Halloween, the department reminded residents that if they plan to dine out with dogs, they should first confirm whether the restaurant is approved to admit dogs and must comply with relevant laws and regulations.

More than 990 restaurants currently hold permission to allow dogs inside. The FEHD said those premises must ensure they meet all licensing conditions and legal requirements, and should strengthen supervision of staff and remind customers with dogs to protect safety and public hygiene.

title: Why BRICS Matters To Its Members – Analysis
summary: [Video 5](https://www.eurasiareview.com/18102026-why-brics-matters-to-its-members-analysis/) Video Muted By Tapan Bharadwaj ## **Key Takeaways:** * BRICS provides its members high-level access among major economies, a platform to amplify co
content:
[Video 5](https://www.eurasiareview.com/18102026-why-brics-matters-to-its-members-analysis/)
Video Muted

By Tapan Bharadwaj

## **Key Takeaways:**

*   BRICS provides its members high-level access among major economies, a platform to amplify collective positions on multilateral reform, opportunities for bilateral sideline meetings, and non-binding declarations that record lowest-common-denominator views.
*   These benefits are constrained by consensus decision-making, which produces gaps between agreed text and national actions, slows institutional development beyond the New Development Bank, and allows outsized influence by China and Russia.
*   The article concludes that BRICS remains relevant to its members more for the strategic autonomy and multi-alignment options it preserves than for concrete collective deliverables.

BRICS, an intergovernmental grouping of eleven emerging markets and developing countries, concluded its 18th Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi on 13 September. BRICS [represents](https://www.mea.gov.in/speeches-statements?dtl/41768/English_Translation_of_Prime_Ministers_Address_at_the_BRICS_Business_Forum_2026_September_11_2026) nearly half the world’s population, about 40 per cent of global GDP, and roughly a quarter of global trade, but still faces questions of relevance. Ultimately, BRICS matters to its members less for what it produces and more for the options it can offer to pursue [strategic autonomy](https://www.vifindia.org/print/14419), the capacity to act independently on issues that impact vital interests, and [multi-alignment](https://indiawrites.org/diplomacy/why-multi-alignment-matters-to-india-explains-jaishankar/), or the freedom to work with multiple partners simultaneously on different issues. However, the consensus model that keeps these options available limits what BRICS can produce.

## **What BRICS offers its members**

BRICS offers its member countries four things: High-level political access annually to a meeting which includes four of the top ten global economies; a platform to amplify individual voices collectively on global multilateral reform; the possibility of bilateral sidelines meetings to discuss contentious issues; and agreed text that records the member countries’ collective positions.

First, the annual participation of leaders and ministers across several sectoral tracks gives each member state regular access to its counterparts. During India’s chairship alone, over [four hundred meetings](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776) were held in thirty Indian cities at the level of ministers, business, and civil society. For example, the [agriculture ministers’ meeting](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2272502&reg=3&lang=1) in Indore led to the launch of a Global Forum on Farmers’ Rights in Seed Systems. These meetings also build working relationships between high to mid-level officials who hardly meet otherwise, helping absorb political shocks without help from an external country or agency. For example, Iran and the UAE were able to meet across different tracks despite being in adversarial positions since the US-Israel-Iran war broke out in May.

Second, BRICS provides a platform for member states to agree on common positions for negotiations in multilateral bodies. In New Delhi, BRICS members agreed on a common line for WTO [agriculture negotiations](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776), which would be difficult to defend alone during WTO negotiation rounds. This also facilitates a stronger, collective objection to rules that BRICS members find hard to [influence alone](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/climate-change/brics-backs-carbon-market-cooperation-while-opposing-unilateral-cbam), such as the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Further, it helps raise the voices of those members facing unilateral economic sanctions or those that are affected by them to condemn coercive measures together.

Third, BRICS offers a venue for bilateral meetings on the sidelines that may not otherwise be politically feasible independently. Indian Prime Minister Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping [met at Kazan](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3vlxx9pgxwo) on the sidelines of the 2024 BRICS Summit, which helped the two sides [manage the thaw](https://www.isas.nus.edu.sg/papers/one-year-after-the-kazan-summit-an-assessment-of-china-india-relations/) in their relations. At New Delhi, the [Iranian and UAE leaders](https://www.outlookindia.com/international/pezeshkian-mbz-meet-in-delhi-how-indias-brics-platform-created-space-for-iran-uae-engagement-amid-west-asia-tensions) held their first high-level bilateral meeting since the war began in May. In this way, BRICS summits are also becoming a ‘multilateral of bilaterals’.

Fourth, the consensus-based annual non-binding declaration, while limited in scope, serves an important purpose. It records where members currently stand on global issues, and shifts in its language demonstrate accommodation of member countries’ concerns. The 2016 [Goa BRICS declaration](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/27491/Goa+Declaration+at+8th+BRICS+Summit), adopted soon after the Uri attack—carried out by the [Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed](https://www.firstpost.com/india/uri-attack-carried-out-by-jaish-e-mohammad-militants-confirms-indian-army-3013332.html)—didn’t name the group. A year later, the [Xiamen declaration](http://english.scio.gov.cn/m/topnews/2017-09/05/content_41531768.htm) named them explicitly, including China’s sign-off, despite its close relationship with Pakistan. Later, both the [Rio](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/39770/Rio_de_Janeiro_Declaration_Strengthening_Global_South_Cooperation_for_a_More_Inclusive_and_Sustainable_Governance) and [New Delhi](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776) declarations condemned the 2025 Pahalgam attack in the strongest terms, though without naming any terrorist organisation. The [foreign ministers’ meeting](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/brics-ministers-fail-to-issue-a-joint-statement-over-differences-on-west-asia-conflict/article70982709.ece) in May this year failed to produce a joint statement on West Asia, but the leaders reached agreement four months later by saying less. It mentioned only “[respective national positions](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776)” on the war and didn’t name any involved parties, which represents accommodation.

## **Where BRICS falls short**

BRICS faces three limitations: the gap between word and action; ie what members agree to in the declaration and their national positions; the slow pace of building institutions beyond the New Development Bank (NDB); and the outsized influence of its heavyweight members, China and Russia. Each limitation is facilitated by the requirement of consensus decision-making, which conversely also keeps its options open, as explained earlier.

First, a declaration records the lowest common denominator of agreement, and not necessarily what members will do independently while pursuing their foreign policies. China signed the Xiamen Declaration naming the LeT and JeM in 2017. Yet, it placed technical holds on India’s proposal at the UN 1267 Committee to designate LeT and JeM leaders as terrorists in 2022 and 2023. Additionally, any collective BRICS voice on UNSC reform or at the WTO has produced little in practice. For example, UNSC reform hasn’t moved an inch, and the WTO dispute resolution mechanism remains defunct.

Second, more than a decade has passed since the creation of the NDB and Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA). CRA has never been tested in practice. Other ideas launched at the Kazan Summit such as the BRICS Grain Exchange, New Investment Platform, and payment initiatives still sit in working groups. On payments initiatives, for example, the New Delhi declaration only asked the task force to explore “[pragmatic solutions](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776)” with “[no one-size-fits-all approach](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776).”

Third, on the Russia-Ukraine war, the [Beijing](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/35435/XIV+BRICS+Summit+Beijing+Declaration) and Johannesburg declarations only recalled “[national positions](https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/speech_docs/Jhb%20II%20Declaration%2024%20August%202023.pdf),” and the New Delhi text dropped the conflict altogether. A grouping that cannot describe a conflict involving its own members could struggle at large to speak for the Global South on peace and security in the way that it claims to do. China’s [economic weight](https://www.indiatoday.in/business/story/brics-economy-growth-trade-more-china-story-export-income-surjit-bhalla-india-2994017-2026-09-14), which accounts for the largest share of BRICS’ output and trade, is difficult to contain as it continues to gain disproportionately more than any other member country.

## **Conclusion**

Taken together, BRICS offers its members more options than what it delivers as a bloc. The necessity of consensus decision-making both enables and limits these options. That said, as long as members can use BRICS to speak collectively, meet adversaries on neutral platforms, and record positions without binding commitments, it will stay relevant to them—even if it delivers little.

*   About the author: Tapan Bharadwaj is Senior Researcher with IPCS’ China Research Programme (CRP).
*   Source: This article was [published by IPCS](https://ipcs.org/comm_select.php?articleNo=5916)

## About IPCS

IPCS (Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies) conducts independent research on conventional and non-conventional security issues in the region and shares its findings with policy makers and the public. It provides a forum for discussion with the strategic community on strategic issues and strives to explore alternatives. Moreover, it works towards building capacity among young scholars for greater refinement of their analyses of South Asian security.

title: Shame About the Hypersonics: Why the United States Needs More Missile Defenses in the Indo-Pacific

content:
By. Diego Arrendondo

DOI. 10.57912/34692192

On September 3, 2025, China held a Victory Day Parade to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II. As is done annually, the display unveiled a range of new weapons, including [laser defense systems](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/), [a stealth fighter](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/f-35i-adir-vs-china-s-new-j-35-stealth-fighter-who-wins-in-summed-up-in-4-words/ar-AA1LYgoC?ocid=BingNewsSerp), and [missiles](https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/what-weapons-china-put-display-its-military-parade-2025-09-03/), signaling a modernization of China’s military that will force a change in U.S. posture and operations in the Pacific. The new weapons will expand China’s strike-force capabilities to include both the First and Second Island Chains in the Indo-Pacific, two U.S.-aligned arcs of archipelagos including Japan, Taiwan, Indonesia, and the Philippines in the First, and Guam and other strategic islands in the Second. The American military facilities on these island chains allow the U.S. to project its forces in the Pacific, enabling it to deter and respond to opposing forces quickly, restrict Chinese naval access, and form a defensive barrier. With China’s modernization of its military and shifting approach to Pacific hegemony, the U.S. should increase its anti-ballistic missile systems to protect its bases in Guam, South Korea, and Japan, and reassure its allies of its continued capability of stabilizing the region.

Military analysts and defense officials [widely agree](https://www.war.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4150802/chinas-military-buildup-threatens-indo-pacific-region-security/)that the main purpose of China’s evolving weapons systems is to counter U.S. military assets, especially the U.S. naval hegemony in the region. Beijing also understands that in the era where drones can overwhelm traditional defenses, a rapid and cost-effective response is critical. The Liaoyuan-1([LY-1](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/)) was one of the weapons on display designed for this purpose. It is [intended](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/)for shipboard self-defense, specifically to disrupt and destroy optical sensors of enemy platforms that detect drones and missiles. Direct-energy weapons (DEW) like the LY-1 offer near-instant engagement at a low cost per shot, providing a financial advantage and an efficient means of countering saturated volumes of incoming threats.

All of these expanding weapons capabilities showcase China’s ambition to be seen as a leader among military powers and challenge American hegemony. The most significant and worrying are the [hypersonic missiles](https://www.eurasiantimes.com/china-hails-yj-21-hypersonic-ship-launched-missile/), most notably the Yingji 21 and DongFeng-26D (DF-26). The Yingji 21 can reach a terminal velocity of roughly Mach 10, making it difficult for missile-defense systems to intercept and earning it the title of an “aircraft carrier killer.” The base DF-26 is an intermediate-range ballistic missile (IRBM) [designed](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-df26d-guam-killer-missile-threatens-us-carriers-bases-pacific/)to deliver conventional and nuclear strikes. The “D” variant specifically has a 5,000-kilometer strike radius, making it able to hit [Guam](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-df26d-guam-killer-missile-threatens-us-carriers-bases-pacific/), an important military base for the United States. These new weapons highlight a central gap in the current U.S. defensive posture in the Indo-Pacific by sending a signal that Beijing not only intends to match the U.S. in stealth but also in navy force projection.

Against this growing threat, the U.S. and its regional allies need to rely on layered missile-defense systems to strengthen deterrence and to counter potential attacks. At this moment, [Guam](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)has a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) battery, each with 6 launchers and 8 interceptors per launcher, capable of intercepting missiles in their terminal phase. [South Korea](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)additionally has one THAAD battery in Seongju, positioned to defend both Seoul and US troops in the Port of Busan. While [Japan](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)does not have a battery, its defenses consist of 8 Aegis BMD ships, with five U.S. Aegis BMD ships permanently stationed in Japan. Defending all three of these territories is critical for the U.S. to manage the region and its global credibility because together, they serve as a multi-tiered system strategically important to the U.S. posture in the Indo-Pacific.

The U.S. should increase its land-based Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense System (ABMD) facilities and its THAAD in Guam, South Korea, and Japan. A layered missile defense increases the probability of intercept by creating multiple engagement windows. While it does not make defended regions invulnerable, it does raise the number of missiles required to achieve a successful hit, thereby lowering the cost-benefit ratio of an attack for China. Complicating the missiles’ reach deters China from employing missiles by reducing confidence in the ability to achieve reliable effects. However, the United States should also develop more cost-effective countermeasures, as it costs the U.S. about[$1 billion](https://www.thepricer.org/how-much-does-a-thaad-missile-cost/)for a THAAD battery, about $13 million for each interceptor, and [$637 million](https://www.forecastinternational.com/budget_site/pdf/FY2024/0300D%5FLineItem%5FMD73%5FLI%2D40%2DAegis%5FAshore%5FPhase%5FIII%5FFY2024%2Epdf)to deploy an Aegis Ashore.

Increasing ABMD and THAAD presence in Guam is essential because it provides the U.S. with a gateway to Asia, as it is home to important Navy and Air Force bases that [support](https://defensefeeds.com/analysis/geopolitics/guam-military-base/)the Air Force’s heavy bomber force, nuclear-powered submarines, the U.S. Pacific Fleet, and all long-range aircraft. Unlike the sea-based Aegis destroyers, which must divide time between escort and maintenance cycles, a land-based Aegis Ashore site provides continuous coverage. Similarly, enhancing South Korea's defenses is critical because of the US bases located within its borders. [South Korea](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan)currently operates 8 Patriot Advanced Capability (PAC-3) systems and its own MDS known as the Korean Air and Missile Defense; both [systems](https://www.missiledefenseadvocacy.org/defense-systems/patriot-advanced-capability-3-missile/)have a short range and cannot effectively engage IRBMs, giving opposing forces the possibility to neutralize U.S. bases and air operations. If the ROK Armed Forces are not able to delay opposing forces due to missiles, it will allow the enemy to neutralize U.S. bases, delaying U.S. reinforcements and disrupting air operations. In addition to holding[50,000](https://www.usfj.mil/About-USFJ/)U.S. military personnel and the [only](https://www.airpac.navy.mil/Organization/USS-George-Washington-CVN-73/About-Us/)forward-deployed aircraft carrier, the USS Geroge Washington, Japan also maintains [6 destroyers](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan), 5 of which are permanently-stationed, one cruiser equipped with [13 Aegis BMD destroyers](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan), and U.S.-operated PAC-3 systems in[Okinawa](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan). That being said, U.S. vessels or Japanese destroyers cannot be counted on to defend Japan if conflict breaks out, as ships would likely prioritize protecting U.S. [carrier strike groups](https://defensefeeds.com/analysis/weapons/carrier-strike-group/#:~:text=This%20layered%20formation%20defines%20standard%20carrier%20strike%20group,and%20operate%20together%20as%20a%20seamless%20combat%20system.). Deploying Aegis Ashore batteries in Japan will keep U.S. bases protected, freeing up ships to protect the USS George Washington, conduct patrols, and perform maintenance.

Although expanding layered missile defense would strengthen the U.S. ability to protect its forces in the Indo-Pacific, advocating for this policy is unlikely to be politically or economically feasible in the near term. The Iran War has shown that American [missile defense](https://sfg.media/en/a/us-patriot-thaad-missile-stockpiles-iran-war/#:~:text=The%20war%20with%20Iran%20has%20significantly%20depleted%20US,Patriot%20missiles%20and%20about%20250%20THAAD%20interceptors%20remaining.)is too [costly](https://jinsa.org/jinsa_report/missile-and-interceptor-cost-estimates-during-the-u-s-israel-iran-war/)and has drained that stockpile as well. Making a large expansion of missile defense in the Indo-Pacific more difficult to sustain. Domestically, the[American public](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/opinion-poll-iran-war/#:~:text=Americans%20do%20want%20the%20Iran%20war%20to%20end,interests%20and%20has%20not%20been%20worth%20the%20costs.)does not want to spend more on the military budget. Washington has also [reduced](https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/army-news/2026/trump-orders-reduction-us-south-korea-military-exercises-north-korea-iran-war#:~:text=On%20August%2016%2C%202026%2C%20U.S.%20President%20Donald%20Trump,before%20the%2011-day%20maneuvers%20were%20scheduled%20to%20begin.)the scale of some U.S.-South Korean military exercises. Japan is more favorable to military buildup, as its government has continued to [increase defense spending](https://blog.modeldiplomat.com/japan-military-spending-2026-budget-strategy)and invested in missile defense, drones, and other capabilities. The United States should instead develop cheaper defensive technologies, investing in [laser technology](https://www.defensenews.com/newsletters/daily-news-roundup/2026/04/28/what-we-know-about-the-us-militarys-new-joint-laser-weapon-system/)or other cost-effective countermeasures.

With the growing threat of China’s advancing military, the U.S. should consider focusing missile defense system expansion on strategic bases critical for combating Chinese regional influence. Guam, South Korea, and Japan are vital to the US for these reasons in stabilizing and maintaining its presence in the region. Additionally, placing defense systems in both Korea and Japan would reassure allies of the U.S.’s continued capability to defend against encroaching Chinese airstrike capabilities.  Deploying defense systems to these three locations will allow the United States to strengthen its naval deterrence as China continues to challenge the U.S.-led international order.

title: China moves to tighten controls on AI exports, citing national security risks
summary: Key takeaways 1. China proposed export controls on 40 advanced technologies, including 23 tied to artificial intelligence. 2. The draft covers major AI models, AI agents, and large computer systems used to train AI. 3. Foreign users could s
content:
Key takeaways

1.    China proposed export controls on 40 advanced technologies, including 23 tied to artificial intelligence.
2.    The draft covers major AI models, AI agents, and large computer systems used to train AI.
3.    Foreign users could still access Chinese AI services through websites, apps, and online software platforms.
4.    Open-source tools and public research would generally stay outside the proposed restrictions.

Key Takeaways by [nexos.ai](https://nexos.ai/), reviewed by Cybernews staff.

**China is weighing new export controls on its advanced technology, including AI, potentially expanding restrictions to 40 technologies amid intensifying competition with the US.**

On October 16th, China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology published a draft document proposing to ban or restrict exports of 40 technologies spanning solar power, AI, chip design, and biomedicine. Of these, 23 are AI-related, including advanced large language models, AI agents, and computing clusters.

Under the proposal, China would control exports of AI models containing restricted technologies, but access through application programming interfaces (APIs), websites, apps, and software-as-a-service platforms would be exempt from the restrictions.

This would let people abroad keep using Chinese AI services from companies like DeepSeek even with the new rules in place.

[![Image 1: elon muskss face with black hat, looking up with blurry flads in the back](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2025/06/elon_musk_blurry_flags.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/musk-ai-and-robots-us-debt-fix/)

[![Image 2: Robot hands on a keyboard](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2026/01/robot_hands_keyboard_ai.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/rogue-ai-agents-hacked-into-indian-companies/)

[![Image 3: jenna-ortega-marrakech](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2025/12/jenna-ortega.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/jenna-ortega-deepfake-tiktok/)

[![Image 4: Arthur Mensch, founder of Mistral AI, at the World Economic Forum in Davos](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2026/05/arthur-mensch-vassal.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/mistral-europe-surrender/)

[![Image 5: Accenture](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2024/06/Shutterstock_2419193795.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/accenture-ai-spending-limits/)

[![Image 6: Voice actor Masako Nozawa alongside Dragon Ball character Goku.](https://media.cybernews.com/images/thumbnail/2026/10/masako-nozawa-goku.jpg)](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/dragon-ball-goku-ai-voice-clone/)

Covered exports [would include](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-16/china-proposes-export-controls-on-ai-models-chips-and-agents) technology for AI models with at least 2 trillion parameters, such as Kimi K3 and Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max, as well as models ranking among the world's top 10 in performance, usage, or safety.

AI models trained on China’s “core data”, defined as “data concerning national security, the lifeline of the national economy, key public livelihoods, and major public interests”, would also be banned from export. The proposal also covers 12 solar power-related technologies, as well as five biomedicine technologies.

However, open-source technologies and research already in the public domain would generally be excluded from the restrictions.

A spokesperson for the Commerce Ministry said the export rules are aimed at ensuring “the safety and controllability” of AI technology, [adding](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zcfb/dwmygl/art/2026/art_61446ab4beee4f63973d4d0ab3097648.html):

“The Chinese government’s necessary management of these technologies aims to solidify the security baseline, prevent misuse and abuse, ensure that AI remains under human control, and promote international governance of AI.”

In September 2026, the US and China made progress towards establishing a formal dialogue on AI risks following talks between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington. Another round of AI-related discussions is planned for November.

At the same time, the US has restricted China's access to advanced semiconductor technology, and China now appears to be tightening its own controls on exports of advanced AI tech.

China has already imposed a temporary registration requirement for companies to register exports of the technologies covered by the proposal. The measure took effect on Friday.

# 2 suspects in Kaohsiung homicide case brought back from South Korea

10/18/2026 05:11 PM

A suspect who allegedly fled to South Korea with another after taking part in a fatal assault in Kaohsiung last month is escorted by authorities upon arriving at Taoyuan International Airport. Photo courtesy of Kaohsiung City Police Department's Criminal Investigation Corps.

Kaohsiung, Oct. 18 (CNA) Two suspects who allegedly fled to South Korea after taking part in a fatal assault in Nanzih District, Kaohsiung, last month have been brought back to Taiwan and taken into custody, police said Sunday.

The suspects, a 25-year-old used-car dealership owner surnamed Lin (林) and a 23-year-old employee surnamed Liu (劉), arrived at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport on Saturday, where they were arrested by a special team investigating the case, according to the Kaohsiung City Police Department's Criminal Investigation Corps.

South Korean police apprehended the two after Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau requested assistance through its liaison officer in South Korea, according to the corps.

Investigators suspect that Lin orchestrated the assault and that Liu took part in beating the victim. Both men have denied any wrongdoing, and the investigation is ongoing.

The case involving Lin and Liu came to light on Sept. 30, when a 22-year-old man surnamed Mu (穆) called the Nanzih Precinct of the Kaohsiung City Police Department to report that he had accidentally beaten a coworker to death.

Mu later drove the victim's body to the police station and turned himself in.

Prosecutors allege that Mu, Liu and several others assaulted a coworker surnamed Chang (張) at Lin's used-car dealership at around 1 a.m. on Sept. 30, striking his head, buttocks and limbs with hot-melt glue sticks and clubs.

Mu told police the attack stemmed from a dispute over NT$100,000 (US$3,079) the victim allegedly owed.

Police had initially questioned Lin and Liu before releasing the pair on Oct. 1, but investigators subsequently gathered more evidence linking them to the case. According to police, prosecutors later identified the two as key suspects.

When authorities could not locate the two for further questioning, they discovered that the pair had flown to South Korea on Oct. 2. Prosecutors then issued warrants for both men's arrest.

Mu and three other suspects surnamed Wu (吳), Yeh (葉) and Chen (陳) have been ordered detained on suspicion of murder after prosecutors argued they were flight risks and could coordinate their accounts or tamper with evidence.

A juvenile surnamed Huang (黃) has been referred to juvenile court.

(By Chang Yi-lien and Evelyn Kao)

Ng Hong-ming, a former Hong Kong deputy to the National People's Congress (NPC) and past principal of Pui Kiu Middle School, has died at the age of 100.

Leung Chun-ying, vice-chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and former chief executive of Hong Kong, said on social media that he "mourns the passing of Principal Ng Hong-ming with deep sorrow".

Maria Tam Wai-chu, former deputy director of the Basic Law Committee, said in response to enquiries that Ng was a model of patriotism and love for Hong Kong, full of righteousness and vitality. She said he nurtured many talents in Hong Kong and that "Ng will forever live in the history of Pui Kiu and Hong Kong".

Ng was born in 1926 in Shantou, Guangdong province. He graduated from National Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou in 1947, then went to Hong Kong to teach at Pui Kiu Middle School. He became the school's principal in 1958, served as its supervisor from 1985, and became chairman of its board of directors in 1997.

In 1975, Ng took part in the founding of the Hong Kong Federation of Education Workers and served as its founding chairman. He was appointed a member of the NPC Standing Committee's Basic Law Committee and served for a long period as a Hong Kong deputy to the NPC, including as head of the Hong Kong delegation and a member of the presidium of the NPC Standing Committee.

# 2026 ELECTIONS/Candidates woo voters with swag ahead of local elections

10/18/2026 07:19 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Taipei, Oct. 18 (CNA) With Taiwan's local elections scheduled for Nov. 28, candidates for mayor and county magistrate are rolling out campaign merchandise and giveaways to win over voters.

The campaign team of Kuomintang (KMT) Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安), who is seeking reelection, has introduced a range of fundraising merchandise, including tote bags, baseball caps, insulated bags, water bottles, sports towels, T-shirts, cellphone lanyards, MagSafe leather phone wallets and near-field communication (NFC) keychains.

Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an's campaign swag. CNA photo Oct. 18, 2026

Lai Kuan-chun (賴冠群), the campaign's event planning chief, told CNA the items were chosen because they are practical, everyday goods that people would want to carry. The NFC keychains are designed to broadcast a signal to compatible cellphones, directing users to the campaign's theme song, he added.

Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Taipei mayoral challenger Puma Shen (沈伯洋) has launched T-shirts, baseball caps, tote bags, handkerchiefs, embroidered patches, towels and plush toys featuring the campaign's mascots.

Tsai I-kai (蔡一愷), a spokesperson for Shen's campaign, said the items were designed to be practical and reflect the campaign slogan, "Future Soon."

Democratic Progressive Party Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen pose with his campaign merchandise. Photo courtesy of the Puma Shen campaign headquarters Oct. 18, 2026

Tsai also thanked supporters who call themselves "Ocean Current" (洋流) -- a play on Shen's Chinese name -- for producing their own campaign items, including posters, stickers, badges, banners and ribbons bearing the group's name. He said he hoped the initiative would spark further creativity and give supporters more ways to express their aspirations for Taipei.

In Changhua County in central Taiwan, DPP magistrate candidate Chen Su-yueh (陳素月) has prepared handouts such as tote bags, cellphone stands and tissues.

Liu Shan-ling (劉珊伶), a spokesperson for Chen's campaign, said several DPP candidates for county council and township chief had also produced items such as scouring sponges and wet wipes printed with photos of themselves alongside Chen.

A campaign worker for Democratic Progressive Party's Changhua County magistrate candidate Chen Su-yueh shows campaign giveaways. CNA photo Oct. 18, 2026

The candidates hope to boost one another's campaigns and help the party win as many county council and township chief seats as possible, Liu said.

KMT Changhua County magistrate candidate Wei Ping-cheng (魏平政) said his campaign had prepared face masks, scouring sponges, tissues, wet wipes, bottled water and UV arm sleeves made at his family's factory.

The daughter of Kuomintang's Changhua County magistrate candidate Wei Ping-cheng poses with Wei's campaign swag. CNA photo Oct. 18, 2026

The tissue packets feature a cartoon portrait of Wei designed by his daughter, he said.

Independent Changhua County magistrate candidate Chiu Chien-fu (邱建富) has prepared pens, placemats, face masks, handheld fans and socks to hand out.

Chiu Chien-fu, an independent candidate running for Changhua County magistrate. Photo courtesy of Chiu Chien-fu Oct. 18, 2026

Chiu said he often walks long distances while campaigning, and the socks symbolize his determination to go farther and move forward together with his supporters.

Another independent Changhua County magistrate hopeful, Chen Chung-chia (陳重嘉), told CNA by phone that he had prepared handouts including face masks. He said everyone has an equal right to participate in politics and urged voters to use their ballots to decide Changhua's future.

In the southern Taiwan city of Tainan, DPP mayoral candidate Chen Ting-fei (陳亭妃) has put up for sale a series of teddy bears inspired by daily life and local culture.

The Democratic Progressive Party's Tainan mayoral candidate Chen Ting-fei (center, holding microphone) poses with her series of campaign merchandise. Photo courtesy of Chen Ting-fei's office Oct. 18, 2026

Chen said supporters could collect the bears that suit their tastes and keep them as keepsakes. The bears also convey her campaign message that "Tainan is home" and that she would care for and cherish her home, she added.

Her KMT rival, Hsieh Lung-chieh (謝龍介), has opted for handheld fans and tissue packets.

Kuomintang Tainan mayoral candidate Hsieh Lung-chieh signs a campaign fan. Photo courtesy of Hsieh’s office, Oct. 18, 2026.

Fans help people keep cool in Tainan's hot weather, while tissues can be used to wipe away sweat or at mealtimes, Hsieh said. His major policy pledges are also printed on the items to help voters understand his plans for the city, he added.

(By Yeh Chen-yun and Wu Kuan-hsien)

【大紀元2026年10月18日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）10月18日，逾五千名來自台灣、韓國、日本、香港、澳門、馬來西亞、印尼、美國、丹麥與澳洲等地的部分法輪功學員齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會（台灣法會）。

今年台灣法會有18位法輪功學員上台發言。他們分享了在工作及日常生活中依循「真、善、忍」原則修煉的身心受益的體會，包括推廣神韻、發揚傳統文化以提升台灣各地社區文化素養及在中共迫害法輪功的27年中持續向世人講真相過程中的心得，也有學員分享了開天目後親歷的奇事。

## 自行車選手訓練途中遭嚴重車禍 修煉法輪功現奇跡

高雄學員莊博尹說，2024年7月他在訓練途中與一輛對向的貨車迎面相撞，造成臉部撕裂、氣胸、血胸及肝臟嚴重破裂。住院期間，父親拿了一本法輪功的主要著作《轉法輪》給他，讀完第一講，隔天他明顯感覺體力大幅恢復。

[![Image 5: 2026年10月18日，來自台灣、韓國、日本、香港、澳門、馬來西亞、印尼、美國、丹麥與澳洲等地的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（許基東／大紀元）](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872043-2610180440282378.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872043-2610180440282378.jpg)

2026年10月18日，來自台灣、韓國、日本、香港、澳門、馬來西亞、印尼、美國、丹麥與澳洲等地的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（許基東／大紀元）

莊博尹說，在普通病房他通讀了《轉法輪》三遍，並忍痛堅持煉功，身體恢復速度超出預期，醫生評估後為他拔除胸管，連原本需要進行的整形手術都不需要了。出院第一天他就重返訓練，回診時，醫生感到不可思議。他更在兩個半月後的自行車比賽中奪下第二名，所有車友都覺得這簡直是奇跡。

修煉前，他看著某些車友表現一般，比賽時卻能拿下冠軍，心裡便會妒忌；面對那些天才選手，也常懊惱自己能力不足。修煉後，他逐漸放下妒忌心與比較的心態，不再因焦慮失眠影響表現，能更加保持冷靜，靈活地改變戰術應賽。

面對隊友，他改變了態度，由嚴厲指責改以耐心分析、幽默善意的提醒，並尊重對方所有的努力和付出，使建議更容易被接受，也改善了團隊氣氛。

面對家人，他由過去的缺少耐心、語氣嚴苛且帶有掌控欲，轉為語氣溫和與善意溝通，給予家人理解與關心。

## 推廣神韻 提升台灣各地社區文化素養

桃園學員林紫榆分享了她在推廣神韻過程中的修煉體會。2025年10月中旬回到台灣後，她就想要如何用兩個多月時間有效率地推廣神韻。她靜心學法增長了智慧，決心「Cold Calling說明會」的方式，自己一人主動聯繫各地社區發展協會，舉辦神韻說明會。

[![Image 6: 2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（宋碧龍／大紀元）](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872084-261018070517100311.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872084-261018070517100311.jpg)

2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（宋碧龍／大紀元）

「每一個接通的電話，都是有緣人。」林紫榆逐漸學會以堅定、尊重對方的方式溝通。在一場神韻說明會中，當時假日的票快賣完了，有位太太說，聽說神韻很好看，她和先生都想看，如果沒有5,000元（台幣）的票，她就不看。這話給了她很大的觸動和啟發。後來只要有人嫌票價貴時，她就舉這位太太為例供對方參考，民眾都會接過資料研究一番。

她說，雖然單獨撥打陌生電話，但是自己並不孤獨，有很多團隊同修默默接力舉辦神韻說明會。她體會到，說明會能讓民眾了解神韻演出的內容並對傳統文化產生共鳴，進而訂票觀賞神韻，提升了各地社區的文化素養。2026年她開發了60餘場說明會，也體會到從Cold Calling、主講、公關、設備到後續接力過程中，同修們形成整體、齊心救人的堅定力量。

## 面對中共跨境迫害 助神韻順利演出

在國防科技研究單位工作的學員韋志龍說，他以「真、善、忍」對待同仁，並能很有效率地突破了關鍵技術研發，成功開發出許多新產品，完成了國防自主任務，深受長官和同仁的信任，得以在職場上從基層一路升遷到現在的主管職位。上司鼓勵他攻讀博士，未來他更有機會晉升到更高一級的管理職位。他對此抱持順其自然的態度，並帶著慈悲心持續在網絡上向更多可貴的中國人講真相。

[![Image 7: 2026年10月18日，來自台灣、韓國、日本、香港、澳門、馬來西亞、印尼、美國、丹麥與澳洲等地的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（許基東／大紀元）](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872042-2610180440162378.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872042-2610180440162378.jpg)

2026年10月18日，來自台灣、韓國、日本、香港、澳門、馬來西亞、印尼、美國、丹麥與澳洲等地的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（許基東／大紀元）

韋志龍提到，他今年1月承接了神韻在台灣巡迴演出某場的後勤安全組協調工作。在演出前的一個晚上的10點左右收到通知，館方稱收到兩封恐嚇信件，因此臨時要求主辦單位當天須完成維護安全計劃書。

他詢問全台保安協調人，他們均表示沒有案例可參考；他放下怕麻煩的想法，站在館方角度思考問題，撰寫維安疏散計劃書，最終他得以順利在晚上12點前完成計劃。

雖然館方這次在維安過程中要求很高，但他們積極配合。最後一場演出結束時，館長放下緊繃的臉，露出燦爛的笑容，祝賀演出圓滿成功，並感謝他們的配合。

## 生活中所遇到的事絕非偶然 應把握機會講真相

台北學員曹慧玲1998年開始修煉法輪功。她說，在未修煉前，就相信命運是天定的。父母過世時，她悲痛萬分；之後她放下對父母的依戀，才不難過了。她得法後體悟到，修煉大法，是對父母最好的回報。

曹慧玲的先生是在社會上有相當影響力的張教授，她回顧了三年前的一段心路歷程。當時她在社團課程中獲知她的先生已送醫搶救，她努力保持平靜，搭計程車趕赴醫院；她才在急救室待了不久，先生便被轉到往生室。

[![Image 8: 2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（宋碧龍／大紀元）](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872086-261018071144100311.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872086-261018071144100311.jpg)

2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾五千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會。（宋碧龍／大紀元）

在先生搶救和處理喪葬期間，她和醫師、禮儀社人員及前來張教授追思會的親友、同儕、長官講了法輪功真相。她分享親歷大法修煉的神奇。台灣1999年9.21地震時，他們在震央山頂的茶園絲毫未損；她的公公煉功，近90高齡安詳離世，身體冷凍兩週後依舊柔軟。

在這期間有親共的教授及幾位親共、罵台的留美同學都肯定張教授的奉獻。有些社會精英對「真、善、忍」產生興趣，甚至到她家了解法輪功。

她提到，今年國際扶輪年會期間活動頻繁，加上推廣《超限戰》特映會，雖然感到很累，但仍然出席了有許多國際友人參加的扶輪社晚宴，順利完成了自己想做的事。她認為，生活中所遇到的事絕非偶然，務必要把握機會救人。

## 新竹學員分享天目看到的神奇景象

新竹學員何遠談到，他修煉沒多久，就開了天目（位於兩眉之間，即俗稱的開天眼），可以看到另外空間的奇特景象，比如他跟家人到歐洲旅行時，看到很多宏偉的大教堂上方有小小的、跟東方的龍不一樣的飛龍在高處接近屋頂的地方飛；在亞洲，他也發現很多寺院外面的天空上有連綿不絕的寺院建築無限延伸，很宏偉、壯觀。

[![Image 9: 2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾5千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會（台灣法會）。（宋碧龍／大紀元）](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872212-261018070510100311.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872212-261018070510100311.jpg)

2026年10月18日，來自台灣、美國、加拿大、日本、韓國、馬來西亞及香港的部分法輪功學員逾5千人齊聚台北和平籃球館，參加2026台灣法輪大法修煉心得交流會（台灣法會）。（宋碧龍／大紀元）

台灣法會10月18日召開前夕，法輪功學員於17日在台北中正紀念堂前舉行大型排字活動。何遠分享，歷年參加排字時，他都能看到另外空間的景象，有一次看到金色的大光柱從排字學員組成的圖案裡往上伸，高到看不到頂；另一次看到從排字圖案裡衝出一條身體巨大的金龍；還有一年，他看到兩邊的黃瓦屋頂上面坐著許多神在看排字；另一年，他看到有一排大神圍著排字場地站成一圈觀看排字。

修煉26年的何遠說，他堅持每天學法，為解決學法時走神的問題，他開始每天背大法書中的若干段落，之後逐步增加進度，至今將大法書背完約9輪。背法能促使他過好心性關。他提到，修煉要向內找，但起初就是找不到自己的問題；後來他體會到，要找出是哪一顆心在起作用，一定是內心有執著才導致行為的產生。他找到自己存在堅持己見、爭鬥心、妒忌心、面子心等執著，並發現它們、去掉它們；他還體會到，要放下認為自己對的心、增加包容。

title: SA pushes for more money to adapt at COP31
summary: Severe climate shocks, record-breaking temperatures and devastating weather events worldwide have marked 2026 as a standout year for extreme climate events globally. South Africa has not been spared. In January, historic floods swept throug
content:
Severe climate shocks, record-breaking temperatures and devastating weather events worldwide have marked 2026 as a standout year for extreme climate events globally.

South Africa has not been spared. In January, historic floods swept through Limpopo and Mpumalanga, killing at least 30 people, damaging thousands of homes and causing billions of rands in infrastructure damage. Four months later, the Western Cape was hit, causing 11 fatalities, displacing over 200,000 people, and battering the province’s agricultural sector.

An unfolding Super El Niño threatens a hotter, drier summer marked by drought, wildfires, water shortages, food insecurity and heat-related illness, placing the responsibility on the government to safeguard residents from a warming world.

That is why, as South Africa heads to the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in November, increased adaptation finance is among the country’s top priorities in the climate negotiations.

### Adaptation and resilience

Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment Minister David Maynier said that the fact that, at only 4%, Africa’s emissions paled in the face of global greenhouse gas emissions made adaptation and resilience one of the main priorities for South Africa, given the country’s severe experience with storms, floods and drought.

Speaking at a national stakeholder consultation on South Africa’s negotiating mandate for COP31 on Friday, 16 October, Maynier said that South Africa’s negotiators would push for a benchmark to triple adaptation finance by 2035, the operationalisation of the global goal on adaptation, and adequate loss and damage funding.

Carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions from burning fossil fuels and industrial processes. This includes emissions from transport, electricity generation, and heating, but not land-use change. (Source: Our World in Data)

While the country’s negotiation team will focus heavily on adaptation, South Africa still has a case to answer for regarding the reduction of emissions. Granted, the country’s global emissions sit at 1.1% to 1.14%. However, the nation is[Africa’s biggest emitter](https://ourworldindata.org/profile/co2/south-africa), accounting for roughly 33% to more than 40% of the continent’s total emissions.

Maesela Kekana, the DFFE’s deputy director-general responsible for climate change and air quality, and the person who would lead the charge during the negotiations, said that nations had clear directions on what needed to be done on mitigation; however, the same could not be said for adaptation.

Maesela Kekana, the DFFE’s deputy director-general responsible for climate change and air quality. (Photo: Dianah Chiyangwa)

“On adaptation, we don’t really know where we are. Hence this Belém to Addis vision becomes quite important because it deals with key indicators that will tell us exactly how far we are in building resilience.”

Established during COP30 in Belém, Brazil, in 2025, the Belém–Addis Vision on Adaptation is a negotiation process intended to help countries put global adaptation goals into practice and measure progress towards them.

### **Loss and Damage fund needs a boost**

South Africa is one of 119 countries that have submitted more than 170 funding proposals to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD). Maynier said that after the floods in January devastated the Kruger National Park and surrounding areas, the country submitted a $20-million proposal to restore the flood-affected and associated conservation landscapes.

Floods sweep through Letaba, Kruger National Park, in January 2026. (Photo: SANParks)

While progress has been made with a dedicated FRLD, Kekana said that South Africa sought greater support for the fund, adding that “there’s quite a big gap between what is required to deal with these permanent losses and damages and what is on the table”.

The FRLD supports developing countries and communities affected by climate-related disasters; however, the fund faces a massive budget and liquidity shortfall.

Responding to questions from Daily Maverick about the likelihood of South Africa receiving funding, given the sheer volume of requests and the money available in the fund, Maynier said he hoped the proposal would succeed, adding that bilateral talks had already taken place to advocate for it.

Kenana said that South Africa’s negotiating team would call for more resources for the fund, but would also seek assistance from other financial institutions outside the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) financial mechanisms, such as the Clean Investment Fund.

David Maynier. (Photo: Gallo Images / Luba Lesolle)

Dipak Patel, deputy chairperson of the Presidential Climate Commission, said South Africa’s request would prove to be a test for the loss and damage fund.

“South Africa should treat this as a test case of what South Africa can actually present [to the summit] that would meet or pass muster with respect to what is required.

“I see the potential for loss and damage to be extended to climate-impacted events, whether that be severe flooding in Durban or severe warming in other parts of the country.

“But let us be aware that in a context where we might not be suffering the most damage, any global fund would have to prioritise on the basis of vulnerability and on the basis of their own socioeconomic position,” Patel said.

A drone view shows houses flooded after heavy rains in Durban, South Africa, February 20, 2025. (Photo: REUTERS/Rogan Ward)

### **Nations to take stock on climate action**

The second Global Stocktake (GST) will begin during this year’s summit. The process serves as an inventory of the planet, where countries and stakeholders assess where they are succeeding and where they are falling short in meeting the Paris Climate Agreement. The GST, which takes two years to complete, aims to inform the next round of climate action plans (nationally determined contributions, or NDCs).

The GST, which takes place every five years, could not come at a more significant time. In September, the United Nations Environment Programme released a report that found a 1.5°C overshoot is now widely unavoidable and would occur within years, bringing more frequent extreme weather events globally.

The Greenland ice sheet, facing intensifying global warming, is melting. (Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images)

The report, titled[Limiting Overshoot: Navigating Exceedance of 1.5°C and Pathways Towards Return](https://www.unep.org/en/news-and-stories/press-release/unep-world-set-cross-15degc-global-warming-can-still-limit-adapt-and), found that best-case projections peaked at 1.8°C and others exceeded 2°C, and it proposed an “overshoot, peak and decline” strategy to minimise the risks of extreme weather, ecosystem loss and irreversible tipping points.

The strategy, which includes immediate emissions cuts, transformational adaptation and governed carbon dioxide removal, would theoretically bring the world back below 1.5°C warming.

TEMPERATURE OVERSHOOT: EXCEED AND RETURN TO 1.5°C
Decades of insufficient action have locked us into three compounding challenges to limiting temperature overshoot, with an urgent need for action now. (Source: United Nations)

According to the UNFCCC, the stocktake can help policymakers and stakeholders strengthen their climate policies and commitments in their next round of NDCs, paving the way for accelerated action.

Referring to the stocktake, Maynier said it should assess progress beyond emissions reductions and focus on advancing climate finance, technology transfer, capacity building for developing countries and addressing loss and damage. **DM**

content:
1.   [回到首页](https://rfi.fr/cn/)
2.   /[中国](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD/)

RFI 法广中文 / 非洲时事

在东非国家索马里（la Somalie），在一项引入普选的选举改革框架内，原定2026年的大选现已延后。依照新的选举时间表，立法选举（les législatives）将于2027年4月展开，总统选举（la présidentielle）则定于2027年5月进行。这是本台法广非洲组（RFI Afrique）今天（2026年10月18号周日）刊出的最新法文消息之一。索马里独立国家选举委员会（la Commission électorale nationale indépendante）于本周四对外宣布的这一安排引发争议。索马里的中文国名也有译作索馬利亞（Federal Republic of Somalia）。

发表时间： 18/10/2026 - 22:58 更改时间： 18/10/2026 - 23:06

14 分钟 浏览时间

RFI carte d'archive / Afrique - Somalie et sa capitale Mogadiscio.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/220de308-cb30-11f1-90a3-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-18-D-FMM-Image-Afrique-Somalie-carte-archive-RFI.jpg)

 法广(RFI)存档地图 / 非洲 - 索马里：首都是摩加迪沙（Mogadiscio） RFI carte d'archive / Afrique - Somalie et sa capitale Mogadiscio. © Studio FMM

[![Image 2: 法广(RFI)存档地图 / 非洲 - 索马里：首都是摩加迪沙（Mogadiscio） RFI carte d'archive / Afrique - Somalie et sa capitale Mogadiscio.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/220de308-cb30-11f1-90a3-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/2026-10-18-D-FMM-Image-Afrique-Somalie-carte-archive-RFI.jpg) 法广(RFI)存档地图 / 非洲 - 索马里：首都是摩加迪沙（Mogadiscio） RFI carte d'archive / Afrique - Somalie et sa capitale Mogadiscio. © Studio FMM](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9C%8B/20261018-rfi%E6%B3%95%E5%BB%A3-%E5%B0%BC%E5%8F%A4%E6%8B%89-%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2-%E7%B4%A2%E9%A6%AC%E9%87%8C%E5%A4%A7%E9%81%B8%E5%BB%B6%E8%87%B32027%E6%9C%89%E7%88%AD%E8%AD%B0)
位于非洲之角(la[Corne de l’Afrique](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/corne-de-l-afrique/))的[索马里](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E5%85%B3%E9%94%AE%E8%AF%8D/%E7%B4%A2%E9%A9%AC%E9%87%8C/)（la [Somalie](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/somalie/)）终于确定了新一届大选的时间表。本台法广[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)组（RFI Afrique）于2026年10月18号星期天刊出的法文消息说，立法选举定于2027年4月投票，随后将在5月份进行总统选举。索马里独立国家选举委员会于10月15日（周四）宣布了这一安排。上述选举原定是在今年（2026年）举行，但为了推进旨在建立“普选制度”（le suffrage universel,）的选举改革，而被推迟。

[![Image 3: Sheikh Mohamud Hassan, Rais wa Somalia](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f486602-1a08-11f0-ad08-005056bf30b7/w:1024/2025-03-28T194711Z_1852271011_RC21ZAANYA9P_RTRMADP_3_SOMALIA-USA-DIPLOMACY.JPG) 存档图片 / 非洲 ：索马里总统哈桑·谢赫·马哈茂德。 Image d'archive / Afrique - Somalie : Instaurer le suffrage universel, une volonté forte du président, Hassan Cheikh Mohamoud. Ici, le président somalien Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. (illustration) REUTERS - Annegret Hilse / archive RFI](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/hassan-cheikh-mohamoud/)
同一法文报道说，任期即将届满的索马里现总统哈桑·谢赫·马哈茂德（le président somalien [Hassan Sheikh Mohamud](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/hassan-cheikh-mohamoud/)）有强烈的意愿要实现普选。那将是索马里民众自​​1969年以来首次能够按照“一人一票”（une personne, un vote）的原则进行投票。不过，这一改革和新的选举时间表已经遭受强烈反对。

**--****索马里推迟大选引起争议****--**

据本台法广（RFI）[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E5%85%B3%E9%94%AE%E8%AF%8D/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)通讯员卡艾乐（Gaëlle Laleix）于发自东非次区的法文报道，这一选举计划面临两方面的异议。首先是反对派（l’opposition）。曾于2017年至2022年担任过索马里总统职务的总统选举候选人之一：穆罕默德·阿卜杜拉希·穆罕默德（[Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, dit Mohamed Farmaajo](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/mohamed-abdullahi-farmajo/)）表示：“这个单方面的选举进程对索马里国家构成一种威胁。”

[![Image 4: 存档图片 / 非洲：索马里：穆罕默德·阿卜杜拉希·穆罕默德（Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, dit Mohamed Farmaajo） Image d'archive / Afrique : le président de la Somalie Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, alias Farmajo, ici à New York, le 23 septembre 2019.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a3991a0-0faf-11ea-a4e9-005056a99247/w:1024/063_1176667261_0.jpg) 存档图片 / 非洲：索马里：穆罕默德·阿卜杜拉希·穆罕默德（Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, dit Mohamed Farmaajo） Image d'archive / Afrique : le président de la Somalie Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, alias Farmajo, ici à New York, le 23 septembre 2019. Riccardo Savi / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / AFP](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/mohamed-abdullahi-farmajo/)
另一位前总统谢里夫·谢赫·艾哈迈德（[Sharif Sheikh Ahmed](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/sharif-sheikh-ahmed/)）补充说：“这一举措可能会导致出现‘平行选举’的风险和政治不稳定（une instabilité politique）。”

[![Image 5: Shugaban Somalia Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/74e42514-14b3-11ea-a946-005056bf7c53/w:1024/Sharif%20Sheikh%20Ahmed_0.JPG) Image d'archive / Afrique : Somalie - Sharif Sheikh Ahmed 非洲 - 索马里：前总统谢里夫·谢赫·艾哈迈德（Sharif Sheikh Ahmed) REUTERS/Murad Sezer](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/sharif-sheikh-ahmed/)
同一法文报道接着继续指出，另一方面的反对来自两个联邦成员州：邦特兰（[Puntland](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/puntland/)）和朱巴兰（Jubaland）。这两个加入联邦的州都认为，现任总统哈桑·谢赫·马哈茂德（Hassan Sheikh Mohamoud）所推行的选举改革，唯一目的就是延长其权力。

**--****索马里准备与普选制接轨****–**

本台法广[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)组（RFI Afrique）的报道介绍说，迄今为止，[索马里](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%97%9C%E9%8D%B5%E8%A9%9E/%E7%B4%A2%E9%A6%AC%E9%87%8C/)的选举一直采取间接方式，并基于氏族制度(**Système clanique**)。由长老们（les anciens）指定议会成员，再由议会成员选出总统。若实行普选，将会大幅削弱氏族在政治游戏（le jeu politique）中的影响力，并增强执政当局的首脑（le chef de l’exécutif.）。

[![Image 6: 存档图片 / 非洲 - 索马里:坐落于首都摩加迪沙（Mogadiscio）的总统府。 Image d'archive / Afrique ：une vue du palais présidentiel à Mogadiscio, en Somalie, le 28 décembre 2021.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c8bdd970-6e95-11ed-a7db-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/2022-11-27T191203Z_866562579_RC2ONR9OLMUA_RTRMADP_3_SOMALIA-ATTACKS.JPG) 存档图片 / 非洲 - 索马里:坐落于首都摩加迪沙（Mogadiscio）的总统府。 Image d'archive / Afrique ：une vue du palais présidentiel à Mogadiscio, en Somalie, le 28 décembre 2021. © FEISAL OMAR / REUTERS](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20261018-somalie-le-calendrier-pour-les-%C3%A9lections-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rales-est-d%C3%A9j%C3%A0-contest%C3%A9)
本台法广（RFI）[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%97%9C%E9%8D%B5%E8%A9%9E/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)通讯员在这篇法文报道的最后一个段落中引述[战略研究所]（Institut des études stratégiques）女研究员塞拉姆·塔德塞·德米西（Mme Selam Tadesse Demissie）的分析指出，在索马里的政治生活中，普选是一个“频繁提及但尚未实现”的计划。她建议要“循序渐进”（_une approche par étape_），从地方选举开始。她提醒说：“否则，索马里将停留于一种恶性循环，即每一次选举都会成为引发冲突的导火索。”

（ 翻译和编辑：法广[RFI](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/)电台记者 尼古拉）

在非洲足联（CAF）2026年至2027年冠军联赛框架内，坦桑尼亚 [非洲青年队]（Young Africans）于2026年10月17日周六以4比0大胜主场的马达加斯加的CFFA足球队。刚果民主共和国（la RD Congo）的TP Mazembe则当天下午晚些时候，在卢本巴希（Lubumbashi）主场踢平突尼斯（la Tunisie）的[非洲人俱乐部队]（Club Africain）。

 非洲足球 / 非洲足球协会联合会（CAF-Confédération Africaine de Football）冠军联赛（Ligue des champions de la CAF）的冠军奖金金额现已增加200万美元，攀升至600万美元。 Image d'archive / RFI Afrique Foot : La Ligue des champions de la CAF - Confédération Africaine de Football passera à 6 millions de dollars, soit une augmentation de 2 millions de dollars. [非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)足球协会联合会（CAF-Confédération Africaine de Football）冠军联赛（[Ligue des champions de la CAF](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/tag/ligue-des-champions-caf/)）的冠军奖金金额现已增加200万美元，攀升至600万美元。

[![Image 2: 存档图片 - 非洲足球 / 非洲足球协会联合会（CAF-Confédération Africaine de Football）冠军联赛（Ligue des champions de la CAF）的冠军奖金金额现已增加200万美元，攀升至600万美元。 Image d'archive / RFI Afrique Foot : La Ligue des champions de la CAF - Confédération Africaine de Football passera à 6 millions de dollars, soit une augmentation de 2 millions de dollars. (illustration) © Courtesy of CAF](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/20261018-rfi%E6%B3%95%E5%BB%A3-%E5%B0%BC%E5%8F%A4%E6%8B%89-%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2%E8%B6%B3%E7%90%832026-2027%E5%85%A9%E5%A0%B4%E5%86%A0%E8%BB%8D%E8%81%AF%E8%B3%BD)
**--****坦桑尼亚球队客场大胜****--**

据本台法广体育组（[RFI Sports](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/sports/)）[[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E5%85%B3%E9%94%AE%E8%AF%8D/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)足球]([Afrique Foot](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique-foot/))的报道，2026年10月17日周六，坦桑尼亚（la Tanzanie）的 [非洲青年队]（Young Africans）在客场以4比0大胜马达加斯加(Madagascar)的CFFA足球队。当天下午晚些时候，在刚果民主共和国的卢本巴希（Lubumbashi），刚果（金）的TP Mazembe足球队主场，被来自突尼斯的[非洲人俱乐部队]（Club Africain）1比1逼平。

Image d'archive / Afrique Foot - Young Africans, Tanzania.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/72cea600-1607-11ea-a92d-005056a99247/w:1024/Young_Africans_SC_%28logo%29.png)

 存档图片 / 非洲足球：坦桑尼亚（la Tanzanie）的[非洲青年队]（Young Africans） Image d'archive / Afrique Foot - Young Africans, Tanzania. wikipedia.org

10月17日星期六，坦桑尼亚（la Tanzanie）[[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)青年队]（Young Africans）在以4比0战胜CFFA队之后，基本锁定了非洲冠军联赛（la Ligue des champions de la CAF）的参赛资格。在对阵马达加斯加CFFA足球队的比赛中，坦桑尼亚（la Tanzanie）[非洲青年队]（Young Africans）没有遭遇麻烦。这场以4比0结束的胜利几乎确保了晋级。双方的下回合较量将于10月21日下周三在达累斯萨拉姆（Dar es Salaam）进行。

**--****刚果****(****金****)****球队主场踢平****--**

10月17日星期六下午晚些时候， 刚果（金）的TP Mazembe足球队主场在卢本巴希（Lubumbashi）与突尼斯的[非洲人俱乐部]（Club Africain）的对阵中，遭遇对手顽强抵抗，最终被以1比1逼平，后续仍要努力。双方的胜负悬念有待10月25日下周日在突尼斯举行的下一回合的比赛中揭晓。

刚果（金）的TP Mazembe足球队](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/93d2f02a-4ab0-11eb-9d0f-005056a964fe/w:1024/home-1609329533_illustration-logo-tout-puissant-mazembe-8-etoiles_1609329533_1609329533.jpg)

 Logo du TP Mazembe 刚果（金）的TP Mazembe足球队 © TP Mazembe

本台法广体育组（RFI Sports）[非洲足球](Afrique Foot)栏目补充说，还有以约翰内斯堡为基地的南非（l’Afrique du Sud）[奥兰多海盗队]（Orlando Pirates）以1-0击败纳米比亚（la Namibie）的[[非洲](https://www.rfi.fr/tw/%E9%97%9C%E9%8D%B5%E8%A9%9E/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2/)之星队]（African Stars），在晋级的道路上赢得了关键一步。

# Taichung Arena on track for completion in 2030: City gov't

10/18/2026 09:02 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Photo courtesy of the Taichung City government

Taichung, Oct. 18 (CNA) The Taichung Arena is nearly 20 percent complete and remains on track to be finished in 2030, the Taichung City government said Sunday.

The project had been scheduled to be 15 percent complete by now. Underground excavation has finished, and construction is entering the main structural phase, the city's Construction Bureau said in a press release.

Located in Taichung's Beitun District, the arena was designed jointly by Japanese and Taiwanese architects. Construction began on June 1, 2024, after years of planning.

Covering about 6.95 hectares, the complex will have four basement levels, a four-story main arena and a three-story secondary arena, the bureau said.

The main arena is designed to seat about 15,500 spectators, and the secondary arena about 3,000, it added.

The main arena will host international sporting events such as basketball, volleyball, badminton, tennis, futsal and martial arts competitions, as well as concerts, exhibitions and other large-scale events. The secondary arena will be used for athletes' warm-ups and training, as well as for smaller performances and exhibitions.

The complex will also incorporate acoustic design, rainwater recycling and an energy-saving design, the bureau said, adding that an elevated open-air walkway linking the two venues will include walking and running paths, and a rooftop garden is also planned.

The city government has said the project is intended to meet central Taiwan's demand for a large indoor sports and entertainment venue, complementing existing facilities in northern and southern Taiwan.

The Taichung Arena is separate from the planned Taiwan Dome (台灣超巨蛋), a much larger indoor baseball stadium for which the city signed a build-operate-transfer agreement on Friday. Initial plans call for the dome to seat at least 45,000 spectators and to include commercial facilities, hotels and space for major events.

(By Chao Li-yen and Lee Hsin-Yin)

content:
## Details

**Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history.
 The way it works is that there is a different theme each month:

*   January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity)
*   February: **industrial modernisation** (industrial revolutions 1-4)
*   March: **"the axial age"** (Moses, Buddha, Socrates, Laozi, Zoroaster)
*   April: **literary history** (oral to internet)
*   May: **energy** (from muscle to nuclear)
*   June: **different modes of living** (e.g. pastoralists, fishing)
*   July: **history of science** (Aristotle, Newton etc)
*   August: **politics and power** (tribes to superpowers)
*   September: **art history** (who and what is art for?)
*   October: **cradles of civilisation** (Egypt, Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Yellow River, Olmecs and Chico Norte)
*   November: **economics and trade** (bartering to bitcoin?)
*   December: **progressive revelation** (Abraham, Moses, Jesus Christ, Muhammed, Baháʼu'lláh)

There are 5 recommended texts each month - you can read one or more of them if you'd like and this will form the basis of the live discussion.

This is considered an "intentional community" which exists to study human history in the spirit of common humanity.

So it's like a community which agrees that the world needs a new meta-narrative because the old ones are mutually exclusive and seen as not inclusive enough by broad segments of the population - which is driving culture wars and distracting massively from sustainable development.

We don't purport to dictate the meta-narrative of human history - however we intend to help people build their own meta-narratives or meta-frameworks for understanding how all people are part of the same story and share common heritage.

Please join us on telegram to build friendships and feel belonging [https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns](https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns).

title: Tech Talk: AI in Practice with Bethany Janos, Fri, Nov 6, 2026, 1:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: **How can developers use AI effectively without losing sight of the fundamentals?** AI is changing how software is built and how developers approach everyday problems. For students and early-career engineers, keeping up with new tools and p
content:
**How can developers use AI effectively without losing sight of the fundamentals?**

AI is changing how software is built and how developers approach everyday problems. For students and early-career engineers, keeping up with new tools and practices can feel overwhelming. Understanding how the industry has evolved and learning to make thoughtful decisions about AI can help you adapt and build skills that last.

Our guest speaker, **Bethany Janos**, is a senior software engineer at GitHub who works on the backend systems powering Copilot chat and agents. Since starting her career in 2018, she has built backend systems across different products and teams. She is also passionate about mentoring students and helping new developers build the technical skills and confidence they need to succeed.

In this live Tech Talk, Bethany will explore practical approaches to working with AI in software engineering. She will cover a brief history of the field, explain harnesses and why they matter, and introduce MCPs, plugins, skills, and the concept of tokenmaxxing. She will also discuss when AI can be useful and when it is better to set it aside.

You will gain a clearer understanding of the tools and workflows shaping AI-assisted development and how to make informed decisions about using them. You will also learn what to consider as you build your skills and prepare for a software industry that continues to evolve.

Bring your questions and curiosity about AI! Follow along with Bethany as she unpacks these tools and approaches, and think about how you can use them in your own learning and development projects.

Join us on **Friday, November 6 at 1 PM PT | 3 PM CT | 4 PM ET** and save your spot now to explore practical ways to work with AI and prepare for the future of software engineering.

title: 限租能压低房租，却多不出一套房
