title: Anatomy of a lie: how misinformation is spreading through US midterm campaigns
summary: W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardia
content:
W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026)

The smear campaign began when Talarico, [the Democratic candidate](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/04/texas-primaries-democrats-texas) for the US Senate in Texas, was not seen in public for nine days. His campaign was slow to explain why. While nature abhors a vacuum, Donald Trump and social media seize on one and weaponise it.

On 30 September, Talarico spoke at a Hispanic Business Council event by video. He had been diagnosed with the flu at an urgent care facility in Dallas after “starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago”, he said, and would not appear in person because he had a fever and was still contagious.

On 7 October, the president held a rally in San Antonio, Texas, and claimed without evidence that “Tala-freako”, as he nicknames the Democrat, is vegan. [Trump asserted](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/08/donald-trumps-texas-rally-rocked-by-repeated-protests): “He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”

On the same day, an X account with the username “Dan The Man, Always with a Plan” and a photo of “Trump 2028” cap tweeted without evidence: “He had a mental health crisis. That is what I heard from someone who would know inside information.”

On 8 October, Steve Bannon, a former White House chief strategist, stirred the pot further on his influential War Room podcast in an interview with former Trump fundraiser Caroline Wren, [who baselessly claimed](https://x.com/RealAmVoice/status/2108313243382952207?s=20): “I’m hearing that he checked himself into a mental institution – that he had a full-blown, like, mental breakdown.”

On the same day, Ken Paxton, the Republican running against Talarico, weighed in with [a social media post](https://x.com/KenPaxtonTX/status/2108250407277588546?s=20) that showed Talarico on a “Wanted” poster and said: “Jimmy appears to be having a full-blown mental Tala-freak-out on the national stage. My campaign has a simple request: proof of life.”

On 9 October, Spencer Pratt, a former candidate for mayor of Los Angeles, [offered his take](https://x.com/spencerpratt/status/2108553958696399249?s=20): “My sources are telling me Talarico is in a mental health facility. His campaign has stopped actively planning events in the vital homestretch of the campaign.”

Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux theater on 31 August. Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images

Right media sites swung into action. RedState, the Daily Wire, the Right Scoop, Twitchy and PJ Media all amplified the false claims. Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, put more toxins in the bloodstream with posts such as: “The Talarico campaign is hiding something big that voters ought to know about.”

Then, on 11 October, came the supposed coup de grâce. Conservative social media influencer Nick Sortor posted a 47-second audio clip on X that he said proved that Talarico had been discharged earlier in the week from [Lindner Center of Hope](https://lindnercenterofhope.org/), a mental health treatment centre in Mason, Ohio.

The call was placed by Rhein Amacher, a self-described “right-wing provocateur”. In the clip, a woman whom Sorter claimed was an employee there says it looked like Talarico “was just discharged this evening”. The online Maga faithful were jubilant.

But not for long. The Bulwark obtained the full phone call showing the purported employee had repeatedly denied any record of Talarico being at the centre. The timeline also did not add up. Amacher said he made the call to the mental health centre on Saturday evening, but Talarico was seen at the Austin City Limits music festival on Friday. On Saturday, he made an appearance at a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas.

The Lindner Center of Hope [wrote in an X post](https://x.com/LindnerCtrHope/status/2109430626562785517?s=20) on Sunday that Talarico “has never received treatment” from the facility. Talarico replied to the post, saying, “I’ve never even been to Ohio.” He included a tears of joy emoji.

JT Ennis, a spokesperson for Talarico, called Sorter’s claim “a lie designed to promote a pathetic conspiracy theory” in an X post and wrote that Talarico had been recovering from the flu at his home in Austin. Talarico has type 1 diabetes, placing him at higher risk for flu-related complications.

Even Maga followers began to acknowledge that the claim had collapsed. But if the episode appeared absurd, its implications for the midterms were serious.

[Reed Galen](https://x.com/reedgalen), a former Republican strategist and cofounder of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group, said: “It was a bit wild but a good reminder to all of us how sophisticated, effective and efficient the rightwing/ bot/ Russian generated misinformation-disinformation machine is.

“This story came from some weirdos in Ohio or whatever but the point is that someone or something picked it up and amplified it to a point where – despite no evidence of reality – it became something that was an issue in the [Texas](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/texas) Senate campaign.”

Galen added: “Even if Talarico wins, that in and of itself was a win for the tactic. If you have the ability and the willingness to do this stuff, it’s not gonna work every time, but if you do it a lot, sometimes you’re gonna have success, and sometimes those successes might be strategic in nature, not just tactical.”

Disinformation has been rampant in elections for at least a decade and 2026 is no different. NewsGuard, a company that tracks online misinformation, says it has identified and debunked [25 false claims](https://www.newsguardtech.com/special-reports/2026-elections-misinformation-tracker/) about the midterms that have gone viral on social media platforms.

Its list of false claims includes [Abdul El-Sayed](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/abdul-el-sayed), the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan, having called for sharia law in the US during a 2022 speech; a Dominion Voting Systems whistleblower accusing US politicians of taking millions of dollars in bribes to rig the 2026 midterm elections; and Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign paying for a Texas billboard that says “Pedos Ain’t That Bad”.

Another example related to an image that purportedly showed Rob Sand, a centrist Democratic candidate for governor of Iowa, campaigning with the progressives Ilhan Omar and Tim Walz. NewsGuard found it was generated by artificial intelligence (AI).

Even as AI gives new tools to nefarious actors, defences have been weakened. Last year, US secretary Marco Rubio [shut down](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/us-state-department-closing-office-aimed-countering-foreign-disinformation-2025-04-16/) the state department’s Counter Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference office, accusing it of censorship and wasting US taxpayer money.

Major tech platforms – notably Musk’s X and Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta – have gutted trust, safety and factchecking teams, turning online spaces into a lawless wild west. Musk has [spent a record $366m](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/13/elon-musk-political-donor-midterm-elections) in ⁠the election cycle so far to help Republicans retain control of Congress.

[Richard Hasen](https://law.ucla.edu/faculty/faculty-profiles/richard-l-hasen), a professor at UCLA School of Law and election law expert, said: “When you’ve got Elon Musk owning one of the important social media platforms and being a vector for spreading the misinformation, and also when you’ve got the companies like Meta no longer doing the same kind of trust and safety work, it’s just an atmosphere where this kind of stuff can spread.”

But there is another, more optimistic perspective. While the Talarico rumours spread like wildfire in corners of the internet, they did not penetrate the mainstream media, and fizzled out once the reality became clear.

Hasen added: “The Talarico case shows the limits of being able to do this. This was something that was easily disproven and could have potentially even backfired, showing that the anti-Talarico forces are so desperate that they have to make up a false claim to try to boost a weak candidate.

“Every election now we’re hearing it’s going to be ‘the AI election’ and voters are going to be tricked. What I think is happening in part is that everyone’s on their guard. We all know that we can’t necessarily believe our eyes or our ears and things that a politician might appear to say or do might not necessarily be true, so that’s a little bit of a natural check.”

Hasen points out that candidates are better equipped to dismantle digital lies. To debunk the rumour, Talarico shared home security camera footage with the New York Times, establishing his presence at home. “Because we’re leaving digital footprints everywhere, that sometimes could be another way to debunk a rumour.”

[Tara Setmayer](https://www.tarasetmayer.com/), a former Republican communications director on Capitol Hill, also believes that the conspiracy theories have lost their novelty value. “The voters have become hip to this game,” she said. “There are too many other negative things going on in everyday American lives, so I don’t think these types of cheap attacks are going to resonate at this point.

“The difference between this election cycle and past election cycles is that, because it seems like we’ve been here before and we know how batshit crazy Maga can be, that mainstream media isn’t platforming the crazy as often,” said Setmayer._“_ They’re actually reporting it in a way with the healthy amount of scepticism that it deserves, so it’s dismissed off the top whereas in the past it was so novel.”

Setmayer added: “At this point now it feels like [Donald Trump](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump) and Maga’s greatest hits: we’re really in the fat Elvis period of the Maga election campaign tactics and it’s obvious to everyone. The absurdity is finally breaking through even with some Republican voters, evidenced by how terrible Donald Trump’s numbers are and Republicans writ large.”

title: What’s Going On With China’s Military Exercises This Week? - Domino Theory
summary: Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they ar
content:
Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they are extraordinary.

“China launches 5-day military exercises after Taiwan’s National Day,” read one typical [headline](https://www.rti.org.tw/en/news?uid=3&pid=237144), from Radio Taiwan International. Reuters [described](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-says-it-is-closely-monitoring-series-chinese-live-fire-drills-2026-10-12/) “a series of Chinese live-fire drills,” based on navigation restriction notices published by the China Maritime Safety Administration for five zones in different regions. These areas are all close to China’s coast and range from the Bohai Sea in the north to the South China Sea in the south.

The Chinese Communist Party’s decision to conduct live-fire drills immediately after the National Day address “does nothing to advance regional peace and will only heighten regional tensions,” said Chuang Jui-hsiung (莊瑞雄), head of the Democratic Progressive Party caucus, speaking at a [press conference](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eYyNoOU-StY) on Monday about a different National Day speech by opposition leader Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜).

In [previous years](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgd4yn45qlo), China has launched major military exercises around Taiwan after National Day, framing them as a response to perceived provocations in the president’s speech.

But is that actually what is happening here?

There are some problems with this theory.

As all the coverage acknowledges, these drills are neither around nor close to Taiwan. China has not publicly commented on the exercises this week, nor tied them to Lai’s speech.

The five drill areas described appear to be a partial snapshot of scheduled Chinese military activity at sea this week. A comprehensive review of the Maritime Safety Administration’s website by Domino Theory revealed a total of 12 relevant notices published before Monday. Four of them were for live-fire exercises, the remaining eight were for non-specified military training. The drills are of varying lengths of time, some even extending longer than seven days.

In September, 28 navigation restriction notices were published for live-fire exercises alone. It doesn’t appear that any of these were reported on as being unusual, despite there being broad crossover in the locations involved with the “five” this week.

“I don’t see anything in these notices that strikes me as particularly unusual or significant,” Ethan Connell for Taiwan Security Monitor, a group at George Mason University, told Domino Theory.

The Maritime Safety Administration regularly issues navigation warnings for live-fire exercises and military training, Connell said in a written response, adding “there isn’t much evidence that these five exercises are part of any larger, coordinated training or operation.”

Taiwan’s defense minister, Wellington Koo (顧立雄), told the legislature on Monday that the drills appear to be a “not particularly large,” routine exercise, adding that Taiwan must be cautious and will continue to monitor the situation, adding, “You can see that the timing was deliberately chosen to follow the October 10th National Day address.”

The drills “are likely a response to Lai’s speech, which is to be expected,” said Lyle Morris, a senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis. “But nothing to panic about.”

The number of exercises is noteworthy, Morris said, but doesn’t rise to the level of something like the “[Joint Sword](https://dominotheory.com/china-announces-military-exercises-around-taiwan/)” drills from previous years. Those were among the exercises that took place around Taiwan.

Other analysts disagree about the timing.

“I would not interpret these as exercises targeting President Lai Ching-te,” said Chieh Chung (揭仲), a fellow at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research think tank in Taipei.

Chieh wrote to Domino Theory that [Lai’s speech](https://dominotheory.com/taiwan-intent-on-increasing-defense-spending/) had been uncontroversial this year, but pointed out: “Leaving observers to speculate whether the drills were triggered by Beijing’s displeasure with President Lai’s speech is enough for Beijing to achieve its objective.”

Lai’s only significant mention of China was to say it was engaged in authoritarian expansion, applying pressure “through military and gray-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.”

“Most notices were issued before Lai’s speech, so the drills look routine,” said Ben Lewis, who runs the website [PLATracker](https://www.platracker.com/), which records Chinese military activity around Taiwan. Lewis doesn’t think that the drills are any more significant than they look. But he warned that a closure moving into the Strait or near Taiwan would change this view.

“The CCP disguises its intrusive actions under the pretexts of law enforcement and scientific research, attempting to expand its operational scope during non-conflict periods and create the illusion of de facto jurisdiction,” the Defense Ministry told Domino Theory, answering a question on whether the five drill areas were different in some way. “These moves severely undermine the international order and challenge our law enforcement authority within our waters.”

The Chinese military near Taiwan had been relatively quiet earlier this week, according to [data](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2109811367033143387?s=20) published by the Ministry of National Defense, although its data for [yesterday](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2110536140809719853?s=20) showed more activity, including a circumnavigation of Taiwan by an [uncrewed aerial vehicle](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110355583971053644?s=20), or UAV.

China has also this week deployed a carrier battle group into the Western Pacific, centered around the Liaoning aircraft carrier. Based on [information](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110317371932205415?s=20) published by the Japanese military, the battle group passed through the Okinawa archipelago and was located approximately 370 kilometers to the east of Taiwan on Wednesday.

Taiwan’s data for Chinese activity do not routinely show information about ship type and location, unlike the data for aircraft. Wednesday’s data do not appear to show any flights by Chinese naval aviation east of but close to Taiwan. Taiwan’s Defense Ministry said today that it wouldn’t comment on specifics of the carrier’s activity.

Jason Wang, the chief operating officer of geointelligence firm ingeniSPACE, said it was wrong to associate the drills with the National Day speech and that tying the two together helped with United Front narratives. “These drills were planned and should be seen in the context of raising overall readiness,” Wang said.

Experts contacted for this story did not think the five drill areas reported on this week are different or more significant than the other announced drills that have received less attention. Nor is there any obvious reason that attention should be placed on these when similar exercises last month were largely ignored.

Nonetheless, even if this week is not unusual, that may be its own problem. This high tempo of training is cause for concern in itself. China, said Wang from ingeniSPACE, is exercising more than it is resting.

title: Nutrition experts call for big food ban at biennial congress
summary: Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event. From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for
content:
Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event.

From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for Dietetics in South Africa (Adsa) hosted their biennial Nutrition Congress, a platform for researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, practitioners and other stakeholders to share and discuss current evidence and developments in nutrition.

This year companies Danone Southern Africa (Danone SA), Unilever South Africa and PepsiCo were exhibitors at the event, which nutrition experts said was a conflict of interest.

According to Tamryn Frank, a nutrition expert and senior lecturer at the University of the Western Cape’s School of Public Health, it is a conflict of interest for an event that aims to improve nutrition in South Africa to have companies like Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo, which produce and sell ultra-processed foods, sponsor it and exhibit at it. Frank added that there was increasing evidence that ultra-processed foods were linked to poor health outcomes like obesity and non-communicable diseases.

PepsiCo’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

If the ultra-processed food industry was allowed to sponsor and exhibit at the Nutrition Congress, to the layman it created the impression that the congress endorsed these companies as part of a solution to SA’s nutrition crisis, Frank said.

Nutrition expert and consultant researcher at the South African Medical Research Council, Catherine Pereira-Kotze, noted that since South Africa was characterised by undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, together with overweight and obesity, and high levels of poverty, inequality, unemployment and various other social problems, families should not be spending the little they had on ultra-processed foods. Rather, families should be prioritising fruit, vegetables and whole foods in accordance with [national food-based dietary guidelines](https://www.fao.org/nutrition/education/food-dietary-guidelines/regions/countries/south-africa/en/).

“The term ‘healthwashing’ comes to mind where by being aligned with this event it indicates that they are part of the solution. Because if you see the Nutrition Congress’ logo alongside the sponsors or the logos of these ultra-processed food companies I think it gives the impression that they are healthy options,” said Frank.

To protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank, Pereira-Kotze and other nutrition experts shared protest slides during their presentations and created a petition.

### Nutrition experts take a stand

Concerned about the alleged conflict of interest, Frank created a slide to use in her presentation condemning the ultra-processed food industry’s involvement in the congress.The slide stated:

“I DO NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Frank saw it fit to make this the third slide of her presentation as the second slide was a mandatory funding disclosure slide, she said. Frank shared the slide with other concerned speakers who also incorporated it into their presentations.

Zandile Kubeka, the Department of Health Deputy Director of Dietetics in the Child and Youth Health Directorate, shared a similar slide inspired by Frank’s during her presentation. The slide stated:

“THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH DOES NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Kubeka also noted the presence of ultra-processed food industry sponsors and exhibitors at the Nutrition Congress, and raised concerns regarding potential conflicts of interest in relation to their participation, according to Department of Health spokesperson Foster Mohale.

To further protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank had created a [petition](https://awethu.amandla.mobi/petitions/ban-big-food-from-the-nutrition-congress)with the help of Amandla.mobi, she said.

The petition first called on the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA to announce that no companies connected with ultra-processed foods would be allowed to sponsor or exhibit at future congresses or events. Second, they must issue an apology for allowing the ultra-processed food industry to participate in the congress.

### Safeguarding integrity

The Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA shared a collective written response by NSSA representative Elize Symington and Adsa president Maria van der Merwe in response to questions sent by Daily Maverick.

According to the Nutrition Society of SA, Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo complied with NSSA and Adsa’s criteria to participate.

All applications for participation as sponsors or exhibitors at the congress were accompanied by the information entities wanted to share and products to be exhibited, and an illustration of the exhibition stand, all of which had to be approved prior to the congress, it said.

It added that the congress organising committee also reviewed exhibition applications against healthy eating guidelines, compliance with applicable regulations, and alignment with the values and principles of the congress as guided by international consensus.

All congress exhibitors were allocated a stand in one of the exhibition areas to display the brands and products at a fee, and exhibition and sponsorship income was paid into pooled congress funds, according to the organisers.

Danone's exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Danone SA)

Although the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA recognised that commercial sponsorship of nutrition-related scientific and professional activities may create actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest, they did not agree that participation under the safeguards described compromised the independence or integrity of the congress, they said.

For this congress, exhibitors and sponsors were screened and had no role in determining the programme or in the selection of abstracts or speakers, according to the organisers. Private sector participation did not constitute or imply endorsement of any exhibitor’s products or practices, and all speakers declared their affiliations and funding during presentations, they added. The congress’ commitment to open debate on this topic was demonstrated by the inclusion of two sessions specifically addressing conflicts of interest in the programme.

Feedback received this year, including differing perspectives from across the nutrition community, would form part of the host organisations’ ongoing review. Any future policy decisions would be guided by the best available evidence and made through the governance structures of the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA, they said when asked if companies connected to the ultra-processed food industry would be excluded from future congresses as demanded in the petition.

### Exhibitors respond

According to Dudu Mthuli, Nutrition and Health Lead at Unilever Southern Africa, there was no conflict of interest. Unilever was involved only in hosting an exhibition stand and in no other elements of the congress, she said.

Unilever’s stand communicated how their brands fitted into healthy eating. Unilever applied to exhibit at the event, because they were committed to partnering with like-minded stakeholders in educational and sponsorship activities that supported their view of making nutritious, balanced diets accessible, affordable, and enjoyable through science and expertise, Mthuli said.

She added that Unilever’s registered dietitians and food scientists also used the opportunity to keep up to date with science as presented at the sessions.

Unilever’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

Danone saw its participation in the congress “not as a conflict of interest, but as a confluence of interest”, according to Head of Corporate and Regulatory Affairs at Danone SA, Leanne Kiezer.

Danone SA participated in the Nutrition Congress as a presenter in the scientific programme and as an exhibitor, she said. The FoodSAMSA Project published the report [Inside our Food Environments South Africa 2025](https://foodsamsa.samrc.ac.za/FOODSAMSA%20Report%20WP2.pdf) that assessed the commitments and practices of 29 food companies in South Africa for supporting healthier food environments and improving population nutrition. The independent report ranked Danone SA as the leading food company assessed, with a score of 83/100 for its commitments and practices for supporting food environments and improving population nutrition, according to Kiezer.

She added that the Association for Dietetics in South Africa had invited Danone SA to submit an abstract to the Nutrition Congress scientific committee, to share the study results and to provide further detail on the commitments and practices that contributed to Danone SA’s score. Danone SA submitted an abstract that was independently reviewed by the congress’s scientific committee and accepted for an oral presentation as part of the scientific programme.

Danone SA also participated as an exhibitor, with a stand focused on sharing evidence on the health and nutritional benefits of yoghurt. The educational content was not brand or product specific and focused on yoghurt and its benefits from a category perspective, Kiezer said.

Danone SA believed that describing a food company or its portfolio through the single lens of “ultra-processed food” oversimplified the broader picture of nutritional quality, according to Kiezer. The overall nutritional profile of individual foods, and their contribution to dietary patterns, were also important considerations, she said.

Based on Danone SA’s assessment of total volumes sold in 2025, 74% passed the nutrient profiling calculator defined in draft Regulation 3337, while 71% would not carry warning labels under the current draft Regulation 3337 criteria, Kiezer claimed. These benchmarks provided important context on the nutritional quality of their portfolio, she said.

Daily Maverick contacted PepsiCo for comment, but had not received a response by the time of publication.**DM**

## Mauritius Imposes Curfew After Violent Protests

[Facebook](https://allafrica.com/#facebook)[Twitter](https://allafrica.com/#twitter)[WhatsApp](https://allafrica.com/#whatsapp)[Flipboard](https://allafrica.com/#flipboard)[LinkedIn](https://allafrica.com/#linkedin)[Reddit](https://allafrica.com/#reddit)[Email](https://allafrica.com/#email)[Share](https://www.addtoany.com/share#url=https%3A%2F%2Fallafrica.com%2Fstories%2F202610150222.html&title=Mauritius%20Imposes%20Curfew%20After%20Violent%20Protests)

[FreeWorldMaps](https://www.freeworldmaps.net/africa/mauritius/mauritius-location-globe.jpg "https://www.freeworldmaps.net/africa/mauritius/mauritius-location-globe.jpg")

Where is Mauritius?

15 October 2026

Mauritius has[imposed](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo "https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo")an overnight curfew following violent protests over water shortages and the rising cost of living, marking the island's worst unrest in decades.

Demonstrations escalated after a woman was shot and injured by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting were not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody.

Protesters burned tyres, blocked roads and vandalised police stations and public infrastructure, prompting school and public transport closures.

The British embassy in Mauritius cautioned its citizens about the possibility of further demonstrations, advising them to steer clear of protests and large gatherings. The French embassy also urged French nationals in the country to remain vigilant.

Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam warned that those responsible would face consequences.

Analysts warn that unrest could return if water shortages persist until the rainy season in December.

title: North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
zh_title: 朝鲜和中国延迟12年后开通新桥
summary: 6 小时前 埃维岛和朱莉安娜·汗 新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州 据中国官方媒体报道，随着邻国之间贸易关系的改善，一座拖延已久的连接中国和朝鲜的公路大桥已经开通。中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是应对国际社会因平壤核武器计划而实施严厉制裁的生命线。新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州，将成为朝鲜的主要陆路通道。
content:
6 小时前

埃威岛和

朱莉安娜·汗

新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州

据中国官方媒体报道，随着邻国之间的贸易关系改善，一座拖延已久的连接中国和朝鲜的公路大桥已经开通。

中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是应对国际社会因平壤核武器计划而实施严厉制裁的生命线。

新鸭绿江大桥全长3公里（1.9英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州，将成为两国之间贸易的主要陆路通道。

该项目最初定于 2014 年启动，但由于与北京的关系变得冷淡，朝鲜停止了道路和海关设施的建设，因此被无限期推迟。

中国国务院总理李强在周四的视频讲话中表示，这座大桥是“象征中朝传统友谊的新地标”，两国关系正在“翻开新的篇章”。

新鸭绿江大桥是具有数十年历史的中朝友谊大桥的替代方案，该大桥建于 1937 年至 1943 年日本帝国占领该地区期间。

中国外交部发言人毛宁周三表示，这座新大桥是两国之间“互联互通的重要设施”，并补充说这条路线将“进一步便利贸易和人员往来”。
去年，双边贸易额达到 27 亿美元，标志着恢复到大流行前的水平，这主要是由中国对朝鲜的出口推动的。

韩国外国语大学中国研究教授康俊英告诉英国广播公司，由于联合国对朝鲜的制裁仍然有效，跨境贸易“不太可能”突然增加。

“平壤还对突然涌入的中国进口产品保持警惕，这将大大扩大中国对其国内市场的影响力，”他补充道。

“中国很清楚这些担忧，因此贸易更有可能逐步增长。”

北京和平壤是长期盟友，双方签署了共同防御条约，这是中国与任何国家签署的唯一条约。这种关系经常被形容为“唇齿相依”，这是中国前领导人毛泽东首先提出的一句话。

但联盟并非没有紧张。

2010年代的大部分时间里，由于北京对平壤核武器计划的耐心逐渐减弱，两国关系一直处于冷淡状态。金正恩于 2017 年进行了核试验，此后加大了对被禁弹道导弹的试验力度，所有这些都增加了美国的警惕性，并加强了其与韩国和日本的军事联盟。

中国的态度最近发生了转变。
牛津大学讲师爱德华·豪厄尔（Edward Howell）告诉英国广播公司（BBC）：“虽然仅仅十年前，北京还公开批评朝鲜核化，甚至呼吁平壤无核化，但现在中国对此几乎没有说什么。”

观察人士称，原因之一是朝鲜因乌克兰战争而与俄罗斯走得更近。

至少 2,300 名朝鲜士兵[据信已死亡](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypr5985ejo) 在乌克兰为俄罗斯作战。作为回报，俄罗斯向朝鲜提供石油，这违反了联合国的制裁。据估计，2024 年俄罗斯已向平壤输送了[超过 10 亿桶石油](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjr4pr0gyyzo) 作为平壤武器和战略物资的付款。

【原文 English Original】
6 hours ago

Koh Ewe and

Julianna Khan

The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea

A long-delayed road bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, Chinese state media report, as trade ties improve between the neighbours.

China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a lifeline against heavy international sanctions over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme.

The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea, and is set to become the main land route for trade between them.

Its launch, initially slated for 2014, had been indefinitely postponed after North Korea halted construction of its roads and customs facilities, as relations with Beijing turned frosty.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang, in a video address on Thursday, said the bridge was a "new landmark symbolising the traditional friendship between China and North Korea", and that the two countries were "opening a new chapter" in bilateral ties.

The New Yalu River Bridge is an alternative to the decades-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which was built between 1937 and 1943 during Imperial Japan's occupation of the region.

The new bridge is an "important facility for connectivity" between the two countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday, adding that the route would "further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges".

Last year, bilateral trade reached $2.7bn, marking a recovery to pre-pandemic levels, mostly fuelled by Chinese exports to North Korea.

A sharp and sudden increase in trade across the border is "unlikely" as the UN sanctions on North Korea remain in effect, Kang Jun-young, a professor of Chinese studies at the Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, tells the BBC.

"Pyongyang is also wary of a sudden flood of Chinese imports that would greatly expand China's influence over its domestic market," he adds.

"China is well aware of these concerns, so trade is more likely to grow gradually."

Beijing and Pyongyang are long-standing allies with a mutual defence treaty, the only one that China has with any country. The relationship is often described "as close as lips and teeth", a remark first made by China's former leader Mao Zedong.

But the alliance is not without tension.

Ties were frosty for much of the 2010s as Beijing's patience over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme wore thin. Kim Jong Un conducted a nuclear test in 2017 and has since ramped up tests of banned ballistic missiles - all of which increased US wariness, and strengthened its military alliances with South Korea and Japan.

China's attitude has shifted more recently.

"Whilst only a decade ago, Beijing was overtly critical of North Korea's nuclearisation - and indeed calling for Pyongyang's denuclearisation - China is now saying little, if anything, to this effect," Edward Howell, a lecturer at the University of Oxford, tells the BBC.

Observers say one reason is that North Korea has grown closer to Russia because of the Ukraine war.

At least 2,300 North Korean soldiers are [believed to have died](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypr5985ejo) fighting for Russia in Ukraine. In return, Russia supplies North Korea with oil, in violation of UN sanctions. In 2024, Russia was estimated to have sent [more than a billion barrels of oil](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjr4pr0gyyzo) as payment for Pyongyang's weapons and troops.

Last month, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge, which Russian state media said would allow the movement of up to 300 vehicles and more than 2,000 people every day.

So Beijing is believed to be trying to reassert its sway over Pyongyang by rekindling ties.

Air China resumed direct flights between Beijing and Pyongyang in March after a six-year hiatus triggered by the pandemic. The two countries [reopened passenger train services](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cdxz8v58xvyo) the same month.

Chinese President Xi Jinping's first state visit of this year, in June, was to Pyongyang, where he met North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

"The opening of the New Yalu River Bridge demonstrates bilateral relations are improving and that Xi Jinping's June visit to North Korea was more than symbolic," says Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul.

"But the long delay, including North Korea's pandemic self-isolation and domestic socioeconomic crackdowns, shows what a difficult partner Pyongyang can be for Beijing."

# 专利巴士申请加票价近两成 官员议员竟帮口 评论指是没抗衡力量的新香港宿命

香港四家专利巴士公司申请大幅加价，加幅由17.7%至8.1%不等，加幅之大，引起市民叫苦已是必然，但相关政策局在向立法会提交的文件则更多是为巴士公司解释，由爱国者垄断的立法会，其议员亦没有代市民叫屈，被报章社评形容官员和议员都是在「为加价保驾护航」；更有评论形容议员是， 巴士公司的「另类发言人」，预料小市民继续默默承受这种在没有民间社会抗衡力量下的「宿命」。

发表时间： 15/10/2026 - 10:39 更改时间： 15/10/2026 - 11:51

 14 分钟 浏览时间

 每天接送三百多萬人次的四家專利巴士公司申請大幅加價，市民叫苦，但負責審批的官員和立法會議員，卻對巴士持「理解」的立場。 © （麥燕庭提供）

 作者： [香港特约记者 麦燕庭](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%89%B9%E7%BA%A6%E8%AE%B0%E8%80%85-%E9%BA%A6%E7%87%95%E5%BA%AD/ "香港特约记者 麦燕庭")

广告

继续浏览后续

在2019年社会运动被打压之前，公用事业的加价申请幅度不单未见有被传媒形容为「狮子开大口」，更会引起立法会内尚有民主派的议员狠批，以及惹来民间的「民间监管公共事业联委会」代市民提出质疑和建议，但在爱国者治港和《港区国安法》实施後，立法会内民主派议员「清零」，不少民间组织亦已解散或偃旗息鼓，以致在运输及物流局各立法会提交四大巴士公司加价申请後，传媒只能街访个别市民表达心声，基本上都是指加幅过巨。

运输及物流局昨(14日)早向立法会提交的文件显示，巴士公司在4月时已提出加价申请，行走港九新界的城巴和九龙巴士公司(九巴)分别申请加价17.7%和16%；主要营运新界往返机场及北大屿山的龙运巴士有限公司(龙运)申请加幅是8.1%；而只在大屿山行驶的新大屿山巴士公司(屿巴)，申请加幅是9.8%。文件解释，巴士公司面对地下铁等交通工具的竞争丶油价持续高企丶营运和人工成本持续上升等挑战，需进一步提升财务状况以继续提供服务。

**「赚少了」便申请加价**

以油价为例，局方指出，受中东战事影响，车用柴油价格急升，3月燃油开支较1月急升85%至逾1.32倍，而8月的油价仍较1月增加近一倍；影响之下，巴士公司首季盈利普遍按年减少两至三成，加上乘客人数仍低於疫情前水平，在过去两年平均每日只录得逾370万乘客人次，仍较2010至2019年平均每日392万人次为低，反映乘客出行习惯出现结构改变，巴士公司面对挑战。

不过，大部分巴士公司并非因为亏蚀而申请加价，而是盈利下跌。文件指出，各巴士公司截至今年6月，临时估算税後盈利均较去年同期大跌55%至31%，当中只有屿巴是录得亏损。时间上，今次巴士公司申请加价亦只是与上次获准加价後不足一年半提出。资料显示，除了龙运巴士公司是在2023年6月加价4.2%之後丶事隔近三年再次申请加价，其馀三间巴士公司均在2025年1月起获准加价4.3%至7,5%後丶事隔一年零四个月後再提出加价降议。

立法会交通事务委员会明(16日)早将举行会议，讨论加价事宜，但传媒采访委员会主席陈恒镔等个别议员所得，议员对巴士公司的经营困难均抱「理解」和「无奈」的态度；个别议员更建议当局协助巴士公司增加非票务收入或提供短期补助来减轻加价压力。至於运输及物流局局长陈美宝亦只是说，会平衡巴士公司财务及市民负担能力，强调政府会做好把关工作。

**四报社评谈加价 半数显体谅 「谁为市民发声？」**

事关民生，香港十馀家报章中，有七家以巴士申请加价为头条新闻，但只有少部分在标题中已提出批评；当中，有四份报章以巴士申请加价为主题，批评的只占半数，但都只能望政府真的把好关，因为专利巴士公司加价须由特首会同行政会议批准。

《明报》社评以《巴士又加价折射困局 高油价时代急需对策》为题指出，政府须顾及加价对民生的影响，而在预见石油库存到明年下半年才有机会恢复而令油价回落，预料电力公司亦会随巴士後尘提出加价，呼吁政府拟定对策，协助市民应付燃料价格持续高企的危机。

《星岛日报》社论则以《专营巴士岂能动辄「嗌加价」 改革票价机制刻不容缓》为题指出，公众对巴士公司「开天杀价」无反制之力，唯一可倚仗的是政府，若港府过度侧重巴士公司的立场，将会引起民怨和消费信心下降，不利经济复苏。长远而言，当局除了帮助公司开源之外，还可考虑引入「可加可减」的票价调整机制，防止突然大幅加价的情况发生。

在社评中提出批评的，分别是《东方日报》和已停止发行实体报章的《成报》。《东方》以《巴士狼死(按：极狠的意思)加价 政府必须把关》为题指出，巴士公司的申请加幅可说是「飞擒大咬」，但「官员和议员则口径一致，松口为加价保驾护航。可怜小市民生活百上加斤，谁为我们发声？」社论续称，「人人化身巴士公司发言人」，估计巴士公司加价必然获批，以去年1月三间巴士公司获批加幅大约较申请加幅少两个百分点为例，预料今年两大巴士公司很大机会加价逾一成。

《东方》又说，巴士公司去年仍有盈利，但脱班丶削班等情况反而加剧，「蚀了一些即喊穷加价，还有官员议员替他们缓颊，商民待遇差距实在太大。」但以现在的情况，只能望声称重视市民负担能力的官员「不要得个讲字，必须做好把关，不能任由巴士公司开天杀价！」

由实体转为网上发表的《成报》，其社评以《4间巴士公司申加价幅度惊人 从没正视开源 只向市民伸手》为题，猛批巴士公司不思进取，经营思维落後，「习惯把自己的无能，变成乘客的帐单」，赚少了便以最省事的方式申请加价，而申靖亦沦为讨价还价的姿态，「彷佛(加幅)报高一点无妨，反正最後总有人替它修饰」，而市民亦被视作最终必须接受结果的一方。

资深新闻工作者李锦洪今早在网上节目中，对巴士加价及小市民反对无从的情况大加批评。他指出，高油价并非今日才出现的问题，但港府缺乏长远策略推动，议员亦没超前建议，反应更是与民生脱节丶对事件了解不足以致回应沦为笑话，慨叹「如此议政质素！」；再加上香港再没有民间社会的抗衡力量，令问题一直原地踏步。

title: Government budgets R9.60 to feed SA’s young children – what it really costs
summary: What does it actually cost to provide nutritious food to young children while they are in early childhood development (ECD) centres? A new ECD Nationally Costed Nutrition Basket tool, launching in October 2026, aims to answer this question.
content:
What does it actually cost to provide nutritious food to young children while they are in early childhood development (ECD) centres? A new ECD Nationally Costed Nutrition Basket tool, launching in October 2026, aims to answer this question. The [ECD Nutrition Basket](https://zero2five.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/From-Menu-to-Framework-to-Basket_Development-of-an-ECD-Nutrition-Basket_TechReport_Oct2026.pdf), designed by the [Zero2Five Trust](https://zero2five.org.za/#) and the [Pietermaritzburg Economic Justice and Dignity Group](https://pmbejd.org.za/) (PMBEJD), together with public health nutrition consultant and registered dietitian Philippa Barnard, translates existing national nutrition guidance into a defined food requirement that can be planned, quantified, costed and monitored over time. Currently, 40% of the Department of Basic Education’s R24-per-child-per-day ECD subsidy provided to registered centres is ring-fenced for nutrition, amounting to R9.60 per child per day. Piloting of the ECD Nutrition Basket in August and September 2026 has shown the gaps that exist between this nutrition allocation and the real cost of buying food for an early learning programme. In September 2026, pilot costing for the [nutrition basket](https://zero2five.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ECD-Nutrition-Basket_Information_14Oct2026.pdf) put estimated food costs at R7.35 per child per day for children aged nine to 23 months, and R13.06 per child per day for children aged two to six years. “There is... increasing attention to what happens in the ECD environment, because young children spend a significant part of their day there and may receive an important part of their food there... I think we also need to raise the standard of what we mean when we say, ‘children are being fed’. It’s not enough for children to have full tummies. We need to make sure that the food they’re eating is of good quality – that means vegetables, fruit, protein and a diversity of foods,” said Barnard. “That is really central to why we developed the basket... We hope to bring to the conversation a connection between the nutritional requirement and the cost.”
](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/StBqAEv_XBtFVuLPkXzTTIlS8GI=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/Tamsin-ECD-nutrition1_927934.jpg) The ECD Nutrition Basket translates existing national nutrition guidance into a defined food requirement that can be planned, purchased, prepared, quantified, costed and monitored over time. (Photo: Supplied / Zero2Five) The contents of the ECD Nutrition Basket are based on a practical one-week menu, developed using the national Department of Health Nutrition Guidelines for ECD Programmes and implementation experience in early learning centres. It includes a diverse range of foods across the major food groups, including fortified staple foods, vegetables, fruit, legumes, eggs, tinned fish, milk and maas. Children in the nine-to-23-month age group usually consume smaller portions of food than older children, and rely on a milk-feeding component in their diet, according to Barnard. The ECD Nutrition Basket does not attempt to monetise breastmilk or include infant formula. ### **Realities in ECD centres** In most cases, ECD centres are attended by a greater number of older children in the two-to-six-years age group than younger children under 23 months, explained Barnard. The September ECD Nutrition Basket included food costing for an “illustrative 20-child ECD centre” comprising 20% younger and 80% older children, where the children attended the programme for 20 days in a month. In this example, estimated food costs sat at R11.92 per child per day, amounting to an overall monthly cost of R4,768.47. If all children in this illustrative centre were covered by the ECD subsidy, there would still be a shortfall of R928 per month for purchasing food items, explained Barnard. In cases where not all children at a centre were eligible for the subsidy, the financing gap could be even larger. The current costing for the nutrition basket covers food ingredients only, excluding additional expenses such as labour, cooking fuel, cleaning materials and equipment. Learners gather for breakfast at Bulungula Preschool in Xhora Mouth, Eastern Cape. The morning meal provides vital nutrition, helping young children start the day ready to learn, play and participate in early childhood development activities. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) An ECD practitioner in Zero2Five’s network, located in Mkhambathini Local Municipality near Pietermaritzburg in KwaZulu-Natal, said that while they received the department’s ECD subsidy, they faced many challenges in providing adequate nutrition at their centre. “The Department of Basic Education does not pay the subsidy on time. Children suffer, and even the workers. We’re not happy at all,” said the practitioner, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “I would like to see changes in the support for nutrition of children, because in rural areas, many parents are not working.” Another practitioner from the same municipality, also speaking anonymously, said that it was challenging to cover the cost of nutrition with the ECD subsidy due to the rising prices of food, electricity, gas and transport. Among the food items the practitioner struggled to afford each month were meat, fruits, vegetables and milk. Reflecting on the changes they would like to see regarding nutrition support for children in ECD centres, the practitioner advocated for an increase in the funding for food costs under the ECD subsidy, and timeous payments of the subsidy to practitioners. ### **Making the cost of adequate nutrition visible** Barnard highlighted the strong national focus on child nutrition and ending child stunting in South Africa. She noted that while there were good nutrition guidelines in place for ECD centres, the gap emerged when it came to the implementation of these recommendations. “[ECD centres are] an environment where we have an opportunity to improve children’s nutritional intake... Instead of saying, ‘What can we provide with the minimum amount of money,’ we’re starting with the question of what children need for good nutrition, and then saying, ‘Okay, now what does that cost?’” she said. The monthly monitoring of food costs through the ECD Nutrition Basket could be useful to a range of stakeholders in the early learning sector, added Barnard. For centres and practitioners, it provided a practical framework for nutritional food provision; for civil society, it was a “transparent reference point” for understanding and discussing the cost of providing nutritious food to young children; and for the government and policymakers, it could be an evidence base for planning and budgeting in ECD settings. “As food prices change and fluctuate month on month, it can also expose potential risk... If one component of the food system comes under pressure and the prices increase, what kind of impact does that have on the foods that can be provided at an ECD centre?” said Barnard. Daily Maverick reached out to the departments of health and basic education about the ECD Nutrition Basket, but had not received a response by the time of publishing. **DM**

title: Zoning in – African countries pair factories, logistics and ports to boost investment
summary: African special economic zones (SEZs) are becoming larger industrial bets as governments and investors bring ports, factories, processing and logistics into the same development. New projects in Kenya and Nigeria are putting major industria
content:
African special economic zones (SEZs) are becoming larger industrial bets as governments and investors bring ports, factories, processing and logistics into the same development.

New projects in Kenya and Nigeria are putting major industrial facilities alongside maritime infrastructure, while operating zones in Togo and South Africa are showing how the model can support processing, exports and manufacturing.

In Kenya, construction has begun on the planned Dangote East Africa Petroleum Refinery in Lamu, part of a proposed $16-billion complex combining refining, petrochemicals and power generation.

The project is being developed in the Lamu Port-South Sudan-Ethiopia-Transport Corridor, linking the planned industrial complex to a wider transport and logistics network serving regional markets.

In Nigeria, DP World, Ogun State and the Ogun Deep Sea Port Company have signed agreements to explore a 10,000ha development combining a proposed deep-sea port with a SEZ. The projects reflect a shift in the business case for SEZs, from providing land and incentives to reducing the cost and complexity of producing and moving goods.

### Investing in Africa

“For us, that’s what successful SEZs are about – capturing more value in Africa, creating jobs, increasing exports and really building globally competitive African industries,” said Osam Iyahen, senior director and head of infrastructure at the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC).

Iyahen was speaking during an Invest Africa webinar on the role of SEZs in building competitive industries in Africa that was held on 1 October.

The AFC invests in power, transport, logistics, natural resources and heavy industry, making integrated zones attractive because they bring several of these requirements together. “SEZs are quite important to us because they bring all these sectors together,” Iyahen said.

The AFC invested $150-million in Arise Integrated Industrial Platforms in 2020 to support its expansion into Benin and Togo.

Iyahen said the platform has helped countries to move from exporting raw commodities towards local processing and manufacturing, attracting additional investment and creating jobs.

Togo provides a concrete example. Togo Soja, a soybean processing company based at the Adétikopé Industrial Platform, shipped its first export of processed shea butter on 1 October, opening the country’s 2026 export season for the product.

The shipment followed the ramp-up of a plant that has been operating since 2023.

The Adétikopé Industrial Platform says the operation is developing an integrated chain from raw-material supply and industrial processing to packaging and international markets.

“This shipment reflects the industrial dynamic developed on the platform and its ability to support companies from the transformation of raw materials to opening up to international markets,” said Idiola Sandah, general administrator of the platform’s coordination authority.

Togo introduced export taxes on cashew nuts, soybeans and shea nuts from January 2026 as it seeks to encourage more processing inside the country. The quantity of shea butter in the first shipment was not disclosed, but the move illustrates the commercial logic behind integrated industrial platforms: export more processed products rather than raw commodities.

### Warehouses and ports

Logistics is another part of that equation. Agility Global is building warehouse parks in African cities, providing ready-to-use facilities for companies entering new markets. “

We’re building large-scale, first-world warehouse parks across the main cities in the continent,” said Geoffrey White, CEO of Agility Africa.

The company has opened facilities in five countries and some are already fully occupied, White said.

Its customers include e-commerce companies, agro-processors, manufacturers, vehicle assemblers and fast-moving consumer goods distributors. About 65% of its tenants are multinationals and 35% are small and medium-sized businesses.

“Our concept is to remove, for companies moving into Africa, the risk of land tenure and project execution, and to remove the capital burden of going into the African marketplace,” White said.

Ports are becoming another piece of the industrial proposition. At the Lagos Free Zone, Nigeria’s Lekki Deep Sea Port sits inside an industrial development designed to combine manufacturing, logistics and maritime access.

Tejaswi Avasarala, director of commercialisation at the Lagos Free Zone, said the project had been shaped by the more than five decades of manufacturing experience in Nigeria of Tolaram, a multinational conglomerate with diversified businesses. The company has a “very deep and first-hand understanding” of the challenges facing investors trying to build deeper value chains and local supply chains, Avasarala said.

“We are trying to bring all that into the way we have conceptualised and delivered Nigeria’s first deep-sea port,” he said.

The same model is now being explored on a larger scale in Ogun State. The proposed Ogun development remains at the planning stage, so its projected investment and employment figures have yet to become operating results.

Kenya is pursuing a similar port-industrial model in Mombasa. DP World and GulfCap Africa signed a shareholders agreement in September for the planned 222ha Mombasa Industrial Park. The first phase is expected to cover 40ha, and more than 60 local and international companies have expressed interest. The completed park is projected to support more than 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.

At Dongo Kundu, the Kenyan government has allocated about $572-million for infrastructure supporting a 3,000-acre SEZ that includes industrial parks, logistics facilities and a free port.

Further south, the Coega SEZ in South Africa shows what the model can look like after years of development. The zone, next to the Port of Ngqura in the Eastern Cape, had 67 operational investors and more than 11,000 operational jobs by the end of the 2024 financial year. – Bird Story Agency/**DM**

title: Shein and Temu ban: Cosatu backs call to save local jobs
summary: The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) backed a motion put forward by the Southern African Clothing and Textile Workers’ Union (Sactwu) for the government to ban international e-commerce platforms [Shein](https://www.dailymaver
content:
The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) backed a motion put forward by the Southern African Clothing and Textile Workers’ Union (Sactwu) for the government to ban international e-commerce platforms [Shein](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2024-09-22-shein-fast-fashion-sacred-cows-and-an-ai-turbocharge/) and [Temu](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/opinionista/2024-04-09-dont-be-fooled-by-shopping-platform-temus-childlike-interface/), citing a 2025 study which estimated that the platforms could jeopardise up to 34,000 local jobs by 2030.

Sactwu made a presentation on day three of Cosatu’s 15th National Conference, held on Wednesday, 15 October, at Emperor’s Palace in Johannesburg, where members displayed placards showing illustrations of handbags, carpets and other textiles on the front with the numbers of local jobs under threat in each industry on the back.

The placards showed estimated job losses based on current employment numbers in existing factories, ranging from seven to 304 across textile, clothing, leather, and cosmetics industries, amounting to a total of 34,000.

“Comrades, Shein and Temu now sell more products than other global retailers in South Africa,” said Sactwu president Susan Khumalo.

“It is causing job losses, it is also pushing down wages, pushing our benefits and our working conditions, as the clothing and textile workers union and the other workers [competing] with the cheap imports. If nothing is done, comrades, to change this, our city and our families will lose 34,000 jobs by 2030 as clothing and textile [industries], including the retailers,” she said.

### ‘They’re selling cheaper and faster’

South African Clothing and Textile Workers’ Union members display placards on 14 October, 2026, showing the potential number of jobs lost by 2030 in the clothing, textile, and manufacturing industries due to the proliferation of international e-commerce platforms. The Cosatu 15th National Congress is being held at Emperor’s Palace, Johannesburg. (Photo: Naledi Mashishi)

Shein, a Chinese-founded and Singaporean-headquartered e-commerce platform, first entered the South African market in 2020 and became the [most downloaded shopping app](https://personal.nedbank.co.za/learn/blog/shein-temu-taxes-south-africa.html) by 2023. Chinese-owned Temu entered the market in 2024. Both companies were able to take advantage of low overheads due to a lack of brick-and-mortar stores, aggressive marketing, high shipment volumes and tax loopholes to undercut local retailers.

In the second quarter of 2024, the Bureau for Economic Research found that confidence among semi-durable goods retailers of products such as textiles, clothing, footwear and leather goods fell to 38% from 68% in the first quarter, [adding](https://www.ber.ac.za/Documents/ViewMode/1212272a-f33b-4dee-b74f-6e7a2660f6d3) that retailers such as Shein “may also strain domestic clothing retailers”.

By the end of 2024, the companies [captured R7.3-billion](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/shein-temu-outpace-global-retail-giants-south-africas-fashion-market-2025-08-05/) in sales, amounting to 37.1% of South Africa’s retail, clothing, textile, footwear and leather e-commerce market.

Previously, clothing retailer Shein made a somewhat slower, but still impressive, splash using a concept of retail and marketplace sales from China.

“These companies have taken off in South Africa. They are selling cheaper and faster than anyone else. But it is putting enormous pressure on workers and our local manufacturers, including retailers and workers in the public sector as well. It’s only four years of Shein and other online shopping, but it took a huge chunk of our clothing, textile, footwear and leather, including the retail market,” said Khumalo in her presentation.

Cosatu resolved to back the call and urged all other members to delete their Shein and Temu apps and commit to only sourcing goods from local retailers, in solidarity.

### Shein’s growth slowed to 11%

Members of the South African Clothing and Textile Workers Union hold up placards showing the number of jobs that could be lost by 2030 in the clothing, textile and manufacturing industries. (Photo: Naledi Mashishi)

However, Shein and Temu are already undergoing significant sales downturns. This is because in 2025, the South African Revenue Service (SARS) cracked down by removing tax exemptions on imported goods priced below R500. Shein, which previously grew between 30% to 50% annually, slowed to just 11% in 2025, while Temu recorded average monthly declines of 42% in the same period.

Independent economic strategist and board adviser Refilwe Moloto told Daily Maverick that the 34,000 figure might be outdated, given that it was calculated before the SARS tax amendments were in place. She warned an outright ban on the apps could be an uncompetitive approach that could have negative trade-offs.

> “Protectionist measures of that nature are likely to encourage, below the table, irregular and non-regulated trading. And what you really do want is for the taxpayer to be able to collect accordingly for value-added products and you’d also want to not have nefarious dealings across the border.”

She said South Africa was not unique in its predicament. Shein and Temu have had a larger impact on the US, French, and Latin American markets. In the US, Shein ranks as the third-largest online retailer.

In addition, the local textile industry has struggled to remain competitive due to local conditions such as high energy prices, the collapse of rail transportation and administrative costs.

“Those are structural issues that will impact the retailers themselves and the margins that they’re able to claim. It is not Shein’s fault that they operate in a country that makes their inputs cheaper, and that’s something that the government may need to address,” she said. **DM**

title: ‘Agriculture minister sounds El Niño warning
summary: As a [super El Niño](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-07-09-godzilla-el-nino-what-it-is-why-it-matters-and-our-complete-coverage) threatens South Africa’s farming sector and the wider economy with drought and potential water sho
content:
As a [super El Niño](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-07-09-godzilla-el-nino-what-it-is-why-it-matters-and-our-complete-coverage) threatens South Africa’s farming sector and the wider economy with drought and potential water shortages, Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp has warned against complacency.

Much of South Africa’s summer rainfall region got decent rains in September, an additional layer of security to good soil moisture and dam levels. But El Niño only typically gains traction here once summer is fully under way.

“We are very much concerned. We had a bit of rain now in September, but I tell farmers, ‘Please, do not be deceived that this is not going to happen.’ Some of our farmers are planting now, and I think we are going to have a very hot and dry November, December and January,” Aucamp told Daily Maverick on the sidelines of the AgriSA congress on Wednesday in Irene.

“We’ve got early-warning systems, but this is going to be next level.”

El Niño usually triggers drought in this region, and the latest event is widely regarded as the strongest on record. It is [expected to last until at least February](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-08-el-nino/).

Aucamp is concerned about the timing of water-use restrictions.

“We should not wait for this to be declared a disaster before municipalities put in water restrictions, and then it spills over and farming communities get less water. I think we need to be proactive in implementing water restrictions from the municipalities’ side,” he said.

> “Every municipality will have to decide that on their own, because they know their own resources. But we cannot have a situation where municipalities wait too long to implement what is required, and then water restrictions might have to be implemented on the farming community. We can’t get to a point where they can't irrigate their crops.”

With municipal elections looming, it may be the case that water restrictions before 4 November are not seen as politically wise in some municipalities – but the consequences could be dire. It’s also the case that many South Africans already experience frequent and unintended “water restrictions” because local government failures lead to dry taps.

### A game of yields

Aucamp said the department was advising farmers to focus on their most fertile sections of land and not plant in marginal areas.

Most commercial farmers are probably doing so anyway, guided by high-tech and capital-intensive tools such as precision farming, which enables the precise distribution of inputs based on soil quality using GPS. This is a [key reason behind the surge in South African crop yields](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-08-01-gmos-and-precision-farming-bring-food-prices-down/), rain or shine, in recent decades.

The first indication of the amount of land that will be devoted to summer grain crops, including maize, will come on 27 October when the government’s Crop Estimates Committee will provide its first estimate on farmers’ planting intentions.

Maize fields face a crucial season ahead as South Africa braces for a potentially severe El Niño-induced drought. (Photo: iStock)

Surging fuel and fertiliser prices triggered by the Ukraine and Iran wars will be a constraint. Aucamp said that fertiliser prices had soared by more than 300% since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Turning to livestock, Aucamp said farmers would have to reduce their herd numbers to prevent overgrazing.

A smaller national cattle herd will also reduce the number of vaccines required to contain the foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak. On that front, Aucamp said that 70% of the national herd of more than 13 million animals has been vaccinated to date and that the goal of 80% by the end of this year was in reach.

> “If you’ve got a cow that’s not giving you a calf any more, or a cow that’s not giving the proper amount of milk any more, get rid of that animal. Rather have less stock but stock of good quality. We can always build up that stock again.”

Amid all the focus on El Niño and FMD, other agriculture issues such as the politically thorny one of land reform have faded on the public’s radar screen. But Aucamp, who assumed the agriculture portfolio 3½ months ago, said it was a priority of his.

“We are busy with a project where we are identifying 100 farms per province, black farmers who are currently renting their farms from government, to transfer the land into their names, and this is just the start,” he said.

“They must have title deeds. We must see that land gets out of the hands of the government. You’re not going to invest in a farm if it’s not yours. You can use it as collateral to obtain finance,” he said. **DM**

# Japan's Kioxia sheds two-thirds of peak market value as China chip rivals emerge

Rising cost of data center debt also poses a risk to memory supplier

Kioxia's April-September earnings, due out Oct. 30, are expected to show a historic profit gain. (Kioxia)

KYOHEI SUGA

October 16, 2026 01:18 JST

English (Original)

[](https://twitter.com/share?text=Japan%27s+Kioxia+sheds+two-thirds+of+peak+market+value+as+China+chip+rivals+emerge&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Ftech%2Fsemiconductors%2Fjapan-s-kioxia-sheds-two-thirds-of-peak-market-value-as-china-chip-rivals-emerge&via=NikkeiAsia)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Ftech%2Fsemiconductors%2Fjapan-s-kioxia-sheds-two-thirds-of-peak-market-value-as-china-chip-rivals-emerge)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Japan%27s+Kioxia+sheds+two-thirds+of+peak+market+value+as+China+chip+rivals+emerge+https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Ftech%2Fsemiconductors%2Fjapan-s-kioxia-sheds-two-thirds-of-peak-market-value-as-china-chip-rivals-emerge)[](https://t.me/share/url?text=Japan%27s+Kioxia+sheds+two-thirds+of+peak+market+value+as+China+chip+rivals+emerge&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Ftech%2Fsemiconductors%2Fjapan-s-kioxia-sheds-two-thirds-of-peak-market-value-as-china-chip-rivals-emerge)[](mailto:?subject=Japan%27s%20Kioxia%20sheds%20two-thirds%20of%20peak%20market%20value%20as%20China%20chip%20rivals%20emerge&body=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Ftech%2Fsemiconductors%2Fjapan-s-kioxia-sheds-two-thirds-of-peak-market-value-as-china-chip-rivals-emerge)

TOKYO -- Japanese memory chip maker Kioxia Holdings' market value has shrunk to one-third of the peak it reached about four months ago, as rising interest rates threaten data centers' business model and Chinese competitors close in.

Kioxia's market capitalization has fallen to around 21 trillion yen ($134 billion) from roughly 60 trillion yen in June, the month that it overtook Toyota Motor to become Japan's most valuable listed company. That lead did not last.

Its Tokyo-listed shares fell as much as 14% on Thursday, part of a [global sell-off](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/markets/asian-stocks-plummet-as-ai-debt-and-inflation-fears-bite) in semiconductor stocks.

Advertisement

"As the negative factors add up, investors are panic selling to liquidate their margin positions," said Kazuyoshi Saito, a senior analyst at IwaiCosmo Securities.

Advantest, a Japanese maker of chip-testing devices that had been holding on to gains relatively well, dropped as much as 16% on Thursday.

One negative factor is credit concerns surrounding U.S.-based cloud services company CoreWeave. Yields on its bonds have soared since around Tuesday amid growing investor doubts about the sustainability of Big Tech's massive debt-fueled data center buildup.

Another headwind is the rise of Chinese rivals. ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has said new products due out this year will feature [breakthrough technology](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/tech/semiconductors/memory-breakthrough-by-china-s-cxmt-puts-chip-rivals-on-back-foot). The company is racing with South Korean competitor Samsung Electronics to bring new advances to market.

Seoul-listed shares in Samsung and rival memory chip maker SK Hynix also fell sharply on Thursday.

CXMT makes DRAM short-term memory, so it is not a direct competitor to Kioxia, which produces NAND for long-term storage. But another Chinese chipmaker that does produce NAND -- Yangtze Memory Technologies -- has indicated a readiness to increase output. Investors see as the rise of Chinese competition as a risk to established chip-related stocks.

Kioxia plans to release its April-September half earnings on Oct. 30. The QUICK Consensus forecast sees its full-year net profit at 5.54 trillion yen -- about 10 times the year-earlier level.

Yet the company's shares are trading at only 3.7 times forward earnings, lower than the multiple of 15.4 for Tokyo Stock Exchange's Prime market as a whole. Samsung and SK Hynix also have low multiples of 4.5 and 3.5, respectively.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. achieved record quarterly profits in its July-September earnings released Thursday. Still, these results are "probably too little, too late to improve sentiment on the chip sector overall," Saito said.

Kioxia is working toward a product strategy less prone to memory market volatility, including a partnership with U.S.-based chip giant Nvidia.

title: Uganda's Sugarcane Boom Leaves Families Hungry - What Needs to Change
summary: Busoga, in eastern Uganda, is a low, fertile plateau [surrounded](https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture "https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture") on three sides by [Lake Victoria](https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria "https
content:
Busoga, in eastern Uganda, is a low, fertile plateau [surrounded](https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture "https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture") on three sides by [Lake Victoria](https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria "https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria"), the [River Nile](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/nile-river/ "https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/nile-river/") and [Lake Kyoga](https://wldb.ilec.or.jp/Lake/AFR-15 "https://wldb.ilec.or.jp/Lake/AFR-15"). Most of its [4.3 million people](https://www.ubos.org/ "https://www.ubos.org/") farm small, rain-fed plots. Yet hunger is common: in the 2024 census, about a third of Busoga households reported going [whole days](https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/3-in-10-ugandans-going-without-food-daily-4795334 "https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/3-in-10-ugandans-going-without-food-daily-4795334") without food.

Sugarcane has been grown commercially here [since the 1920s](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210"), when one family established a large sugar processing facility. New investors followed after the government stopped setting sugar prices and [opened the industry](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/249121468110056798/pdf/multi-page.pdf "https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/249121468110056798/pdf/multi-page.pdf") to the private sector in 1991.

**Read more: [South Africa's small sugar farms are producing less than they could: study finds ways to boost them](https://theconversation.com/south-africas-small-sugar-farms-are-producing-less-than-they-could-study-finds-ways-to-boost-them-285098 "https://theconversation.com/south-africas-small-sugar-farms-are-producing-less-than-they-could-study-finds-ways-to-boost-them-285098")**

[Seven mills now operate](https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/growth-of-sugar-mills-in-busoga-threatens-wetlands-4724652 "https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/growth-of-sugar-mills-in-busoga-threatens-wetlands-4724652") in and around the Busoga region, with the amount of sugar cane planted tripling in size between [2000 and 2024](https://www.newsecuritybeat.org/2026/08/unenforced-rules-in-ugandas-sugar-sector-food-insecurity-and-climate-change/ "https://www.newsecuritybeat.org/2026/08/unenforced-rules-in-ugandas-sugar-sector-food-insecurity-and-climate-change/"). Tens of thousands of families also grow cane on their own land as "outgrowers", [selling this](https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2020/13 "https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2020/13") on contracts to the sugar mills.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

I spent over 20 years working in Uganda's civil service before becoming an academic. For my [doctoral research](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210"), I set out to understand why decades of sugarcane growth had not reduced hunger in Busoga. I visited two parts of Busoga - the Jinja and Buyende districts - and interviewed 27 officials, local leaders and farmer representatives. I also asked four groups of farmers for their views.

I asked who decides how land is used, who signs contracts, who receives the money, and how households eat while waiting for the harvest.

[My research found](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210") that the hunger in Busoga isn't caused by farmers not growing enough sugarcane to sell. [The prices](https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-busoga-sugarcane-farmers-fume-as-prices-drop-for-seventh-year/ "https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-busoga-sugarcane-farmers-fume-as-prices-drop-for-seventh-year/") of sugarcane [are dropping](https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-sets-minimum-sugarcane-price-to-protect-farmers-in-busoga/ "https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-sets-minimum-sugarcane-price-to-protect-farmers-in-busoga/"), but my research found that the main problem is that sugar mills mainly sign contracts with men.

This means that decisions about what to use land and cash for are solely in the hands of the men. They don't always use the cash to feed their families. The work of feeding families falls mainly on women, who are left only with the option of planting what little land is left with food crops.

**Read more: [Child labour, poverty and terrible working conditions lie behind the sugar you eat](https://theconversation.com/child-labour-poverty-and-terrible-working-conditions-lie-behind-the-sugar-you-eat-95242 "https://theconversation.com/child-labour-poverty-and-terrible-working-conditions-lie-behind-the-sugar-you-eat-95242")**

To solve the problem, the government and sugar companies all need to end the practice of only contracting with men, set up contracts with women farmers too and make sure that women from sugarcane farming families inherit contracts automatically when their husbands die.

**One fifth of the land, all the responsibility**

[Only about 20%](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210") of the available farmland in the Jinja and Buyende districts of Busoga is available to grow food crops. Up to 80% of farmland owned by families is used to grow sugarcane to sell.

Mills recruit sugarcane farmers through male household heads, whose names appear on the contracts. In one focus group, women described husbands signing multi-year contracts covering the family's entire land without consulting them. When they questioned this, the women were told the decision was not theirs.

**Read more: [Why Ethiopia's showcase sugar projects face huge challenges](https://theconversation.com/why-ethiopias-showcase-sugar-projects-face-huge-challenges-122871 "https://theconversation.com/why-ethiopias-showcase-sugar-projects-face-huge-challenges-122871")**

The payment, a lump sum at harvest, is made to whoever signed the contract. A political leader in Buyende, speaking anonymously, told me that many men now keep the cane money and don't use it to buy food for the home.

[Uganda's Land Act](https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1998/16/eng@2023-12-31 "https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1998/16/eng@2023-12-31") says family land cannot be sold, leased, or mortgaged without a spouse's written consent. But cane deals rarely go through a land office, so no one checks if consent is being given.

**A widow inherits the cane, but not the contract**

[Uganda's constitution recognises](https://ulii.org/en/akn/ug/act/statute/1995/constitution/eng@2023-12-31 "https://ulii.org/en/akn/ug/act/statute/1995/constitution/eng@2023-12-31") the right of women to inherit land. Yet my research found that when an outgrower dies, the contract usually remains in his name, and his widow has no standing with the mill.

The mill's recruitment agent, who signs up farmers, might decide not to allow her to take over her husband's contract. A clan meeting may instead hand the land to a male relative. A bank may refuse her credit without a man's signature. Although this is not legal, my research found that it is common practice and the government hasn't put in place any way of stopping it.

**Read more: [33 million women grow food on plots in sub-Saharan Africa. Greener farming can boost their earnings - study](https://theconversation.com/33-million-women-grow-food-on-plots-in-sub-saharan-africa-greener-farming-can-boost-their-earnings-study-261880 "https://theconversation.com/33-million-women-grow-food-on-plots-in-sub-saharan-africa-greener-farming-can-boost-their-earnings-study-261880")**

Government extension officers, who advise farmers, visit only registered contract holders, and don't advise the wives of contract holders. [Researchers call this](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1549-0831.2003.tb00133.x "https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1549-0831.2003.tb00133.x") the gap between holding a right and being able to use it.

In some cases, young men inherit the family's land but then sell it to pay for a motorcycle, school fees, or a family obligation. With the land gone, many end up cutting and loading cane for daily wages. A technical officer in Buyende told me that most of those workers are children. Uganda's [employment law](https://mglsd.go.ug/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Employment-Act.pdf "https://mglsd.go.ug/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Employment-Act.pdf") bars this, but enforcement is weak: one study found that there were only [83 labour officers](https://globalmarch.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Policy-Brief_s.pdf "https://globalmarch.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Policy-Brief_s.pdf") in Uganda, but that 1,344 were needed to make sure that labour laws were not being broken.

**What needs to happen next**

All the different organisations in the sugar industry have a role to play in protecting the rights of women in sugarcane growing families.

First, the sugar mills should stop signing contracts with males only. Kidera Sugar, a new mill in Buyende that [opened in 2026](https://worldbusinessjournal.com/4385-2/ "https://worldbusinessjournal.com/4385-2/"), is now recruiting outgrowers, and has not set its contracting rules yet, so there's an opportunity for at least this sugar mill to introduce practices where women benefit equally.

**Read more: [How harvesting natural products can help rural people beat poverty](https://theconversation.com/how-harvesting-natural-products-can-help-rural-people-beat-poverty-108271 "https://theconversation.com/how-harvesting-natural-products-can-help-rural-people-beat-poverty-108271")**

Second, [the Sugar Industry Stakeholders Council](https://allafrica.com/stories/202512190520.html), the sugar industry regulator, gives mills their licences. It could change the situation by refusing to approve contracts without both spouses' signatures in the case of married couples. It could also start a new practice of requiring that all contracts pass on to widows. It could even make a rule that widows should retain a share of each farm's food crops.

Third, district land offices could register cane agreements so the Land Act's consent rule applies. Fourth, the labour ministry should fund the jobs of more inspectors in cane-growing areas.

As contract farming spreads, who signs the contract can determine who controls the income and whether the family has enough to eat.
